docs.t: D. Mass. — Same-day e-filing cutoff: 6:00 p.m.
docs.x: D. Mass.. Same-day e-filing cutoff: 6:00 p.m.. ECF is open around the clock, but a filing must be completed before 6:00 p.m. local time to count as filed that day. Most federal courts use midnight. (L.R. 5.4(d))

docs.t: D. Mass. — Put everything in the opening brief
docs.x: D. Mass.. Put everything in the opening brief. There is no reply as of right, except on summary judgment. Put every argument in the opening motion, because you may never get another word. Check the judge’s session order: some allow short replies, some bar sur-replies. (LR 7.1(b)(3))

docs.t: D. Mass. — Discovery is capped, and the client signs extension requests
docs.x: D. Mass.. Discovery is capped, and the client signs extension requests. 10 depositions, 25 interrogatories, 25 admissions, and only 2 sets of document requests per side. Parties can’t stipulate to extend response times, and requests to extend discovery or postpone trial must be signed by the lawyer and the client. (LR 26.1(c); LR 26.2(b))

docs.t: D. Mass. — Some things happen without a court order
docs.x: D. Mass.. Some things happen without a court order. No proof of service by day 90 plus a good-cause motion by day 104, and the clerk dismisses. No certified state court record within 42 days of removal, and the case goes back. (LR 4.1; LR 81.1)

docs.t: D. Mass. — Discovery motions follow LR 37.1’s procedure
docs.x: D. Mass.. Discovery motions follow LR 37.1’s procedure. Movant arranges the conference; the other side has 7 days to answer the request; item-by-item memorandum; 14 calendar days to respond to the motion; certificate in the margin of the last page. (LR 37.1)

docs.t: D. Mass. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: D. Mass.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

docs.t: D. Mass. — overview
docs.x: D. Mass.. E-filing closes at 6:00 p.m.,LR 5.4(d),ECF is open around the clock, but a filing is timely only if completed before 6:00 p.m. that day. No reply brief without leave,LR 7.1(b)(3),After the motion and the opposition, every other paper needs leave of court, replies included. The exception is summary judgment: LR 56.1 lets the movant reply within 14 days. Many judges’ session orders set their own reply rules, so check before you draft. Confer before every motion, and say so,LR 7.1(a)(2),No motion may be filed unless counsel certify that they conferred and tried in good faith to resolve or narrow the issue. docs.t: D.P.R. — Pay bar renewal fees by October 1 every year
docs.x: D.P.R.. Pay bar renewal fees by October 1 every year. To stay in good standing, pay the annual bar membership renewal fee on or before October 1. Lawyers who don’t lose CM/ECF access and eligibility for criminal and pro bono appointments. You can request inactive status so fees stop accruing, and to return you file a written request and pay that year’s renewal fee. The court’s fee schedule lists the annual amount as $75 (FJC 2024). (D.P.R. LR 83A(d))

docs.x: D.P.R.. English only, certified. Anything not in English must come with a certified English translation, or the court won’t consider it. Budget time and money for translations from day one. (LR 5(c))

docs.x: D.P.R.. Oppose in 14 days or waive. Missing the 14-day objection deadline is deemed a waiver of objection. (LR 7(b))

docs.x: D.P.R.. Replies need leave; continuances need three dates. Ask leave to reply (7 days, 10 pages, new matters only). To continue a hearing or conference, certify three alternative dates that work for everyone. (LR 7(c); LR 16(j))

docs.x: D.P.R.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.x: D. Ariz.. Text-searchable PDFs,LRCiv 7.1(c),Convert filings straight from the word processor. Don’t print and scan. Proposed orders,LRCiv 7.1(b)(2), (3),Lodge a separate proposed order when you ask for specific relief (not needed for Rule 12(b) or 56 motions). No firm name or identifying information, no date or signature block, and email it to chambers separately. Extensions,LRCiv 7.3(b),A motion to continue or extend must state the other side’s position, or that you tried and couldn’t get it. Caption,LRCiv 7.1(a)(3),Use proper capitalization for the parties’ names in the caption. Magistrate judge consent,LRCiv 3.7(b),When a case draws a magistrate judge, every party must file the consent or election form. docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — 20 pages, and replies need leave
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. 20 pages, and replies need leave. Memoranda for and against a motion can’t exceed 20 pages, and a reply can’t exceed 5. On ordinary motions a reply is allowed only if the court grants a motion for leave, which must be filed within 7 days of service of the response. (LR 7.2(e), (c))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — 14 days to respond, 28 for motions to dismiss and summary judgment
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. 14 days to respond, 28 for motions to dismiss and summary judgment. Respond to most motions within 14 days after service. A response to a Rule 12(b) or 12(c) motion is due in 28 days, and a response to a summary judgment motion in 28 days or when a responsive pleading is due, whichever is later. (LR 7.2(a)(2); 12.1(b); 56.1(b))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Certificate of consultation, or the motion can be denied
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Certificate of consultation, or the motion can be denied. Every motion except those under Rules 12, 56, 59 and 60, discovery motions included, needs a certificate saying you consulted and couldn’t reach accord, or all agree. Name the participating lawyers and the date and manner. The movant starts the conference and gives reasonable notice. Skipping the certificate can be good grounds for denial. (LR 7.2(a)(1)(B))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Proposed order goes to the judge’s ECF mailbox
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Proposed order goes to the judge’s ECF mailbox. All motions except those under Rules 12, 56, 59 and 60 come with a proposed order in a word processing format, sent only to the presiding judge’s ECF mailbox, not the regular email address. (LR 7.2(a)(1)(A))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Silence can lose the motion
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Silence can lose the motion. Failing to respond on time to a motion other than one to dismiss may be deemed good grounds for granting it. (LR 7.2(a)(2))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Summary judgment: 10-page fact statement, answered fact by fact
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment: 10-page fact statement, answered fact by fact. The movant files a separate, numbered statement of facts with record citations, up to 10 pages. The opponent answers each fact right below it as undisputed, undisputed for this motion only, or disputed with a citation. Missing the deadline means the facts are treated as undisputed. (LR 56.1)

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Reconsidering an interim order is narrow
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Reconsidering an interim order is narrow. Motions to reconsider interlocutory orders are allowed only as motions for revision under Rule 54(b). You must show a material new fact or law you couldn’t earlier know, new facts or a change in law, or a manifest failure to consider material arguments. No repeating old arguments, on pain of sanctions. (LR 7.3)

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — No continuance by stipulation
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. No continuance by stipulation. Cases aren’t continued on stipulation. Ask as soon as the need appears, by written motion (oral only in emergencies), and show good cause. The motion must follow LR 7.2. (LR 16.5)

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.x: W.D. Tenn. deadline. Reply on summary judgment: 14 days after service of the response, no leave needed (L.R. 56.1(c))

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — 14 days to respond, 25 pages, and a 5-page optional reply
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. 14 days to respond, 25 pages, and a 5-page optional reply. Respond within 14 days after service of the motion, in no more than 25 pages. If you don’t respond in time, the motion is treated as unopposed. A reply is optional, due 7 days after the response, and limited to 5 pages. (LR 7.01(a)(3), (4))

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Say you conferred, except on a few motions
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Say you conferred, except on a few motions. When all parties have lawyers, every motion must state that you conferred with all other counsel and whether the relief is opposed, or describe your attempts. Motions under Rules 12, 55, 56, 59 and 60, and pro hac vice motions, are excepted. (LR 7.01(a)(1))

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Memorandum of law, separate or combined
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Memorandum of law, separate or combined. A motion that needs a legal ruling comes with a memorandum citing authority. A combined filing must be titled “MOTION AND MEMORANDUM OF LAW.” A separate memorandum can’t be filed as an exhibit to the motion. 25 pages without leave. (LR 7.01(a)(2))

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Seal in two steps: motion first, document second
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Seal in two steps: motion first, document second. File a motion for leave to file under seal and do NOT attach the document. Right after, file the proposed document using the “Sealed Document” event. Get this wrong and the document may be public, and the clerk can’t fix it without an order. (LR 5.03(b))

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Sealing needs compelling reasons, document by document
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Sealing needs compelling reasons, document by document. The motion must overcome the presumption that records are public and show the sealing is narrowly tailored, analyzing each document with facts and authority. An unopposed motion or agreed order that skips the standard doesn’t comply. (LR 5.03(c))

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Discovery fights start with a joint statement
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Discovery fights start with a joint statement. Before a motion to compel, to quash, or for a protective order, confer in good faith. If that fails, file a joint discovery dispute statement before asking for a discovery conference, and attach it to any discovery motion. (LR 37.01)

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Summary judgment: separate memo, numbered facts, and 21 days
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment: separate memo, numbered facts, and 21 days. The memorandum and the Statement of Facts are separate docket entries. Number each fact and cite the record, and give opposing counsel an editable copy. The response is due in 21 days, and each response to a fact starts with “Undisputed,” “Undisputed for Summary Judgment Purposes Only,” or “Disputed.” (LR 56.01)

docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — 25 pages, and replies aren’t expected
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. 25 pages, and replies aren’t expected. A brief can’t exceed 25 pages unless the court orders otherwise. The court says reply briefs are not necessary or required, and a reply can’t reargue the opening brief. It must respond directly to the answering brief. (LR 7.1(b), (c))

docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — 14 days to answer, 21 for dispositive motions
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. 14 days to answer, 21 for dispositive motions. File the opening brief with the motion. The answering brief is due 14 days after service of the opening brief, or 21 days for a dispositive motion. A reply is due 7 days after the answering brief. The court can change this, or the parties can stipulate to a schedule within 14 days after the motion is filed. (LR 7.1(a))

docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — Extra briefs need approval
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. Extra briefs need approval. No more briefs, affidavits or papers on a motion without the court’s approval. The one exception is a supplemental brief of up to 5 pages on developments after the last brief. The response is due in 7 days and is limited to 5 pages. (LR 7.1(d))

docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — Silence can be treated as waiver
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. Silence can be treated as waiver. Failure to respond to a motion may be deemed a waiver of any opposition to the relief sought. The court can also act before the response time runs out in exceptional circumstances. (LR 7.2)

docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — Seal only after an order
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. Seal only after an order. Nothing goes under seal until the court enters an order specifying what is sealed. Documents that are the subject of a motion to seal may sit under seal temporarily. File redacted versions where only part is sealed, unless the court says otherwise. (LR 26.2(b))

docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — No continuance by stipulation
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. No continuance by stipulation. Cases aren’t continued on stipulation of counsel. You need a written motion with a supporting affidavit and a showing of good cause. (LR 38.2)

docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — Discovery motions quote the discovery
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. Discovery motions quote the discovery. A discovery motion must recite word for word each interrogatory, request, answer, response and objection at issue, or attach the discovery document. (LR 37.2)

docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.x: E.D. Tenn. deadline. Reply brief: 7 days after service of the answering brief (L.R. 7.1(a)(3))

docs.x: E.D. Tenn. deadline. Response to a supplemental brief: 7 days after service, 5 pages at most (L.R. 7.1(d))

docs.x: E.D. Tenn. deadline. Bill of costs: 21 days from entry of judgment (L.R. 54.1)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Watch for the Notice of Motion Setting
docs.x: W.D. La.. Watch for the Notice of Motion Setting. On a contested motion the clerk ordinarily issues a notice with briefing deadlines and chambers-copy rules. If none issues and the judge gives no instructions, oppose within 14 days of the motion and reply within 7 days of the opposition. (LR 7.4)

docs.t: W.D. La. — 25 pages, and a reply gets 10
docs.x: W.D. La.. 25 pages, and a reply gets 10. A memorandum or brief can’t exceed 25 pages, excluding tables, and a reply can’t exceed 10. Any memorandum over 10 pages needs a table of contents and a table of authorities with page references. Exceeding the limit takes the judge’s leave. (LR 7.1, 7.8)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Certificate of conference on non-dispositive motions
docs.x: W.D. La.. Certificate of conference on non-dispositive motions. Before filing, confer with every interested party and include a certificate describing the substance of the conference. If they don’t respond, state your efforts. The court can sanction failure to communicate. (LR 7.4.1)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Discovery motions need an in-person or phone conference
docs.x: W.D. La.. Discovery motions need an in-person or phone conference. The certificate must say counsel conferred in person or by telephone and why they couldn’t agree, or that opposing counsel refused. The movant arranges the conference and attaches a proposed order. (LR 37.1)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Summary judgment lives in the memoranda
docs.x: W.D. La.. Summary judgment lives in the memoranda. The movant’s memorandum states the legal basis, the undisputed material facts, and a pinpoint reference to the exhibit for each fact. The opposition states the genuinely disputed facts with pinpoint references. (LR 56.1, 56.2)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Extension and continuance motions need a certificate
docs.x: W.D. La.. Extension and continuance motions need a certificate. State whether the request is opposed and why, or the efforts made to find out. (LR 7.9)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: W.D. La.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.x: W.D. La. formatting. Page limits: 25 pages for a memorandum, 10 for a reply, excluding tables (LR 7.1, 7.8)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Tables
docs.x: W.D. La. formatting. Tables: Over 10 pages needs a table of contents and table of authorities (LR 7.1)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Paper
docs.x: W.D. La. formatting. Paper: 8½ by 11, paginated, double-spaced, with single-spaced footnotes and quotations allowed (LR 10.1)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Caption
docs.x: W.D. La. formatting. Caption: Division, district judge, magistrate judge, and the Rule 10 information (LR 10.1)

docs.x: W.D. La. formatting. Proposed orders: On a separate page with ex parte and discovery motions, except summary judgment and Rule 12 motions (LR 7.3)

docs.t: W.D. La. — Opposition (default if no setting issues)
docs.x: W.D. La. deadline. Opposition (default if no setting issues): 14 days after the motion is filed (L.R. LR 7.4)

docs.x: W.D. La. deadline. Reply (default if no setting issues): 7 days after the opposition is filed (L.R. LR 7.4)

docs.x: W.D. La. deadline. ADR discussion: Before the Rule 26(f) conference and within 60 days after discovery closes (L.R. LR 16.3.1)

docs.t: M.D. La. — 21 days to respond to a motion
docs.x: M.D. La.. 21 days to respond to a motion. File the response, with opposing affidavits and supporting documents then available, within 21 days after service. The court can set a shorter or longer time for good cause. (LR 7(f))

docs.t: M.D. La. — Replies without leave only on Rule 12 and Rule 56
docs.x: M.D. La.. Replies without leave only on Rule 12 and Rule 56. Reply memoranda on Rule 12 and Rule 56 motions are due within 14 days after the response is served. Surreplies on those motions need leave. Replies and surreplies on every other motion need leave. (LR 7(f))

docs.t: M.D. La. — 25 pages, 10 for a reply
docs.x: M.D. La.. 25 pages, 10 for a reply. Memoranda are limited to 25 pages excluding attachments. Tables, certificate of service, and a signature block that begins on or before the last page don’t count. Replies and surreplies get 10 pages. Exceeding the limit takes leave. (LR 7(g))

docs.t: M.D. La. — Every contested motion needs a separate memorandum
docs.x: M.D. La.. Every contested motion needs a separate memorandum. The memorandum states the reasons and cites authority, and you file all evidence the motion needs from outside the record. Memoranda can’t be supplemented without leave. (LR 7(d))

docs.t: M.D. La. — Summary judgment: numbered fact statements, admit, deny or qualify
docs.x: M.D. La.. Summary judgment: numbered fact statements, admit, deny or qualify. The movant files a short statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs, without footnotes or tables, each with a record cite. The opponent admits, denies or qualifies each numbered paragraph and supports each denial or qualification. (LR 56(b), (c))

docs.t: D.S.C. — 35 pages for a first brief, 15 for a reply
docs.x: D.S.C.. 35 pages for a first brief, 15 for a reply. No memorandum can exceed 35 double-spaced pages for an initial brief or 15 for a reply unless the court allows an exception. Affidavits, supporting documents and required copies of authority don’t count. (Rule 7.05(B))

docs.t: D.S.C. — Replies are discouraged, and due in 7 days
docs.x: D.S.C.. Replies are discouraged, and due in 7 days. Reply only to matters first raised in the response or its attachments, within 7 days after the response is served unless the court orders otherwise. (Rule 7.07)

docs.t: D.S.C. — Confer first on most motions, but not dispositive ones
docs.x: D.S.C.. Confer first on most motions, but not dispositive ones. Motions must carry counsel’s affirmation that they conferred or tried to confer in good faith. Excluded are motions to dismiss, for summary judgment, for new trial or judgment as a matter of law, other similar dispositive motions, foreclosure cases and stay motions under Rule 16.00(C). There is no duty to consult a pro se litigant. (Rule 7.02)

docs.t: D.S.C. — Sealing without prior approval is summarily denied
docs.x: D.S.C.. Sealing without prior approval is summarily denied. Attach a non-confidential descriptive index and counsel’s certification. Skip the procedure and the request is denied. (Rule 5.03)

docs.t: D.S.C. — Discovery is served, not filed
docs.x: D.S.C.. Discovery is served, not filed. Interrogatories, document requests, requests for admission, their responses, and deposition transcripts are not filed. File only the relevant portion when you seek relief or need it for a motion or trial. (Rule 5.01)

docs.t: D.S.C. — Extension motions need specifics
docs.x: D.S.C.. Extension motions need specifics. State the current deadline, any earlier extension, the days requested with the new date, and whether other deadlines move. Discovery extensions are granted only in unusual cases. (Rule 6.01)

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — “Suggestions,” not briefs, and no oral argument unless you mark it
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. “Suggestions,” not briefs, and no oral argument unless you mark it. Motions are supported and opposed with “suggestions.” Any request for oral argument must be clearly marked on the first page of the motion or the suggestions. The court may or may not hold argument. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 7.0(a), (e))

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Fourteen days to oppose, twenty-one on summary judgment
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Fourteen days to oppose, twenty-one on summary judgment. Opposing suggestions are due 14 days after the motion is filed, or 21 days for summary judgment. The moving party may reply within 14 days after the opposing suggestions are filed. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 7.0(c))

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Fifteen pages to support, fifteen to oppose, ten for a reply
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Fifteen pages to support, fifteen to oppose, ten for a reply. Statements of fact, exhibits, signature blocks, and certificates of service don’t count. Anything over 10 pages needs a table of contents and a table of authorities. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 7.0(d))

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Pro hac vice lawyers have 14 days to finish the paperwork
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Pro hac vice lawyers have 14 days to finish the paperwork. You may appear first, but if you don’t associate with a bar member, file the petition, and pay the fee within 14 days of appearing, the court can remove you from the case, on motion or on its own. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 83.5(f)(2))

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Summary judgment: your first paragraph admits or controverts every fact
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Summary judgment: your first paragraph admits or controverts every fact. The movant begins its suggestions with a numbered statement of uncontroverted facts. The opponent begins by admitting or controverting each paragraph with support. Facts not specifically controverted are deemed admitted. The same applies to the movant’s reply on additional facts. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 56.1)

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Discovery motions: phone call to the judge first
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Discovery motions: phone call to the judge first. After a good-faith phone or in-person conference (a demand letter is not enough), arrange an immediate telephone conference with the judge and opposing counsel, certifying your compliance. You may not file a written discovery motion until after that call. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 37.1(a))

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — A scheduling extension needs a detailed proposed new order
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. A scheduling extension needs a detailed proposed new order. Show a specific need, attach a detailed proposed amendment to the scheduling order, and state the other side’s position. For discovery, name each remaining deponent and the date, time, and place of each deposition. The court requires good cause and active discovery. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 16.3)

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Bill of costs: 21 days
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Bill of costs: 21 days. File a verified bill of costs on the clerk’s form within 21 days of final judgment. Objections are due in 14 days, and the reply in 14 more. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 54.1(a))

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Notify the clerk of a settlement before noon the day before trial
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Notify the clerk of a settlement before noon the day before trial. In a jury case, notice must reach the clerk before noon on the last business day before trial. Otherwise the court may assess jury costs, including Marshal fees, mileage, and per diem, against the parties and their attorneys. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 83.10)

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Unpaid annual bar fee puts you on inactive status
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Unpaid annual bar fee puts you on inactive status. The clerk places you on inactive status and disables your CM/ECF account if you don’t pay the annual fee. You can’t appear while inactive, and a late payment can cost a reinstatement fee. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 83.5(d))

docs.t: W.D. Mo. — Former law clerks are barred from their judge’s old cases
docs.x: W.D. Mo.. Former law clerks are barred from their judge’s old cases. A former clerk may not work on any case that was pending before that judge during the clerkship. The court can disqualify the lawyer and the employer, and the employer must have procedures to prevent it. (W.D. Mo. L.R. 83.1(a))

docs.t: D.N.D. — Forty-page briefs, 28 days to respond, on dispositive motions
docs.x: D.N.D.. Forty-page briefs, 28 days to respond, on dispositive motions. A Rule 12 or Rule 56 motion needs a supporting memorandum of up to 40 pages filed with it. The response is due 28 days after service and filing and can run 40 pages. The reply is due 14 days after the response and is limited to 10 pages. Tables of contents and authorities are excluded. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 7.1(A)(1))

docs.t: D.N.D. — Non-dispositive motions: 20 pages, 14 days, 7-page reply
docs.x: D.N.D.. Non-dispositive motions: 20 pages, 14 days, 7-page reply. The memorandum is filed with the motion and limited to 20 pages. The response is due in 14 days (20 pages) and the reply in 7 days (7 pages). (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 7.1(A)(2))

docs.t: D.N.D. — Injunction motions follow the dispositive clock and page limits
docs.x: D.N.D.. Injunction motions follow the dispositive clock and page limits. Responses and replies on preliminary injunctions and other injunctive relief follow the 28 and 14 day deadlines, and the 40 and 10 page limits apply, including to temporary restraining orders. TRO timing itself is governed by Rule 65. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 7.1(A)(3))

docs.t: D.N.D. — Silence can be treated as an admission
docs.x: D.N.D.. Silence can be treated as an admission. A missed response may be deemed an admission that the motion is well taken, and a missing supporting memorandum an admission that the motion lacks merit. Either can lead to a summary ruling. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 7.1(B)(5))

docs.t: D.N.D. — The clock starts after both filing and service
docs.x: D.N.D.. The clock starts after both filing and service. Your time to respond or reply doesn’t begin until the motion or response has been both served and filed, whichever is later. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 7.1(B)(2))

docs.t: D.N.D. — No proposed orders unless the court asks
docs.x: D.N.D.. No proposed orders unless the court asks. Unless ordered, a proposed order should not be filed. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 7.1(B)(3))

docs.t: D.N.D. — Summary judgment: facts in the memorandum, with specific cites
docs.x: D.N.D.. Summary judgment: facts in the memorandum, with specific cites. The movant’s memorandum recites the uncontested material facts, separate from the argument, and the response states the facts it relies on and clearly identifies those contested. Failing to comply may result in denial or in granting the motion. The response must explain in its argument why contested facts are material. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 7.1(A)(1)(b), (c))

docs.t: D.N.D. — Discovery motions need a conference, and then one with the magistrate judge
docs.x: D.N.D.. Discovery motions need a conference, and then one with the magistrate judge. Confer in person, by phone, or in real time (an emailed demand is not enough). Then ask the assigned magistrate judge’s chambers for a conference before filing, unless the court grants leave. Noncompliance can lead to summary grant or denial and an award of costs and fees. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 37.1)

docs.t: D.N.D. — Costs: motion with a verified statement within 14 days
docs.x: D.N.D.. Costs: motion with a verified statement within 14 days. If the parties can’t stipulate, move for costs within 14 days of judgment with an attorney-verified itemized statement. Failure to comply may be deemed a waiver. Objections are due in 14 days and any reply in 7. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 54.1(A))

docs.t: D.N.D. — Stipulations bind only if filed and adopted by the court
docs.x: D.N.D.. Stipulations bind only if filed and adopted by the court. An agreement is not binding unless signed by all parties or their attorneys, filed, and adopted by the court, or made in open court on the record and adopted. (D.N.D. Gen. L.R. 1.7)

docs.x: D.N.D.. Exhibits: one attachment each, and no refiling. File a complete PDF of any transcript you offer. File each exhibit as a separate, well-described attachment, and cite the docket number of anything already on file rather than refiling it. (D.N.D. Civ. L.R. 7.1(B)(4))

docs.t: D. Neb. — The court’s generative AI rule: verify everything
docs.x: D. Neb.. The court’s generative AI rule: verify everything. You are responsible for the accuracy of quotations, citations, paraphrases, and analysis whether or not AI drafted them. If you use generative AI you must verify the contents, and a filing that was not properly verified may be stricken or draw sanctions. (NECivR 7.1(d)(2))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Word limits, not page limits: 13,000 and 6,500
docs.x: D. Neb.. Word limits, not page limits: 13,000 and 6,500. Supporting and opposing briefs may not exceed 13,000 words and reply briefs 6,500, counting everything including the caption, headings, footnotes, and quotations. Each brief needs a certificate stating the word count and the software used. (NECivR 7.1(d)(1))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Don’t file a motion to strike over word counts
docs.x: D. Neb.. Don’t file a motion to strike over word counts. A noncompliant brief may be stricken by the court on its own, with or without notice. An opposing party must not file a motion to strike for noncompliance. (NECivR 7.1(d)(1)(E))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Don’t call it an “opposition” or “response”: file a brief
docs.x: D. Neb.. Don’t call it an “opposition” or “response”: file a brief. A party opposing a motion must not file an answer, opposition, objection, or response. File a brief stating the reasons and authority. (NECivR 7.1(b)(1)(A))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Twenty-one days to oppose dispositive-type motions, fourteen for the rest
docs.x: D. Neb.. Twenty-one days to oppose dispositive-type motions, fourteen for the rest. A brief opposing a motion to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, for a more definite statement, or for summary judgment is due 21 days after the motion and brief are filed. Any other motion gets 14 days. (NECivR 7.1(b)(1)(B))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Failing to oppose forfeits your side of the facts
docs.x: D. Neb.. Failing to oppose forfeits your side of the facts. It is not a confession of the motion, but it precludes you from contesting the movant’s statement of facts. (NECivR 7.1(b)(1)(C))

docs.t: D. Neb. — The brief must be separate from the motion and from the evidence
docs.x: D. Neb.. The brief must be separate from the motion and from the evidence. A motion raising a substantial issue of law needs its own brief, filed with the motion and not attached to or incorporated in it. Failing to brief an issue may be treated as a waiver, and not following the rule may be treated as abandoning your position. (NECivR 7.1(a)(1)(A))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Evidence goes in separately with an index
docs.x: D. Neb.. Evidence goes in separately with an index. Evidentiary materials are filed separately with an evidence index listing each item and the related motion. Each exhibit needs a category (Exhibit A) and a description. An affidavit must authenticate the documents, and the exhibits cannot be in the same document as the affidavit. (NECivR 7.1(a)(2))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Summary judgment: a separate statement of facts, with page and line cites
docs.x: D. Neb.. Summary judgment: a separate statement of facts, with page and line cites. File a brief, the motion, and a separate statement of short numbered paragraphs with pinpoint cites, including page and line for depositions. A missing statement or missing cites may be grounds to deny the motion. Properly cited facts are admitted unless the response controverts them. (NECivR 56.1(a))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Bill of costs: 30 days, and post-trial motions don’t extend it
docs.x: D. Neb.. Bill of costs: 30 days, and post-trial motions don’t extend it. File a verified bill of costs within 30 days of judgment. Failing to do so waives taxable costs. (NECivR 54.1(b), (d))

docs.t: D. Neb. — No block billing in a fee application
docs.x: D. Neb.. No block billing in a fee application. Entries with multiple tasks and a single time increment are prohibited. (NECivR 54.3(b))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Midnight Central is the filing cutoff, and email is not filing
docs.x: D. Neb.. Midnight Central is the filing cutoff, and email is not filing. A document is not filed until you get the NEF. A document emailed or faxed to the clerk or judge is not considered filed. The judge may order a time certain instead. (NECivR 5.1(d), (e))

docs.t: D. Neb. — A judge can require a resident lawyer with full authority
docs.x: D. Neb.. A judge can require a resident lawyer with full authority. A judge may require a nonresident lawyer to associate with a lawyer who lives in the district and is a member of this bar. That lawyer’s name goes on every later filing, stays in the case unless another resident replaces them, and need not attend every proceeding unless ordered, but must have full authority to act for the client. (NEGenR 1.7(h))

docs.t: D. Neb. — The pro hac vice fee is mandatory
docs.x: D. Neb.. The pro hac vice fee is mandatory. The fee funds the court’s roll of attorneys and the Federal Practice Fund. Failing to pay it is cause to deny your admission to proceed pro hac vice. (NEGenR 1.7(g))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Fourteen days to resist; the brief rides with the motion
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Fourteen days to resist; the brief rides with the motion. Every motion needs a brief, filed as an electronic attachment under the same docket entry. A brief filed on a later day may be stricken as untimely. The resistance is due 14 days after service, except on summary judgment. (Iowa LR 7(b), (e))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — “Resistance,” not “opposition,” and no cross-motions inside it
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. “Resistance,” not “opposition,” and no cross-motions inside it. A resistance may not include a separate motion or cross-motion. File it as a new motion. (Iowa LR 7(e))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Silence means the motion may be granted without notice
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Silence means the motion may be granted without notice. If no timely resistance is filed, the court may grant the motion without notice. If you won’t resist, file a statement saying so. (Iowa LR 7(f))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Replies are rare: 7 days, 5 pages, new arguments only
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Replies are rare: 7 days, 5 pages, new arguments only. Replies are ordinarily unnecessary. You may file one without leave within 7 days of the resistance, up to 5 pages, to cite new authority or answer new arguments. Don’t reargue your opening brief. (Iowa LR 7(g))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Twenty-page limit, with a 10-page table-of-contents trigger
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Twenty-page limit, with a 10-page table-of-contents trigger. Briefs are limited to 20 pages, not counting tables of contents and authorities or the signature block. A brief over 10 pages needs a subject-matter table of contents on its first page. (Iowa LR 7(h), 10(b))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Summary judgment: 21 days to resist, and everything goes in an appendix
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Summary judgment: 21 days to resist, and everything goes in an appendix. The motion needs a brief, a statement of material facts, and an appendix, all filed together. The response is due in 21 days with its own brief, a response to each numbered fact, additional facts, and an appendix. All record cites go to specific appendix page numbers. (Iowa LR 56(a), (b), (e))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Don’t respond to a fact, and it may be admitted
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Don’t respond to a fact, and it may be admitted. A failure to respond to an individual statement of material fact, with appendix citations, may constitute an admission of that fact. The moving party replies to additional facts within 7 days. (Iowa LR 56(b), (d))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Paper copy if your summary judgment papers pass 100 pages
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Paper copy if your summary judgment papers pass 100 pages. If a motion, resistance, or reply with its appendix exceeds 100 pages and was e-filed, deliver a bound, tabbed paper copy to the clerk within 7 days. (Iowa LR 56(f), 10(c))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Costs: AO 133 within 14 days or the right is waived
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Costs: AO 133 within 14 days or the right is waived. File the AO 133 form within 14 days of judgment. Failing to do so waives the right to have costs taxed. Resist within 14 days of service. The clerk taxes costs 21 days after service. (Iowa LR 54(a)(1))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — A personal conference is required before discovery motions
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. A personal conference is required before discovery motions. Attach a declaration that you conferred personally in good faith and could not agree. Letters and a single phone message do not count. Motions to compel are due within 14 days after the discovery deadline unless there is good cause. (Iowa LR 37(a))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Annual bar fee, per district
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Annual bar fee, per district. Every lawyer admitted to the bar must pay an annual fee to each district where admitted, or the Chief Judge may suspend the lawyer until it is paid. (Iowa LR 83(b), (c)(3))

docs.t: S.D. Iowa — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: S.D. Iowa. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Only five local rules: the judge’s procedures do the rest
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Only five local rules: the judge’s procedures do the rest. The local rules cover admission, magistrate judges, ADR, juror contact, and e-filing. Briefing deadlines, page limits, and motion practice come from the Federal Rules and each judge’s own procedures, so read those before you file. (W.D. Wis. LR 1 through 5)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Everything is e-filed, with narrow paper exceptions
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Everything is e-filed, with narrow paper exceptions. All civil and criminal documents must be filed electronically. Paper is allowed only for administrative records, state court records and transcripts, criminal case-initiating documents, trial exhibits, pro se filings by non-Filing Users, juvenile criminal matters, and highly sensitive documents. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures II.B, II.C)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Open a civil case one way, never both
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Open a civil case one way, never both. Either email the clerk for a shell case number, or use the self-serve option in CM/ECF. The procedures say do not do both. A lawsuit is not filed until your complaint or notice of removal shows on the docket. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures IV.A)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Briefs, affidavits, and declarations are separate docket entries
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Briefs, affidavits, and declarations are separate docket entries. File each one as its own docket entry, not as an attachment to a motion. Exhibits are separate attachments with descriptive titles. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures V.C)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — PDFs: no passwords, 35 MB maximum
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. PDFs: no passwords, 35 MB maximum. Larger files must be filed in pieces, each under 35 MB. Password-protected or encrypted PDFs are rejected. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.A)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Consider ADR within 30 days of the defendants’ appearance
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Consider ADR within 30 days of the defendants’ appearance. Litigants must consider alternative dispute resolution within 30 days of defendants’ appearance. The clerk mediates civil cases at no charge. Pro se plaintiff cases, collection and U.S. mortgage foreclosure actions, social security appeals, and bankruptcy matters (except adversary proceedings) are exempt. (W.D. Wis. LR 16.6(A))

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — You must redact, and keep the unredacted copy for two years
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. You must redact, and keep the unredacted copy for two years. Use only the last four digits of SSNs and account numbers, initials for minors, birth year only, and city and state for home addresses in criminal filings. The clerk does not check. Keep the unredacted version for two years after the appeal period ends. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures VI.A)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Sealing follows Administrative Order 460
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Sealing follows Administrative Order 460. Use the “Motion to Seal” event. If it is denied, the documents are unsealed and public. Don’t move to seal a document already covered by a protective order. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures VI.B)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Jury instructions also go to chambers by email
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Jury instructions also go to chambers by email. Send proposed instructions and the verdict form in Word or WordPerfect to the judge’s chambers address, with the case number in the subject and file name. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures V.B)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — A technical failure is not an excuse for your own equipment
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. A technical failure is not an excuse for your own equipment. Only a failure of the ECF website counts. If it caused a late filing, file a declaration with any error message, and file on the first day the court is open after the deadline. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.G)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Bar renewal: not yet checked
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Bar renewal: not yet checked. We haven’t yet checked whether this court makes its lawyers renew their admission or pay periodic fees. Ask the clerk before assuming a lifetime admission. (Not yet checked)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — File type
docs.x: W.D. Wis. formatting. File type: PDF only, not password protected, under 35 MB each (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.A)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Signature
docs.x: W.D. Wis. formatting. Signature: “s/ full name” plus address, email, and phone (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.E)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Scans
docs.x: W.D. Wis. formatting. Scans: 300 dpi, black and white; color only where the original is in color (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures II.E, V.D)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Exhibits
docs.x: W.D. Wis. formatting. Exhibits: Each a separate attachment with a descriptive title (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures V.D)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Jury instructions and verdict form
docs.x: W.D. Wis. formatting. Jury instructions and verdict form: Word or WordPerfect emailed to chambers, named with the case number (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures V.B)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Consider alternative dispute resolution
docs.x: W.D. Wis. deadline. Consider alternative dispute resolution: Within 30 days of defendants’ appearance (L.R. W.D. Wis. LR 16.6(A))

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Counsel’s free PACER copy of a filing
docs.x: W.D. Wis. deadline. Counsel’s free PACER copy of a filing: Retrieve within 15 days of filing (L.R. W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures I)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — File after an ECF outage made you late
docs.x: W.D. Wis. deadline. File after an ECF outage made you late: First day the court is open after the deadline (L.R. W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.G)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Keep the unredacted version
docs.x: W.D. Wis. deadline. Keep the unredacted version: Two years after appeal time expires (L.R. W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures VI.A.2)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Keep signed originals for multiple-signature filings
docs.x: W.D. Wis. deadline. Keep signed originals for multiple-signature filings: Two years after final resolution, including appeals (L.R. W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.E)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — overview
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Admission is open to any lawyer licensed in a state or D.C.,W.D. Wis. LR 83.5(A), (B),Complete a verified application and pay the fee. Reciprocal discipline applies automatically in this court. Magistrate judges can decide most pretrial matters,W.D. Wis. LR 72.1,They hear pretrial matters except injunctions, judgment on the pleadings, summary judgment, dismissals, class certification, and suppression. On those, they submit recommendations. Consent cases go to the full-time magistrate judge in Madison. The NEF is your certificate of service,W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.D,No separate certificate is needed for documents served on Filing Users by a Notice of Electronic Filing. You do need one for anyone not served through ECF. Multiple signatures need care,W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.E,Type “s/ full name” for each signer or file a scan with all signatures, and keep the

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — The first 28-day extension is a notice, not a motion
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. The first 28-day extension is a notice, not a motion. Initial extensions of a pleading response or a discovery response must be made by a Notice of Parties’ First Extension of Time, with no proposed order, unless a party objects. It can’t exceed 28 days, must confirm no earlier extension and no conflict with court deadlines, and must report each other party’s agreement or your attempts to reach them. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 6-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Thirty-page briefs, fifteen-page replies, cut in 2024
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Thirty-page briefs, fifteen-page replies, cut in 2024. Supporting and response briefs may not exceed 30 pages, excluding tables, appendices, and certificates of service. Replies may not exceed 15 pages. The limit was reduced in July 2024. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(e))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Twenty-one days for Rule 12 motions, fourteen for others
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Twenty-one days for Rule 12 motions, fourteen for others. A response to a Rule 12(b), (e), or (f) motion is due 21 days after service, unless you amend as of course. Everything else is 14 days. Replies are 7 days. The court may rule summarily if no response is filed. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(c))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Don’t bury a motion inside a brief
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Don’t bury a motion inside a brief. A motion must not be contained in a brief, response, or reply to another motion unless the court orders it. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Summary judgment: 28 days to respond, and a surreply only for new evidence
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Summary judgment: 28 days to respond, and a surreply only for new evidence. The response and evidence are due 28 days after service and reply 14 days after that. A surreply is allowed only if the reply cites new evidence or objects to your evidence, within 7 days, limited to those issues. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(b), (d))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Facts live inside the brief, and they count against your pages
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Facts live inside the brief, and they count against your pages. There is no separate fact statement. The brief must contain a “Statement of Material Facts Not in Dispute,” and the response a “Statement of Material Facts in Dispute.” Each fact needs a record cite to a page or paragraph, and the court has no duty to search the record. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(a), (b))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Unrebutted facts are admitted without controversy
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Unrebutted facts are admitted without controversy. The court assumes the movant’s supported facts are admitted unless the non-movant specifically controverts them with admissible evidence. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(f))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — No motions to strike during summary judgment
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. No motions to strike during summary judgment. Raise objections to evidence in your brief. Collateral motions are disfavored. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(i))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Costs and fees: both within 14 days of final judgment
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Costs and fees: both within 14 days of final judgment. You can’t recover attorney’s fees and costs unless you file a bill of costs and a fee motion within 14 days after final judgment. An extension requires a motion filed before the deadline. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 54-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Call the magistrate judge before a discovery motion
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Call the magistrate judge before a discovery motion. After a good-faith conference fails, contact the magistrate judge’s chambers to see if a phone conference can resolve the dispute before you file. A deposition objection that threatens the deposition lets you recess to call chambers. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 37-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Fee, Rule 11, and disqualification motions need a conference statement
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Fee, Rule 11, and disqualification motions need a conference statement. The court may not grant these motions without a statement of reasonable efforts to confer, with the date, time, and place of every conference and everyone who took part. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(g))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Bar renewal: not yet checked. We haven’t yet checked whether this court makes its lawyers renew their admission or pay periodic fees. Ask the clerk before assuming a lifetime admission. (Not yet checked)

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Briefs
docs.x: S.D. Ind. formatting. Briefs: 30 pages (replies 15), excluding tables, appendices, and certificates of service (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(e))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Briefs over 30 pages
docs.x: S.D. Ind. formatting. Briefs over 30 pages: Table of contents with pages, statement of issues, and table of authorities (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(e)(3))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Summary judgment brief
docs.x: S.D. Ind. formatting. Summary judgment brief: Section labeled “Statement of Material Facts Not in Dispute”; response labeled “Statement of Material Facts in Dispute” (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(a), (b))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Record citations
docs.x: S.D. Ind. formatting. Record citations: To a page or paragraph of evidence that is in the record or in an appendix (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(e))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Bill of costs
docs.x: S.D. Ind. formatting. Bill of costs: AO Form 133 preferred (S.D. Ind. L.R. 54-1(b))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — First extension to respond to a pleading or discovery (by notice)
docs.x: S.D. Ind. deadline. First extension to respond to a pleading or discovery (by notice): Up to 28 days (L.R. S.D. Ind. L.R. 6-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Response to a Rule 12(b), (e), or (f) motion
docs.x: S.D. Ind. deadline. Response to a Rule 12(b), (e), or (f) motion: 21 days after service (L.R. S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(c)(2))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Response to any other motion
docs.x: S.D. Ind. deadline. Response to any other motion: 14 days after service (L.R. S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(c)(3)(A))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Reply on a motion
docs.x: S.D. Ind. deadline. Reply on a motion: 7 days after the response (L.R. S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(c)(3)(B))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Response to summary judgment
docs.x: S.D. Ind. deadline. Response to summary judgment: 28 days after service (L.R. S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(b))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Reply on summary judgment
docs.x: S.D. Ind. deadline. Reply on summary judgment: 14 days after the response (L.R. S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(c))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Surreply on summary judgment (new evidence or objections only)
docs.x: S.D. Ind. deadline. Surreply on summary judgment (new evidence or objections only): 7 days after the reply (L.R. S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(d))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Bill of costs and fee motion
docs.x: S.D. Ind. deadline. Bill of costs and fee motion: 14 days after final judgment (L.R. S.D. Ind. L.R. 54-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — overview
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Routine motions come with a proposed order,S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(d),File a suitable proposed order with any routine or uncontested motion. The court can rule before the response deadline unless the motion says someone objects. Authorities are not attached, unless Westlaw and Lexis don’t have them,S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(f),Attach a cited authority only if it is not on Westlaw or Lexis. Give electronic-only authority to the court or another party on request. Notify the court when you settle,S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(h),Tell the court immediately if you reasonably expect to settle the case or resolve a pending motion. Stipulate to facts for summary judgment only,S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(g),Parties may stipulate to facts for the motion and say the stipulation is not otherwise binding. Summary judgment against an unrepresented party needs a notice,S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(k),File and serve the notice in A

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — A 28-day automatic extension, by notice, once
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. A 28-day automatic extension, by notice, once. The deadline to respond to a pleading or discovery request is extended automatically by filing a notice, if it was not extended before, the extension is 28 days or less, and the notice states the old and new deadlines and that everyone you could reach agreed. It is not available when a party is unrepresented. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 6-1(b))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Twenty-one days to respond to a Rule 12 motion, fourteen for everything else
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Twenty-one days to respond to a Rule 12 motion, fourteen for everything else. Responses to Rule 12 motions are due 21 days after service, unless you first amend as of course. Other motions get 14 days. Replies are due 7 days after the response. The court may rule summarily if no response is filed on time. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(d))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Twenty-five pages for briefs, fifteen for replies
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Twenty-five pages for briefs, fifteen for replies. Supporting and response briefs ordinarily can’t exceed 25 pages, excluding tables and appendices, and replies can’t exceed 15. A brief over 25 pages (allowed only for extraordinary and compelling reasons) must include a table of contents, an issue statement, and a table of authorities. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(e))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Summary judgment: a separate fact statement, and a 28-day response
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Summary judgment: a separate fact statement, and a 28-day response. The movant files a motion, a brief, and a Statement of Material Facts with numbered paragraphs and record cites. The opponent has 28 days to file a brief and a Response that restates each paragraph verbatim, answers it, and cites evidence for every dispute. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(a), (b))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — No motion to strike on summary judgment
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. No motion to strike on summary judgment. Raise disputes about admissibility or materiality in your briefs. A separate motion to strike must not be filed. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(f))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — A Rule 12 defense is ignored until you file a motion and brief
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. A Rule 12 defense is ignored until you file a motion and brief. Motions under Rules 12, 37, 56, and 65(b) need a supporting brief. The court will not rule on a Rule 12 defense until the party who raised it files a motion and brief. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(b), (c))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Costs: file AO 133 within 14 days
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Costs: file AO 133 within 14 days. To recover costs, file and serve a completed AO Form 133 within 14 days after final judgment. You can ask for more time for good cause, but only by motion filed before the deadline. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 54-1(a))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Discovery motions need a certification with date, time, place, and names
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Discovery motions need a certification with date, time, place, and names. File a separate certification of your good-faith effort to confer, with the date, time, and place of the conference and who took part. The court may deny the motion without it, except where a pro se party is involved. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 37-1)

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Oral argument is requested in a separate document
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Oral argument is requested in a separate document. File a separate document explaining why argument is needed and how long it should take, with your supporting, response, or reply brief. No new evidence at argument. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-5(a))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Don’t put a hearing date in your notice
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Don’t put a hearing date in your notice. Don’t specify a hearing date in a motion unless the court or clerk authorized it. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-5(b))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Bar renewal: not yet checked. We haven’t yet checked whether this court makes its lawyers renew their admission or pay periodic fees. Ask the clerk before assuming a lifetime admission. (Not yet checked)

docs.x: N.D. Ind. formatting. Papers: 8.5 by 11 inch pages, 1-inch margins, double-spaced, consecutively numbered, with a title on the first page (N.D. Ind. L.R. 5-4(a))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Type
docs.x: N.D. Ind. formatting. Type: At least 12-point in the body and 10-point in footnotes (N.D. Ind. L.R. 5-4(a)(4))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Briefs
docs.x: N.D. Ind. formatting. Briefs: 25 pages (replies 15), excluding tables of contents, tables of authorities, and appendices (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(e))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Signature block
docs.x: N.D. Ind. formatting. Signature block: Filer’s name, address, phone, fax, and email, except on proposed orders and affidavits (N.D. Ind. L.R. 5-4(a)(9))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Manual filings
docs.x: N.D. Ind. formatting. Manual filings: Flat, unfolded, white paper, no cover or back, original signature (N.D. Ind. L.R. 5-4(b))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Automatic extension to respond to a pleading or discovery (by notice, once)
docs.x: N.D. Ind. deadline. Automatic extension to respond to a pleading or discovery (by notice, once): Up to 28 days (L.R. N.D. Ind. L.R. 6-1(b))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Response to a Rule 12 motion
docs.x: N.D. Ind. deadline. Response to a Rule 12 motion: 21 days after service (L.R. N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(d)(2)(A))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Response to any other motion
docs.x: N.D. Ind. deadline. Response to any other motion: 14 days after service (L.R. N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(d)(3)(A))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Reply brief
docs.x: N.D. Ind. deadline. Reply brief: 7 days after the response (L.R. N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(d)(2)(B), (3)(B))

docs.x: N.D. Ind. deadline. Response to summary judgment: 28 days after service (L.R. N.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(b))

docs.x: N.D. Ind. deadline. Reply on summary judgment: 14 days after the response (L.R. N.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(c))

docs.x: N.D. Ind. deadline. Bill of costs (AO 133): 14 days after final judgment (L.R. N.D. Ind. L.R. 54-1(a))

Extension motions: say the old and new dates and whether anyone objects,N.D. Ind. docs.t: D.S.D. — Twenty-one days to oppose, fourteen to reply; briefs capped at 30 pages
docs.x: D.S.D.. Twenty-one days to oppose, fourteen to reply; briefs capped at 30 pages. An opposed motion raising a question of law needs a brief. The response is due 21 calendar days after the motion and brief are served, and the reply 14 calendar days after the response. Briefs may not exceed 30 pages, excluding tables, certificate, and attachments, without prior approval. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 7.1(B))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Local counsel must attend everything, even by phone
docs.x: D.S.D.. Local counsel must attend everything, even by phone. Pro hac vice lawyers need local counsel who signs and files all documents and is present at every proceeding, including telephone and video conferences, unless the court orders otherwise. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 83.2(E))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Summary judgment: uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted
docs.x: D.S.D.. Summary judgment: uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. The movant files a separate, short, numbered statement of material facts with record cites. The opponent answers each numbered paragraph. Any fact in the movant’s statement not controverted is deemed admitted. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 56.1(A)–(D))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Attorney’s fees: 28 days from judgment or a possible waiver
docs.x: D.S.D.. Attorney’s fees: 28 days from judgment or a possible waiver. Move for fees and file an affidavit of time within 28 calendar days of judgment. Failure to move in time may be treated as a waiver of the claim. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 54.1(C))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Costs: verified bill within 28 days
docs.x: D.S.D.. Costs: verified bill within 28 days. File and serve a verified bill of costs within 28 calendar days after judgment or dismissal. Exceptions are due 14 days after, and a request to review the clerk’s taxation must come within 7 days. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 54.1(A))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Discovery motions need a separate good-faith certification
docs.x: D.S.D.. Discovery motions need a separate good-faith certification. File a separate certification describing the parties’ good-faith efforts to resolve the dispute. If a hearing is set, file a statement of the issues you could not resolve at least 7 calendar days before it. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 37.1)

docs.t: D.S.D. — Oral argument only by order, and you have to ask in time
docs.x: D.S.D.. Oral argument only by order, and you have to ask in time. Ask in a separate statement at the end of the motion or responsive brief, or in a separate document within 14 calendar days after filing the motion or responsive brief. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 7.1(C))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Witness lists are sealed and due by noon the day before trial
docs.x: D.S.D.. Witness lists are sealed and due by noon the day before trial. File a sealed witness list by noon on the last business day before trial, with the town or city and state of each witness. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 39.2)

docs.t: D.S.D. — Settle at least 14 days before trial or risk sanctions

docs.t: D.S.D. — Former law clerks are barred from their judge’s cases
docs.x: D.S.D.. Former law clerks are barred from their judge’s cases. A former law clerk cannot appear in any case assigned to that judge during the clerkship, or in any case before that judge for one year after the clerkship ends. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 83.12)

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — Thirty days to respond to dispositive motions; fourteen for the rest
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Thirty days to respond to dispositive motions; fourteen for the rest. Motions to remand, dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, for summary judgment, to exclude experts, and all post-trial motions need a brief and get 30 days to respond, with replies due 14 days after the response. Every other civil motion gets 14 days, with replies due 7 days after the response. (SDIL-LR 7.1(b)(1), (2))

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — Silence on a routine motion can be consent
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Silence on a routine motion can be consent. In civil cases, failing to file a timely response to a non-dispositive motion may be deemed consent to the relief requested. (SDIL-LR 7.1(a)(5))

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — Reply briefs are disfavored: five pages, exceptional cases only
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Reply briefs are disfavored: five pages, exceptional cases only. Replies shall not exceed five pages and should be filed only in exceptional circumstances. Sur-replies are never accepted. Read the judge’s case management procedures first, because they can change the reply rules. (SDIL-LR 7.1(a)(4))

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — Twenty-page brief limit, with a long list of exclusions
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Twenty-page brief limit, with a long list of exclusions. Briefs may not exceed 20 double-spaced pages in 12-point font unless the court authorizes more. Cover pages, tables, signature pages, certificates, exhibits, and the summary judgment fact statements do not count. (SDIL-LR 7.1(a)(3))

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — Dispositive motions are due 100 days before trial
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Dispositive motions are due 100 days before trial. Motions to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, and for summary judgment must be filed no later than 100 days before the trial date, or before the first day of the presumptive trial month if no date is set. (SDIL-LR 7.1(b)(1)(C))

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — You cannot notice a hearing; you have to move for oral argument
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. You cannot notice a hearing; you have to move for oral argument. A party may not schedule or notice oral argument. File a formal motion stating why you want it, and check the judge’s procedures. The court may decide on the papers, by phone, or by referral to a magistrate judge. (SDIL-LR 7.1(c)(1))

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — Summary judgment: numbered facts with record cites, or they are deemed admitted
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Summary judgment: numbered facts with record cites, or they are deemed admitted. The movant lists each material fact in a numbered paragraph with page-specific record cites. The opponent answers each paragraph (admitted, disputed, partly, or unsupported) with cites. Any fact not specifically disputed is deemed admitted, and unsupported facts are disregarded. (SDIL-LR 56.1(a), (b), (g))

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — An amended pleading starts from scratch and moots motions against the old one
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. An amended pleading starts from scratch and moots motions against the old one. No amendment by interlineation. The amended pleading must contain every claim against every party, with new material underlined or redlined. Unless the court orders otherwise, filing it moots any motion attacking the original. (SDIL-LR 15.1(b))

docs.t: S.D. Ill. — Costs: ask within 30 days or the request is stricken
docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Costs: ask within 30 days or the request is stricken. Unless a statute says otherwise, a request for costs must be filed no later than 30 days after judgment. The court will strike late requests. (SDIL-LR 54.2(c))

docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Bar membership carries a renewal fee. Members of the court’s bar must periodically pay a renewal fee, with the amount and interval set in the Fee Schedule. Check the fee schedule before you rely on your admission. (SDIL-LR 83.1(a)(4))

docs.x: S.D. Ill.. General admission by registration,SDIL-LR 83.1(a),Any lawyer licensed in a state or D.C. is admitted generally by paying the fee and registering through PACER, with a certificate of good standing less than 60 days old, every bar number, and an oath. Documents that need leave go in as an exhibit,SDIL-LR 15.1(a),File the document as an exhibit to the motion for leave. If leave is granted, you must file it as its own docket entry. The clerk will not do it for you. Supplemental pleadings: a two-page motion,SDIL-LR 7.1(a)(6),After a change in law or facts, move for leave in no more than two pages, point to the specific pages being supplemented, and attach the new authority or evidence. docs.t: C.D. Cal. — Pay $25 by September 1 every year
docs.x: C.D. Cal.. Pay $25 by September 1 every year. The annual renewal fee is $25, due September 1 each year for lawyers admitted before September 1 of the prior year, paid online. If you haven’t paid by September 30 you are subject to removal from the court’s rolls and must reapply under L.R. 83-2.1.2.2 and pay the full admission fee. (C.D. Cal. L.R. 83-2.1.2.3; G.O. 21-05)

docs.x: C.D. Cal.. Judges’ own rules change the Local Rules. Read the assigned judge’s page before you file anything. (Judges’ Procedures and Schedules)

docs.t: C.D. Cal. — You must hold the L.R. 7-3 conference before filing
docs.x: C.D. Cal.. You must hold the L.R. 7-3 conference before filing. At least 7 days before filing almost any motion, confer in person, by phone, or by video, and discuss the motion thoroughly. The motion must include a declaration under penalty of perjury describing the conference. Skipping it gets motions denied or stricken. Discovery motions, TROs and preliminary injunctions follow their own rules. (L.R. 7-3)

docs.t: C.D. Cal. — Discovery motions are joint stipulations
docs.x: C.D. Cal.. Discovery motions are joint stipulations. Send a letter requesting a conference; meet within 10 days. If unresolved, the movant drafts a single joint stipulation with both sides’ positions issue by issue. It must be filed at least 21 days before the hearing; supplemental memoranda 14 days before. No conventional motion-and-opposition. (L.R. 37-1 to 37-4)

docs.t: N.D. Cal. — Briefing runs from filing, not the hearing
docs.x: N.D. Cal.. Briefing runs from filing, not the hearing. Notice the motion for a hearing at least 35 days out. The opposition is due 14 days after the motion is filed; the reply 7 days after the opposition was due. Lawyers used to the Central District’s count-back calendar get this wrong. (Civil L.R. 7-2(a); 7-3)

docs.t: N.D. Cal. — No separate evidentiary objections, no sur-replies
docs.x: N.D. Cal.. No separate evidentiary objections, no sur-replies. Evidentiary objections go inside the opposition or reply brief. After the reply, the only papers allowed without approval are an Objection to Reply Evidence (5 pages, within 7 days) and a statement of a recent decision. (Civil L.R. 7-3)

docs.t: N.D. Cal. — Standing orders run discovery
docs.x: N.D. Cal.. Standing orders run discovery. Most judges and magistrate judges require joint discovery letters, with a meet-and-confer in person or by phone, instead of noticed discovery motions. Read the standing order before you draft anything. (Judges’ standing orders)

But Judge Tigar, Judge Noël Wise, and Judge Rita Lin each order that all filing deadlines are at 5:00 p.m., unless otherwise ordered. Check your judge’s standing order. (Civil L.R. 5-1(d)(4); judges’ civil standing orders)

docs.t: D. Conn. — Register every year, June 1 to August 31, $50
docs.x: D. Conn.. Register every year, June 1 to August 31, $50. Lawyers admitted by regular admission must register annually between June 1 and August 31 and pay $50 to stay active. Active status is also required to practice in the Bankruptcy Court for the District of Connecticut. If you miss it, your filing privileges may be suspended and you can be removed from the bar rolls. (D. Conn. L. Civ. R. 83.1(c))

docs.t: D. Conn. — 21 days from filing, and silence can lose the motion
docs.x: D. Conn.. 21 days from filing, and silence can lose the motion. Opposition memoranda are due 21 days after the motion is filed. Failing to file one may be deemed sufficient cause to grant the motion. (D. Conn. L. Civ. R. 7(a)(2))

docs.t: D. Conn. — Replies: 14 days, 10 pages, new matters only
docs.x: D. Conn.. Replies: 14 days, 10 pages, new matters only. Replies are allowed but not required. They must be filed within 14 days of the response, run no more than 10 pages, address only matters raised in the response and cite its pages. (D. Conn. L. Civ. R. 7(d))

docs.t: D. Conn. — Rule 56(a) statements are paragraph-by-paragraph
docs.x: D. Conn.. Rule 56(a) statements are paragraph-by-paragraph. The movant files a Local Rule 56(a)1 Statement. The opponent’s 56(a)2 Statement answers each paragraph “Admitted” or “Denied” with specific citations and adds its own facts separately. Facts not properly denied are deemed admitted. (D. Conn. L. Civ. R. 56(a))

docs.x: D. Conn.. Pro hac needs a Connecticut sponsor. Only a member of this court’s bar can move for your admission. The sponsor stays in the case and is expected to appear unless the court excuses it. (D. Conn. L. Civ. R. 83.1)

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — Pay the periodic membership fee
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. Pay the periodic membership fee. To maintain membership you must pay a periodic fee set by administrative order. The FJC’s 2024 compilation lists it as $15 every five years, so check the current administrative order and the clerk’s notice. (M.D. Fla. R. 2.01(b)(2)(A))

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — The typeface rule is enforced
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. The typeface rule is enforced. Main text at least 13-point in Book Antiqua, Calisto MT, Century Schoolbook, Georgia, or Palatino. Times New Roman is allowed only at 14-point (quotes 13, footnotes 12). One-inch margins, double-spaced, page numbers bottom center. (Rule 1.08)

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — No reply without leave
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. No reply without leave. Except on summary judgment (reply within 14 days, 7 pages) and social security briefs, you need leave to reply. The motion for leave is 3 pages, must not attach the reply, and gets no response. Put everything in the motion. (Rule 3.01(e))

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — Confer before almost everything, including motions to dismiss
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. Confer before almost everything, including motions to dismiss. Exempt only: Rule 11, injunctive relief, judgment on the pleadings, summary judgment, class certification. End the motion with a section headed “Local Rule 3.01(g) Certificate.” If the other side is unavailable, keep trying for three days after filing, then supplement. (Rule 3.01(g))

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — One document, 25 pages, everything counts
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. One document, 25 pages, everything counts. The motion and its legal memorandum are a single document of no more than 25 pages. Only the caption, signature block, certificates, and attachments are excluded, so the table of contents counts. (Rule 3.01(a), (b))

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — Response in 14 days, but 21 for the big motions
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. Response in 14 days, but 21 for the big motions. The response is due 14 days after service. It is 21 days for a motion to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, for summary judgment, to exclude or limit expert testimony, to certify a class, for a new trial, or to alter or amend a judgment. A late response leaves the motion subject to treatment as unopposed. (Rule 3.01(d))

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — Sealing takes a real motion
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. Sealing takes a real motion. A confidentiality agreement, protective order, or stipulation never justifies sealing. Show filing and sealing are both necessary and that redaction or a pseudonym won’t work, propose a duration, and certify who else has an interest. Unless the order says otherwise, a seal expires 90 days after the case closes and appeals end, so move before then. (Rule 1.11)

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — Fee claims run in two steps
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. Fee claims run in two steps. Within 14 days after judgment, move only on entitlement. After that order, you have 45 days for a supplemental motion on amount, with lead counsel’s verification of each rate and task. Skipping step one is the common mistake. (Rule 7.01)

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — No proposed orders, letters, or notices of unavailability
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. No proposed orders, letters, or notices of unavailability. Don’t submit a proposed order without leave, and don’t use a letter or email to ask for relief. A notice of unavailability or a motion for protection is prohibited. Put the request in a motion. (Rule 3.01(k), (l); 3.08(c))

docs.t: M.D. Fla. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
