docs.t: M.D. Fla. — overview
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. Response limits,Rule 3.01(c), (d),Responses: 20 pages. 14 days to respond generally; 21 days for motions to dismiss, judgment on the pleadings, summary judgment, to exclude experts, class certification, new trial, or to alter judgment. Missing the deadline lets the court treat the motion as unopposed. Say “unopposed” in the title,Rule 3.01(b),If everyone agrees to the relief, the title must include “unopposed.” Emergencies,Rule 3.01(f),Put “emergency” or “time-sensitive” in the title and open with a paragraph explaining the exigency and the date you need a ruling. Unwarranted emergency labels draw sanctions. No incorporation by reference,Rule 3.01(h),A motion or brief can’t adopt arguments from another paper. Hearings are requested separately,Rule 3.01(i),Ask for oral argument or an evidentiary hearing in a separate document, stating how much time you need. Supplemental author

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Rule changes take effect December 1, 2026
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Rule changes take effect December 1, 2026. Default judgment motions lose their no-memorandum exemption and need a full package (new L.R. 7.1(a)(3)); the conferral rule moves to 7.1(a)(4); pro hac vice certifications must disclose any past suspension (Attorney Rule 4(b)(1)); and new L.R. 7.4 applies the federal Supplemental Rules to individual Social Security review cases. Anything filed on or after December 1 follows the new text. (Admin. Order 2026-94)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Fee motions have their own procedure
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Fee motions have their own procedure. File within 60 days of the final judgment, even if an appeal is pending. At least 30 days before that deadline, serve (don’t file) a draft motion. Within 21 days the parties must confer, and the opposing side must spell out its objections in writing, item by item, with authority. Courts treat objections not made in that process as waived. The motion must be verified and detailed. Bills of costs are due in 30 days. (L.R. 7.3)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Discovery disputes have a 28-day deadline
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Discovery disputes have a 28-day deadline. Raise a discovery dispute within 28 days of the event that caused it, or risk losing it. Most magistrate judges require a discovery hearing or joint motion under their standing orders instead of a written motion. (L.R. 26.1(g))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Pre-filing conference and certificate
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Pre-filing conference and certificate. Before most motions, confer with everyone affected and certify it. Motions to dismiss, for injunctive relief, judgment on the pleadings, and summary judgment are among the exceptions. Judges strike motions missing the certificate. (L.R. 7.1(a)(3) (7.1(a)(4) from Dec. 1, 2026))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Local counsel does the filing
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Local counsel does the filing. Pro hac vice lawyers can’t e-file; local counsel files the motion, pays the fee and files everything after. (Attorney Rule 4(b))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — One 20-page document; replies are 10 and rebuttal only
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. One 20-page document; replies are 10 and rebuttal only. A motion and its memorandum are a single document, and neither it nor the opposing memorandum may exceed 20 pages without prior permission. A reply is capped at 10 pages and strictly limited to rebutting matters in the opposition. The caption, tables, signature block, and certificates don’t count. (L.R. 7.1(a)(1), (c)(2))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Opposition in 14 days, reply in 7, or the motion may be granted by default
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Opposition in 14 days, reply in 7, or the motion may be granted by default. The opposing memorandum is due 14 days after service, and failing to file one may be sufficient cause to grant the motion by default. The movant has 7 days after the opposition to reply. For a motion served with the summons and complaint, the opposition is due when the response to the complaint is due. (L.R. 7.1(c)(1))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Summary judgment needs separate statements of fact
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Summary judgment needs separate statements of fact. File a Statement of Material Facts as a separate document of no more than 10 pages, in numbered paragraphs, each fact with a pinpoint record cite. The opponent responds the same way and may add up to 5 pages of “Additional Facts,” and the movant then files a reply statement. (L.R. 56.1)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Tell the court within two court days when a case settles
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Tell the court within two court days when a case settles. File a joint notice of settlement within 2 court days after the agreement is reached, or a Rule 41 notice. For a settled jury case, the clerk and judge must hear at least one full business day before jury selection, or juror costs can be assessed. (L.R. 16.4)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Sealing: move first, and attach nothing
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Sealing: move first, and attach nothing. File a public motion describing the material with as much particularity as possible without revealing it, and state the proposed duration. The proposed sealed material isn’t filed unless the court grants the motion. (L.R. 5.4(b)(1))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — 12-point type and 1½-line spacing
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. 12-point type and 1½-line spacing. Type must be at least 12 points, footnotes and quotations included. Lines are spaced at least 1½, except quotations of 50 words or more and footnotes, which may be single-spaced. Number pages consecutively at the bottom center, and use one side of the paper only. (L.R. 5.1(a)(4))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Most magistrate judges bar written discovery motions
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Most magistrate judges bar written discovery motions. The local rule’s ten-page motion process applies only if the assigned judge’s procedures don’t say otherwise, and they usually do. Judges Torres, Strauss, Reinhart, Hernandez, and Shaw-Wilder bar or strictly control written discovery motions and use a hearing request instead, while Judges Louis, Sanchez, McCabe, and Augustin-Birch permit short motions with set page limits. Read the paired magistrate judge’s procedures before any dispute. (L.R. 26.1(g)(1); judges’ procedures)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Deposition rulings: no calls, no instant relief
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Deposition rulings: no calls, no instant relief. Judge McCabe won’t take calls for immediate rulings during a deposition, Judge Louis says the same, and Judge Torres requires a notice of objection served within five days after you receive a deposition notice. Raise deposition disputes by the judge’s process afterward. (Judges’ procedures)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. docs.t: D. Me. — Missing the objection deadline waives your objection
docs.x: D. Me.. Missing the objection deadline waives your objection. Objections to any motion are due 21 days after the motion is filed. If you don’t file on time, your objection is waived. The only exception is motions filed during trial. (Local Rule 7(b))

docs.t: D. Me. — No discovery motion without permission
docs.x: D. Me.. No discovery motion without permission. You cannot file a contested discovery motion. Confer, then file the court’s Request for Hearing form; the judge hears it by phone or video. A written motion comes only if the judge allows one. (Local Rule 26(c))

docs.t: D. Me. — overview
docs.x: D. Me.. Motions carry their own memorandum,Local Rule 7(a),Every motion must incorporate its memorandum of law, with supporting affidavits filed together with it. Reply is limited to new matter,Local Rule 7(c),Reply within 14 days of the objection, confined to new matter raised in it. Page limits are tight,Local Rule 7(d),Nondispositive memoranda: 10 pages. Dispositive (dismiss, judgment on the pleadings, summary judgment, injunctions): 20. Replies: 7. A motion to exceed is due 3 business days before the deadline. Oral argument is by request,Local Rule 7(e),Ask in the caption of your motion, objection or reply, or on the court’s form within 5 days after the reply is filed. Reconsideration,Local Rule 7(f),Interlocutory reconsideration needs a manifest error of fact or law and is due within 14 days of the order. Moving to reconsider a magistrate judge’s ruling extends the Rule 72 objection

docs.t: D. Nev. — Pro hac vice is due within 14 days
docs.x: D. Nev.. Pro hac vice is due within 14 days. File the complete verified petition within 14 days of your first appearance: verified (sworn) on the clerk’s form, with good-standing certificates (issued within six months) from every state where you’re admitted, the fee, and a designation of resident counsel with a Nevada office. Until it’s granted you can’t do anything beyond the first filing, and that filing must say you “has complied” or “will comply with LR IA 11-2 within ___ days.” Miss it and the court can strike everything you filed. (LR IA 11-2)

docs.t: D. Nev. — Not opposing a motion counts as consent
docs.x: D. Nev.. Not opposing a motion counts as consent. Failing to file points and authorities opposing a motion consents to granting it (summary judgment and fee motions excepted). A movant who files no points and authorities consents to denial. Calendar every opposition. (LR 7-2(d))

docs.t: D. Nev. — Email doesn’t count as meeting and conferring
docs.x: D. Nev.. Email doesn’t count as meeting and conferring. Wherever the rules require you to meet and confer, it has to be direct dialogue: in person, by phone or by video. Letters and email chains don’t satisfy it, and the court can sanction you. (LR IA 1-3(f))

docs.t: D. Nev. — Discovery runs on a short default clock
docs.x: D. Nev.. Discovery runs on a short default clock. Plaintiff must set the Rule 26(f) conference within 30 days after the first defendant answers or appears, and the stipulated discovery plan is due 14 days later. Discovery longer than 180 days from that first appearance needs “special scheduling review.” Extension requests must reach the court at least 21 days before the deadline, or show good cause (and excusable neglect if the deadline has passed). (LR 26-1; LR 26-3)

docs.t: D. Nev. — Filing deadline: 11:59 p.m. Pacific
docs.x: D. Nev.. Filing deadline: 11:59 p.m. Pacific. Unless the court orders otherwise, a document due by a rule or order deadline must be filed by 11:59 p.m. on the date due, measured by the date and time on the Notice of Electronic Filing in the court’s time zone. The deadline printed in a Notice of Electronic Filing is only a courtesy; the court order or the rules control. If a technical failure makes you late, you may ask for relief. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (LR IC 3-1(a))

docs.t: D. Nev. — overview
docs.x: D. Nev.. Who can’t appear pro hac vice,LR IA 11-2(a),Members of the State Bar of Nevada, Nevada residents and people regularly employed in Nevada are ineligible. They need full admission. Repeat visitors get scrutiny,LR IA 11-2(f),More than five pro hac vice appearances in three years is presumptively excessive. You need special circumstances and good cause, shown by affidavit. Resident counsel’s role,LR IA 11-2(d),Resident counsel must be able to sign binding stipulations, and deadlines run from service on resident counsel. Resident counsel need not attend every proceeding unless the court orders. Page limits,LR 7-3,Summary judgment motions and responses: 30 pages; replies 20. All other motions and responses: 24; replies 12. Exhibits don’t count. Asking for more pages,LR 7-3(c),The court disfavors it. docs.t: D.N.J. — Motions run on motion days
docs.x: D.N.J.. Motions run on motion days. Motion days are the first and third Mondays. A motion is returnable on the first motion day at least 24 days after filing; opposition is due 14 days before that day and reply 7 days before. Put the motion day on the brief’s cover. (L.Civ.R. 7.1(c), 78.1)

docs.t: D.N.J. — Pro hac vice lawyers can’t file anything
docs.x: D.N.J.. Pro hac vice lawyers can’t file anything. Only a member of this court’s bar may file papers, enter appearances, sign stipulations, or sign and receive payments on judgments. Pro hac lawyers can’t register as ECF filers. (L.Civ.R. 101.1(c)(4))

docs.t: D.N.J. — Discovery disputes go to the magistrate judge by letter or call first
docs.x: D.N.J.. Discovery disputes go to the magistrate judge by letter or call first. Confer, then present the dispute to the magistrate judge by letter or phone conference before any formal motion. Case management disputes work the same way (L.Civ.R. 16.1(f)). (L.Civ.R. 37.1(a))

docs.t: D.N.J. — Using the wrong font cuts your page limit
docs.x: D.N.J.. Using the wrong font cuts your page limit. Briefs are 40 pages (replies 15) in 12-point non-proportional or 14-point proportional font. Use 12-point Times New Roman and your limits drop 25%, to 30 and 11.25 pages. (L.Civ.R. 7.2(d))

docs.t: D.N.J. — Opposing a dispositive motion? You can adjourn it once, by letter
docs.x: D.N.J.. Opposing a dispositive motion? You can adjourn it once, by letter. Before your opposition is due, file and serve a letter stating the motion day hasn’t been adjourned before and invoking the rule. The motion moves to the next available motion day, opposition is then due 14 days before it, and the reply 7 days before. Any other extension takes a court order. (L.Civ.R. 7.1(d)(5))

docs.t: D.N.J. — No statement of facts, no summary judgment
docs.x: D.N.J.. No statement of facts, no summary judgment. A summary judgment motion without a separate statement of material facts is dismissed. The statement is a separate document of numbered paragraphs with record cites and no legal argument. The opponent answers each paragraph and any fact it doesn’t dispute is deemed undisputed. (L.Civ.R. 56.1(a))

docs.t: D.N.J. — Costs: 30 days or they’re waived
docs.x: D.N.J.. Costs: 30 days or they’re waived. File and serve a verified Bill of Costs within 30 days after the judgment allowing costs, or after the last timely post-trial motion is decided, appeal or not. Append the invoices. Failing to comply waives all costs. (L.Civ.R. 54.1)

docs.t: D.N.J. — Fee motions: 30 days, with detailed affidavits
docs.x: D.N.J.. Fee motions: 30 days, with detailed affidavits. Move for attorney’s fees and expenses within 30 days of the judgment or order unless the court extends it. The supporting certification must set out the services, dates, who did each task and their experience, the time spent, and each person’s normal billing rate. (L.Civ.R. 54.2(a))

docs.t: D.N.J. — A settlement doesn’t end the case until you file the dismissal
docs.x: D.N.J.. A settlement doesn’t end the case until you file the dismissal. Tell the court promptly. It enters a 60-day order administratively terminating the case and pending motions. File the stipulation of dismissal within 60 days, or the court dismisses with prejudice and without costs. A case with no activity for 90 days is dismissed for lack of prosecution. (L.Civ.R. 41.1(b))

docs.t: D.N.J. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: D.N.J.. Bar renewal: none found. We haven’t read this court’s rule on it. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of every federal bar’s admission rules lists no renewal, dues, or re-registration fee for this court. A court can add one by General Order after that date, as E.D. docs.x: D.N.J.. Brief is a separate document,L.Civ.R. 7.1(d)(1),File the notice of motion, a separate brief with the motion day on its cover, and proof of service. You may file a statement that no brief is necessary instead, explaining why. Every motion gets a proposed order,L.Civ.R. 7.1(e),Annex a proposed order to every motion. Automatic adjournment,L.Civ.R. 7.1(d)(5),An opponent may adjourn a dispositive motion once, to the next motion day, by letter filed before the opposition is due. No other extension without an order. Replies are limited,L.Civ.R. 7.1(d)(3), (6),No reply without leave on cross-motions, reconsideration, case management, or discovery motions. No sur-replies without the judge’s permission. docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Judges’ own rules change the Local Rules
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Judges’ own rules change the Local Rules. Most S.D.N.Y. judges require a pre-motion letter and often a conference before motions to dismiss, for summary judgment or on discovery. Many set their own page or word limits, courtesy-copy and redaction rules. Read them before you do anything. (Individual Practices)

docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Words, not pages
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Words, not pages. Briefs in support and opposition: 8,750 words. Replies: 3,500. Include a certificate of compliance with the word count. (Local Civ. R. 7.1(c))

docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Rule 56.1 statements
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Rule 56.1 statements. Summary judgment requires a separate statement of undisputed facts in numbered paragraphs, each cited to admissible evidence. The opponent answers paragraph by paragraph; anything not specifically controverted is deemed admitted. (Local Civ. R. 56.1)

docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Early interrogatories are restricted
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Early interrogatories are restricted. At the start of discovery, interrogatories are limited to basics like witness names, documents and damages. Contention interrogatories wait until the end of discovery. Lawyers from elsewhere who serve broad first-wave interrogatories draw objections. (Local Civ. R. 33.3)

docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.x: N.D. Ohio. Tell the judge before you file a discovery motion. Confer first. If that fails, notify the judicial officer, who may hold a phone conference, and then ask for letters. Memoranda come only on a date the judge sets. (L.R. 37.1)

docs.t: S.D. Ohio — Exhaust everything before a discovery motion

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Admission to this bar does not excuse local counsel
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Admission to this bar does not excuse local counsel. Local counsel is required whenever the lawyer appearing does not reside or keep a principal office in the district, whether or not that lawyer is admitted here. Local counsel must live or have a principal office in the district. The old 50-mile rule is gone, but the presiding judge can impose a distance requirement or exempt a party. (LR 83.10 (eff. Sept. 1, 2026))

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Most motions need a certificate of conference
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Most motions need a certificate of conference. State whether the motion is opposed. If opposed, give the date of the conference, who conferred, and why you couldn’t agree. If you couldn’t confer, explain why, and the motion is presumed opposed. Dispositive motions are exempt. (LR 7.1(a), (b))

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Response time runs from filing, not service
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Response time runs from filing, not service. A response and brief to an opposed motion are due 21 days from the date the motion is filed. A reply is due 14 days from the date the response is filed. (LR 7.1(e), (f))

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Briefs, appendices, and length
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Briefs, appendices, and length. Briefs are 25 pages (replies 10), summary judgment briefs 50 (replies 25). Over 10 pages needs tables of contents and authorities. Evidence goes in a separate, self-contained appendix. (LR 7.1(i); LR 7.2; LR 56.5)

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Disclose generative AI on page one
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Disclose generative AI on page one. A brief prepared using generative AI must say so on its first page under the heading “Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence,” and the judge can direct you to identify the specific parts. A brief without the disclosure certifies that no part of it was prepared with generative AI. (LR 7.2(f))

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Evidence goes in a separate, numbered appendix
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Evidence goes in a separate, numbered appendix. Anything you rely on, including depositions, documents, affidavits, and discovery answers, goes in a self-contained appendix separate from the motion, response, reply, and brief. Pages are 8½ by 11 and numbered consecutively from 1 in the lower right corner across the whole appendix. Your brief must cite each appendix page that supports each assertion. (LR 7.1(i), 56.6)

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Summary judgment: one motion, no argument in it, and not late
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Summary judgment: one motion, no argument in it, and not late. Unless the judge says otherwise, you can’t file a summary judgment motion within 90 days of the trial setting, and you get only one. The motion states the elements of each claim or defense on page one under “summary” and contains no argument. The brief is a separate document of up to 50 pages, and a reply 25. (LR 56.2, 56.3)

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Sealing takes a motion, and paper seals expire
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Sealing takes a motion, and paper seals expire. Unless a statute or rule permits it, you can file under seal only by motion and the judge’s permission. You may file the motion itself under seal and attach the proposed sealed document. Sealed paper documents are deemed unsealed 60 days after final disposition, so move before then to keep them sealed. (LR 79.3, 79.4)

docs.t: N.D. Tex. — Removing a case has a required package
docs.x: N.D. Tex.. Removing a case has a required package. File a civil cover sheet, a supplemental cover sheet, a notice of related case if one applies, and a notice of removal attaching an index, the state docket sheet, every state-court filing except discovery, and a signed certificate of interested persons. The plaintiff has 21 days after removal to file its own certificate. (LR 81.1, 3.3)

docs.t: W.D. Wash. — Motions are noted on a 14-, 21- or 28-day schedule
docs.x: W.D. Wash.. Motions are noted on a 14-, 21- or 28-day schedule. Every motion carries a noting date in the caption. Most motions are 21-day motions (response at day 15). Dispositive, class, injunction, and forum motions are 28-day motions (response at day 21). Relief-from-deadline and protective order motions are 14-day motions (response at day 9). (LCR 7(d))

docs.t: W.D. Wash. — Word limits, with a certification
docs.x: W.D. Wash.. Word limits, with a certification. Most motions: 4,200 words, replies 2,100. Dispositive and other 28-day motions: 8,400, replies 4,200. The signature block must certify the word count. (LCR 7(e))

docs.t: W.D. Wash. — Motions to shorten time don’t exist here
docs.x: W.D. Wash.. Motions to shorten time don’t exist here. The court abolished them. For a real emergency, confer and file a stipulation, or ask for a telephonic motion under LCR 7(i). (LCR 6(b))

docs.t: W.D. Wash. — Meet and confer means talking
docs.x: W.D. Wash.. Meet and confer means talking. A conference must be in person or by phone. Discovery and protective order motions need a certification listing the date, manner and participants, or the court can deny them without reaching the merits. (LCR 1(c)(6), 26(c), 37(a))

docs.t: W.D. Wash. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: W.D. Wash.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: W.D. Wash. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: W.D. Wash.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

docs.t: W.D. Wash. — overview
docs.x: W.D. Wash.. One document for motion and argument,LCR 7(b)(1),The argument goes in the motion itself, not a separate brief. File a proposed order and email an editable Word version to chambers. No separate motions to strike,LCR 7(g),Put requests to strike in your response brief. The only exception is material in a reply, which you challenge with a short surreply after filing a notice of intent. Reconsideration is a one-way street,LCR 7(h),File within 14 days, noted the same day. No response is allowed unless the court asks for one, and no motion is granted without that request. Sealing starts with a conference,LCR 5(g),Before filing under seal, confer with the party that designated the material. The motion must certify the date, manner and participants of that conference. Diversity complaints must plead citizenship,LCR 8(a),Name every party’s citizenship, including each member of an LLC o

docs.t: E.D. Wash. — Every local rule yields to the judge
docs.x: E.D. Wash.. Every local rule yields to the judge. The rules say they are subject to any order of the presiding judge in an individual case. Read the scheduling order and the judge’s own practices before relying on any deadline or limit on this page. (LCivR 1)

docs.t: E.D. Wash. — Hearing dates: 30 days for ordinary motions, 50 for dispositive ones
docs.x: E.D. Wash.. Hearing dates: 30 days for ordinary motions, 50 for dispositive ones. The hearing date for a nondispositive motion must be at least 30 days after filing, and for a dispositive motion at least 50 days after filing. Put the hearing date, time, and place in the motion’s caption. Only the court can change these times, and an expedited hearing needs a separate motion to expedite. (LCivR 7(i)(2))

docs.t: E.D. Wash. — Response and reply deadlines
docs.x: E.D. Wash.. Response and reply deadlines. Counsel respond within 14 days after a nondispositive motion and 21 days after a dispositive one. Replies are due 7 days after the response (nondispositive) or 14 days after it (dispositive). These periods include the 3-day mail allowance, so they apply however service was made. (LCivR 7(c)(2); 7(d)(2))

docs.t: E.D. Wash. — Page limits: 20 and 10
docs.x: E.D. Wash.. Page limits: 20 and 10. Dispositive motions and responses are limited to 20 pages. Nondispositive motions and responses are limited to 10 pages, and replies to 10 pages. Class certification motions count as dispositive. Exceeding a limit needs prior approval for good cause. (LCivR 7(f))

docs.t: E.D. Wash. — The motion is the brief
docs.x: E.D. Wash.. The motion is the brief. There is no separate memorandum. The motion sets out the facts and legal authority and also serves as the notice of hearing. File a proposed order with it and email an editable Word version to chambers. (LCivR 7(b)(1))

docs.t: E.D. Wash. — Ignoring the rules can cost you the motion
docs.x: E.D. Wash.. Ignoring the rules can cost you the motion. Failing to comply with the motion and response requirements may be deemed consent to an order adverse to the violating party. (LCivR 7(e))

docs.t: E.D. Wash. — overview
docs.x: E.D. Wash.. Oral argument must be elected,LCivR 7(i)(3),To be heard without oral argument, set the motion on any weekday on or after the required date. To have oral argument, agree on dates with the other side, then contact the courtroom deputy. If the movant doesn’t elect it, the opposing party may elect it in the response caption. If argument isn’t elected it is waived absent a motion and good cause, each side gets no more than 15 minutes, and the court may still decide without argument. Expedited hearings,LCivR 7(i)(2)(C),File a motion to expedite showing good cause, stating the opposing party’s position (or your efforts to learn it), and setting a hearing not less than 7 days after filing. A response to an expedited motion is due the day before the hearing. Notify chambers if the matter is more urgent. Chasing a ruling,LCivR 7(j),If you have no order within 30 days after the motion w

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Admission runs five years, then renew
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Admission runs five years, then renew. Admission has a five-year term. The court’s renewal instructions list a $25 fee, which the FJC’s 2024 compilation shows as annual, so read the court’s renewal instructions. We haven’t read this rule ourselves. (S.D. Tex. LR 83.1.F; FJC 2024)

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Opposed motions are submitted at 21 days, with no hearing
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Opposed motions are submitted at 21 days, with no hearing. The judge takes an opposed motion on the papers 21 days after filing, without notice from the clerk and without counsel appearing. Argument happens only if you request it in the motion or response, or the court orders it. (LR 7.3)

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Silence is consent
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Silence is consent. Failing to respond to a motion is taken as a representation of no opposition. A response is due by the submission day and must come with authority and a separate form order denying the relief sought. (LR 7.4)

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Most opposed motions need a conference averment and a proposed order
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Most opposed motions need a conference averment and a proposed order. State that you conferred with the respondent and counsel can’t agree, and attach a separate proposed order. Motions under Rule 12(b), (c), (e), or (f) and Rule 56 skip the conference averment. (LR 7.1)

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — The attorney-in-charge signs everything
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. The attorney-in-charge signs everything. Every document is signed by, or with permission of, the attorney-in-charge, who attends every proceeding or sends a fully informed lawyer with authority to bind the client. A visiting lawyer moves for leave to appear in that role and pays a $100 fee. (LR 11, 83.1(I))

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — The local rules set no page limits, so read your judge’s procedures
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. The local rules set no page limits, so read your judge’s procedures. Nothing in the Local Rules caps brief length or sets a response time other than the 21-day submission day. Each judge’s posted procedures usually do, and a judge can shorten or extend any period (LR 7.8). Read them before you draft. (Local Rules; judges’ procedures)

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Disclose related litigation
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Disclose related litigation. The parties must tell the Court about related current or recent litigation and directly affected non-parties. (LR 5.2)

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Costs and fees: 14 days, objections in 7
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Costs and fees: 14 days, objections in 7. File a bill of costs within 14 days of final judgment. The clerk keeps no record of your costs, so keep your own. If attorney’s fees are taxable as costs, apply for them with the bill. Objections to the bill or the fees are due within 7 days of its filing. (LR 54.2)

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Report discipline or a conviction within 30 days
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Report discipline or a conviction within 30 days. Notify the court in writing within 30 days, with a certified copy, if you are convicted of a felony or qualifying misdemeanor, disciplined by any licensing authority, or disciplined by any federal or state court. The clerk then serves a reciprocal-discipline order effective in 30 days, and you have 30 days to move to modify or revoke it. (App. A, Rules 2 to 4)

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Renew your bar membership every five years
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Renew your bar membership every five years. Membership expires five years from admission unless you file a renewal application and pay the fee. You can renew after it expires, but after 10 years expired you must apply to be readmitted. (LR 83.1(F))

docs.t: S.D. Tex. — Settled? Tell the Court immediately
docs.x: S.D. Tex.. Settled? Tell the Court immediately. Notify the Court at once of any settlement that makes court settings unnecessary. Summoning jurors or disrupting the schedule through an inexcusable failure to notify can bring sanctions. (LR 16.3)

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — Renew every three years, $25
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Renew every three years, $25. Membership must be renewed every three years with a $25 fee, per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. We haven’t read this rule ourselves, so confirm with the clerk. (W.D. Tex. AT-1(h); FJC 2024)

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — Responses are due in 7 or 14 days
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Responses are due in 7 or 14 days. A response to a discovery or case management motion is due 7 days after the motion is filed. A response to any other motion is due in 14 days. If you don’t respond, the court may grant the motion as unopposed. (CV-7(d))

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — Page limits are tight
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Page limits are tight. Discovery and case management motions and responses get 10 pages, and other motions and responses get 20. Replies get 5 and 10. Legal authority goes in the motion itself, not in a separate brief. (CV-7(c), (d), (e))

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — Confer before you file
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Confer before you file. The court may refuse to hear or may deny a nondispositive motion unless the motion says counsel conferred in a good-faith attempt to agree and certifies the specific reason no agreement could be made. (CV-7(g))

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — Discovery motions die with the deadline
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Discovery motions die with the deadline. Absent exceptional circumstances, no discovery motion can be filed after the discovery deadline unless it’s filed within 14 days afterward and concerns conduct in the final 7 days of discovery. (CV-16(e))

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — Put your legal authority in the motion itself
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Put your legal authority in the motion itself. Legal authority supporting a motion must be cited in the motion, not in a separate brief. Facts go in an optional appendix that must include every affidavit, deposition transcript, or document you rely on. A motion states its grounds and cites the rule or statute that justifies the relief. (Rule CV-7(c)(1))

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — Renew your bar membership every three years
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Renew your bar membership every three years. Members must renew every 3 years after admission by paying the prescribed fee. If the fee isn’t timely paid you are removed from the rolls and must reapply for admission. (Rule AT-1(h))

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — Two trial packages: 14 days and 7 days before the earliest setting
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Two trial packages: 14 days and 7 days before the earliest setting. At least 14 days before trial, jury selection, docket call, or the final pretrial conference (whichever is first), serve and file voir dire questions, a half-page statement of claims, stipulated facts, exhibit and witness lists, deposition designations, instructions, verdict forms, motions in limine, and a trial-length estimate. At least 7 days before, file objections to designations and exhibits, and responses to motions in limine. Exhibit objections not disclosed are waived, except Rules 402 and 403. (Rule CV-16(f), (g))

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — ADR is mandatory and must finish 60 days before trial
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. ADR is mandatory and must finish 60 days before trial. Unless ordered otherwise, the parties agree on an ADR method, provider, fees, and completion date, and finish at least 60 days before the trial setting. Counsel, party representatives with authority, and insurers must attend in person. A party opposing ADR must move to be exempted. (Rule CV-88)

docs.t: W.D. Tex. — overview
docs.x: W.D. Tex.. Proposed orders go through the clerk,CV-5(b), CV-7(f),Proposed orders are filed with the clerk, never sent to the judge. One is required for every discovery and case management motion. Sealing starts with a motion, and it’s disfavored,CV-5.2,A document to be sealed is filed as an exhibit to a sealing motion, not with the motion it supports. Draft around confidential material, redact what you can, or use a sealed appendix. Amending after a first Rule 12(b) motion,CV-15,You can respond to a first Rule 12(b) motion by amending as a matter of course within 21 days after the motion is filed, with no motion for leave. The proposed scheduling order is due early,CV-16(c),Not later than 60 days after any defendant appears, the parties confer under Rule 26(f) and submit a proposed scheduling order. Disagreements go in the proposal, with reasons. Producing a document authenticates it,CV-

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Filed by midnight, but served the next day after 5:00 p.m.
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Filed by midnight, but served the next day after 5:00 p.m.. Filing is timely until midnight Central. But a document filed after 5:00 p.m. Central is deemed served the following day, for computing response deadlines. (Local Rule CV-5)

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Responses are due in 14 days, or 21 for summary judgment
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Responses are due in 14 days, or 21 for summary judgment. A response is due 14 days after the motion is served, or 21 days for summary judgment motions. Failing to oppose in the prescribed way creates a presumption that you don’t controvert the movant’s facts and have no evidence to offer. (CV-7(d), (e))

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Confer by phone or in person, and certify it
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Confer by phone or in person, and certify it. Emails and letters don’t satisfy the meet-and-confer rule. A certificate of conference at the end of the motion gives the date, manner, participants, why no agreement was reached, and that talks ended in an impasse. Skipping the conference without bad faith by the other side breaks Local Rule AT-3. (CV-7(h), (i))

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Page limits: 30, 15, and 10 or 5 for replies
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Page limits: 30, 15, and 10 or 5 for replies. Dispositive motions and responses get 30 pages. Nondispositive ones, including partial summary judgment, venue transfer, and Rule 59 motions, get 15. Replies and sur-replies get 10 and 5. Several summary judgment motions share 60 pages. (CV-7(a))

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Discovery doesn’t pause for pending motions
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Discovery doesn’t pause for pending motions. A pending motion to dismiss, remand, or change venue doesn’t excuse you from responding to discovery, except in qualified immunity cases or by court order. A duty judge rules on discovery disputes by hotline during business hours. (CV-26(a), (e))

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Sealing: certify, file the motion first, and redact publicly in 7 days
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Sealing: certify, file the motion first, and redact publicly in 7 days. Mark the document “Filed Under Seal.” After the certificate of service, certify that a motion to seal is filed or leave was granted. File the motion separately and immediately before the document, and serve the sealed document by some means other than CM/ECF. Within 7 days, publicly file a redacted version unless the whole document is confidential. (Local Rule CV-5(a)(7))

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Dispositive and summary judgment motions have extra content
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Dispositive and summary judgment motions have extra content. A case dispositive motion must contain a statement of the issues, and the response must answer it. A summary judgment motion also needs a Statement of Undisputed Material Facts, which the response must answer. The court won’t scour the record for an undesignated dispute, and facts you support are assumed admitted unless controverted. (Local Rule CV-7(a)(1), CV-56)

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Multiple summary judgment motions share a page budget
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Multiple summary judgment motions share a page budget. If you file more than one summary judgment motion, they total 60 pages collectively, responses 60, replies 20, and sur-replies 20, excluding attachments. The same totals apply to motions for judgment as a matter of law. (Local Rule CV-7(a)(3), CV-50)

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Costs: share the bill first, then file within 14 days
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Costs: share the bill first, then file within 14 days. Before filing a bill of costs, send it to opposing counsel and confer on disagreements. File within 14 days after the clerk enters judgment. If you can’t agree, file a joint motion or your own motion listing the agreed and disputed items, with a conferral certificate. (Local Rule CV-54)

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — Patent cases run on their own rules
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Patent cases run on their own rules. The Rules of Practice for Patent Cases apply to any civil action alleging infringement of a utility patent, or seeking a declaration on one, unless the judge opts out by order. Infringement contentions are due 10 days before the initial case management conference and invalidity contentions 35 days after it. (Local Rule CV-1(c))

docs.t: E.D. Tex. — A trial postponement request needs the party’s signature
docs.x: E.D. Tex.. A trial postponement request needs the party’s signature. Any request to postpone trial must be signed by the party making it as well as the lawyer. (Local Rule CV-11(b))

docs.x: E.D. Tex.. Motion and brief are one document,CV-7(c), (d),The motion and its briefing go in a single document, and so do a response and its briefing. Each pleading, motion, or response is its own filing, except for alternative-relief motions. Summary judgment needs two statements,CV-56,A summary judgment motion includes a statement of issues and a “Statement of Undisputed Material Facts.” The court assumes the movant’s supported facts are admitted unless the response controverts them, and it won’t search the record for you. Sealing starts with a motion,CV-5(a)(7),File the motion to seal separately and immediately before the document, which carries “Filed Under Seal” at the top and a statement after the certificate of service. A public redacted version follows within 7 days. Long filings go to chambers on paper,CV-5(a)(9),Unless the judge opts out, a filing over ten pages, including attac

docs.t: N.D.N.Y. — Biennial registration, $50
docs.x: N.D.N.Y.. Biennial registration, $50. Submit the biennial registration when the clerk’s notice arrives, with a $50 fee. The fee can be waived for hardship and is waived for full-time public-sector lawyers. Fail to register and pay and you are automatically removed from the bar roll, and must satisfy every admission requirement again unless the Chief Judge excuses it. (N.D.N.Y. L.R. 83.1(g))

docs.t: N.D.N.Y. — 21 days to oppose, and a short reply
docs.x: N.D.N.Y.. 21 days to oppose, and a short reply. The opposition to any motion is due no more than 21 days after service. On a dispositive motion, the reply is due 7 days later and can’t run over 10 pages, and no surreply is allowed. On a non-dispositive motion, there’s no reply without the Court’s permission. (L.R. 7.1(a))

docs.t: N.D.N.Y. — A court conference comes before a non-dispositive motion
docs.x: N.D.N.Y.. A court conference comes before a non-dispositive motion. Confer in good faith first. If that fails, you must request a conference with the assigned magistrate judge, and your Notice of Motion has to give the conference date or the Court may reject it. Discovery motions work the same way. Incarcerated pro se parties are exempt. (L.R. 7.1(a)(2), 37.1)

docs.t: N.D.N.Y. — 25 pages, with a table of contents
docs.x: N.D.N.Y.. 25 pages, with a table of contents. A memorandum of law can’t exceed 25 double-spaced pages unless you get the judge’s leave before filing. It needs a table of contents and numbered pages. A combined cross-motion and opposition brief gets the same 25 pages. (L.R. 7.1(b)(1))

docs.t: N.D.N.Y. — Deadlines move only for good cause
docs.x: N.D.N.Y.. Deadlines move only for good cause. The Court won’t modify case management deadlines, even on stipulation, without good cause, and the request must come before the deadline expires. Ask at least three business days ahead, and state the old deadlines, the prior extensions, and the new dates. (L.R. 16.1(f), 7.1(j))

docs.t: N.D.N.Y. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: N.D.N.Y.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: N.D.N.Y. — overview
docs.x: N.D.N.Y.. The Notice of Motion is the main document,L.R. 7.1(b)(5),File the Notice of Motion as the lead document on ECF, with the supporting papers attached. It names the case, the supporting papers, and the relief and grounds, and it states why you want oral argument if you do. Don’t reattach what’s on the docket,L.R. 7.1(b),Documents already on file in the same action should be cited by docket number, not attached to the motion papers as exhibits. A courtesy copy goes to the judge only if the judge asks. Summary judgment needs two statements,L.R. 56.1,The motion has a separate Statement of Material Facts in numbered paragraphs with record citations. The opposition mirrors it, admitting or denying each paragraph with its own citations, and the Court may deem admitted anything not specifically controverted. Amended pleadings are complete and marked,L.R. 15.1,Attach an unsigned, complete

docs.t: E.D. Cal. — Notice motions at least 35 days out
docs.x: E.D. Cal.. Notice motions at least 35 days out. Every motion is noticed on the assigned judge’s own motion calendar for a hearing not less than 35 days after service and filing. A defectively noticed motion is filed but not set for hearing, and you have to serve a new notice. (L.R. 230(b))

docs.t: E.D. Cal. — Opposition in 14 days, reply in 10
docs.x: E.D. Cal.. Opposition in 14 days, reply in 10. An opposition is due 14 days after the motion was filed. If you won’t oppose, file a statement saying so. A reply is due no later than 10 days after the opposition was filed. A party with no timely opposition can’t be heard in opposition at oral argument. (L.R. 230(c), (d))

docs.t: E.D. Cal. — Proposed orders go in twice
docs.x: E.D. Cal.. Proposed orders go in twice. File the proposed order as a PDF on CM/ECF and also email a Word version to the judge’s email box, with “proposed order” and the case number in the subject line. Doing only one isn’t proper submission. (L.R. 137(b))

docs.t: E.D. Cal. — A sealing request isn’t a filing
docs.x: E.D. Cal.. A sealing request isn’t a filing. File a public Notice of Request to Seal Documents. The Request, proposed order, and documents go by email to the judge’s box, or on paper to the Clerk, and aren’t filed. Serve everyone, and any opposition is due 3 days after service of the Notice. (L.R. 141)

docs.t: E.D. Cal. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: E.D. Cal.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. docs.t: S.D.W. Va. — You need a sponsor who lives and practices in West Virginia
docs.x: S.D.W. Va.. You need a sponsor who lives and practices in West Virginia. A visiting attorney must associate with a Sponsoring Attorney who is a member of this court’s bar, has a West Virginia law office, and practices primarily in West Virginia. The sponsor signs every paper that requires an attorney’s signature. No motion is required, but the Statement of Visiting Attorney and the fee are due at or before your first appearance, including when you sign a pleading. (LR Civ P 83.6(a))

docs.t: S.D.W. Va. — West Virginia charges its own pro hac vice fee
docs.x: S.D.W. Va.. West Virginia charges its own pro hac vice fee. The West Virginia State Bar’s fee is separate from the court’s and is paid to the State Bar, not the clerk. Under Rule 8 of the state’s admission rules it is currently $350 per applicant per case, plus an annual fee if the admission lasts a year or more. Check the current amounts before you file. (LR Civ P 83.6(c)(2); W. Va. Admission Rule 8)

Motions to dismiss stand alone,LR Civ P 7.1(a)(6),File a motion to dismiss as a separate pleading. docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Finish the court’s online tutorial before seeking pro hac vice
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Finish the court’s online tutorial before seeking pro hac vice. Visiting lawyers must complete N.D. Fla.’s online Attorney Admission Tutorial and review the CM/ECF Attorney User’s Guide before applying. The tutorial can’t be waived, and no substitute training counts. Local counsel isn’t required, and visiting lawyers file their own motion once the registration is processed. The fee is $219 per case. (LR 11.1(E); Attorney Admission Memo)

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Only Florida Bar members can join this court’s bar
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Only Florida Bar members can join this court’s bar. Admission to the N.D. Fla. bar requires good standing in The Florida Bar; a license elsewhere doesn’t qualify, no matter how long you have practiced federally. Everyone else appears pro hac vice in each case. Don’t file or appear before admission or pro hac vice leave, except in an emergency while the application is pending. (LR 11.1(A), (C)–(D))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Use 14-point type
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Use 14-point type. Every document must be double spaced, in at least 14-point font, with one-inch margins and numbered pages. Most districts accept 12-point; this one doesn’t. (LR 5.1(C))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Hold a real conference before filing, and certify it
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Hold a real conference before filing, and certify it. Before filing, confer meaningfully with opposing counsel. An email sent at or near filing doesn’t count, and a written conference ordinarily allows at least 24 hours to respond. The motion or memorandum must include a certificate, under a separate heading, confirming compliance and the results. (LR 7.1(B)–(C))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — 8,000 words, with a word-count certificate
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. 8,000 words, with a word-count certificate. Memoranda are capped at 8,000 words, including headings, footnotes, and quotations, and must include a certificate of the word count. A motion over 500 words counts against the memorandum’s limit. (LR 7.1(F))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — No replies without leave, except on summary judgment
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. No replies without leave, except on summary judgment. A party ordinarily may not file a reply. Leave is granted only in extraordinary circumstances and must be obtained before tendering the reply. Replies are limited to 3,200 words. (LR 7.1(I))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — No separate statement of facts on summary judgment
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. No separate statement of facts on summary judgment. Facts go in the memorandum, written as in an appellate brief, with pinpoint record citations. Neither side may file a separate statement of facts or a separate response to one. The opposition is due in 21 days, with no extra 3 days. (LR 56.1(B)–(C))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Fee motions are two-step, and the clock starts at judgment
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Fee motions are two-step, and the clock starts at judgment. Move for entitlement within 14 days after judgment; an appeal doesn’t extend the deadline. Fees are awarded only on contemporaneous, detailed time records to the nearest tenth hour, and the amount phase requires an independent attorney’s declaration. (LR 54.1)

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Never write to the judge, including by email
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Never write to the judge, including by email. A request for action can never be made by letter, and “letter” includes email. Sentencing letters go to the probation office. (LR 7.1(A), (M))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Tell the court the moment a case settles
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Tell the court the moment a case settles. Notify the court immediately of a settlement, a motion resolved by agreement, or an expected motion to continue, and by phone if a trial or hearing is near. If notice comes less than 2 days before a jury panel reports, juror fees and mileage can be assessed against the party, the lawyer, or both. (LR 16.2)

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Patent cases use another district’s rules
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Patent cases use another district’s rules. In a patent case, the Northern District of Georgia’s Local Patent Rules apply unless the court orders otherwise. They are not in this rulebook, so get them before the first conference. (LR 88.3)

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: N.D. Fla. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: N.D. Fla.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

docs.t: D. Guam — Pro hac vice renewal fee, due January 1
docs.x: D. Guam. Pro hac vice renewal fee, due January 1. A lawyer admitted, or previously admitted, under subsection (d) owes an annual renewal fee the court sets, due on or before January 1. If it isn’t paid, the court gives 30 days’ notice and then enters an order removing your name from the case. We found no renewal requirement for regular members of the bar. The court’s fee schedule lists the pro hac vice renewal as $100 (FJC 2024). (D. Guam GNLR 17.1(d)(4))

docs.t: D. Guam — Oppositions run from filing, not service
docs.x: D. Guam. Oppositions run from filing, not service. An opposition is due 21 days after the motion is filed, and a reply 14 days after the opposition. There is no service-based counting. (CVLR 7(f))

docs.t: D. Guam — Agreed extensions have hard caps
docs.x: D. Guam. Agreed extensions have hard caps. Without a scheduling order, parties may agree once to extend an opposition up to 14 days or a reply up to 7 days, by filing notice before the original deadline. Court-set deadlines can’t be changed by agreement. (CVLR 7(g))

docs.t: D. Guam — Email proposed orders to chambers in Word
docs.x: D. Guam. Email proposed orders to chambers in Word. Every motion needs a proposed order, emailed to chambers@gud.uscourts.gov in a word-processing format and served on all parties. (CVLR 7(a))

docs.t: D. Guam — Summary judgment: separate concise statements, or your facts lose
docs.x: D. Guam. Summary judgment: separate concise statements, or your facts lose. The movant files a concise statement of material facts, capped at 5 pages unless it is 1,500 words or less. Facts not controverted by the opponent’s own concise statement are deemed undisputed, and the Court won’t search the record. (CVLR 56)

docs.t: D. Guam — Discovery motions need an in-person or phone conference
docs.x: D. Guam. Discovery motions need an in-person or phone conference. Before any discovery motion, counsel must confer in person or by telephone on all disputed issues, and the motion must certify compliance. Expedited letter briefs are limited to five pages, including exhibits. (CVLR 37(a)–(b))

docs.t: D. Guam — Ask for oral argument on time
docs.x: D. Guam. Ask for oral argument on time. Motions are decided on the papers. A request for argument is due no later than 7 days after the last day a reply could be filed. (CVLR 7(i))

docs.t: D. Guam — Late bill of costs means no costs
docs.x: D. Guam. Late bill of costs means no costs. File the bill of costs within 30 days after judgment. Missing the deadline waives costs. (CVLR 54(b)(2))

docs.t: D. Guam — Dress code: yes, shoes
docs.x: D. Guam. Dress code: yes, shoes. Men need a dress shirt, necktie, jacket or blazer, dress slacks, socks, and dress shoes; women, professional attire with a jacket and dress shoes. Islandwear is allowed Fridays and throughout March. The Court may refuse to hear a noncompliant attorney. (GNLR 18.1(b))

docs.t: D. Guam — overview
docs.x: D. Guam. Page limits and tables,CVLR 7(c)–(d),Memoranda are capped at 25 pages and replies at 15. Briefs over 12 pages need tables of contents and authorities. Motions to exceed are disfavored, filed ex parte, two pages or less, and due no later than the brief. Noncompliant papers may be ignored,CVLR 7(e), (h),The Court need not consider papers that break CVLR 7. Supplemental briefs need leave. Shortened time and evidentiary hearings,CVLR 7(j)–(k),Motions to shorten time need a detailed affidavit. For evidentiary hearings, witness and exhibit lists are due 7 days before, and exhibit copies 3 business days before. Reconsideration is narrow and fast,CVLR 7(p),File within 14 days of the ruling, label it plainly, and rely only on new facts or law, or a manifest failure to consider material facts. docs.t: D. Haw. — Confer at least seven days before filing
docs.x: D. Haw.. Confer at least seven days before filing. Before most motions, counsel must discuss the motion thoroughly with opposing counsel, preferably in person, at least 7 days before filing. The motion must state the conference date. TROs, discovery motions, pro se matters, and trial motions are exempt. (LR7.8)

docs.t: D. Haw. — Two different briefing clocks
docs.x: D. Haw.. Two different briefing clocks. For motions set for hearing, oppositions are due 21 days and replies 14 days before the hearing. For nonhearing motions, oppositions are due 14 days after service and replies 14 days after the opposition. Untimely papers may be disregarded or stricken. (LR7.2)

docs.t: D. Haw. — Not opposing? Say so in writing
docs.x: D. Haw.. Not opposing? Say so in writing. A party that doesn’t oppose must file a statement of no opposition or no position by the opposition deadline. (LR7.2)

docs.t: D. Haw. — New arguments in reply are disregarded
docs.x: D. Haw.. New arguments in reply are disregarded. Replies respond only to the opposition. Supplemental briefing needs leave. (LR7.2)

docs.t: D. Haw. — Over 25 pages needs a word-count certificate
docs.x: D. Haw.. Over 25 pages needs a word-count certificate. Memoranda are capped at 25 pages, or 6,250 words with a certificate; replies at 15 pages, or 3,750 words with a certificate. Briefs over 10 pages need tables of contents and authorities. (LR7.4)

docs.t: D. Haw. — Summary judgment: one-sentence facts, or they’re admitted
docs.x: D. Haw.. Summary judgment: one-sentence facts, or they’re admitted. Each fact is a single sentence with a pinpoint citation in a separate concise statement of 5 pages or 1,500 words. The opponent must admit or dispute each fact in its own concise statement; uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. (LR56.1)

docs.t: D.N.H. — Objections are due 14 days from filing, or they’re waived
docs.x: D.N.H.. Objections are due 14 days from filing, or they’re waived. Objections are due 14 days after the motion is filed, or 30 days for summary judgment. The clock runs from filing, not service, and the court deems late objections waived. (LR 7.1(b))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Replies: as of right only for dispositive motions
docs.x: D.N.H.. Replies: as of right only for dispositive motions. On dispositive motions, a reply of up to 10 pages is due within 7 days of the objection. On nondispositive motions, move for leave within 7 days and attach a proposed reply of up to 5 pages. (LR 7.1(e))

docs.t: D.N.H. — One motion per filing
docs.x: D.N.H.. One motion per filing. Each motion must say “motion” in its title. Don’t combine motions seeking distinct relief, and never fold an affirmative motion into an objection. (LR 7.1(a)(1))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Seek concurrence and say “assented-to”
docs.x: D.N.H.. Seek concurrence and say “assented-to”. Nondispositive motions must certify a good-faith attempt to obtain concurrence. If it is obtained, state it in the body and put “assented-to” in the title. (LR 7.1(c))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Pro hac vice: one motion per lawyer, with years of admission
docs.x: D.N.H.. Pro hac vice: one motion per lawyer, with years of admission. Local counsel files a separate motion for each visiting lawyer, with an affidavit listing every court of admission and the year, and disclosing prior pro hac vice denials or revocations. The $100 fee per lawyer isn’t refunded. Local counsel signs all filings and attends all proceedings. (LR 83.2(b))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Two disclosure statements, filed separately
docs.x: D.N.H.. Two disclosure statements, filed separately. File the corporate disclosure statement (Form 4) and, in a diversity case, the diversity disclosure statement (Form 4.1) as separate documents. They can’t be combined. An unincorporated party must name and give the citizenship of every person or entity whose citizenship is attributed to it, tracing through any unincorporated member until all are disclosed. (LR 7.1.1 (Dec. 1, 2025))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Summary judgment opposition needs its own fact statement
docs.x: D.N.H.. Summary judgment opposition needs its own fact statement. The opposing memorandum must include a short, concise statement of the material facts in genuine dispute, with record citations. Properly supported facts in the movant’s statement may be deemed admitted unless you properly oppose them. (LR 56.1(b) (Dec. 1, 2025))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Form violations can be fined, and you must contest before paying
docs.x: D.N.H.. Form violations can be fined, and you must contest before paying. The court may fine the lawyer for violating a rule on the form of a filing. To contest a fine, file a motion to vacate before you pay. A motion filed after payment won’t be considered. (LR 1.3(a))

docs.t: D.N.H. — No email or fax filings
docs.x: D.N.H.. No email or fax filings. The clerk’s office won’t accept filings by fax or email without an oral or written court order. (LR 5.1(e))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Bar number follows your typed name
docs.x: D.N.H.. Bar number follows your typed name. Every filing shows your name, address, phone, email, and New Hampshire bar number, or its equivalent if you’re not a member. The number goes right after the typed name in the signature block. (LR 5.1(b))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Extension motions must say what moves, and attach Civil Form 3
docs.x: D.N.H.. Extension motions must say what moves, and attach Civil Form 3. A motion to extend time must say whether the extension would continue any hearing, conference, or trial, and give the proposed new date. A motion to extend deadlines set in the scheduling order must also attach a completed Civil Form 3. (LR 7.2(a))

docs.t: D.N.H. — The summary judgment fact statement goes inside your memorandum
docs.x: D.N.H.. The summary judgment fact statement goes inside your memorandum. The movant’s memorandum must incorporate a short, concise statement of material facts, with record citations, as to which there is no genuine issue to be tried. Properly supported facts may be deemed admitted if the other side doesn’t oppose them. (LR 56.1(a))

docs.t: D.N.H. — A motion to compel must quote the request
docs.x: D.N.H.. A motion to compel must quote the request. A discovery motion must include a verbatim recitation of each request at issue, or a copy of the discovery document. Judges have faulted motions that leave it out. (LR 37.1(a))

docs.t: D.N.H. — A motion to amend must attach the proposed pleading
docs.x: D.N.H.. A motion to amend must attach the proposed pleading. Attach the proposed amended filing, and identify in the motion or a supporting memorandum any new factual allegations, legal claims, or parties. The rule also asks for an explanation of the new material, so read its full text before filing. (LR 15.1(a))

docs.t: D.N.H. — A court deadline can’t be moved by agreement
docs.x: D.N.H.. A court deadline can’t be moved by agreement. Deadlines set by the court can’t be changed by agreement without court approval. The one exception is discovery. A stipulation extending the time to respond to a discovery request or to take a deposition needs no approval if the new date is before the discovery completion date, or at least 30 days before the final pretrial conference, whichever is earlier. (LR 16.4)

docs.t: D.N.H. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: D.N.H.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: D.N.H. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: D.N.H.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

Facts outside the record need affidavits. Page limits depend on the motion,LR 7.1(a)(3),Nondispositive memoranda are capped at 15 pages and dispositive memoranda at 25. Exceeding them needs prior leave. What counts as dispositive,LR 7.1(g),Injunctive relief, Rule 12(b) and 12(c) motions, summary judgment, class-action motions, and involuntary dismissal. Sanction-based dismissals follow the nondispositive schedule. Surreplies are rare,LR 7.1(e)(3),After a permitted reply, a surreply of up to 5 pages may follow within 5 days, but only in exceptional circumstances. Argument is the exception,LR 7.1(d),Motions are decided on the papers. To get argument, file a written statement of why it would help; each side gets 15 minutes. Expedited t

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Renewal fee every two years, due February 15
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Renewal fee every two years, due February 15. Unless you were admitted pro hac vice, pay the fee the court sets every two years, due on or before February 15. After a missed payment the court sends a 30-day notice that adds a late fee, then a second 30-day notice. If you still don’t pay, you are removed from the roll and must qualify for admission anew. The fee is $30 per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. (D.N. Mar. I. LR 83.5(c))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Oppose within 14 days, or concede
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Oppose within 14 days, or concede. Oppositions are due 14 days after service. The court may disregard and strike a late opposition and may treat the failure to oppose on time as an admission that the motion is meritorious. (LR 7.1(c)(2))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Pro hac vice requires local counsel
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Pro hac vice requires local counsel. Visiting lawyers petition for pro hac vice admission and must associate with local counsel who agrees to the requirements of LR 83.5(f). (LR 83.5(f))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Dress code: yes, shoes
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Dress code: yes, shoes. Men need at least a jacket, dress shirt, necktie, dress slacks, socks, and shoes; women, a dress or suit, slacks or skirt and blouse, and shoes. The court may refuse to hear an attorney who doesn’t comply. (LR 83.4(e))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — A motion is heard on a Thursday, at least 34 days out
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. A motion is heard on a Thursday, at least 34 days out. Motion day is Thursday. A motion is noticed for hearing on the first Thursday at least 34 days after it is filed, unless you arrange another date with the docket clerk. Non-hearing motions, such as motions to extend time and stipulated motions, are decided on the papers. (LR 7.1(b)(1), (c)(1))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Put the hearing date and time on the first page
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Put the hearing date and time on the first page. The first page of every motion, opposition, reply, or other filing aimed at a hearing must show the hearing date and time, for example “Hearing: June 29, 2017 / Time: 9:00 a.m.” (LR 5.2(e))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — The reply is 7 days, and then nothing more
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. The reply is 7 days, and then nothing more. The reply is due 7 days after the opposition is served and is limited to 10 pages. No further filings are accepted without leave, and any filed in violation of the rule are stricken. (LR 7.1(c)(3), (4))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Briefs are 25 pages, replies 10
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Briefs are 25 pages, replies 10. A brief or memorandum may not exceed 25 pages, and a reply 10. Anything over 10 pages needs a table of contents and a table of authorities. To go over, move first, without attaching the brief. Excess pages are stricken. (LR 7.1(d))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — An extension motion has a required caption
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. An extension motion has a required caption. The caption must read, in capitals and bold, MOTION TO EXTEND (OR SHORTEN) TIME UNDER LOCAL RULE 7.1(f). State the earlier extensions, the reasons, and the effect on other deadlines. Without a stipulation, certify that you tried to meet and confer. An emergency motion (action within 48 hours) also needs phone and email notice. (LR 7.1(f))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Proposed orders go by email, not CM/ECF
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Proposed orders go by email, not CM/ECF. Email proposed orders in Word format to usdcnmi@nmid.uscourts.gov and serve the other parties. Don’t file them in CM/ECF. (LR 7.1(b)(4); App. A § 5)

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Foreign-language exhibits: translation 28 days out
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Foreign-language exhibits: translation 28 days out. A foreign-language exhibit needs a certified English translation and the translator’s affidavit, served at least 28 days before trial. Objections are due 14 days before trial. Miss the first deadline and the document is inadmissible. Miss the second and you waive your objection. (LR 16.5(a)(4))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — 12-point serif type, numbered lines, big margins
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. 12-point serif type, numbered lines, big margins. Use a serif font of 12 points or larger, double-spaced, with line numbers down the left margin. Leave 1.5 inches at the top and three inches blank in the upper right corner of page one. The clerk can order a fix, and you have two business days to cure it. (LR 5.2(a))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — Filing deadline: midnight, Northern Mariana Islands time
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Filing deadline: midnight, Northern Mariana Islands time. Electronic filing must be completed before midnight local time in the Northern Mariana Islands for a filing to be timely that day. The Northern Mariana Islands are on Chamorro Standard Time (UTC+10) and don’t observe daylight saving time, so they are 15 hours ahead of Eastern Standard Time and 14 hours ahead of Eastern Daylight Time. (Local Rules, Appendix A § 3)

docs.x: D.N. Mar. I. formatting. Attire: Jacket, shirt, tie, slacks, socks, and shoes; women, professional dress and shoes (LR 83.4(e))

docs.x: D.N. Mar. I. formatting. Margins: 1.5 inches at the top, 1 inch at the bottom, 1 inch on the left, one-half inch on the right (LR 5.2(a))

docs.t: D.N. Mar. I. — overview
docs.x: D.N. Mar. I.. Hearings can be vacated,LR 7.1,The court may vacate a noticed hearing and decide the motion on the papers. A territorial court,48 U.S.C. § 1821,The court sits in Saipan with one judge serving ten-year terms. It has the same jurisdiction as a U.S. district court, and appeals go to the Ninth Circuit. The case management conference,LR 16.2,The court issues an order within 14 days after any defendant appears, setting the conference about 35 days out. The parties confer at least 21 days before it and file a joint case management statement at least 7 days before. The lawyer who attends must have authority to bind the client. Habeas, Social Security, default, and enforcement cases are usually exempt. Case tracks,LR 16.1(b),Expedited cases are expected to finish within 6 months after the conference, with 15 interrogatories and 15 requests for admission. Standard cases are expected

docs.t: D.R.I. — Renew your registration every two years: the 2026 period began June 1
docs.x: D.R.I.. Renew your registration every two years: the 2026 period began June 1. The court amended LR Gen 203(c) so members renew every two years. The 2026 renewal period began June 1, 2026, costs $35, and renewals after August 31, 2026 carry a late fee, so if you haven’t renewed, do it now. Full-time lawyers for a federal or Rhode Island government agency or a non-profit pay no fee. Renewal is an event in CM/ECF. The next period is presumably two years later, but we haven’t seen that date. The older rule in our April 2024 edition, every fourth year in January to March, has been replaced. (D.R.I. LR Gen 203(c); clerk’s 2026 renewal instructions)

docs.x: D.R.I.. Memoranda attach to the motion. A separate memorandum isn’t required. If you file one, attach it to the motion; don’t docket it separately. The motion itself must state the grounds, relief, and argument with particularity. (LR Cv 7(a)(2)(B))

docs.x: D.R.I.. Summary judgment runs on numbered fact statements. File a separate Statement of Undisputed Facts with numbered paragraphs and page-and-line cites. docs.t: D.R.I. — overview
docs.x: D.R.I.. Additional facts get their own statement,LR Cv 56(a)(4)–(5),An opponent’s additional facts go in a separate statement, numbered consecutively after the movant’s. The movant contests them in a statement filed with its reply. Attach only what matters,LR Cv 56(b),Include only the relevant portions of supporting documents unless the Court asks for more. Local counsel’s duties are real,LR Gen 204(d),Local counsel must be ready to take sole responsibility if pro hac vice counsel can’t continue, and must be kept fully informed. Revocation and updates,LR Gen 204(e)–(f),The judge may revoke pro hac vice status. Pro hac vice counsel must promptly report contact changes. Administrative appeals need record cites,LR Cv 7(b),In appeals from agencies, including Social Security, every motion, response, and reply cites the administrative record. Sealing: provisional, and redact first,LR Gen 102,F

docs.t: D. Utah — Register and pay by July 1 every year
docs.x: D. Utah. Register and pay by July 1 every year. To keep active status, register through CM/ECF and pay the annual fee, set by the court, by July 1 each year. Active status also means accepting pro bono assignments unless a government employer prohibits it. You owe nothing until 12 months after admission, and federal attorneys are exempt from the fee. The fee is $30 per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. (DUCivR 83-1.2)

docs.t: D. Utah — Motion and memorandum in one document
docs.x: D. Utah. Motion and memorandum in one document. The motion and its supporting memorandum are a single document, opening with a separate section stating the relief sought and the grounds. Only a few motions, such as an unopposed extension filed before the deadline, skip the facts and authority. (DUCivR 7-1(a)(1))

docs.t: D. Utah — No motions inside responses, and no joinders
docs.x: D. Utah. No motions inside responses, and no joinders. Every motion, including a Rule 56(d) request or a cross-motion, is filed separately. A “Notice of Joinder” is improper: file your own motion and incorporate the other side’s arguments by reference. (DUCivR 7-1(a)(3), (a)(8))

docs.t: D. Utah — Limits and deadlines depend on the motion
docs.x: D. Utah. Limits and deadlines depend on the motion. Rule 12(b), 12(c), 23(c) and Rule 56 motions get 28 days to respond. Rule 65 and all other motions get 14. Replies are due 14 days after the response. Page and word limits vary from 10 to 40 pages. (DUCivR 7-1(a)(4))

docs.t: D. Utah — Stipulated extensions are ineffective without an order
docs.x: D. Utah. Stipulated extensions are ineffective without an order. To extend a briefing deadline, file a stipulated motion before the time runs out and get an order. No stipulation that affects the course of the case takes effect until the court approves it. (DUCivR 7-1(a)(5), 83-4)

docs.t: D. Utah — Discovery disputes: short-form motion within 45 days
docs.x: D. Utah. Discovery disputes: short-form motion within 45 days. Send a prompt written deficiency letter that asks to meet and confer. If the dispute persists, file a Short Form Discovery Motion of 500 words or less within 45 days of that letter, or it can be automatically denied. The response is due 5 business days later. (DUCivR 37-1)

docs.t: D. Utah — Get overlength permission first
docs.x: D. Utah. Get overlength permission first. Unless the judge’s practices page says otherwise, you need an order authorizing extra pages or words before you file the long document. An overlength filing also needs a table of contents. (DUCivR 7-1(a)(7))

docs.t: D. Utah — Don’t move to strike evidence
docs.x: D. Utah. Don’t move to strike evidence. A motion to strike evidence in another party’s brief is improper. Raise an evidentiary objection in your response or reply, or within 7 days after new evidence appears in a reply. (DUCivR 7-1(b))

docs.t: D. Utah — Pro hac vice has limits
docs.x: D. Utah. Pro hac vice has limits. Pro hac vice isn’t open to Utah State Bar members or lawyers with a Utah law office, and not to a lawyer already admitted in 3 unrelated cases in the past 5 years here without good cause. Local counsel must be in this court’s bar and attend whenever you appear. (DUCivR 83-1.1(c))

It’s required for the short list of motions that skip facts and authority, and whenever the court orders it.
