docs.t: D. Vt. — Put “motion” in the title, or it won’t be considered
docs.x: D. Vt.. Put “motion” in the title, or it won’t be considered. The court will not consider any motion that lacks the word “motion” in its title. (L.R. 7(a)(1))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Oppositions: 30 days for dispositive, 14 for others
docs.x: D. Vt.. Oppositions: 30 days for dispositive, 14 for others. Oppositions to dispositive motions are due 30 days after service; all others, 14 days. Replies of up to 10 pages are due 14 days after the opposition. (L.R. 7(a)(3))

docs.t: D. Vt. — “Stipulated” in the caption when the other side agrees
docs.x: D. Vt.. “Stipulated” in the caption when the other side agrees. Non-dispositive motions must certify a good-faith attempt to obtain agreement. If obtained, say so in the body and put “Stipulated” in the caption. (L.R. 7(a)(7))

docs.t: D. Vt. — First and Second Circuit lawyers can join the bar outright
docs.x: D. Vt.. First and Second Circuit lawyers can join the bar outright. Members of any First or Second Circuit district court bar may apply for full admission, with a sponsor’s affidavit, a certificate of good standing, and the fee. (L.R. 83.1(a)(1)(B))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Pro hac vice: local counsel signs and attends everything
docs.x: D. Vt.. Pro hac vice: local counsel signs and attends everything. Local counsel files the motion with your affidavit listing every bar you’ve joined, a certificate of good standing, and a non-refundable fee. Local counsel signs all filings and attends all proceedings unless waived, and is your agent for service. (L.R. 83.1(b))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Discovery schedule: 45 or 75 days, or discovery is waived
docs.x: D. Vt.. Discovery schedule: 45 or 75 days, or discovery is waived. File the joint Discovery Schedule within the earlier of 75 days after any defendant is served or 45 days after any defendant appears. Failure to strictly comply waives the need for discovery, and the case is set for trial. Discovery runs no more than 8 months after the last answer, and a motion to dismiss doesn’t stay it. (L.R. 26(a)(2), (5))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Summary judgment needs a numbered fact statement
docs.x: D. Vt.. Summary judgment needs a numbered fact statement. File a separate, concise statement in numbered paragraphs, each with a citation to admissible evidence. Leaving it out may be a ground for denial. The response answers each paragraph by number, and any paragraph not specifically controverted may be deemed admitted. (L.R. 56(a), (b), (d))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Discovery motions need conferral and an affidavit
docs.x: D. Vt.. Discovery motions need conferral and an affidavit. Confer in good faith first. Then file an affidavit giving the dates, participants, and length of the conferences and the issues still open. The memorandum must list each discovery item verbatim, with the reason it should be allowed or disallowed. (L.R. 26(c))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Replies: 14 days, 10 pages
docs.x: D. Vt.. Replies: 14 days, 10 pages. A reply is due no more than 14 days after the opposition and can’t exceed 10 pages. (L.R. 7(a)(5))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Page limits: 25 and 15
docs.x: D. Vt.. Page limits: 25 and 15. A memorandum supporting or opposing a dispositive motion runs 25 pages. For any other motion, 15. Exhibits and attachments don’t count. Anything longer needs the judge’s leave first. (L.R. 7(a)(4))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Reconsideration in 14 days
docs.x: D. Vt.. Reconsideration in 14 days. A motion to reconsider an order, other than one under Rule 59 or 60, must be filed within 14 days of the order. (L.R. 7(c))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Amend with a redline and a clean copy
docs.x: D. Vt.. Amend with a redline and a clean copy. A motion to amend must include a redlined version showing additions and deletions and a non-redlined copy of the entire amended filing. An amendment can’t incorporate an earlier filing by reference without the court’s permission. (L.R. 15)

docs.t: D. Vt. — A visiting lawyer’s response clock waits for local counsel
docs.x: D. Vt.. A visiting lawyer’s response clock waits for local counsel. A pro hac vice lawyer may file original pleadings, but the time to respond doesn’t start until the court receives the local attorney’s notice of appearance. (L.R. 83.1(b)(5))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: D. Vt.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: D. Vt. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: D. Vt.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

Early Neutral Evaluation,L.R. 16.1,Many civil case types go to ENE near the midpoint of discovery. A neutral evaluator is paid $500 per case, split by the parties. docs.t: D.V.I. — Annual renewal fee, $45
docs.x: D.V.I.. Annual renewal fee, $45. An annual renewal fee of $45 is required, per the FJC’s 2024 compilation of the court’s fee schedule. We haven’t read this rule ourselves, so confirm with the clerk. (D.V.I. LR 83.1(c)(2); FJC 2024)

docs.t: D.V.I. — Three pro hac vice cases a year, maximum
docs.x: D.V.I.. Three pro hac vice cases a year, maximum. A lawyer may be admitted pro hac vice in no more than three cases per calendar year, and not at all while already in three active cases. Every filing needs local counsel’s signature and is deemed approved by local counsel. (LRCi 83.1(b)(2))

docs.t: D.V.I. — No separate memorandum; argument goes in the motion
docs.x: D.V.I.. No separate memorandum; argument goes in the motion. A motion includes the relief, background, and argument with authority. Separate memoranda aren’t allowed, and further briefing needs leave before filing. (LRCi 7.1(a)(1))

docs.t: D.V.I. — Every motion needs a draft order, with real dates
docs.x: D.V.I.. Every motion needs a draft order, with real dates. Attach a draft order stating the specific relief. For extensions, state the actual new deadline date. (LRCi 7.1(a)(5))

docs.t: D.V.I. — Rule 12 and 56 responses run from filing
docs.x: D.V.I.. Rule 12 and 56 responses run from filing. Responses are due 21 days after the motion is filed for Rule 12 and Rule 56 motions; 14 days after service for most others; 7 days after filing for motions in limine. (LRCi 6.1(b))

docs.t: D.V.I. — 20 pages or 6,000 words; ask two days ahead
docs.x: D.V.I.. 20 pages or 6,000 words; ask two days ahead. Leave to exceed the limit must be sought at least two days before filing. Over 20 pages requires a word-count certificate. (LRCi 7.1(b))

docs.t: D.V.I. — One of each
docs.x: D.V.I.. One of each. Without leave, a party may file only one Rule 12(b)(2)–(6) motion, one Rule 56 motion, and one motion in limine. (LRCi 7.1(c))

docs.t: D.V.I. — Seek consent 24 hours before filing
docs.x: D.V.I.. Seek consent 24 hours before filing. Non-dispositive motions must state that consent was sought from each party at least 24 hours before filing, and whether it was given or denied. (LRCi 7.1(e))

Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: D.V.I. — overview
docs.x: D.V.I.. Continuances need alternative dates,LRCi 7.1(f),Consult the other parties and propose several agreeable dates. Oral argument requests go at the end,LRCi 7.1(d),State the request separately at the conclusion of the motion, response, or reply. Post-trial motions need record cites,LRCi 7.1(g),Cite the specific record portions and order transcripts promptly. Holidays include court closures,LRCi 6.1(a),Any day both divisions are closed counts as a legal holiday. Special admission for public-interest work,LRCi 83.1(c),Lawyers representing the V.I. government, public interest groups, or pro bono clients may seek special admission for up to three years. Keep to the schedule,LRCi 83.1(d),Strictly observe all dates. Noncompliance can cost pro hac vice permission.

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Confer first, and say exactly how
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Confer first, and say exactly how. Non-dispositive motions must state the specific efforts made to confer and the other side’s position. A motion may be summarily denied without that. The duty doesn’t apply when a pro se party is involved. (L.R. 7.1(b)(1)(A))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Discovery disputes start with a phone call
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Discovery disputes start with a phone call. After conferring, counsel jointly contact the assigned magistrate judge for an informal telephonic discovery call. The court allows a written discovery motion only if the call doesn’t resolve it. (L.R. 37.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — 14 days to respond, or risk a confession
docs.x: D. Wyo.. 14 days to respond, or risk a confession. Responses to dispositive and non-dispositive motions are due 14 days after the motion is filed. The court may treat a late or missing response as a confession of the motion. (L.R. 7.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Short limits: 10, 25, 5, and 10
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Short limits: 10, 25, 5, and 10. Briefs on non-dispositive motions run 10 pages and on dispositive motions 25. Replies are due 7 days after the response and capped at 5 pages (non-dispositive) or 10 (dispositive). Reply extensions need extraordinary circumstances. (L.R. 7.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — No replies on motions set for hearing
docs.x: D. Wyo.. No replies on motions set for hearing. If a motion is set for hearing, no reply may be filed. Missing a noticed hearing can be treated as waiving your motion or confessing the one against you. (L.R. 7.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Nothing under seal without prior permission
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Nothing under seal without prior permission. In civil cases, no case or document may be filed under seal or as non-public without prior court authorization or order. (L.R. 5.1(g))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — No stipulated continuances
docs.x: D. Wyo.. No stipulated continuances. Cases aren’t continued on the parties’ stipulation alone. The court must approve, and only on good cause. Any extension request must disclose prior extensions, objections, and a date certain (L.R. 6.1(e)). (L.R. 40.1(b))

docs.t: D. Wyo. — Local counsel must be in both bars
docs.x: D. Wyo.. Local counsel must be in both bars. Local counsel must belong to the Wyoming State Bar and this court’s bar, appear before anything is filed, move for your admission, and attend every proceeding unless excused. (L.R. 84.2(b))

docs.t: D. Mont. — Re-registration fees, and your state license must stay active
docs.x: D. Mont.. Re-registration fees, and your state license must stay active. You must pay the admission fee and any re-registration fees the court imposes, and failing to pay can deactivate your filing privileges. docs.x: D. Mont.. Clocks run from docket entry. Responses to motions to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, or for summary judgment are due 21 days after docket entry; all others, 14. docs.t: E.D. Mich. — Pro hac vice doesn’t exist here
docs.x: E.D. Mich.. Pro hac vice doesn’t exist here. The court hasn’t allowed pro hac vice since 1981. Join the court’s bar instead. Anyone in good standing in a U.S. court of record is eligible. (LR 83.20(c)(1))

docs.t: E.D. Mich. — Seek concurrence, and mean it
docs.x: E.D. Mich.. Seek concurrence, and mean it. Before filing, confer in good faith in a way that allows a real back-and-forth. An email that doesn’t engage the other side won’t do. If you don’t get concurrence, the motion must say which of the listed reasons applies. Several judges strike motions that skip this. (LR 7.1(a))

docs.t: E.D. Mich. — Non-Michigan lawyers need local counsel
docs.x: E.D. Mich.. Non-Michigan lawyers need local counsel. If you’re admitted here but not an active State Bar of Michigan member, name local counsel with an office in the district. Local counsel appears, must be ready to run the case, and attends every scheduled appearance unless excused. (LR 83.20(f))

docs.t: E.D. Mo. — Renew every four years; this cycle is due January 31, 2027
docs.x: E.D. Mo.. Renew every four years; this cycle is due January 31, 2027. Every member of the bar must re-register every four years. The current period opened in fall 2026, and renewal is due January 31, 2027. The fee is set by court order before each period; the FJC’s 2024 compilation listed $75, which we haven’t confirmed for this cycle. Miss it and you are provisionally removed and can’t file or appear; with no renewal within three months, you’re removed from the roll and must apply again. (E.D. Mo. L.R. 12.01(E); court’s Attorney Re-Registration page)

docs.t: E.D. Mo. — Fifteen numbered pages, and summary judgment has its own statements
docs.x: E.D. Mo.. Fifteen numbered pages, and summary judgment has its own statements. Briefs can run 15 numbered pages without leave, not counting tables, signature page, and attachments. Statements of facts don’t count toward that limit. (Rule 4.01(D), (E))

docs.t: E.D. Mo. — Summary judgment: two separate filings
docs.x: E.D. Mo.. Summary judgment: two separate filings. File a Statement of Uncontroverted Material Facts with a numbered paragraph for each fact and its record cite, using that filing event. The opponent files a Response to Statement of Material Facts. Every fact you don’t dispute is deemed admitted. (Rule 4.01(E))

docs.t: E.D. Mo. — Replies only at 10 days, and extra memos need leave
docs.x: E.D. Mo.. Replies only at 10 days, and extra memos need leave. The movant may reply within 10 days after the opposition is served. Any other memorandum needs leave of court. (Rule 4.01(C))

docs.x: E.D. Mo.. Opposition clock: 14 days, or 21 for summary judgment. Oppose most motions within 14 days of service, and summary judgment motions within 21. Extension oppositions are due in 7 days. (Rule 4.01(B), (F))

docs.t: E.D. Mo. — Attach the evidence

docs.t: D. Idaho — 20 pages, and replies 10
docs.x: D. Idaho. 20 pages, and replies 10. No memorandum can exceed 20 pages, and no reply 10 pages, without leave granted only in unusual circumstances. Small fonts and tight spacing to fit the limit aren’t acceptable. (Loc. Civ. R. 7.1(a)(2))

docs.t: D. Idaho — Summary judgment: separate fact statements
docs.x: D. Idaho. Summary judgment: separate fact statements. The moving party files a separate statement of undisputed material facts, capped at 10 pages. The responding party files its own statement of disputed facts, also capped at 10 pages. (Loc. Civ. R. 7.1(b)(1), (c)(2))

docs.t: D. Idaho — Motions need a separate brief
docs.x: D. Idaho. Motions need a separate brief. Every motion other than a routine or uncontested one needs its own brief containing all reasons and authorities. (Loc. Civ. R. 7.1(b)(1))

docs.t: D. Idaho — Responses in 21 days, replies in 14
docs.x: D. Idaho. Responses in 21 days, replies in 14. The response brief is due 21 days after service of the opening brief, with any evidence attached. The reply is due 14 days after service of the response. (Loc. Civ. R. 7.1(b)(3), (c)(1))

docs.t: D. Idaho — Failure to respond can decide the motion
docs.x: D. Idaho. Failure to respond can decide the motion. Failing to file a required document can waive the motion or be deemed consent. Summary judgment is different: silence isn’t consent, but unsupported or unaddressed facts can be treated as undisputed. (Loc. Civ. R. 7.1(f)(1))

docs.t: E.D.N.C. — Special appearance needs a local signer
docs.x: E.D.N.C.. Special appearance needs a local signer. Out-of-state lawyers appear by special appearance in association with a member of this court’s bar, who signs every filing. Filings must show that member’s state bar number and fax number. The local member must review every filing before it goes in. (Loc. Civ. R. 83.1(d), (e))

docs.t: E.D.N.C. — Three cases a year, three at once
docs.x: E.D.N.C.. Three cases a year, three at once. Special appearance is for occasional appearances. Unless the court finds good cause, no attorney may appear in more than three unrelated cases in a 12-month period, or in more than three active unrelated cases at once. (Loc. Civ. R. 83.1(e)(5))

docs.t: E.D.N.C. — Local counsel attends
docs.x: E.D.N.C.. Local counsel attends. Local counsel must attend all court proceedings unless the court excuses it. Service on local counsel alone is enough. (Loc. Civ. R. 83.1(f))

docs.t: E.D.N.C. — Motions: concise, with a memorandum
docs.x: E.D.N.C.. Motions: concise, with a memorandum. Motions must be concise and state the relief precisely. Every motion needs a supporting memorandum, and any affidavits must accompany it. (Loc. Civ. R. 7.1(b)(1), (e))

docs.t: E.D.N.C. — Discovery motions need a specific good-faith certification
docs.x: E.D.N.C.. Discovery motions need a specific good-faith certification. A discovery motion must set out, item by item, the specific question or request and any objection. It must also certify a good-faith effort to resolve the dispute before filing. Without that, the court won’t consider it. (Loc. Civ. R. 7.1(c)(2))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Briefs are counted in words, with a signed certificate
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Briefs are counted in words, with a signed certificate. A computer-prepared brief can run 6,250 words and a reply 3,125, counting the body, headings, and footnotes. Each brief must carry a signed certificate of word count. Typed or handwritten briefs are limited to 20 pages and replies to 10. (LR 7.3(d)(1))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Silence loses the motion
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Silence loses the motion. If you don’t file a response within the time allowed, the motion is decided as uncontested and ordinarily granted without further notice. A motion that lacks a required brief may be summarily denied. (LR 7.3(k))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Response time depends on the motion
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Response time depends on the motion. Responses are due 21 days after service, 30 days for summary judgment, and 14 days for discovery motions. Replies are due 14 days after the response, or 7 days for discovery motions, and are limited to matters newly raised. (LR 7.3(f), (h))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Summary judgment starts with a notice
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Summary judgment starts with a notice. File a notice of intention to file a dispositive motion within 14 days after discovery closes. File the motion and brief within 30 days after discovery closes. All summary judgment issues must go in a single motion and brief unless the court allows otherwise. (LR 56.1(a)–(b))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Don’t file a motion to strike evidence
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Don’t file a motion to strike evidence. Make an evidentiary objection in your response or reply instead. A separate motion to strike may be summarily denied. (LR 7.6)

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Sealing is disfavored
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Sealing is disfavored. Nothing is filed under seal unless a statute, rule, or order allows it, and filing a document under temporary seal pending a motion is allowed only as LR 5.4 and 5.5 provide. Overbroad or unsupported sealing motions can draw sanctions, including fees. (LR 5.4(a))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Tell the court early if sealed filings are likely
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Tell the court early if sealed filings are likely. Address sealing at the Rule 26(f) meeting. Your Rule 26(f) report must either say no sealed documents are expected or say a separate LR 5.5 Report has been filed. If you were wrong, meet and confer and file the report within 10 days. (LR 5.4(b), 5.5)

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Discovery motions need a personal conference
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Discovery motions need a personal conference. Your certificate must give the date of the conference, who took part, and what came of it. Movant’s counsel arranges it. At any party’s request it can be by phone or video. (LR 37.1(a))

docs.t: M.D.N.C. — Pro hac vice is a special appearance, not a motion
docs.x: M.D.N.C.. Pro hac vice is a special appearance, not a motion. Associate with a member of this court’s bar, register for CM/ECF, and file a Notice of Special Appearance. No motion is required, and the local lawyer signs everything and attends key proceedings. (LR 83.1(d))

Use a proportional font of at least 13 point, and no more than 27 lines of regularly spaced text a page. Signature block,LR 7.1(b),Give your telephone number, mailing address, and email address. docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — 25 pages, with strict formatting
docs.x: N.D.W. Va.. 25 pages, with strict formatting. Dispositive motions and sanctions motions need a memorandum of up to 25 pages, with the supporting materials attached. docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — Response 14 days, 21 for summary judgment
docs.x: N.D.W. Va.. Response 14 days, 21 for summary judgment. Responses are due 14 days after service, 21 days for summary judgment. Replies are due 7 days after the response, 14 days for summary judgment, and are limited to 15 pages. No surreply without leave. (LR Civ P 7.02(b)(1))

docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — Mark your motion to dismiss as one
docs.x: N.D.W. Va.. Mark your motion to dismiss as one. The court gives motions to dismiss priority only if they are designated prominently as a motion to dismiss and filed as a separate pleading. (LR Civ P 12.02)

docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — Don’t file discovery
docs.x: N.D.W. Va.. Don’t file discovery. Initial and pretrial disclosures, depositions, interrogatories, document requests, admissions and responses aren’t filed unless the court orders it. File only certificates of service. (LR Civ P 5.01(a))

docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — Motions to compel expire in 30 days
docs.x: N.D.W. Va.. Motions to compel expire in 30 days. A motion to compel or other discovery motion is deemed waived if not filed within 30 days after the response or disclosure was due, absent excusable neglect or the other side’s conduct. Set out each disputed request verbatim. (LR Civ P 37.02(b))

docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — Objections are waived if late
docs.x: N.D.W. Va.. Objections are waived if late. An objection not made within the time for responding is waived absent good cause. Privilege claims must identify the privilege and the documents or communications. (LR Civ P 26.04(a))

docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — Pro hac vice needs a West Virginia-office lawyer
docs.x: N.D.W. Va.. Pro hac vice needs a West Virginia-office lawyer. The responsible local attorney must keep a physical office in West Virginia, sign everything with a state bar number, and attend all hearings and depositions unless the court permits telephone attendance. (LR Gen P 83.02)

docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — Continuances need three agreed dates
docs.x: N.D.W. Va.. Continuances need three agreed dates. Before moving to continue, meet and confer to agree on three non-consecutive new dates, and put them in the motion. If you can’t agree, each side tells the court its suggested dates. (LR Gen P 88.02)

docs.t: N.D.W. Va. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time

docs.t: W.D.N.C. — The judge’s Standing Civil Order sets page limits
docs.x: W.D.N.C.. The judge’s Standing Civil Order sets page limits. Page limits, fonts, and spacing come from the assigned judge’s Standing Civil Order or the Case Management Order. If neither speaks to it, the default is 25 pages, 12-point font, double-spaced, one-inch margins, numbered pages. (LCvR 7.1(d))

docs.t: W.D.N.C. — 14 days to respond, 7 to reply, no sur-reply
docs.x: W.D.N.C.. 14 days to respond, 7 to reply, no sur-reply. A response is due 14 days after service and a reply 7 days after that, limited to matters newly raised. If you won’t file a reply, tell the court and opposing counsel promptly by filed notice. Sur-replies need leave. (LCvR 7.1(e))

docs.t: W.D.N.C. — Confer first, or risk summary denial
docs.x: W.D.N.C.. Confer first, or risk summary denial. Civil motions must show you conferred in good faith, or describe your timely attempts. No conference is needed for dispositive motions, represented-versus-unrepresented motions, or extensions to respond to an initial pleading. (LCvR 7.1(b))

docs.t: W.D.N.C. — A motion to dismiss in an answer does nothing
docs.x: W.D.N.C.. A motion to dismiss in an answer does nothing. It is treated as preserving the issue and won’t be addressed. To get a ruling, file a separate motion with a brief. (LCvR 7.1(c)(1))

docs.t: W.D.N.C. — Court-enforceable discovery waits for the scheduling order
docs.x: W.D.N.C.. Court-enforceable discovery waits for the scheduling order. Discovery can’t be enforced until issues are joined and a Scheduling Order issues, except early Rule 34 requests. You may seek leave for early discovery. (LCvR 26.1; 16.1(f))

docs.t: W.D.N.C. — Certificate of Initial Attorney’s Conference
docs.x: W.D.N.C.. Certificate of Initial Attorney’s Conference. Confer within 14 days of joinder of the issues and file the Certificate, with a proposed discovery plan, within 7 days after the conference. (LCvR 16.1(a)–(b))

docs.t: W.D.N.C. — The AI order is binding, with sanctions
docs.x: W.D.N.C.. The AI order is binding, with sanctions. Filing any document certifies that facts have support, legal contentions are warranted, all authorities exist and are accurately cited, and quotations are accurate. A human must verify. Sanctions can reach disbarment from practice here. (AI Order (July 29, 2026))

docs.t: D.D.C. — 45 pages for briefs, 25 for replies
docs.x: D.D.C.. 45 pages for briefs, 25 for replies. A memorandum supporting or opposing a motion cannot exceed 45 pages, and a reply cannot exceed 25, without prior court approval. Documents over the limit won’t be filed by the clerk. (LCvR 7(e))

docs.t: D.D.C. — Summary judgment: the facts you don’t controvert are admitted
docs.x: D.D.C.. Summary judgment: the facts you don’t controvert are admitted. The moving party’s statement of material facts comes with the motion. The opposition needs a separate statement of genuine issues. The court may treat any fact you don’t controvert as admitted. (LCvR 7(h)(1))

docs.x: D.D.C.. Confer before every nondispositive motion. Confer with opposing counsel before filing any nondispositive motion. The motion must state that the conference happened and whether the motion is opposed. (LCvR 7(m))

docs.x: D.D.C.. Every motion and opposition needs a proposed order. Each motion and each opposition comes with a proposed order. A motion without one can be rejected. (LCvR 7(c))

docs.t: D.D.C. — Failure to oppose can concede the motion
docs.x: D.D.C.. Failure to oppose can concede the motion. If the opposition isn’t filed within the time allowed, the court may treat the motion as conceded. (LCvR 7(b))

docs.t: D. Alaska — Page limits: 20 pages, or 5,700 words
docs.x: D. Alaska. Page limits: 20 pages, or 5,700 words. Motion and opposition memoranda can’t exceed 20 pages or 5,700 words, and replies can’t exceed 10 pages or 2,750 words. Rule 12(b), 12(c), and 56 motions get 35 pages or 10,000 words, with 20 pages or 5,700 words for replies. Captions and tables don’t count. (L.Civ.R. 7.4(a)(2))

docs.t: D. Alaska — Proposed orders on nondispositive motions
docs.x: D. Alaska. Proposed orders on nondispositive motions. Lodge a proposed order with every nondispositive motion and with every opposition to one. Dispositive motions under Rules 12 and 56 don’t need one. (L.Civ.R. 7.1(b)(2))

docs.t: D. Alaska — Oral argument must be requested on the filing
docs.x: D. Alaska. Oral argument must be requested on the filing. Write “Oral Argument Requested” under the title of the motion or response, or file a separate request within 5 days of the last filing. Oral argument is discretionary. (L.Civ.R. 7.1(f))

docs.t: D. Alaska — Non-dispositive motions not answered may be summarily decided
docs.x: D. Alaska. Non-dispositive motions not answered may be summarily decided. Failing to respond to a nondispositive motion can lead to a summary ruling, and the court may treat it as an admission that the motion is well taken. (L.Civ.R. 7.1(h))

docs.t: D. Alaska — Reconsideration is limited to 5 pages, and only for specific reasons
docs.x: D. Alaska. Reconsideration is limited to 5 pages, and only for specific reasons. The court ordinarily denies reconsideration unless there’s manifest error, new facts, or a change in law. Motions are capped at 5 pages and due 7 days after the order (or 14 days after new facts or a change in law). (L.Civ.R. 7.3(h))

docs.t: D. Alaska — Sealing needs leave and a sealed declaration
docs.x: D. Alaska. Sealing needs leave and a sealed declaration. Don’t file under seal without leave. The sealing motion is docketed publicly, and its supporting declaration is filed under seal and must state the basis, the related filings, and why redaction isn’t practicable. (L.Civ.R. 7.3(f))

docs.t: D. Kan. — Register by June 30 every year, $25
docs.x: D. Kan.. Register by June 30 every year, $25. Complete annual registration on the online portal and pay the annual fee by June 30. Registration certifies your CLE hours and that you’ve read the local rules. Payment on or after July 1 adds a $100 late fee before reinstatement. Pro hac vice lawyers and court employees are exempt, and a lawyer admitted after January 1 isn’t charged for the first period. The fee is $25 per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. (D. Kan. Rule 83.5.3)

docs.t: D. Kan. — Page limits: 15, but 10 for discovery and 40 for summary judgment
docs.x: D. Kan.. Page limits: 15, but 10 for discovery and 40 for summary judgment. Most briefs run 15 pages with 5-page replies. Discovery-related briefs run 10 with 3-page replies, and summary judgment and class certification briefs run 40 with 15-page replies. A motion to exceed them is due at least 3 days before the brief. (D. Kan. Rule 7.1(d))

docs.t: D. Kan. — Response clocks depend on the motion
docs.x: D. Kan.. Response clocks depend on the motion. Dispositive-type motions get 21 days to respond and 14 to reply. Everything else gets 14 and 7. A late response means the motion is decided as uncontested and ordinarily granted (Rule 7.1(c)). (D. Kan. Rule 6.1(d))

docs.t: D. Kan. — Call the judge before a discovery motion
docs.x: D. Kan.. Call the judge before a discovery motion. After a real conversation to confer, which a letter or email doesn’t satisfy, arrange a telephone conference with the judge and opposing counsel. Don’t file or submit the dispute beforehand unless the court asks. (D. Kan. Rule 37.1(a), 37.2)

docs.t: D. Kan. — Discovery motions are due in 30 days
docs.x: D. Kan.. Discovery motions are due in 30 days. File within 30 days of the default or of the response, objection, or disclosure at issue, or the court may deny it as untimely unless you show diligence. (D. Kan. Rule 37.1(c))

docs.t: D. Kan. — Extension motions: 3 days ahead, with specifics
docs.x: D. Kan.. Extension motions: 3 days ahead, with specifics. File at least 3 days before the deadline, stating consultation and views, when the act was first due, prior extensions, and cause. Stipulations that move discovery, hearing, pretrial, or trial dates need court approval and good cause. (D. Kan. Rule 6.1(a), (c))

docs.t: D. Kan. — Pro hac vice counsel can’t e-file
docs.x: D. Kan.. Pro hac vice counsel can’t e-file. Local counsel moves for admission, you pay $50 per case, and local counsel signs every filing and participates meaningfully. Pro hac vice attorneys can’t file electronically unless they work for the United States. (D. Kan. Rule 5.4.1(b), 83.5.4)

docs.t: D. Kan. — Sealing runs on a short clock
docs.x: D. Kan.. Sealing runs on a short clock. A provisional sealed filing is followed by a notice of proposed sealed record. A motion to seal is due 7 days later, a response in 3, and a reply in 1. Stipulations alone don’t justify sealing, and a missed deadline waives the claim. (D. Kan. Rule 5.4.2)

docs.t: D. Kan. — Summary judgment facts are numbered, and deemed admitted
docs.x: D. Kan.. Summary judgment facts are numbered, and deemed admitted. The brief opens with numbered material facts with record cites. Facts not specifically controverted are deemed admitted, for the movant and for the opponent’s added facts alike. (D. Kan. Rule 56.1)

docs.t: D.N.M. — Federal Bar dues every odd-numbered year
docs.x: D.N.M.. Federal Bar dues every odd-numbered year. Federal Bar dues are payable by January 31 of every odd-numbered year, so the next due date is January 31, 2027. A delinquent member can’t practice here. The FJC’s 2024 compilation lists the dues as $25 every two years. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 83.2(h))

docs.t: D.N.M. — Ask for concurrence in good faith
docs.x: D.N.M.. Ask for concurrence in good faith. The movant must find out whether a motion is opposed. A motion that omits a good-faith request for concurrence may be summarily denied. Pro se inmate cases are the exception. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 7.1(a))

docs.t: D.N.M. — Silence means consent
docs.x: D.N.M.. Silence means consent. Failing to file and serve a response within the time allowed constitutes consent to grant the motion. Failing to reply means briefing is complete. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 7.1(b))

docs.t: D.N.M. — Challenge discovery objections in 21 days
docs.x: D.N.M.. Challenge discovery objections in 21 days. After an objection to an interrogatory, request for production, or request for admission, proceed under Rule 37.1 within 21 days of service (or 21 days after the production) or the objection is accepted. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 26.6)

docs.t: D.N.M. — Page limits: 27, 24, and 12
docs.x: D.N.M.. Page limits: 27, 24, and 12. A motion with its supporting brief gets 27 pages, a response 24, and a reply 12. All exhibits together may not exceed 50 pages unless every party agrees or the court allows it. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 7.5, 10.5)

docs.t: D.N.M. — Decided on the briefs, then say it’s ready
docs.x: D.N.M.. Decided on the briefs, then say it’s ready. Absent an order, motions are decided without a hearing. When briefing ends, the movant files a notice certifying the motion is ready for decision and listing every related filing. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 7.6, 7.4(e))

docs.t: D.N.M. — Costs and fees are waived after 30 days
docs.x: D.N.M.. Costs and fees are waived after 30 days. A motion to tax costs and a motion for attorney’s fees (outside the EAJA) are each due within 30 days of entry of judgment. Missing either waives the claim. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 54.1, 54.5)

docs.t: D.N.M. — Scheduling dates move only for good cause
docs.x: D.N.M.. Scheduling dates move only for good cause. Changing any scheduling-order deadline, opposed or not, takes good cause and the court’s approval. Briefing extensions can’t interfere with those deadlines, and a trial continuance needs good cause. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 16.1, 7.2, 40.1)

docs.t: D.N.M. — No limited appearances; join or associate
docs.x: D.N.M.. No limited appearances; join or associate. An out-of-district lawyer appears by associating a Federal Bar member and paying $100 per case, or by applying for admission. A limited appearance is allowed only by court order. (D.N.M.LR-Civ. 83.3, 83.4(c))

docs.x: D.N.M.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: D. Colo. — Pay the $60 renewal fee every two years: this period runs October 1 to December 31, 2026
docs.x: D. Colo.. Pay the $60 renewal fee every two years: this period runs October 1 to December 31, 2026. The court’s attorney information page confirms a $60 biennial renewal fee collected every even year from October 1 to December 31, and says the next period is October 1 to December 31, 2026, which is open now. Attorneys who don’t pay are removed from the roll and can’t e-file here. Federal agency lawyers pay no admission or renewal fees. The rulebook’s language about administrative suspension for an unpaid annual fee concerns your state license. (D.C.COLO.LAttyR; clerk’s attorney information page)

docs.t: D. Colo. — Confer before you file, with exceptions
docs.x: D. Colo.. Confer before you file, with exceptions. Describe your specific efforts to confer in the motion or in an attached certificate. The duty doesn’t apply to Rule 12 motions, Rule 56 motions, motions in prisoner or detainee cases, or motions under LAttyR 5(a) and (b). (D.C.COLO.LCivR 7.1(a), (b))

docs.t: D. Colo. — No motion inside a response or reply
docs.x: D. Colo.. No motion inside a response or reply. A motion is always a separate document. A cross-motion for summary judgment is also filed separately. (D.C.COLO.LCivR 7.1(d))

docs.t: D. Colo. — Responses 21 days, replies 14
docs.x: D. Colo.. Responses 21 days, replies 14. The response is due 21 days after service and the reply 14 days after service of the response, for ordinary and summary judgment motions alike, unless the court allows otherwise. The local rules set no page limits. (D.C.COLO.LCivR 7.1(d), 56.1(a))

docs.t: D. Colo. — One stipulated extension, no order needed
docs.x: D. Colo.. One stipulated extension, no order needed. The parties may stipulate once to an extension of up to 21 days to respond to a pleading or written discovery. File it before the deadline and it takes effect on filing. Any other extension needs a motion and an order. (D.C.COLO.LCivR 6.1(a))

docs.t: D. Colo. — Filing day ends at 11:59:59 p.m. Mountain
docs.x: D. Colo.. Filing day ends at 11:59:59 p.m. Mountain. Electronic filings are due by 11:59:59 p.m. Mountain Time. Paper filings must reach the clerk between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Mountain Time, Monday through Friday. (D.C.COLO.LCivR 77.1)

docs.t: D. Colo. — Restricting access takes a public motion
docs.x: D. Colo.. Restricting access takes a public motion. A motion to restrict is itself public and must show a serious, clearly defined injury and why no alternative will do. A stipulation or stipulated protective order alone isn’t enough. Anyone may object within 3 court business days after notice is posted. (D.C.COLO.LCivR 7.2)

docs.t: D. Colo. — No pro hac vice; join the bar
docs.x: D. Colo.. No pro hac vice; join the bar. Only an unrepresented party or a member of this court’s bar may appear, sign, or take part in a deposition, hearing, or trial. Local counsel isn’t required, but we recommend a local attorney. (D.C.COLO.LAttyR 3, 5(a)(5))

docs.t: D. Colo. — Verbose filings can be stricken
docs.x: D. Colo.. Verbose filings can be stricken. Motions, responses, and replies must be concise. A verbose, redundant, or unintelligible one may be stricken or returned, and may lead to sanctions. (D.C.COLO.LCivR 7.1(i))

docs.x: E.D. Pa.. Every motion and response needs a proposed order. Each motion comes with a form of order granting the relief. Each response in opposition comes with a form of order denying or amending it. (Local Civ. R. 7.1(a))

docs.x: E.D. Pa.. 14 days to oppose, or the motion may be granted as uncontested. docs.t: N.D. Ill. — 15 pages, and a table of contents past that
docs.x: N.D. Ill.. 15 pages, and a table of contents past that. Neither a motion nor a brief supporting or opposing one, nor objections to a magistrate judge’s report, can exceed 15 pages without prior approval. A longer brief needs a table of contents with page numbers and a table of cases. A noncompliant filing can be stricken. (LR 7.1)

docs.t: N.D. Ill. — Check the judge’s own procedures first
docs.x: N.D. Ill.. Check the judge’s own procedures first. Each judge’s page on the court’s website sets how motions are filed and presented. A judge may require a notice of presentment, with a date no more than 14 days after the motion is delivered. (LR 5.3(a)–(b))

docs.t: N.D. Ill. — Discovery motions need a call or meeting first
docs.x: N.D. Ill.. Discovery motions need a call or meeting first. The court refuses to hear a discovery motion unless it states that, after consulting in person or by telephone and trying in good faith, the parties couldn’t agree, or that the other side wouldn’t confer. Recite the date, time, and place and who took part. (LR 37.2)

docs.t: N.D. Ill. — Summary judgment runs on numbered fact statements
docs.x: N.D. Ill.. Summary judgment runs on numbered fact statements. The movant files a memorandum and a statement of material facts, capped at 80 numbered paragraphs, with the evidence attached. An opponent’s statement of additional facts is capped at 40. Going over needs the court’s permission. (LR 56.1(a), (d))

docs.t: N.D. Ill. — Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted
docs.x: N.D. Ill.. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. To dispute a fact, cite specific evidence that contradicts it and explain how. Asserted facts may be deemed admitted if you don’t. (LR 56.1(e)(3))

docs.t: N.D. Ill. — Missing a brief doesn’t waive the motion, but missing a reply does
docs.x: N.D. Ill.. Missing a brief doesn’t waive the motion, but missing a reply does. If a memorandum isn’t filed, the court can strike the motion or grant it without a hearing. A reply that isn’t filed on time is waived. (LR 78.3)

docs.t: N.D. Ill. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: N.D. Ill.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: E.D. Wis. — No pro hac vice; join the bar
docs.x: E.D. Wis.. No pro hac vice; join the bar. The court doesn’t allow pro hac vice motions. A lawyer licensed and in good standing before any U.S. court or a state’s highest court, or D.C., applies for full admission through PACER. The court may require a nonresident lawyer to get local counsel at any time. (General L.R. 83(c)(2)(E))

docs.t: E.D. Wis. — 30 pages, 15 for replies, and ask before you file long
docs.x: E.D. Wis.. 30 pages, 15 for replies, and ask before you file long. The principal memorandum can’t exceed 30 pages and the reply 15, excluding the caption, tables, and signature block. An oversized memorandum is filed only if the court granted leave beforehand. (Civil L.R. 7(f))

docs.t: E.D. Wis. — Responses 21 days, replies 14
docs.x: E.D. Wis.. Responses 21 days, replies 14. For motions other than summary judgment and expedited motions, the response is due within 21 days of service and the reply within 14 days of the response. If you don’t respond, the court may decide the motion without your input. (Civil L.R. 7(b), (c))

docs.t: E.D. Wis. — Every motion cites its rule and brings a brief or a certificate
docs.x: E.D. Wis.. Every motion cites its rule and brings a brief or a certificate. A motion must state the statute or rule it rests on and come with a supporting memorandum, with affidavits or declarations if needed, or a certificate that no memorandum will be filed. (Civil L.R. 7(a))

docs.t: E.D. Wis. — Summary judgment: capped fact statements
docs.x: E.D. Wis.. Summary judgment: capped fact statements. The movant files a memorandum and a statement of proposed material facts, capped at 150 numbered paragraphs, each with record citations. Failing to submit the statement is grounds for denial. An opponent gets 100 additional facts. (Civil L.R. 56(b))

docs.t: E.D. Wis. — Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted
docs.x: E.D. Wis.. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. The court deems uncontroverted statements of material fact admitted, for deciding summary judgment only. Cite to the numbered paragraphs in your memoranda. (Civil L.R. 56(b)(4))

docs.t: E.D. Wis. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time

docs.x: E.D. Wis.. Opposing summary judgment: 30 days, reply 14,Civil L.R. 56(b)(2)–(3),The opposition, with a response to each numbered fact, is due within 30 days of service. docs.t: M.D. Pa. — Every motion needs a concurrence certificate and a proposed order
docs.x: M.D. Pa.. Every motion needs a concurrence certificate and a proposed order. A motion must be written, with a certification that you sought concurrence from each party and that it was given or denied. It also needs a form of order granting the relief. Pro se prisoner cases are exempt from seeking concurrence, but discovery motions still need the LR 26.3 conference. (LR 7.1)

docs.t: M.D. Pa. — Brief within 14 days of the motion, or the motion is deemed withdrawn
docs.x: M.D. Pa.. Brief within 14 days of the motion, or the motion is deemed withdrawn. File the supporting brief within 14 days after the motion. A protective-order motion needs its brief filed with it. No brief is needed for a motion to extend time with the reasons stated, a motion everyone concurs in, or a motion to appoint counsel. (LR 7.5)

docs.t: M.D. Pa. — Oppose within 14 days of the brief, or you’re deemed not to oppose
docs.x: M.D. Pa.. Oppose within 14 days of the brief, or you’re deemed not to oppose. The opposing brief is due 14 days after service of the movant’s brief, or 7 days after service of the motion if no brief is required. A party who doesn’t comply is deemed not to oppose. Summary judgment gets 21 days. (LR 7.6)

docs.t: M.D. Pa. — One reply, 14 days, and nothing more without leave
docs.x: M.D. Pa.. One reply, 14 days, and nothing more without leave. The movant may reply within 14 days after service of the opposing brief. No further briefs may be filed without leave of court. (LR 7.7)

docs.t: M.D. Pa. — 15 pages, or 5,000 words with a certificate
docs.x: M.D. Pa.. 15 pages, or 5,000 words with a certificate. A brief can’t exceed 15 pages. It may run longer up to 5,000 words if it includes a certificate stating the actual word count. Anything beyond that needs prior authorization, requested by motion at least 2 working days before the brief is due. (LR 7.8(b))

docs.t: M.D. Pa. — Summary judgment: separate numbered facts, and unanswered facts are admitted
docs.x: M.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: separate numbered facts, and unanswered facts are admitted. The motion comes with a separate, short statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs with record citations. The opposition responds paragraph by paragraph. Every fact the movant states is deemed admitted unless the opponent controverts it. (LR 56.1)

docs.t: M.D. Pa. — Filing deadline: midnight Eastern
docs.x: M.D. Pa.. Filing deadline: midnight Eastern. Electronic filing must be completed before midnight Eastern time to be timely that day. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (M.D. Pa. ECF Policies and Procedures)

docs.x: M.D. Pa. formatting. Pro hac vice petition: The court’s form through CM/ECF; $50 (LR 83.8.2.1)

docs.x: M.D. Pa. deadline. Opposition brief: 14 days after service of the movant’s brief (L.R. LR 7.6)

docs.x: M.D. Pa. deadline. Opposition if no brief is required: 7 days after service of the motion (L.R. LR 7.6)

docs.x: M.D. Pa. deadline. Opposition to summary judgment: 21 days after service of the movant’s brief (L.R. LR 7.6)

docs.x: M.D. Pa. deadline. Reply brief: 14 days after service of the opposition (L.R. LR 7.7)

docs.x: M.D. Pa. deadline. Reconsideration: 14 days after the order (L.R. LR 7.10)

docs.x: M.D. Pa. deadline. Appeal of a magistrate judge’s non-dispositive order: 14 days after the order (L.R. LR 72.2)

docs.x: M.D. Pa. deadline. Close of discovery, absent an order: 6 months after the party’s last pleading (L.R. LR 26.4)

docs.x: M.D. Pa.. Long briefs need tables,LR 7.8(a),A brief over 15 pages needs a table of contents with page references and a table of citations. docs.t: W.D. Pa. — Every motion needs a proposed order
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. Every motion needs a proposed order. All motions must be accompanied by a proposed order. The clerk sends back filings that lack one, including motions for pro hac vice admission. (LCvR 7(D))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — The assigned judge’s posted practices are part of the rules
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. The assigned judge’s posted practices are part of the rules. Motions must comply with the Federal Rules, the Local Rules, the assigned judge’s orders, and the judge’s practices and procedures posted on the court’s website. Check the judge’s page before you file. (LCvR 7(A))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — Discovery motions and motions in limine have their own rules
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. Discovery motions and motions in limine have their own rules. A discovery motion must follow LCvR 37.1 and 37.2, which haven’t been reviewed for this page. A motion in limine must follow LCvR 16.1.C.4: confer with all counsel first, and attach a Motion in Limine Certificate if you can’t agree. (LCvR 7(C))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — Summary judgment: a separate numbered statement of facts and an appendix
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: a separate numbered statement of facts and an appendix. The motion states its grounds succinctly without argument. It comes with a separately filed concise statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs, each citing the record, a supporting memorandum, and an appendix of the documents referenced. (LCvR 56(B))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — Opposition in 30 days, with a response to each numbered fact
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. Opposition in 30 days, with a response to each numbered fact. The opposing party has 30 days from service. It files a responsive statement that admits or denies each paragraph, gives the basis and record reference for each denial, and adds its own numbered facts, plus a memorandum and appendix. (LCvR 56(C))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — Facts you don’t specifically deny are admitted
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. Facts you don’t specifically deny are admitted. Facts in either side’s concise statement that are claimed to be undisputed are deemed admitted for the motion unless specifically denied or otherwise controverted by a separate concise statement. (LCvR 56(E))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — The Rule 26(f) report comes before the first conference
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. The Rule 26(f) report comes before the first conference. Within 30 days after a defendant appears, the court enters an order setting the initial scheduling conference and the dates to confer and file the Rule 26(f) Report. The Report must follow the court’s form, Appendix LCvR 16.1.A, whose own instructions ask that it be filed at least 21 days before the conference. The conference takes place within the earlier of 90 days after any defendant is served or 60 days after any defendant appears. (LCvR 16.1(A)(2))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — ADR is mandatory in almost every case
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. ADR is mandatory in almost every case. Parties must use mediation, early neutral evaluation, or arbitration, except in Social Security and prisoner cases. They choose a process and a time frame in the Rule 26(f) Report and file a Stipulation Selecting ADR Process with it. (LCvR 16.2)

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — A motion to modify the schedule needs a certificate
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. A motion to modify the schedule needs a certificate. Confer with all counsel first. Unless every party joins the motion, attach a Scheduling Motion Certificate saying that the parties conferred and whether all of them consent. (LCvR 16.1(B)(5))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — Evidence left out of your pretrial statement can be excluded
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. Evidence left out of your pretrial statement can be excluded. If you fail to fully disclose the substance of the evidence you plan to offer, in your pretrial statement or at or before the final pretrial conference as the court permits, it may be excluded at trial. Impeachment evidence is the only exception. (LCvR 16.1(C)(7))

docs.t: W.D. Pa. — Filing deadline: midnight Eastern
docs.x: W.D. Pa.. Filing deadline: midnight Eastern. Electronic filing must be completed before midnight Eastern time to be timely that day. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (W.D. Pa. ECF Policies and Procedures)

docs.t: N.D. Ala. — Renewal fee every five years, due January 1
docs.x: N.D. Ala.. Renewal fee every five years, due January 1. Each January 1, members whose status hasn’t been renewed in the preceding five years must file a statement of eligibility with the court’s renewal fee. If you don’t within 60 days of the due date, you cease to be a member in good standing until you do. The fee is $50 (FJC 2024). (N.D. Ala. LR 83.1(a)(2))

docs.t: N.D. Ala. — Your judge’s initial order is the motion rule
docs.x: N.D. Ala.. Your judge’s initial order is the motion rule. The Local Rules don’t set briefing deadlines or page limits. Each judge’s initial order does, and many follow the court’s Uniform Initial Order. Read the order the day it is entered. (Judges’ initial orders)

docs.t: N.D. Ala. — Summary judgment runs on Appendix II
docs.x: N.D. Ala.. Summary judgment runs on Appendix II. Summary judgment motions follow Appendix II of the judge’s initial order. Under the typical order, the opposition is due 21 days after the motion is filed, with briefs of 30 pages and replies of 15. (Appendix II to the initial orders)

docs.t: N.D. Ala. — Other motions: put the argument in the motion
docs.x: N.D. Ala.. Other motions: put the argument in the motion. For motions other than summary judgment, the typical order wants the argument in the motion itself, and some judges discourage separate briefs. Briefs run 15 pages, and replies 10. (Judges’ initial orders)

docs.t: N.D. Ala. — You can’t appear until pro hac vice is approved
docs.x: N.D. Ala.. You can’t appear until pro hac vice is approved. A non-resident lawyer may not appear until a judge approves the pro hac vice application. Designated local counsel files a notice of appearance within 10 days after approval. (LR 83.1(b))

docs.x: M.D. Ala.. No local motion-briefing rule: your judge sets it. The Local Rules have no general motion rule. Each judge posts practices and procedures, scheduling orders, and Rule 26 orders on the court’s website. Read your judge’s before you file. (Local Rules; judge pages)

docs.t: M.D. Ala. — Every party files a conflict disclosure statement
docs.x: M.D. Ala.. Every party files a conflict disclosure statement. All parties and amici, including individuals and government entities, file a Conflict Disclosure Statement with their first filing. If that is impracticable, file within 7 days. List parents, subsidiaries, partners, LLC members and managers, trustees, and affiliates. (LR 7.1)

docs.t: M.D. Ala. — No letter briefs or letter motions
docs.x: M.D. Ala.. No letter briefs or letter motions. The court won’t consider letter motions, letter briefs, or “supplemental information” sent by letter. Every request must be filed properly. (LR 5.7)

docs.t: M.D. Ala. — Discovery motions quote the discovery
docs.x: M.D. Ala.. Discovery motions quote the discovery. A discovery motion must quote verbatim each interrogatory, request, answer, response, and objection at issue, or attach the actual discovery document. (LR 37.1)

docs.t: M.D. Ala. — Bill of costs: 35 days or waived
docs.x: M.D. Ala.. Bill of costs: 35 days or waived. File the request for taxation of costs within 35 days after entry of final judgment. Missing the deadline is deemed a waiver. (LR 54.1(a))

docs.t: M.D. Ala. — Settling before trial? Tell the clerk a business day ahead
docs.x: M.D. Ala.. Settling before trial? Tell the clerk a business day ahead. Notify the clerk’s office at least one full business day before jury selection or trial. Otherwise juror costs are assessed against the parties and counsel. (LR 54.2)

docs.t: M.D. Ala. — Rules give way to your judge’s order, and violations draw sanctions
docs.x: M.D. Ala.. Rules give way to your judge’s order, and violations draw sanctions. Any judge can suspend the local rules in a case, and an order that conflicts with them suspends them in that case to that extent. General and standing orders can also change them. A violation of any local rule can be sanctioned in the assigned judge’s discretion, so read your judge’s scheduling order first. (LR 1.1(d), (e); 1.2)

docs.t: M.D. Ala. — Apply for pro hac vice with your first filing
docs.x: M.D. Ala.. Apply for pro hac vice with your first filing. A lawyer admitted to the federal district court where the lawyer lives or practices may be admitted pro hac vice by any district judge, magistrate judge, or bankruptcy judge. Attach that court’s certificate of good standing, and apply when you file your first paper, not after. No local counsel is required. (LR 83.1(b))

docs.t: M.D. Ala. — Never contact jurors without a motion
docs.x: M.D. Ala.. Never contact jurors without a motion. Neither you nor anyone acting for you may contact jurors to ask what they thought, or give a juror’s identifying information to a non-party, without a formal motion and the court’s permission. Questionnaire information stays confidential, and every copy must be destroyed when the jury is empaneled. (LR 47.1)

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — Rule 12(b) and 56 motions need a brief
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. Rule 12(b) and 56 motions need a brief. A Rule 12(b) or Rule 56 motion must be supported by a brief, filed with the motion. Failing to file one is sufficient cause to deny the motion. (Civil L.R. 7(b))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — 14 days to oppose, or the motion may be granted
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. 14 days to oppose, or the motion may be granted. Unless the court orders otherwise, oppose any motion other than summary judgment within 14 days of service. Failing to oppose a motion other than a Rule 12(b) or 56 motion may be sufficient cause to grant it. (Civil L.R. 7(c))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — Replies in 7 days
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. Replies in 7 days. A reply on any motion other than summary judgment is due within 7 days of service of the response. (Civil L.R. 7(d))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — 30 pages, 15 for replies, and ask first
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. 30 pages, 15 for replies, and ask first. Principal briefs can’t exceed 30 pages and replies 15. A longer brief may be filed only if the court granted leave beforehand. (Civil L.R. 7(e))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — Summary judgment: facts go in the brief
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. Summary judgment: facts go in the brief. There is no separate statement of facts. The brief states every fact with a pinpoint record citation. No other supporting documents are allowed without an order. (Civil L.R. 56(a), (b))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — Summary judgment clocks: 28 days, then 14
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. Summary judgment clocks: 28 days, then 14. The opposition is due 28 days after service of the motion, and the reply 14 days after the response. Uncontroverted material facts are deemed admitted for the motion. (Civil L.R. 56(b), (c))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — 12-point type, one-inch margins, nothing in the margins
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. 12-point type, one-inch margins, nothing in the margins. Text is double-spaced in a plain Roman font of 12 points or larger, footnotes included. Case names are italicized or underlined, and margins are at least one inch on all four sides. Page numbers may sit in a margin, but no text or footnote may. (General L.R. 5(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — Costs: 14 days, verified
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. Costs: 14 days, verified. File a verified bill of costs on the clerk’s form within 14 days after judgment, or within 14 days after a timely Rule 50(b) or 59 motion is resolved. Objections are due in 14 days, your response in 7, and a motion to review the clerk’s taxation in 7 more. An appeal doesn’t extend any of it. (Civil L.R. 54(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — Seal the whole document or nothing
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. Seal the whole document or nothing. Only an entire document can be sealed, never part of one. File an unsealed motion with a generic description, why alternatives won’t work, and the duration, attach a proposed unsealed order, and file the document in camera under seal. Absent an order, sealed documents open after 120 days. (General L.R. 5.2)

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — Discovery: 25 interrogatories, and quote the request
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. Discovery: 25 interrogatories, and quote the request. Interrogatories are capped at 25 including subparts, but questions asking who has knowledge or where documents are don’t count. The court won’t compel answers to an excess set. Every answer or objection to an interrogatory, production request, or admission request must reproduce the request. (Civil L.R. 33, 34, 36)

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — The joint pretrial document is due a week before the conference
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. The joint pretrial document is due a week before the conference. Missing it can bring dismissal or default. (Civil L.R. 16(c))

docs.t: S.D. Ala. — overview
docs.x: S.D. Ala.. Say what rule you’re moving under,Civil L.R. 7(a),Every motion must state the statute, rule, or principle it is made under. Big exhibits need a courtesy copy,Civil L.R. 7(g),If exhibits exceed 50 pages in total, send chambers a courtesy copy printed from PACER, so the ECF headers appear on every page. Unreported opinions are fine to cite,Civil L.R. 7(f),You may cite them. If one isn’t in a public database, file and serve a copy. Supplemental authority: two pages, no argument,Civil L.R. 7(f)(3),Notify the court of new authority in two pages or fewer, tied to a page of a brief or an oral point, without new argument. Oral argument must be justified,Civil L.R. 7(h),Requests must give specific reasons. Argument usually runs 30 minutes. Declaratory or injunctive summary judgment needs a proposed judgment,Civil L.R. 56(a),A movant seeking non-monetary relief files a proposed judgment

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — Silence means no opposition
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. Silence means no opposition. Respond within 14 days, or 21 for summary judgment. Failing to respond indicates there is no opposition. (LR 7.1(B))

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — Most motions are due within 30 days after discovery opens
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. Most motions are due within 30 days after discovery opens. Unless a specific rule sets another time, motions must be filed within 30 days after discovery begins, absent the court’s permission. (LR 7.1(A)(2))

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — The font rule is strict
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. The font rule is strict. Times New Roman 14, Courier New 12, Century Schoolbook 13, or Book Antiqua 13. Certify the font at the end of every brief. Briefs run 25 pages, replies 15. (LR 5.1(C), 7.1(D))

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — Reconsideration is not routine
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. Reconsideration is not routine. File only if absolutely necessary, within 28 days. You can’t move to reconsider the denial of a reconsideration motion. (LR 7.2(E))

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — Local counsel signs everything
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. Local counsel signs everything. Local counsel files the pro hac vice application and signs all papers. You can’t appear until admitted. (LR 83.1(B))

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — Summary judgment needs separate numbered statements
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. Summary judgment needs separate numbered statements. The movant files a separate, concise, numbered statement of material facts with record citations. The court won’t consider a fact without an evidence cite, cited only to a pleading, stated as an issue or legal conclusion, or set out only in the brief. The respondent answers each number, and any fact not properly disputed is deemed admitted. File within 30 days after discovery closes. (LR 56.1(B))

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — The pretrial order is due 30 days after discovery
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. The pretrial order is due 30 days after discovery. File the signed, consolidated pretrial order on the court’s form within 30 days after discovery closes or the summary judgment ruling, whichever is later. It replaces the Rule 26(a)(3) disclosures, and no more motions to compel are allowed after it is filed. Objections to exhibits not stated there are waived, and Daubert motions are due by then too. (LR 16.4)

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — No continuances by stipulation, and late settlements cost jurors
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. No continuances by stipulation, and late settlements cost jurors. A continuance takes exceptional circumstances and an order, never a stipulation alone. If a jury case settles, notify the courtroom deputy and the Jury Section at least one full business day before trial, or juror costs for a day are assessed equally against the parties and their counsel. (LR 39.5, 39.2)

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — You must be admitted to bill or sign, not just to appear
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. You must be admitted to bill or sign, not just to appear. A lawyer who will appear, sign a filing, apply for fees, or substantially participate in a case must be admitted, either as a member or pro hac vice. A firm’s other lawyers need not be admitted if admitted lawyers who appeared are directing their work. (LR 83.1(B)(1))

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

docs.t: N.D. Ga. — overview
docs.x: N.D. Ga.. Discovery starts 30 days after the first answer,LR 26.2(A),Tracks run zero, four, or eight months. Extending discovery is hard,LR 26.2(B),Move before it expires. It’s granted only in exceptional cases. Daubert motions have a deadline,LR 26.2(C),File by the date the proposed pretrial order is submitted, or the objection is waived. Motions to compel,LR 37.1,Quote each request verbatim. File before discovery closes or within 14 days after the response. Meet in person early,LR 16.1, 16.2,Lead counsel confer in person within 16 days after a defendant appears. The Joint Preliminary Report is due within 30 days after the first appearance. No letters to the judge,LR 7.4,Requests for rulings, including extensions, go by motion. Certificate of interested persons,LR 3.3,File it at first appearance. Diversity cases list everyone whose citizenship is attributed to the party. Judge’s initial

docs.t: D. Md. — Renew every six years, $75
docs.x: D. Md.. Renew every six years, $75. Membership must be renewed periodically, which the court’s fee schedule sets at every six years for $75, per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. We haven’t read this rule, so confirm with the clerk. (D. Md. Local Rule 701(2)(b); FJC 2024)

docs.t: D. Md. — Motions to compel are served, not filed
docs.x: D. Md.. Motions to compel are served, not filed. Serve the motion within 30 days of receiving the responses. Briefing is served, 14 and 14. Only after a failed conference do you file the certificate with all the papers. (L.R. 104.8)

docs.t: D. Md. — Email isn’t conferring
docs.x: D. Md.. Email isn’t conferring. A reasonable effort means meeting in person, by video, or by phone. The court won’t consider a discovery motion without a certificate of conference. (L.R. 104.7)

docs.t: D. Md. — Fees: 14 days, then 35, or waived
docs.x: D. Md.. Fees: 14 days, then 35, or waived. Move for fees within 14 days of judgment. The supporting memorandum is due 35 days after the motion. Missing either deadline waives the claim. (L.R. 109.2.a)

docs.t: D. Md. — Appendix B governs fee petitions
docs.x: D. Md.. Appendix B governs fee petitions. Time records go in litigation-phase format. Travel over 2 hours each way is billed at half rate. The 2025 amendments replace the rate table with the Fitzpatrick Matrix less 5% to 20%. (L.R. 109.2.b; Appendix B)

docs.t: E.D. Ark. — Silence on a nondispositive motion is consent
docs.x: E.D. Ark.. Silence on a nondispositive motion is consent. Failing to timely respond to a nondispositive motion is enough, without more, to grant it. (Local Rule 7.2(f))

docs.t: E.D. Ark. — Summary judgment needs a separate fact statement

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Briefs: FRAP’s lengths apply
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Briefs: FRAP’s lengths apply. The First Circuit’s local rules don’t change the length limits, so a principal brief is 13,000 words (30 pages) and a reply 6,500 (15 pages). A motion to file an oversized opening brief must be filed at least 10 days before the due date, an oversized reply at least 7 days, and each must state the length sought and be supported by a detailed statement of grounds. The court grants them only for compelling reasons. (FRAP 32(a)(7); 1st Cir. R. 32.4)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — 14-point type
docs.x: 1st Cir.. 14-point type. FRAP 32(a)(5) requires a proportionally spaced serif face of 14 points or larger. (FRAP 32(a)(5))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Briefing dates follow FRAP 31(a)
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Briefing dates follow FRAP 31(a). Schedules are set once the record, including any transcripts, is complete. The appellant has 40 days, the appellee 30, and the reply 21 and at least 7 days before argument. A reply may be rejected if it repeats the main brief or contains matter that belonged in it. Unavailability of a transcript is cause for an extension, subject to the 14-day transcript-ordering rule. (1st Cir. R. 31.0(a))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — The appellant’s brief carries a bound addendum
docs.x: 1st Cir.. The appellant’s brief carries a bound addendum. The addendum goes at the rear of the appellant’s brief with a table of contents. It must include the judgments, rulings, or orders appealed from with their supporting explanation, and the lower-level decision if the court below was reviewing one, such as a magistrate judge’s recommended decision or an ALJ’s initial decision. If the ruling is a text-only docket entry, include that docket page. It may also include up to 25 pages of record excerpts, not counting statutes and rules. The appellee may add an addendum for omitted material on the same terms. Sealed items, including presentence reports and statements of reasons, go in a separate sealed addendum. (1st Cir. R. 28.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Paper covers are color-coded
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Paper covers are color-coded. Appellant is blue, appellee red, intervenor or amicus green, and reply gray. In a cross-appeal the first brief is blue, the second red, the third yellow, and the fourth gray. (FRAP 32(a)(2); court checklist)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — File your appearance within 14 days
docs.x: 1st Cir.. File your appearance within 14 days. Counsel for both sides must file a notice of appearance within 14 days after the case opens. New or additional counsel can appear later, but not after the appellee’s brief is filed without leave. You can’t file pleadings until your appearance is on file. (LR 12.0(a))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Sealed material goes in paper, in its own volume
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Sealed material goes in paper, in its own volume. Briefs are public documents. Sealed or confidential material is filed in paper only, as a separate volume marked “SEALED,” with a motion for leave to file under seal. (LR 28.1; court checklist)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — File the docketing statement within 14 days, and pay the fee
docs.x: 1st Cir.. File the docketing statement within 14 days, and pay the fee. Within 14 days after docketing, the person taking the appeal submits a separate statement listing all parties, last known counsel, and their addresses and emails, on the clerk’s form, and serves it. The other side reports inaccuracies in writing within 14 days. If the appellant doesn’t pay the docket fee within 14 days of the notice of appeal, or misses the statement or another deadline, the appeal may be dismissed for want of diligent prosecution. (1st Cir. R. 3.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Order the transcript within 14 days; the court would rather you didn’t
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Order the transcript within 14 days; the court would rather you didn’t. Use the court’s Transcript Order/Report within 14 days of the notice of appeal, and CJA form 24 if the government pays. A late order can mean dismissal. The court thinks many cases don’t need transcripts and urges stipulations, but the 14-day rule isn’t suspended unless the court orders it for good cause. (1st Cir. R. 10.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Appearances: 14 days, and none after the appellee’s brief without leave
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Appearances: 14 days, and none after the appellee’s brief without leave. Both sides file the appearance form within 14 days after docketing. No lawyer may appear after the appellee’s brief is filed without leave. To file motions or briefs or argue, a lawyer must be admitted and have filed an appearance, and a member of a bar listed in FRAP 46(a) can have the appearance entered subject to applying for admission. No lawyer may withdraw without the court’s consent. (1st Cir. R. 12.0, 46.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Defaults dismiss the appellant and silence the appellee
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Defaults dismiss the appellant and silence the appellee. If the appellant defaults on the brief or required appendix, the clerk dismisses the appeal, and a motion to set it aside must be filed within 14 days showing special circumstances. A defaulting appellee won’t be heard at argument except by leave. (1st Cir. R. 45.0)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Sealing: paper motion, labeled, and think small
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Sealing: paper motion, labeled, and think small. Material sealed below stays sealed here. To seal anything else, file a paper motion explaining the basis and duration, stamp the item “FILED UNDER SEAL,” and don’t rely on agreement. Sealed material doesn’t go in the regular appendix but in a separate, sealed supplemental volume, and counsel should consider putting the sealed discussion in a separate supplemental filing. (1st Cir. R. 11.0(c), (d); 28.1)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Cite state cases twice, and don’t cite unpublished articles
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Cite state cases twice, and don’t cite unpublished articles. State or Commonwealth court citations must give both the official and the National Reporter citation when published in both. Law review articles unpublished when you file can’t be cited without permission. (1st Cir. R. 32.2)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Translations: Puerto Rico opinions need an English version
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Translations: Puerto Rico opinions need an English version. The court won’t receive non-English documents or cited opinions without translations, and an opinion of a Commonwealth of Puerto Rico court that doesn’t appear in English in the bound volumes needs an official, certified, or stipulated translation. Partial translations must be submitted at least 30 days before argument if only one side submits them. (1st Cir. R. 30.0(e))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Emergency motions: move promptly or risk denial
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Emergency motions: move promptly or risk denial. Motions for a stay or other emergency relief may be denied for failure to present them promptly. If you may need emergency action while the Clerk’s Office is closed, consult the Clerk’s Office at the earliest opportunity; failing to consult may delay action. (1st Cir. L.R. 27.0(b); FRAP 8, 27)

docs.t: 1st Cir. — Filing deadline: midnight Eastern (Boston)
docs.x: 1st Cir.. Filing deadline: midnight Eastern (Boston). For electronic filing in the court of appeals the day ends at midnight in the time zone of the circuit clerk’s office in Boston. (FRAP 26(a)(4)(B); 1st Cir. R. 25.0)

docs.x: 1st Cir. deadline. Paper copies of an accepted brief or appendix: Received within 7 days of the clerk’s acceptance notice (L.R. 1st Cir. R. 25.0(b)(3))

docs.x: 1st Cir. deadline. Docket fee: 14 days after the notice of appeal (L.R. 1st Cir. R. 3.0(b))

docs.x: 1st Cir. deadline. Motion to set aside a default dismissal: 14 days (L.R. 1st Cir. R. 45.0(a))

docs.t: 1st Cir. — overview
docs.x: 1st Cir.. You join the bar instead of appearing pro hac vice. Motions: 5,200 words,FRAP 27(d)(2),A motion or response runs 5,200 words or 20 pages. A reply runs 2,600 words or 10 pages. Motion clock: 10 days, then 7,FRAP 27(a)(3), (4),A response to a motion is due 10 days after service. A reply is due 7 days after the response.
