docs.t: 11th Cir. — Pay the $20 renewal fee every five years
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Pay the $20 renewal fee every five years. Pay the bar membership renewal fee the court posts every five years from your admission date. The clerk sends notice in the first week of the due month and payment is due by that month’s last day. If the notice bounces because your contact information is stale, no further notice is sent. Unpaid, you go inactive and may not practice before the court. After 12 months inactive the clerk strikes your name from the roll. The court’s website lists the fee as $20. (11th Cir. R. 46-2)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Briefs: 13,000 words; replies 6,500
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Briefs: 13,000 words; replies 6,500. This page shows the FRAP baseline. We haven’t yet checked this circuit’s local rules for a different limit. (FRAP 32(a)(7)(B))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — 14-point type
docs.x: 11th Cir.. 14-point type. FRAP 32(a)(5) requires a proportionally spaced serif face of 14 points or larger. (FRAP 32(a)(5))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Briefing times follow FRAP 31
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Briefing times follow FRAP 31. The appellant’s brief is due 40 days after the record is filed, the appellee’s 30 days after service of the appellant’s brief, and the reply 21 days after the appellee’s. The clerk sends a letter confirming the date, but a missed letter doesn’t change the deadline. (11th Cir. R. 31-1)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — The CIP: 14 days for appellants, 28 for appellees, or at your first filing
docs.x: 11th Cir.. The CIP: 14 days for appellants, 28 for appellees, or at your first filing. Appellants and petitioners file the Certificate of Interested Persons and Corporate Disclosure Statement within 14 days after docketing, or with their first filing if earlier. Appellees, intervenors, and respondents file within 28 days, or with their first filing if earlier, whether or not the appellant has filed, and may instead file a notice that an existing CIP is correct and complete or adds omitted persons. A petition that starts a proceeding carries its CIP. Every amicus puts a CIP in every motion and brief. On the same day you first file a CIP, counsel must complete the court’s web-based CIP, entering stock ticker symbols or “nothing to declare.” (11th Cir. R. 26.1-1)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Fix a deficient brief within 14 days or lose the appeal
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Fix a deficient brief within 14 days or lose the appeal. In a civil appeal, failing to correct a deficiency in a brief or appendix within 14 days of the clerk’s notice leads to dismissal. A request for more time to correct must also come within that 14 days. (11th Cir. R. 42-3)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Missing the appellant’s brief deadline can end the appeal
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Missing the appellant’s brief deadline can end the appeal. In a civil appeal, the appeal is dismissed if the appellant doesn’t file the brief or the appendix by the due date. (11th Cir. R. 42-2)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Paper copies only when the clerk asks
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Paper copies only when the clerk asks. At the end of briefing the clerk sends each party a notice directing it to send the court two paper copies of its brief or briefs. Pro se parties aren’t required to. (11th Cir. R. 31-3)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — No appearance form, no processing
docs.x: 11th Cir.. No appearance form, no processing. The clerk generally can’t process an attorney’s filings until the attorney files an appearance form, which is due within 14 days of the clerk’s notice. For a lawyer who isn’t a member of the bar, the clerk may conditionally file certain papers, such as a time-sensitive motion, and then gives 21 days to apply for admission or pro hac vice status. (11th Cir. R. 46-5, 46-6)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Nothing is acted on until the CIP and web-based CIP are done
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Nothing is acted on until the CIP and web-based CIP are done. The court won’t act on any papers, emergency filings included, until the CIP is filed and the web-based CIP completed, except to prevent manifest injustice. The clerk can’t submit a brief or motion to the court without them, and failure can mean dismissal under R. 42-1(b). (11th Cir. R. 26.1-5)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — The table of citations: no passim, and asterisk your key cases
docs.x: 11th Cir.. The table of citations: no passim, and asterisk your key cases. List every page on which an authority is cited, using ranges if it’s cited on every page of the range, and mark with asterisks in the margin the citations you primarily rely on. (11th Cir. R. 28-1(d))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — The summary of argument: seldom two pages, never five
docs.x: 11th Cir.. The summary of argument: seldom two pages, never five. It must be a condensation of the argument actually made, not a repeat of the headings. Criminal appeals must say whether the client is incarcerated, and the statement of facts must include unfavorable facts and identify inferences as inferences. (11th Cir. R. 28-1(i))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Cite the record by document number and page, and say which format you use
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Cite the record by document number and page, and say which format you use. The transcript page is the one in the header generated by the district court’s electronic filing system if available, otherwise the court reporter’s page number. The brief must note the format. (11th Cir. R. 28-5)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Only the cover and the signature block may be single-spaced
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Only the cover and the signature block may be single-spaced. Only the cover page, certificate of service, direct quotes, headings, and footnotes may be single-spaced. Everything else is double-spaced, including the tables. A noncompliant brief can be rejected or conditionally filed, with replacement briefs due within 14 days of the clerk’s notice. (11th Cir. R. 32-3)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Move to exceed length at least 7 days early
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Move to exceed length at least 7 days early. A motion for leave to file an overlength brief must be filed at least 7 days before the due date and is granted only for extraordinary and compelling reasons. Front matter and statutory addenda don’t count toward the limit. (11th Cir. R. 32-4)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Appellee’s supplemental appendix: 7 days after its brief
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Appellee’s supplemental appendix: 7 days after its brief. If the appellant’s appendix is deficient or the appellee’s brief relies on record parts not in it, the appellee files a supplemental appendix within seven days of filing its brief, without duplicating the appellant’s. Only documents submitted to the trial court may go in the appendix, except state court opinions in a § 2254 appeal. (11th Cir. R. 30-1(b))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Pending motions move the brief deadline
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Pending motions move the brief deadline. If a motion to proceed in forma pauperis, for a certificate of appealability, of a type in FRAP 4(a)(4)(A) or 4(b)(3)(A), about excusable neglect, for appointment or withdrawal of counsel, or for a transcript at government expense is pending, the appellant’s brief is due 40 days after it is resolved or 40 days after the record is deemed filed, whichever is later. The appellee gets 30 days. Otherwise a pending motion doesn’t postpone a brief. (11th Cir. R. 31-1(b))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Extension requests have four rules to know
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Extension requests have four rules to know. A first request for 30 days or less may be made by phone or in writing and the clerk can grant it. A first request for more than 30 days must be a written motion filed at least 7 days before the due date. If a first request filed 14 or more days ahead is denied within 7 days of the due date or later, you automatically get 7 more days. A second request is extremely disfavored and needs extraordinary, unforeseeable circumstances, and no request is accepted after the due date. (11th Cir. R. 31-2)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Rehearing: 21 days, and en banc is extraordinary
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Rehearing: 21 days, and en banc is extraordinary. File a petition for panel or en banc rehearing within 21 days of judgment, or 45 days in a civil appeal where the United States is a party. En banc review is for precedent-setting errors of exceptional importance or a conflict with precedent, not state-law, factual, or sufficiency errors. A rehearing petition against a stay, counsel, or leave-to-appeal order is treated as a motion to reconsider instead. (11th Cir. R. 40-2, 40-6, 40-7)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Reconsideration of a motion order: 21 days, and only once
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Reconsideration of a motion order: 21 days, and only once. Move to reconsider, vacate, or modify an order within 21 days, with no extra time for mailing. You get one motion per order, and you can’t seek reconsideration of the order that disposes of it. (11th Cir. R. 27-2, 27-3)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Failing to object to a magistrate judge’s report waives appeal
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Failing to object to a magistrate judge’s report waives appeal. If you were told the time to object and the consequences, not objecting waives your right to challenge unobjected-to factual and legal conclusions on appeal. The court may still review for plain error when justice requires. (11th Cir. R. 3-1)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — A motion pending below can stall your appeal
docs.x: 11th Cir.. A motion pending below can stall your appeal. If you file a motion in the district court that it can’t grant because of the appeal, move in this court within 14 days after filing it to stay the appeal. If the court stays it, file status reports every 30 days. (11th Cir. R. 12.1-1)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Attorney’s fees: 14 days after rehearing runs out
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Attorney’s fees: 14 days after rehearing runs out. File the application with the clerk within 14 days after the time to petition for rehearing expires, or after the ruling on a timely petition, whichever is later. Support it with a memorandum, the clerk’s form, contemporaneous time records, and an affidavit on the rate. Damages and costs under FRAP 38 and 39 and sanctions under 27-4 are separate. (11th Cir. R. 39-2)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Report a state-bar lapse within 14 days
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Report a state-bar lapse within 14 days. You can’t practice here unless you are an active member in good standing of a state bar. If that lapses for any reason, including inactive status, unpaid dues, or missed CLE, tell the clerk within 14 days and list every other bar you belong to. The court may put your membership on inactive status until you document good standing. (11th Cir. R. 46-7)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Emergency motions: moot within seven days
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Emergency motions: moot within seven days. A motion is an emergency motion only if it will be moot unless decided within seven days and, when reviewing a district court order, it is filed within seven days of that order (otherwise it may be “time sensitive”). Label it “Emergency Motion,” put any date-certain deadline in bold on the caption page, explain why it wasn’t filed earlier, and address likelihood of success, irreparable injury, harm to others, and the public interest. Attach the district court filings and ruling on the issue, notify the other side electronically, and phone the clerk early. (11th Cir. R. 27-1(b); FRAP 8, 27)

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Briefs: 13,000 words; replies 6,500
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Briefs: 13,000 words; replies 6,500. This page shows the FRAP baseline. We haven’t yet checked this circuit’s local rules for a different limit. (FRAP 32(a)(7)(B))

docs.x: D.C. Cir.. 14-point type. FRAP 32(a)(5) requires a proportionally spaced serif face of 14 points or larger. (FRAP 32(a)(5))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — The briefing schedule is set by order
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. The briefing schedule is set by order. The court issues a scheduling order and the briefs are due on its dates, not the FRAP 31(a) default clock. (D.C. Cir. R. 31(a))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Open with the Certificate as to Parties, Rulings, and Related Cases
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Open with the Certificate as to Parties, Rulings, and Related Cases. Immediately inside the cover and before the table of contents, every brief (including intervenor and amicus briefs) needs a certificate with separate paragraphs, in the same order, for parties and amici, rulings under review, and related cases. The appellant lists every party, intervenor, and amicus in the district court and here, and an appellee may adopt that list with a set sentence. Rulings need the date, the judge’s name, the place in the appendix, and the official or Federal Register citation. Related cases means substantially the same parties and the same or similar issues, in any other court of appeals or any other federal or local court in D.C., and if there are none the certificate says so. Entities include the Rule 26.1 disclosure. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(1))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Length: what is excluded
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Length: what is excluded. Length follows FRAP 28.1 and 32(a)(7). In addition to the FRAP 32(f) items, the certificate of parties, rulings, and related cases, the glossary, and any addendum of standing evidence may be excluded from the word count. An intervenor’s principal brief is limited to 19 pages and its reply to 9, unless it complies with the word limits in R. 32(e)(2). (D.C. Cir. R. 32(e)(1); 28(c))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — In direct agency review, a Standing section is required
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. In direct agency review, a Standing section is required. The brief of an appellant or petitioner in direct review of administrative action must set out the basis for standing in a section titled “Standing” that follows the summary of argument and immediately precedes the argument. It must argue and cite evidence showing standing by a “substantial probability.” Evidence not in the administrative record goes in an addendum, separated from the brief by a colored page, and bound separately if over 40 pages. A brief with a Standing section needn’t have the summary of argument rule’s placement. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(7))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Say “Complex” on the cover
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Say “Complex” on the cover. In cases the court designates “Complex,” the cover of the brief should say so. (Handbook § IX.A.6)

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — The table of authorities: no passim, optional asterisks
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. The table of authorities: no passim, optional asterisks. The table must identify each page where an authority is cited, and passim or similar terms may not be used, in the table or in record and authority citations. You may asterisk the authorities you chiefly rely on, with the notation at the bottom of the first page of the table. A glossary on the page right after the table must define every abbreviation or acronym that isn’t common usage. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(2), (b))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Statutes and regulations: in the brief or an addendum
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Statutes and regulations: in the brief or an addendum. Pertinent statutes and regulations go in the body after the statement of issues, or in an addendum with its own table of contents, introduced by a statement in the brief. An addendum over 40 pages must be bound separately, and one bound with the brief is separated by a distinctly colored page. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(5))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Say on the cover if the case is argued or submitted
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Say on the cover if the case is argued or submitted. If a case has been scheduled for argument, already argued, or is submitted without argument, the brief must say so in capital letters at the top of the front cover, with the argument date where applicable. Motions, responses, and replies must say the same at the top of page one (R. 27(a)(3)). (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(8))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Extension and length motions: at least 7 days before the brief is due
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Extension and length motions: at least 7 days before the brief is due. The court disfavors motions to exceed length or extend brief time that affect the oral argument schedule and grants them only for extraordinarily compelling reasons. File at least 7 days before the due date, attempt to get the other side’s consent first, and recite the other side’s position in the opening paragraph. Untimely motions are denied absent exceptional circumstances, though the clerk may grant an unopposed late motion for an extension that doesn’t affect argument. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(e))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — The briefing schedule is the court’s scheduling order
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. The briefing schedule is the court’s scheduling order. Parties serve and file briefs by the scheduling order, including in cross-appeals. File the original and 8 copies of every brief (for ECF filers, 8 paper copies follow the electronic filing within two business days by first-class mail), except that in a deferred-appendix case initial briefs go in electronic form only. (D.C. Cir. R. 31(a), 28.1(c))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — The docketing statement and provisional certificate
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. The docketing statement and provisional certificate. As the court directs, the appellant files a docketing statement on the clerk’s form with a provisional certificate containing the information Rule 28(a)(1) requires. Errors must be reported to the clerk by letter served on all parties within 7 days of service, and an appellee, intervenor, or amicus must file any disclosure statement within 7 days. (D.C. Cir. R. 12)

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Dispositive motions within 45 days of docketing
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Dispositive motions within 45 days of docketing. A motion that would dispose of the appeal or petition entirely, or transfer the case, must be filed within 45 days of docketing unless a scheduling order sets another time. Briefing is deferred pending a timely one. Attach the pertinent opinion or findings, or the transcript extract if the reasons were oral. (D.C. Cir. R. 27(f))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Every motion carries the certificate and disclosure statement
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Every motion carries the certificate and disclosure statement. Attach as an addendum a certificate of parties and amici as in Rule 28(a)(1)(A) and any required disclosure statement, unless already filed, and file the original and 4 copies unless the court directs otherwise. A response combined with a cross-motion for affirmative relief may run 7,800 words, and the answer to it, with any reply, is due within 10 days and limited to 5,200 words. (D.C. Cir. R. 27(a)(4), (b))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Stays and emergency relief: the four factors, with specificity
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Stays and emergency relief: the four factors, with specificity. A motion for a stay or other emergency relief must say whether you asked the district court first and how it ruled, and discuss with specificity likelihood of success, irreparable injury, harm to other parties, and the public interest. Try to notify the other side by phone before filing and describe those efforts. Attach the order and any decision or findings (or the transcript extract if oral), plus the certificate of parties and amici and the disclosure statement. (D.C. Cir. R. 8(a); FRAP 8, 27)

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Filing deadline: before midnight Eastern
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Filing deadline: before midnight Eastern. Unless a time is specified by court order, filing must be completed before midnight Eastern Time to be considered timely filed that day. (D.C. Cir. R. 26(a))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Briefs: 14,000 words; replies 7,000
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Briefs: 14,000 words; replies 7,000. A principal brief may exceed 30 pages if it has no more than 14,000 words (or 1,300 lines of monospaced text), and a reply may exceed 15 pages if it has no more than 7,000 words (650 lines). In cross-appeals the appellant’s principal brief and its response and reply brief may each run 14,000 words, the appellee’s principal and response brief 16,500, and the appellee’s reply 7,000. Excluded from the count: the certificate of interest, statement of related cases, any addendum, the cover and the exemplary patent claims inside it, and Rule 25.1(e) material, plus the FRAP 32(f) items. A brief over the page limit needs a certificate of compliance, Form 19. (Fed. Cir. R. 32(b), 28.1)

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — 14-point type
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. 14-point type. FRAP 32(a)(5) requires a proportionally spaced serif face of 14 points or larger. That includes footnotes. (FRAP 32(a)(5))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Briefing runs 60 days, then 40, then 21
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Briefing runs 60 days, then 40, then 21. The appellant’s principal brief is due 60 days after docketing (or 60 days after the certified list or index is served in an agency appeal). The appellee’s or cross-appellant’s principal brief is due 40 days after the appellant’s brief is served. In a cross-appeal the appellant’s response and reply brief is due 40 days after the cross-appellant’s principal and response brief, and the cross-appellant’s reply 21 days after that. A brief answering multiple parties runs from the last one served. A motion that would end the appeal suspends briefing, and if denied the next brief is due in the balance of the time, but not fewer than 14 days from the order. (Fed. Cir. R. 31(a))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Certificate of Interest: with your first entry of appearance
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Certificate of Interest: with your first entry of appearance. Each party, intervenor, amicus, or movant files a certificate of interest at the same time as its first entry of appearance, with negative answers where applicable. It lists every entity represented, any real party in interest, parent corporations and publicly held 10% owners, the law firms and lawyers who appeared below or are expected here but haven’t entered an appearance, and whether related or prior cases exist. It is repeated in each motion, petition, response, principal brief, and amicus brief. The United States and unrepresented individuals are exempt unless disclosing under FRAP 26.1(b). (Fed. Cir. R. 47.4)

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Entry of appearance within 14 days, and one principal counsel
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Entry of appearance within 14 days, and one principal counsel. Counsel retained before docketing file the form within 14 days after docketing, and designate one principal counsel. Counsel retained later file within 14 days of being retained or admitted, whichever is later. Counsel who don’t enter an appearance aren’t listed on the docket or any decision, intervenor and amicus counsel file with their first document, and a lawyer appearing for the first time after the case goes to a merits panel needs leave. Only counsel with an appearance on file may argue. Unrepresented parties file a notice of appearance within 14 days of docketing. (Fed. Cir. R. 47.3)

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Confidential material: 15 unique words, 50 in two case types
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Confidential material: 15 unique words, 50 in two case types. A motion, petition, response, reply, or brief may mark confidential up to 15 unique words, including numbers, and up to 50 in cases under 19 U.S.C. § 1516a or 28 U.S.C. § 1491(b). Marking is allowed only if the information is covered by a protective order and a statute, regulation, or rule authorizes it. Repeating the same material doesn’t use more of the allotment, and a response doesn’t count material the earlier filing already marked. The limit doesn’t apply to appendices, attachments, exhibits, and addenda. To mark more, move to waive. Redaction beyond FRAP 25(a)(5) and Rule 25.1 is prohibited, and counsel are solely responsible for what is redacted. (Fed. Cir. R. 25.1(d))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — The appendix is filed after the reply brief
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. The appendix is filed after the reply brief. The appellant files the appendix within 7 days after the last reply brief is served and filed, or within the time for the reply if none is filed (and in a cross-appeal within 7 days after the time for the cross-appellant’s reply expires). The parties compile a designation of appendix material no later than 45 days before the appellant’s principal brief is due. Every appendix includes the entire docket sheet or certified list and, in a jury case, the charge, verdict, and interrogatory answers, and in a patent appeal the patents at issue in their entirety. Record parts not cited in the briefs stay out, and no volume may exceed 400 printed sheets, each with a table of contents and Roman-numeral volume cover. If the appellant fails to file it, the clerk may dismiss. (Fed. Cir. R. 30(a)(2); 30(b))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Six paper copies of each brief and the appendix
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Six paper copies of each brief and the appendix. Six paper copies of each brief (three for an informal brief) and of any appendix go to the court on the schedule in Rule 25(c)(3), and when all parties have counsel, one more copy goes to principal counsel for the others unless they say it isn’t needed. No copies need go to amicus counsel. Page proofs may not be filed. (Fed. Cir. R. 31(b), 30(a)(3), 25(c)(3))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Electronic filing: before midnight Eastern
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Electronic filing: before midnight Eastern. Unless the court sets a time, filing must be completed before midnight Eastern Time on the due date. Legal holidays include the day after Thanksgiving and any day the clerk’s office is closed by order. Timeliness of a response runs from service of the original, not any correction. (Fed. Cir. R. 26(a)(2))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — The docketing statement is due in 14 days
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. The docketing statement is due in 14 days. Except for unrepresented parties, each appellant, cross-appellant, or petitioner files the clerk’s docketing statement within 14 days after docketing, which also satisfies FRAP 10(b)(3)(A)’s statement of issues. (Fed. Cir. R. 47.6)

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Motions: say you consulted, and attach the certificate
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Motions: say you consulted, and attach the certificate. Every motion has a caption, a statement of consent or opposition showing you discussed it with the other parties, a certificate of interest, and a declaration if the facts are disputed. A motion to expedite is labeled “Motion to Expedite” and proposes an expedited schedule. A motion to strike a brief is prohibited if you can respond in your own brief. Motions to dismiss, transfer, or remand should be made as soon as the grounds are known. (Fed. Cir. R. 27(a))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Patent claims go on the inside of the cover
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Patent claims go on the inside of the cover. When the language of a patent or application is at issue, each party’s principal brief must reproduce illustrative claims inside the front cover, single-spaced if you like, and they don’t count toward the limit. “Nonconfidential” or “public” may appear on a cover only if there is a corresponding confidential version. (Fed. Cir. R. 32(a)(3))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Corrections need a Notice of Correction
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Corrections need a Notice of Correction. You can’t fix a filed document with an errata sheet. File a corrected document marked “corrected” with a Notice of Correction listing each change, and file corrected paper copies if you’ve submitted them. Substantive changes need leave. (Fed. Cir. R. 25(i))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Oral argument: visual aids and conflicts
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Oral argument: visual aids and conflicts. Tell the court by letter 14 days ahead if you’ll display a visual aid used at trial or an agency hearing, and 21 days ahead for any other, with notice to opposing counsel. Objections are due 7 days before argument. Presentation programs and projectors need leave on a motion filed 21 days before. When the clerk asks for scheduling conflicts you must answer within 7 days, with good cause shown for each conflict, even if you have none. (Fed. Cir. R. 34(c), (d))

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — No separate emergency-motion rule beyond FRAP
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. No separate emergency-motion rule beyond FRAP. Consi’s copy of the Federal Circuit Rules has no separate emergency-motion provision. For a stay or injunction pending appeal, follow FRAP 8 (move first in the district court or agency) and FRAP 27, and contact the Clerk’s Office before filing. (FRAP 8, 27; Fed. Cir. R. 27)

docs.t: Fed. Cir. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: Fed. Cir.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

R. 46,Eligible lawyers are of good character and admitted and in good standing in the courts listed in FRAP 46(a), or in the Court of International Trade, Court of Federal Claims, Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims, or D.C. Court of Appeals. Admission can be on a sponsor’s motion in open court, a member’s written motion, or the lawyer’s own motion with a certificate of good standing dated within 30 days. Attorneys for any federal, state, or local government office may appear in their official duties without admission. The rule has no separate pro hac vice procedure. Motions: 5,200 words,FRAP 27(d)(2),A motion or response runs 5,200 words or 20 pages. A reply runs 2,600 words or 10 pages. docs.t: SCOTUS — Cert petition due in 90 days
docs.x: SCOTUS. Cert petition due in 90 days. Ninety days from entry of judgment, or from the denial of rehearing if anyone timely sought it below. The clock doesn’t run from the mandate. The Clerk won’t file a petition that is jurisdictionally out of time. (Sup. Ct. R. 13.1, 13.3)

docs.t: SCOTUS — Extensions: one Justice, 60 days, apply 10 days early
docs.x: SCOTUS. Extensions: one Justice, 60 days, apply 10 days early. A Justice may extend the time by up to 60 days for good cause. File the application at least 10 days before the due date, name every party it covers, and expect little: they are not favored. Once denied, it can’t be renewed. (Sup. Ct. R. 13.5, 30.2, 30.3)

docs.t: SCOTUS — 9,000 words, booklet format, Century type
docs.x: SCOTUS. 9,000 words, booklet format, Century type. A cert petition or brief in opposition gets 9,000 words in 12-point Century, with footnotes in 10-point and counted. Merits briefs get 13,000 words, merits replies 6,000, and rehearing petitions 3,000. Attach a certificate stating your word count. (Sup. Ct. R. 33.1)

docs.t: SCOTUS — Forty paper copies, plus electronic filing
docs.x: SCOTUS. Forty paper copies, plus electronic filing. Paid cases file 40 booklets. Represented filers must also submit to the electronic system under the Clerk’s guidelines, and if they filed electronically the paper copies are due within three days. (Sup. Ct. R. 12.1, 29.7, 33.1(f))

docs.t: SCOTUS — Only a Bar member can be counsel of record
docs.x: SCOTUS. Only a Bar member can be counsel of record. Counsel of record must be admitted to this Court’s Bar, except lawyers appointed under the Criminal Justice Act. Only one counsel of record appears on a document’s cover. (Sup. Ct. R. 9.1, 34.1(f))

docs.t: SCOTUS — Brief in opposition: 30 days, optional
docs.x: SCOTUS. Brief in opposition: 30 days, optional. A brief in opposition is due 30 days after docketing. It is optional except in a capital case or when the Court asks for one. The respondent can waive, and objections that aren’t jurisdictional may be waived if not raised in it. (Sup. Ct. R. 15.1, 15.3)

docs.t: SCOTUS — Amicus notice 10 days before the due date
docs.x: SCOTUS. Amicus notice 10 days before the due date. At the cert stage, tell every counsel of record at least 10 days before the amicus brief is due. The brief is due 30 days after docketing or a call for a response, whichever is later, and that can’t be extended. The first footnote must disclose who authored and funded it. (Sup. Ct. R. 37.2, 37.6)

docs.t: SCOTUS — Rehearing in 25 days, no extensions for cert denials
docs.x: SCOTUS. Rehearing in 25 days, no extensions for cert denials. A petition for rehearing is due 25 days after the judgment or order. Time to seek rehearing of a cert denial won’t be extended. It needs 3,000 words or less, a good-faith certificate, and a $200 fee. (Sup. Ct. R. 44.1, 44.2, 33.1(g))

docs.t: SCOTUS — Timely filing: received by the deadline, or mailed by it
docs.x: SCOTUS. Timely filing: received by the deadline, or mailed by it. A document is timely if the Clerk receives it within the time for filing, or if it is sent by first-class mail or by third-party commercial carrier on or before the last day, with proof of the date. (Sup. Ct. R. 29.2)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — 21 days to respond, 14 to reply
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. 21 days to respond, 14 to reply. Serve a response within 21 days after the motion and brief. The movant replies within 14 days after the response. (LR 7.2, 7.3)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — Briefs are 20 pages; replies 10
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. Briefs are 20 pages; replies 10. Including objections to a report and recommendation. To exceed, move in writing at least 5 days before the brief is due, and say how many pages you want. (LR 7.4)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — Every motion needs a brief
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. Every motion needs a brief. Every civil motion is accompanied by a memorandum of law citing authorities. Motions alleging facts need a statement of fact. Enlargement-of-time motions are excepted. (LR 7.1)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. Attach a separate, numbered statement of material facts with record citations. The respondent answers each one. Facts not specifically controverted are deemed admitted. (LR 56)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — Discovery limits are tight
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. Discovery limits are tight. Without written permission: 25 interrogatories, 10 requests for production, and 15 requests for admission. (LR 33.1, 34, 36)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — Fees in 14 days, or waived
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. Fees in 14 days, or waived. File the fee motion within 14 days of judgment, with an itemized bill, a per-attorney breakdown, the hourly rate and how you got there, and a certification. (LR 54.1)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — Continuances can’t be stipulated, and answer extensions are capped
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. Continuances can’t be stipulated, and answer extensions are capped. Only the court continues a trial, pretrial conference, or hearing, and never by stipulation. Counsel may file one written stipulation per complaint to extend the answer by up to 30 days. For more time, move under Rule 6(b). (LR 6.1)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — Reconsideration: 14 days, 5 pages, no reply
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. Reconsideration: 14 days, 5 pages, no reply. Motions for reconsideration are not routine. File within 14 days after the order (Rule 59(e) motions excepted), limit every brief to 5 pages, expect no reply brief, and don’t move to reconsider the ruling on a reconsideration motion. The clerk can’t extend these deadlines. (LR 7.6)

docs.t: M.D. Ga. — overview
docs.x: M.D. Ga.. Surreplies are not favored,LR 7.3.1,Briefing ends with the reply. To file a surreply, move within 14 days and don’t attach the proposed brief. Reconsideration in 14 days,LR 7.6,Not a routine practice. Briefs are 5 pages, with no reply, and you can’t move to reconsider a denial of reconsideration. Retype each discovery question,LR 33.1,The answering party retypes the question with the answer or objection immediately below. Confer before moving to compel,LR 37,The motion must certify a good-faith conference. Seven-hour depositions,LR 30.2,Seven full hours of interrogation, excluding breaks and document review. Clerk extensions,LR 6.1, 6.2,A filed stipulation extends the answer deadline up to 30 days, once. The clerk can extend a brief deadline once, up to 14 days. Bill of costs: 30 days,LR 54.2.2,The other side gets 21 days to respond. Diversity disclosure,LR 87,Corporate parties

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — Combined motion and brief, 6,500 words
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. Combined motion and brief, 6,500 words. File the motion and brief as one document of up to 6,500 words, with a reply of up to 2,500. Filing or signing it certifies that you complied. Handwritten filings are limited by pages instead. (LR Civ. 7(a), (e))

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — 14 days to respond, 21 on summary judgment
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. 14 days to respond, 21 on summary judgment. Respond within 14 days of service, or 21 days for summary judgment. Failing to respond timely indicates there is no opposition. (LR Civ. 7(b), 56(b))

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — Replies get 7 days
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. Replies get 7 days. A reply is due 7 days after the response is served. Anything beyond the motion, response, and reply needs leave of court first. (LR Civ. 7(c), 56(c))

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — Informal conference before any discovery motion
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. Informal conference before any discovery motion. Before filing a motion to compel, to quash, or for a protective order, you must ask the court for an informal discovery dispute conference. Motions about subpoenas in this district work the same way. (LR Civ. 26(d), 45(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — The Rule 26 clock starts at the first answer
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. The Rule 26 clock starts at the first answer. No 26(f) conference, report, or initial disclosures are due until a defendant answers. Confer within 28 days of the first answer (28 days from removal in a removed case), file the court’s report form within 7 days, and serve initial disclosures within 14 days after the conference. (LR Civ. 26(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — Summary judgment: one filing plus a separate fact statement
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. Summary judgment: one filing plus a separate fact statement. File the motion and brief as one document with sequentially numbered exhibits, each behind a cover page, and complete deposition transcripts. Add a separate Statement of Undisputed Material Facts, numbered, with pinpoint record citations. (LR Civ. 56(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — Bar renewal: none found
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. Bar renewal: none found. We found no periodic renewal, re-registration fee, or dues requirement in the rulebook we read for this court, apart from any fee at admission. The FJC’s 2024 compilation of federal bar rules lists none either. A court can add one by General Order after our sources, as E.D. Okla. did in 2024, so confirm with the clerk, and keep your home-state license active, because losing it can end your admission here. (Rulebook as read)

docs.t: S.D. Ga. — overview
docs.x: S.D. Ga.. Pro hac vice is closed to local lawyers,LR Gen. 1B(b)(2),Attorneys who reside in the district or keep their principal place of business here may not appear pro hac vice. They must join the bar. Cite the record for every fact,LR Civ. 7(f), (g),Every motion must name the statute, rule, or legal principle at issue, and every factual assertion must cite the record or an attached exhibit. Hearings are requested by separate motion,LR Civ. 7(h), (i),State the reasons, the time needed, and whether evidence will be presented. Before any motion hearing, give the court and opposing counsel a written witness and exhibit list, normally three business days ahead. Ministerial motions need a proposed order,LR Civ. 7(j), (k),The court may rule at once on extension motions and joint or consent motions. For other motions it typically waits until the reply time has run. Clerk extensions: 14 days,

docs.t: D. Del. — Annual dues, $25
docs.x: D. Del.. Annual dues, $25. The court charges $25 in annual dues under a 2009 standing order, per the FJC’s 2024 compilation. We haven’t read the order, so confirm the current amount and due date with the clerk. (D. Del. standing order (2009); FJC 2024)

docs.t: D. Del. — Filing deadline: 5:00 p.m. Eastern
docs.x: D. Del.. Filing deadline: 5:00 p.m. Eastern. On the due date, filing must be completed by 5:00 p.m. Eastern, not midnight. Initial pleadings are the exception. Most federal courts use midnight, so this one catches people. (CM/ECF Administrative Procedures)

docs.t: D. Del. — 14 days to answer, 7 to reply
docs.x: D. Del.. 14 days to answer, 7 to reply. The answering brief is due 14 days after the opening brief, and the reply 7 days after the answering brief. The docket states the dates for you. (LR 7.1.2(b))

docs.t: D. Del. — 20 pages, 10 for replies, 12-point
docs.x: D. Del.. 20 pages, 10 for replies, 12-point. Opening and answering briefs run 20 pages, replies 10, all in 12-point type. Some judges set word limits instead in their scheduling orders, so read yours. (LR 7.1.3(a)(4); LR 5.1.1(a))

docs.t: D. Del. — Delaware counsel file everything
docs.x: D. Del.. Delaware counsel file everything. Once you’re in pro hac vice, Delaware counsel are the registered CM/ECF users and file all papers. (LR 83.5(d))

docs.t: D. Del. — No argument held back for the reply
docs.x: D. Del.. No argument held back for the reply. The party filing the opening brief can’t reserve argument for the reply. (LR 7.1.3(a)(2))

docs.t: D. Del. — A nondispositive motion needs a phone call first
docs.x: D. Del.. A nondispositive motion needs a phone call first. Every nondispositive motion must come with an averment that counsel made a reasonable effort to reach agreement. A reasonable effort must include oral communication between Delaware counsel for both sides. A motion without the averment may be dismissed. Pro se cases and nonparty motions are exempt. (LR 7.1.1)

docs.t: D. Del. — The reply ends the briefing, apart from new authority
docs.x: D. Del.. The reply ends the briefing, apart from new authority. After the reply is served, no more papers are filed without court approval. The one exception is a non-argumentative cover letter that cites newly available authority and identifies the pending motion it affects. (LR 7.1.2(b), (c))

docs.t: D. Del. — Ask for oral argument within 7 days of the reply
docs.x: D. Del.. Ask for oral argument within 7 days of the reply. An application for oral argument must be in writing and made no later than 7 days after service of the reply brief. The court may grant it or deny it, or set argument on its own. (LR 7.1.4)

docs.t: D. Del. — Reargument: 14 days, 10 pages, rarely granted
docs.x: D. Del.. Reargument: 14 days, 10 pages, rarely granted. A motion for reargument is due within 14 days after the court’s decision. Rule 59(e) motions follow Rule 59(e)’s own deadline. The motion and the answer, due 14 days after filing, are each limited to 10 pages, and no reply is allowed unless the court grants one. You can’t move for reargument of a magistrate judge’s ruling. Object under Rule 72 and LR 72.1(b) instead. (LR 7.1.5)

docs.t: D. Del. — A motion to amend needs a redline
docs.x: D. Del.. A motion to amend needs a redline. Attach the signed proposed pleading with its exhibits, plus a second version marked to show the changes, with deleted text in brackets or struck through and added text underlined. (LR 15.1(a))

docs.t: D. Del. — A discovery motion must quote the discovery
docs.x: D. Del.. A discovery motion must quote the discovery. Put a verbatim recitation of each interrogatory, request, answer, response, or objection in the motion or the brief, or attach a copy of the discovery document. (LR 37.1)

docs.t: D. Del. — Don’t file discovery. File a notice of service
docs.x: D. Del.. Don’t file discovery. File a notice of service. When every party has counsel, discovery requests, responses, and Rule 26(a) disclosures are served but not filed. File a Notice of Service certifying what was served, when, and how. A deposition notice or proof of service of a subpoena counts as the notice. (LR 5.4(b))

docs.t: D. Del. — Ask to extend a deadline before it passes
docs.x: D. Del.. Ask to extend a deadline before it passes. A request to extend discovery deadlines or postpone trial must be made by motion or stipulation before the deadline expires, and it must state the reasons. (LR 16.4)

docs.t: D. Del. — Bill of costs: meet and confer, then 28 days
docs.x: D. Del.. Bill of costs: meet and confer, then 28 days. The prevailing party files a bill of costs within 28 days after the appeal time expires or the mandate issues, after meeting and conferring about what is taxable. Missing the deadline or skipping the procedure waives costs unless the court orders otherwise. (LR 54.1(a))

docs.x: D. Del. deadline. Notice of a deposition: At least 10 days (L.R. LR 30.1)

docs.x: D. Del. deadline. Motion to review the clerk’s taxation: 7 days after service (L.R. LR 54.1(d))

docs.t: D. Del. — Fee application in a settled case
docs.x: D. Del. deadline. Fee application in a settled case: 21 days after approval, or after signing if no approval is sought (L.R. LR 54.3(b))

docs.t: D. Del. — Jury costs if a case is resolved late
docs.x: D. Del. deadline. Jury costs if a case is resolved late: Less than 3 full business days before jury selection (L.R. LR 54.2)

docs.t: D. Del. — Dismissal for inaction
docs.x: D. Del. deadline. Dismissal for inaction: After 3 months with no action (L.R. LR 41.1)

docs.t: D. Del. — Motion to withdraw served on the client

docs.t: D. Del. — Statement of pending matters after removal or transfer
docs.x: D. Del. deadline. Statement of pending matters after removal or transfer: Within 45 days (L.R. LR 81.2)

docs.t: D. Del. — overview

Annual fund fee,Standing Order for District Court Fund,The certification confirms the $25 annual fee has been paid. docs.t: C.D. Ill. — No pro hac vice here
docs.x: C.D. Ill.. No pro hac vice here. The court does not permit pro hac vice admissions generally. Plan on general admission, which takes a motion, a questionnaire, an oath, and the fee. (CDIL-LR 83.5(F))

docs.t: C.D. Ill. — Replies need leave, within 7 days
docs.x: C.D. Ill.. Replies need leave, within 7 days. A reply is permitted only with leave of court. Move within 7 days after the response and attach the proposed reply as an exhibit. Summary judgment is different: that reply is due within 14 days, with no leave. (CDIL-LR 7.1(B)(3))

docs.t: C.D. Ill. — Silence means no opposition
docs.x: C.D. Ill.. Silence means no opposition. Respond within 14 days of the motion and memorandum. If no response is filed, the judge presumes there’s no opposition and may rule without further notice. (CDIL-LR 7.1(B)(2))

docs.t: C.D. Ill. — 15 pages, or 7,000 words with a certificate
docs.x: C.D. Ill.. 15 pages, or 7,000 words with a certificate. Memoranda are double-spaced and capped at 15 pages, unless they meet the type-volume limit of 7,000 words or 650 lines of monospaced type, with a certificate of compliance. Headings, footnotes, and quotations all count. (CDIL-LR 7.1(B)(4))

docs.t: C.D. Ill. — Unanswered summary judgment facts are admitted
docs.x: C.D. Ill.. Unanswered summary judgment facts are admitted. Summary judgment has its own format: numbered undisputed facts with exhibit and page cites, a response that sorts each fact into four categories, and a reply. Failing to respond to a numbered fact is an admission. (CDIL-LR 7.1(D))

docs.t: C.D. Ill. — Extensions must be asked for in time
docs.x: C.D. Ill.. Extensions must be asked for in time. Motions for extensions must be filed within the original time allowed. On summary judgment, late extension motions may be summarily denied. (CDIL-LR 7.1(A)(3))

docs.t: C.D. Ill. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: C.D. Ill.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: C.D. Ill. — overview
docs.x: C.D. Ill.. Four divisions, named in the caption,CDIL-LR 40.1,Peoria, Springfield, Rock Island, and Urbana. Every filing names the division, and the initial pleading states why you filed there. Statewide and nationwide cases are spread,CDIL-LR 40.1(E)(4)(b),Cases seeking to bar or mandate statewide or nationwide enforcement are assigned district-wide, not just to the division’s judges, unless a party objects within 14 days. Type and format,CDIL-LCrR 49.2,Double-spaced, 12- or 14-point body text, footnotes no smaller than 10-point, 1-inch margins, numbered pages, in a plain roman style. docs.t: E.D. Okla. — Pay the $60 biennial fee, October 1 to January 31
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. Pay the $60 biennial fee, October 1 to January 31. Pay the $60 biennial renewal fee through CM/ECF, with your own PACER login, and only if you are in good standing. The first period ran October 1, 2024 to January 31, 2025 and recurs every other year, so the next should run October 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 (confirm the dates). Not paying by the end removes you from the active rolls, and repeated failure can require reapplying and paying the full admission fee. Federal agency attorneys are exempt, but CJA panel attorneys are not. (E.D. Okla. General Order 24-06)

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — Confer in person before any non-dispositive motion
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. Confer in person before any non-dispositive motion. The court refuses to hear a non-dispositive motion, discovery and motions in limine included, unless counsel certify in writing that they met personally and tried in good faith to resolve it. A telephone call counts only for a late discovery response or when distance makes a meeting infeasible, and offices within 30 miles are always close enough. State where the offices are. (LCvR 7.1(f))

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — 14 days to respond, and no cross-motions in a response
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. 14 days to respond, and no cross-motions in a response. A response is due 14 days after the motion was filed, and it can’t also contain a cross-motion. File any cross-motion separately. At the court’s discretion, an unopposed non-dispositive motion may be deemed confessed after 14 days. (LCvR 7.1(d))

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — 25 pages for a brief, 10 for a reply
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. 25 pages for a brief, 10 for a reply. No brief may exceed 25 pages without leave. Ask for more no later than 1 day before the brief is due, and state the page count you want. A reply is limited to 10 pages and may address only new matters in the response. Briefs over 15 pages need a table of contents and a table of authorities. (LCvR 7.1(c), (e))

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — A motion to dismiss must explain why amendment would be futile
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. A motion to dismiss must explain why amendment would be futile. Every motion to dismiss has to include a section on why amending the complaint or petition would be futile. Leaving it out invites a denial or a chance to amend. (LCvR 7.1(o))

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — One summary judgment motion per party
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. One summary judgment motion per party. Absent leave, each party may file only one Rule 56 motion. The brief opens with numbered material facts, each with a pinpoint record cite, and any fact the response doesn’t specifically controvert may be deemed admitted. (LCvR 56.1(a), (b), (e))

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — Extension motions need six things and a proposed order
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. Extension motions need six things and a proposed order. The clerk may grant a defendant the first extension to answer, up to 14 days. Every other extension motion must be filed before the deadline runs, and must give the due date, prior extensions, specific reasons, the other side’s position, any objection’s basis, and the effect on trial. It needs a proposed order. (LCvR 7.1(h), (i))

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — Costs and fees are due 14 days after judgment
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. Costs and fees are due 14 days after judgment. A bill of costs and a motion for attorney fees are each due within 14 days after entry of judgment, filed as separate documents with their own briefs. The other side has 14 days to object. (LCvR 54.1, 54.2)

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — Pro hac vice needs Oklahoma local counsel
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. Pro hac vice needs Oklahoma local counsel. A lawyer outside the Oklahoma bar must associate an Oklahoma bar member who is admitted here and appears personally. That lawyer files the pro hac vice motion, signs the first pleading, and stays in the case unless replaced. (LCvR 83.3(a), (b))

docs.t: E.D. Okla. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: E.D. Okla.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

Admission ceremonies usually are held on the first Monday of each month, subject to changes in the court calendar.

docs.t: Judge Anne Traum (D. Nev.) — Force and filing
docs.x: Judge Anne Traum, D. Nev.. Force and filing: This order controls over inconsistent local rules and federal rules. If a case was reassigned to her, her procedures replace the earlier judge’s from the date of reassignment forward. Her chambers is paperless: no courtesy copies unless requested, and you needn’t follow LR IC 2-2(g) or LR IA 10-3(i) when filing electronically. Send courtesy copies of manual filings to her chambers in Reno on a USB flash drive, not a disc, even in a Las Vegas case. Manual filings go to the Reno Clerk’s Office. Contact her courtroom administrator before delivering exhibits that can’t be sent electronically. File searchable PDFs.

docs.t: Judge Anne Traum (D. Nev.) — Requests for hearings
docs.x: Judge Anne Traum, D. Nev.. Requests for hearings: She distinguishes oral argument, which is only counsel’s arguments, from an evidentiary hearing, with witnesses and exhibits. Put “Oral Argument Requested” or “Evidentiary Hearing Requested” in the heading of the filing. She won’t schedule one automatically and will contact counsel if she thinks a hearing will help. A request to continue a hearing must be made at least seven days before it unless good cause is shown.

docs.t: Judge Anne Traum (D. Nev.) — Civil cases
docs.x: Judge Anne Traum, D. Nev.. Civil cases: She generally grants requests to appear remotely for good cause. A granted stay denies pending motions without prejudice, and a party may move to reinstate them. Civil cases generally go to the magistrate judge for a settlement conference after dispositive motions are resolved, and you may ask for an early settlement or pretrial conference under LR 16-2. Trial is set after the joint pretrial order on the first available trial stack. She encourages consent to trial by a magistrate judge under LR IB 2-2.

docs.t: Judge Anne Traum (D. Nev.) — Communications with chambers
docs.x: Judge Anne Traum, D. Nev.. Communications with chambers: For docketing, scheduling and calendar matters, contact the courtroom administrator by phone or email. Ex parte calls about the substance of a case are prohibited under LR IA 7-2. If a submission needs immediate attention, phone the courtroom administrator after filing on ECF.

docs.t: Judge Indira Talwani (D. Mass.) — Motions and briefs
docs.x: Judge Indira Talwani, D. Mass.. Motions and briefs: Follow the page and paper limits in Local Rule 7.1(b)(3) and (4). All text, footnotes included, must be at least 12-point. A memorandum over ten pages needs a table of contents and a table of authorities, which don’t count toward the page limit. File supporting and opposing documents separately from the motion, using the matching event under CM/ECF’s “Memoranda, Responses, and Replies” tab. An affidavit goes in separately, and each of its exhibits is a separate attachment with docket text giving the exhibit number and a short title. File memoranda after the evidence is docketed. Cite the docket as: Document Title (including Exhibit Number), Doc. No. __ at __. After the first cite, use Doc. No. __ at __ (except “Id.”) so the citations hyperlink.

docs.t: Judge Indira Talwani (D. Mass.) — Courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Indira Talwani, D. Mass.. Courtesy copies: Within three business days after docketing a motion-related filing over twenty pages, deliver one courtesy copy to the Clerk’s Office with CM/ECF headers on every page, three-hole punched, with exhibit tabs. Mark it “COURTESY COPY – DO NOT SCAN, Original Filed Electronically.”

docs.t: Judge Indira Talwani (D. Mass.) — Junior lawyers
docs.x: Judge Indira Talwani, D. Mass.. Junior lawyers: Judge Talwani has a separate Standing Order on courtroom opportunities for relatively inexperienced attorneys, which encourages them to take speaking roles.

docs.t: Judge Myong J. Joun (D. Mass.) — Motions and briefs
docs.x: Judge Myong J. Joun, D. Mass.. Motions and briefs: Confer in good faith before filing any motion (L.R. 7.1(a)(2) and 37.1). The 20-page limit in L.R. 7.1(b)(4) applies, and longer papers need leave. Dispositive motions include motions to dismiss, for summary judgment, for judgment on the pleadings, and for judgment as a matter of law. Opposition is due in 14 days (21 for summary judgment). A reply is allowed as of right within 7 days (14 for summary judgment) and may not exceed five pages. A longer reply or more time needs a motion for leave. Sur-replies aren’t permitted. Cite docket entries as (Doc No. at __), not Bluebook-style by document title, so the ECF citation links work.

docs.t: Judge Myong J. Joun (D. Mass.) — Discovery motions
docs.x: Judge Myong J. Joun, D. Mass.. Discovery motions: Discovery motions must be filed by the close of fact discovery or expert discovery, whichever applies, absent good cause. If the court compels more discovery after the deadline, the deadline extends only for that discovery. The memorandum must quote each interrogatory, deposition question, request, or other item at issue and the response, then state your position on each contested issue with authority right after it (L.R. 37.1(b)).

docs.t: Judge Myong J. Joun (D. Mass.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Myong J. Joun, D. Mass.. Summary judgment: Number the moving party’s facts. The opposing party restates each of those facts in the same order and responds directly beneath it, then lists any additional facts starting with the next number, and the reply follows the same pattern. Cross-motions: plaintiff files first (20 pages); defendant has 30 days for a single combined opposition and cross-motion memorandum (30 pages); plaintiff has 21 days for a combined reply and opposition (15 pages); defendant has 14 days for a reply (5 pages).

docs.t: Judge Myong J. Joun (D. Mass.) — Exhibits
docs.x: Judge Myong J. Joun, D. Mass.. Exhibits: File exhibits in chronological order with a descriptive table of contents, labeled by number (not letter). The opposing party continues the numbering. Cite exhibits already on file rather than refiling them. With more than five exhibits, or lengthy ones, give the Courtroom Deputy a tabbed paper courtesy copy.

docs.t: Judge Myong J. Joun (D. Mass.) — Courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Myong J. Joun, D. Mass.. Courtesy copies: Deliver one double-sided courtesy copy to the Clerk’s Office of any motion, opposition, or reply with its exhibits over 100 pages, marked “COURTESY COPY – DO NOT SCAN,” within three business days of filing, with exhibit tabs. Litigants proceeding in forma pauperis are exempt.

docs.t: Judge Myong J. Joun (D. Mass.) — Hearings and privacy
docs.x: Judge Myong J. Joun, D. Mass.. Hearings and privacy: Request oral argument in a separate paragraph of the motion or opposition (L.R. 7.1(d)). The court decides whether a hearing is needed and otherwise rules on the papers. Follow the privacy rules (last four digits, minors’ initials, year of birth, city and state). If a restricted item is mentioned in court, the right to have it stricken or redacted from the transcript is waived.

docs.t: Judge Myong J. Joun (D. Mass.) — Junior lawyers
docs.x: Judge Myong J. Joun, D. Mass.. Junior lawyers: Review the court’s standing order on courtroom opportunities for relatively inexperienced attorneys. The court strongly encourages the lawyer who wrote most of the briefing to argue it.

docs.t: Judge Leo T. Sorokin (D. Mass.) — Courtesy copies

docs.x: Judge Leo T. Sorokin, D. Mass.. Junior lawyers: Counsel must review the Standing Order Regarding Courtroom Opportunities for Relatively Inexperienced Attorneys (March 15, 2017), which encourages relatively inexperienced lawyers to take part in hearings and arguments.

docs.t: Judge Angel Kelley (D. Mass.) — Courtesy copies

docs.t: Judge Margaret R. Guzman (D. Mass.) — Before you file
docs.x: Judge Margaret R. Guzman, D. Mass.. Before you file: Confer in good faith to resolve or narrow issues before any motion (L.R. 7.1(a)(2) and 37.1). Failing to do so may result in denial of the motion. Follow L.R. 5.1 (double spacing), 7.1, and 56.1.

docs.t: Judge Margaret R. Guzman (D. Mass.) — Summary judgment briefing
docs.x: Judge Margaret R. Guzman, D. Mass.. Summary judgment briefing: The moving party files a motion, a memorandum of up to 20 pages, and a statement of material facts filed concurrently. Opposition is due in 21 days, up to 20 pages, with a unified statement of material facts that responds to each of the movant’s facts. A reply is allowed as of right within 7 days (not the 14 days in L.R. 56.1), up to five pages. A reply may also include a separate response to additional facts the opposition raised. A longer reply or more time needs leave, and sur-replies aren’t allowed without leave.

docs.t: Judge Margaret R. Guzman (D. Mass.) — Cross-motions
docs.x: Judge Margaret R. Guzman, D. Mass.. Cross-motions: Plaintiff files first (20 pages with a statement of facts). Defendant has 30 days for a single combined opposition and cross-motion memorandum (30 pages) with its own statement of facts. Plaintiff has 21 days for a combined reply and opposition (20 pages) and a final unified statement of facts that carries forward all prior facts and responses. Defendant has 7 days for a reply (5 pages).

docs.t: Judge Margaret R. Guzman (D. Mass.) — Statements of material fact
docs.x: Judge Margaret R. Guzman, D. Mass.. Statements of material fact: Number the moving party’s facts in a document headed “[Moving Party’s] Statement of Material Facts.” The opposing party restates each fact in the same order with its response directly beneath, then adds a section titled “Statement of Additional Material Facts” starting with the next number. The reply follows the same pattern. Facts in the movant’s statement are deemed admitted unless controverted with record citations (L.R. 56.1).

docs.t: Judge Margaret R. Guzman (D. Mass.) — Exhibits and privacy
docs.x: Judge Margaret R. Guzman, D. Mass.. Exhibits and privacy: File exhibits in chronological order with a descriptive table of contents, labeled by number, and continue the numbering in responses and replies. Cite exhibits already filed instead of refiling copies. Follow the privacy rules (last four digits, minors’ initials, year of birth, city and state).

docs.t: Judge Allison D. Burroughs (D. Mass.) — Courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Allison D. Burroughs, D. Mass.. Courtesy copies: Don’t submit a paper courtesy copy of any electronic document unless the court asks for one. In the MDL she manages, she likewise ordered that no courtesy copies are necessary.

docs.x: Judge Allison D. Burroughs, D. Mass.. Everything else: I found no separate motion-practice standing order for Judge Burroughs. docs.x: Judge Denise J. Casper, D. Mass.. docs.t: Judge Denise J. Casper (D. Mass.) — Case management
docs.x: Judge Denise J. Casper, D. Mass.. Case management: At the initial conference she sets the fact discovery schedule, the deadline to amend pleadings, the summary judgment deadline, and expert deadlines if needed. She asks whether a settlement demand has been made and sets a short date for one if not, and asks about interest in a magistrate judge mediation. Status conferences usually follow the close of fact discovery and may be by Zoom. Be ready to discuss sequencing or bifurcating discovery, and whether expert discovery can wait until after summary judgment. She will consider bifurcation if you explain why it is warranted.

docs.t: Judge Denise J. Casper (D. Mass.) — Discovery motions
docs.x: Judge Denise J. Casper, D. Mass.. Discovery motions: She typically refers discovery motions to the magistrate judge, usually without a hearing. She checks that the L.R. 37.1 conferral certification was filed and may order further conferral if the discussion looks pro forma.

docs.t: Judge Denise J. Casper (D. Mass.) — Dispositive motions
docs.x: Judge Denise J. Casper, D. Mass.. Dispositive motions: Replies need leave, usually capped at 10 pages, and sur-replies are not typically allowed. She typically holds hearings on motions to dismiss and summary judgment and often sets time limits. Post-argument briefs are rare. On summary judgment, the movant emails the opposing side a Word version of its statement of undisputed facts when it files. The opposing party answers each fact paragraph by paragraph in that same Word document with record citations, filing it and serving the Word version. The movant then responds to any separately identified disputed facts in the same document with its reply.

docs.t: Judge Denise J. Casper (D. Mass.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Denise J. Casper, D. Mass.. Trial: Trial dates are usually set at a status conference or after summary judgment. Motions in limine are typically due two weeks before trial, with oppositions, witness and exhibit lists, voir dire, and jury instructions due a week before. Also send her a Word copy of the proposed jury instructions and verdict form. Courtesy copies of trial exhibits are required electronically only, typically the week before trial. Agreed exhibits are pre-marked with numbers and disputed ones with letters, with a joint chart giving each objection and the response. She typically sets a total time limit for each side’s whole case, seats eight civil jurors, and requires use of the podium for witness examination. A trial brief isn’t required but helps on pre-trial issues.

docs.t: Judge Denise J. Casper (D. Mass.) — Remote proceedings and courtroom
docs.x: Judge Denise J. Casper, D. Mass.. Remote proceedings and courtroom: She continues to hold civil scheduling and status conferences by Zoom and will consider Zoom for civil non-evidentiary motion hearings for good cause if the other side doesn’t object. Before a trial, ask her courtroom deputy to arrange a preview of the courtroom technology.

docs.t: Judge John J. McConnell Jr. (D.R.I.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge John J. McConnell Jr., D.R.I.. Discovery disputes: No discovery motion may be filed until you’ve tried in good faith to resolve the dispute with opposing counsel. If that fails, you must first have an informal conference with the Court, arranged through the judge’s case manager. This language is now in the district judges’ pretrial scheduling orders (court notice of August 2, 2021). Chief Judge McConnell’s case manager (as listed in the 2021 notice): Ryan Jackson, (401) 752-7213.

docs.t: Judge John J. McConnell Jr. (D.R.I.) — Rule 16(b) scheduling conference
docs.x: Judge John J. McConnell Jr., D.R.I.. Rule 16(b) scheduling conference: Lead counsel must confer beforehand about exchanging information, disputed facts, legal issues, the discovery contemplated, settlement, and possible referral to ADR. Each party asserting a claim (including a counterclaim or cross-claim) files a written statement of no more than three pages summarizing the facts and legal issues, at least seven days before the conference in the standard notice. Trial counsel, including counsel admitted pro hac vice, must attend unless excused.

docs.t: Judge John J. McConnell Jr. (D.R.I.) — Final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge John J. McConnell Jr., D.R.I.. Final pretrial conference: Be ready to give the trial length and scheduling conflicts, a witness list in order with the length of direct and cross, any special witness needs, how exhibits will be presented and which come in without objection, and whether testimony will be by deposition, with designation deadlines. Unless the court orders otherwise, motions in limine and memoranda are due 14 days before jury empanelment, with objections 7 days after that. Trial counsel must confer and give the court a paper list of exhibits to be admitted without objection 7 days before empanelment.

docs.t: Judge John J. McConnell Jr. (D.R.I.) — Trial notice and settlement
docs.x: Judge John J. McConnell Jr., D.R.I.. Trial notice and settlement: Voir dire questions and, in civil cases, a brief statement of the facts are due by the date in the trial notice. A settlement must be reported to the clerk and a stipulation of dismissal filed at least seven days before empanelment, or jury costs and fees may be assessed for unreasonable lateness.

docs.t: Judge John J. McConnell Jr. (D.R.I.) — ADR referral
docs.x: Judge John J. McConnell Jr., D.R.I.. ADR referral: A standard order refers cases to mediation. Parties, lead counsel, and a representative with full settlement authority must attend in person. Mediation briefs go to the mediator only, not to the other side. No extension of the mediation date without the mediator’s written assent, and the parties must participate in good faith.

docs.t: Judge Gina R. Méndez-Miró (D.P.R.) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Gina R. Méndez-Miró, D.P.R.. Contacting chambers: Don’t call chambers at any time, especially the law clerks’ lines, about case-related questions, scheduling, CM/ECF technical help, calendaring, or court appearances. A motion is the only appropriate way to contact the Court. Chambers staff may not give time estimates for rulings, legal advice, or discuss the merits of any pending case. Every filing on CM/ECF is reviewed daily, so urgent matters in a filing will get prompt attention.

docs.t: Judge Gina R. Méndez-Miró (D.P.R.) — Who to contact instead
docs.x: Judge Gina R. Méndez-Miró, D.P.R.. Who to contact instead: Criminal matters go to the Courtroom Deputy. Questions about filings go to the assigned Docket Clerk or Docket Quality Analyst. CM/ECF technical questions go to the Help Desk at (787) 772-3449. Law clerks don’t handle the calendar or CM/ECF.

docs.t: Judge Gina R. Méndez-Miró (D.P.R.) — Consequences and expectations
docs.x: Judge Gina R. Méndez-Miró, D.P.R.. Consequences and expectations: Any direct or indirect violation will result in sanctions. Attorneys are absolutely prohibited from contacting chambers about their appearance before the Court, and are expected to appear on time. Calls to the Court and Clerk’s Office must conform to the Canons of Professional Conduct and Judicial Ethics.

docs.t: Judge Raúl M. Arias-Marxuach (D.P.R.) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Raúl M. Arias-Marxuach, D.P.R.. Contacting chambers: Chief Judge Arias-Marxuach issued a Standing Order on September 20, 2019 on communications by counsel and their staff with his chambers. I couldn’t read it, but Judge Méndez-Miró’s 2023 order says hers was adapted from his on the same subject: no calls to chambers or law clerks about case matters, scheduling, or filing help, and a motion is the proper way to contact the Court. Read the order itself before relying on this.

docs.t: Judge Raúl M. Arias-Marxuach (D.P.R.) — Other standing orders
docs.x: Judge Raúl M. Arias-Marxuach, D.P.R.. Other standing orders: He has issued amended standing orders of disqualification (the latest listed is dated January 2, 2024) and a general standing order on transcript requests in criminal cases. I found no civil motion-practice order for him.

docs.t: Judge Brian E. Murphy (D. Mass.) — Posted orders
docs.x: Judge Brian E. Murphy, D. Mass.. Posted orders: His page posts a Scheduling Order (with topics counsel must address in the joint statement beyond Local Rule 16.1(D)) and a Standing Order Regarding Summary Judgment Motion Practice. Read both before the scheduling conference. He doesn’t require anything extra on case budget and ADR, but will ask about interest in mediation.

docs.t: Judge Brian E. Murphy (D. Mass.) — Case management and discovery
docs.x: Judge Brian E. Murphy, D. Mass.. Case management and discovery: He sets a schedule through summary judgment at the initial conference and holds status conferences at the close of discovery and on request. He generally won’t bifurcate discovery. Move for a protective order as soon as the need appears. He prefers to resolve discovery motions himself rather than refer them, usually holds a hearing after reviewing the filings, and rules from the bench. He stresses compliance with L.R. 37.1(b) and will hear emergency discovery motions only if the parties have meaningfully conferred.

docs.t: Judge Brian E. Murphy (D. Mass.) — Dispositive motions
docs.x: Judge Brian E. Murphy, D. Mass.. Dispositive motions: No extra requirements beyond the page limits in L.R. 7.1(b). Courtesy copies are appreciated for large records but not required. Additional briefs need leave, and replies or sur-replies are typically limited to five pages. He decides motions to dismiss case by case (possibly on the papers) and generally holds a hearing on summary judgment without time limits. Post-argument briefs are allowed if helpful.

docs.t: Judge Brian E. Murphy (D. Mass.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Brian E. Murphy, D. Mass.. Pretrial and trial: He requires a trial brief. Deadlines for voir dire, jury instructions, verdict forms, witness and exhibit lists, and motions in limine are typically set three weeks before trial at the initial pretrial conference. Send an electronic Word copy of proposed voir dire, instructions, and verdict forms to the Courtroom clerk. Courtesy copies of trial exhibits are required one week before trial, in a tabbed binder. Pre-mark exhibits with a single numbering series (Exhibit 13, grouped as 13.1, 13.2), with no letters and no separate plaintiff and defendant series, and numbers never change. He aims to resolve motions in limine and Daubert motions before empanelment. Civil trials run 9 AM to 1 PM with a 12-person jury, and he may set time limits. He provides a draft jury charge and asks counsel for redline changes.

docs.t: Judge Brian E. Murphy (D. Mass.) — Remote proceedings

docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. Scheduling and case management (survey): He does not as a rule convene in-person scheduling conferences. docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. docs.x: Judge Richard G. Stearns, D. Mass.. Trial practice (survey): A trial brief is required in civil and criminal cases. Agreed exhibits are pre-marked numerically, objected-to exhibits by letter. Civil openings are typically limited to 25 minutes and closings to 45, with strict limits for trials over a week. He seats 8 civil jurors, allows no attorney voir dire, and holds no sidebar conferences during trial.

docs.x: Judge Julia Kobick, D. Mass.. Discovery and dispositive motions (survey): She usually resolves discovery motions herself, sometimes referring them to a magistrate judge, and holds a hearing only if the dispute is complex or she has questions. Emergency discovery motions are entertained rarely, and only in true emergencies. Counsel should meaningfully confer before dispositive motions. On summary judgment, the opposing party should put its response under each fact in the movant’s concise statement so the fact and response are in one document. docs.t: Judge Julia Kobick (D. Mass.) — Trial practice (survey)
docs.x: Judge Julia Kobick, D. Mass.. Trial practice (survey): A trial brief is required. POLICY REGARDING TELEPHONIC APPEARANCES: Telephonic appearances are not permitted in lieu of personal appearances unless the Court has provided prior written permission for a party to appear telephonically. A request to appear by telephone must be made in writing at least two business days prior to the scheduled appearance and must state the reason why an exception should be made. Requests will never be granted for trials or evidentiary hearings, for which all counsel and witnesses must appear in person. Requests should be submitted electronically via CM-ECF or via fax to (212) 805-6326.

docs.t: Judge Jed S. Rakoff (S.D.N.Y.) — 7. Proposed Jury Charges
docs.x: Judge Jed S. Rakoff, S.D.N.Y.. 7. Proposed Jury Charges: In all jury cases, whether civil or criminal, proposed jury charges must be submitted to the Court at least one week before trial. Any proposed jury charge submitted thereafter will not be considered by the Court, except upon a showing that the proposed charge relates to an issue that could not reasonably have been expected to arise at trial. In addition, the Court’s standard practice is to give the jury a one- page preliminary instruction shortly before or after opening statements, highlighting some of the issues and legal requirements in the case. The parties should submit their proposals in that regard at least three business days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Jed S. Rakoff (S.D.N.Y.) — 8. Proposed Voir Dire Requests
docs.x: Judge Jed S. Rakoff, S.D.N.Y.. 8. Proposed Voir Dire Requests: In all jury cases, whether civil or criminal, proposed voir dire requests must be submitted to the Court at least three business days before the start of jury selection . In both civil and criminal cases, the jury will be selected by the traditional “jury box” method. The Court does not use jury questionnaires. Except in rare circumstances, the Court will conduct all questioning at voir dire.

Any party referencing a proposed trial exhibit in such motion papers must submit a courtesy copy of that exhibit to the Court along with the motion papers.
