docs.t: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead (W.D. Wash.) — Extensions and scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead, W.D. Wash.. Extensions and scheduling (trap): Parties may agree to extend the time to answer without filing anything. Initial scheduling order deadlines may be extended by contacting the courtroom deputy, with no stipulation filed. Deadlines falling before the dispositive motions deadline may be extended by a Stipulated Notice (not a motion) in the judge’s prescribed language, only if all parties stipulate (non-opposition won’t do), the deadline was not previously extended, and no hearing or related final-submission date changes. Otherwise dates are firm absent good cause, and the judge generally won’t shorten the gap between the dispositive motion deadline and trial. Don’t file notices of unavailability; they have no effect on deadlines.

docs.t: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead (W.D. Wash.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead, W.D. Wash.. Motions (trap): Meet and confer before any Rule 12(b) motion to see if amendment can avoid it; the motion must include a certification of conferral. Don’t oppose a timely motion, or withhold a stipulation, to amend. Daubert motions are due by the dispositive motion deadline and can’t be raised or renewed as motions in limine. Oral argument may be requested but is not granted as a matter of course; the deputy schedules it, and the noting date is not the hearing date. Less experienced attorneys and those from historically underrepresented backgrounds are encouraged to argue, and more than one attorney may argue per party.

docs.t: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead (W.D. Wash.) — Cross-motions for summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead, W.D. Wash.. Cross-motions for summary judgment (trap): Anticipated cross-motions must be briefed in four sequential briefs, not six: opening 8,400 words; combined opening/opposition 10,500; combined opposition/reply 10,500; reply 4,200. The court assumes the defendant files first, but the parties may choose. File a stipulated motion proposing the schedule and word limits before the first brief; all briefing must be complete by the dispositive motion deadline.

docs.t: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead (W.D. Wash.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead, W.D. Wash.. Discovery (trap): Discovery motions are a last resort. Good-faith conferral requires affirmative suggestions and compromise, not just stating positions; the court will deny or strike a motion for failure to confer. Motions must state the grounds and relief with specificity or be denied. The court urges use of the LCR 37(a)(2) expedited joint motion procedure. Don’t file initial disclosures or expert reports unless ordered or at issue. Deposition objections must be concise and non-suggestive (e.g., “Objection, compound”); no conferring with the witness while a question is pending except on privilege; instruct not to answer only to preserve privilege, enforce a court limit, or present a Rule 30(d)(3) motion.

docs.t: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead (W.D. Wash.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead, W.D. Wash.. Hearings: Hearings are in person in Courtroom 16A, Seattle, unless ordered otherwise. On Zoom (if warranted): each participant needs their own camera and microphone, video on, muted unless speaking, no screenshare, professional attire, a quiet room (not a car); recording is illegal. Telephonic proceedings use the court’s conference line with credentials from the deputy; use a landline if possible and identify yourself each time you speak.

docs.x: Judge Jamal N. Whitehead, W.D. Wash.. docs.x: Judge Robert J. Bryan, W.D. Wash.. Deposition testimony is protected only if designated on the record and then identified in a Notice of Designation served within 14 days of transcript delivery. docs.x: Judge Nannette Jolivette Brown, E.D. La.. Discovery: Discovery is typically not stayed while motions are pending, even motions to dismiss or remand; claims remain subject to disclosure and discovery until dismissed. The court strictly adheres to Rule 26.

docs.x: Judge Arthur J. Schwab, W.D. Pa.. Extensions and discovery (trap): The court is not inclined to grant extensions. docs.t: Judge Arthur J. Schwab (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Arthur J. Schwab, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Extensions to file pretrial motions are generally granted; the proposed order should include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language. The court uses a written plea colloquy, available on request. Witness lists with offers of proof are filed under seal and not served. docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: A post-discovery status conference is held within 30 days after discovery closes; meet and confer beforehand on settlement and any planned summary judgment motion, and the court then sets deadlines. When responding to a statement of facts, reprint each original fact followed by the response, seriatim. Otherwise follow Local Rule 56.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Settlement and pretrial
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Settlement and pretrial: Settlement conferences are for cases headed to jury trial. Lead trial counsel, client representatives, and any insurer representative (even with a coverage dispute) must attend in person with ultimate settlement authority, without needing to consult anyone. The same attendees must appear in person at the final pretrial conference. Motions in limine and Daubert deadlines are set by order. Confer first and file a Local Civil Rule 16.1.C.4 certificate. Each motion in limine (or each motion’s portion of an omnibus brief) is capped at 5 double-spaced pages.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — TROs and injunctions
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. TROs and injunctions: No TRO if the opposing party has been served, if the motion lacks a certification that prompt service cannot be made, or if it lacks a Rule 65(b)(1)(A) affidavit or verified complaint. Arrange any bond when filing. Support with affidavits attaching all relevant documents; responses should include affidavits. Be ready to argue and present witnesses immediately.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Objections, R&Rs, and bankruptcy appeals
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Objections, R&Rs, and bankruptcy appeals: Object on the record immediately; if no reporter is present, request one. Briefs on objections to a magistrate judge’s report and recommendation are capped at 15 pages. Bankruptcy appeals: appellant’s brief 30 days after the notice of appeal, appellee’s 30 days later, reply 14 days after that.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Confer before moving to extend the pretrial-motion deadline, and include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language in the proposed order. File only after the status conference unless it falls after the deadline; premature motions are denied. Pre-plea presentence reports require the defendant’s written consent in the form set out in the procedures. Motions to travel must state the government’s and Pretrial Services’ positions. Protective order, pretrial, and discovery motions require good-faith conferral and a certificate of conferral under Local Civil Rule 16.1.C.4.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Motions and briefing (trap): A brief must accompany every motion except motions for continuance, extension of time, to compel discovery, or to present an uncontested matter. Responses (with brief) are due 14 days after service, but 28 days for dispositive motions. Replies are allowed as of right only for dispositive motions and motions for injunctive relief (14 days after the response); otherwise only with leave, then due in 7 days. Briefs may not exceed 25 pages without leave. Oral argument only on matters the court selects, usually complex ones. No courtesy copies unless requested. An unexcused failure to file a motion or response on time can lead to summary grant or denial of the motion; noncompliance with the case management order can lead to dismissal or judgment.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Motions must comply with Local Rule 56, with a concise statement of material facts citing the record and an appendix under LR 56.B.3. The counter statement must track the movant’s paragraphs and address every disputed fact; a reply statement is limited to new facts raised by the non-movant. Unsupported propositions may be rejected or the record read as the opponent presents it, and facts not specifically controverted are deemed admitted (LR 56.E).

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Communications and conferences
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Communications and conferences: In urgent situations, letters or phone calls to chambers are allowed (for example, a 1–2 day extension when something unexpected prevents a timely filing), but the judge strongly prefers a docketed motion. Law clerks may be contacted about status. Phone participation in case management and status conferences is allowed mainly for out-of-town counsel. Lead trial counsel must attend conciliation and pretrial settlement conferences in person. Trial counsel must attend all conferences with settlement authority or with principals immediately available by phone; principals are encouraged to attend settlement conferences. At settlement conferences a principal with full authority must appear.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Case management and discovery
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Case management and discovery: Initial case management conference about 60 days after all counsel appear, followed by the case management order and ADR referral order. Discovery is normally 150 days. Pending motions, including motions to dismiss and for summary judgment, do not stay discovery or any other deadline; stays are granted only when grounds are “obvious.” The discovery deadline is extended only with leave, by a motion giving reasons and listing every prior extension; the proposed order must extend all remaining pretrial deadlines. Counsel must confer in good faith on discovery and scheduling disputes. Rule 11 and Rule 37 motions must be briefed and are generally decided at the end of the case; the judge is hesitant to award fees as sanctions.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — TROs and injunctions
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. TROs and injunctions: Opposing counsel must be identified and contacted; ex parte rulings are extremely rare. The judge prefers a prompt status conference, then schedules a preliminary injunction hearing promptly or as counsel request.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial (trap): Pretrial narrative statements must specify all material facts and case-in-chief exhibits; anything not specified may be excluded. Parties file the posted Pretrial Stipulation (relief sought, jurisdiction, stipulated and disputed facts and law, deposition testimony, experts, and trial days estimated in 6-hour days). Non-jury cases: with its narrative statement, plaintiff files numbered proposed findings and conclusions with record cites and a pretrial brief; defendant’s counter-findings must track plaintiff’s numbering. Revised findings may follow the transcript (plaintiff’s 30 days after the transcript, defendant’s 30 days after plaintiff’s). A pretrial settlement conference follows resolution of dispositive motions, and a Trial Management Order then sets trial deadlines. Challenged deposition designations require a memorandum on admissi

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Trial management order (civil)
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Trial management order (civil): Plaintiff’s exhibits are numbered and defendant’s lettered. Motions in limine briefs are limited to 15 pages; the judge generally rules on them shortly before or at trial. Substantive jury instructions with authority are filed by the set date. Objections must quote the full instruction, identify the objectionable language, cite authority, and offer an alternative; argumentative or formula instructions will not be given. Stipulations cover expert CVs (read into the record if unopposed), facts, exhibits, medical records, expert reports, and a brief statement of claims and defenses for the jury. The jury is 8 persons.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Trial: A firm civil trial date is set after the final pretrial settlement conference, sometimes with an earlier back-up date; other obligations of counsel and witnesses generally won’t move the firm date. Jury trials Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Jurors generally may not take notes. The judge conducts voir dire; counsel may propose added questions by the order’s deadline. Visual aids in opening need all counsel’s consent; an exhibit must generally be offered before substantive testimony about it. Instructions are discussed at an informal charge conference, and formal objections are made after the charge is read. During deliberations, counsel must be able to return within 15 minutes.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Proposed orders on extensions must include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language. Special voir dire and points for charge filed after the deadlines in the trial management order are deemed waived absent good cause. No special interrogatories; Apprendi issues are charged as elements. The government is encouraged to disclose Jencks material at least 5 business days before trial. A defendant needs a formal motion for leave to travel outside the district even if the AUSA and probation consent. Sentencing memoranda are optional but must come early enough to be considered.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Special case types
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Special case types: Patent cases follow a posted case management order under the Local Patent Rules, with a Rule 16 conference within 30 days after the claim construction ruling and summary judgment motions 30 days after expert depositions close (response 30 days, reply 15, sur-reply 10). The judge uses a standard Social Security order and requires a RICO statement after the initial status conference in RICO cases. Bankruptcy appeals are briefed under Bankruptcy Rule 8009; oral argument only on request.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Motion form and response deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Motion form and response deadlines (trap): Every motion is two documents: the motion and a separate brief. Evidentiary materials go in a separate tabbed document, and a proposed order stating the specific relief must be attached; a response must also attach a proposed order. The opposing party must file a response to every motion, even if it does not oppose; letters are not responses, and failure to respond may be deemed consent. Responses are due 14 days after service for discovery motions, 7 days for motions in limine, 30 days for summary judgment, and 21 days for all other motions.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Page limits and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Page limits and format (trap): Briefs are limited to 10 pages for discovery motions, 5 for motions in limine, 20 (excluding tables) for summary judgment, and 15 for all other motions. Text and footnotes in 12-point font with 1-inch margins; text double-spaced, footnotes may be single-spaced. Evading these limits gets the brief stricken or the excess treated as outside the record without notice. Reply briefs are discouraged and need leave except on summary judgment; they must identify the novel matter warranting reply. Replies and surreplies (also by leave only) are limited to 10 pages.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: File a separate statement of material facts with numbered paragraphs, each citing the evidence; the opponent files a separate paragraph-by-paragraph response citing and attaching evidence for each disputed fact. The argument must, for each claim, set out its elements with current Third Circuit authority if available. Noncompliance may result in the motion being decided against that party. Oral argument is generally not held on summary judgment, though it is on most other substantive motions, especially motions to dismiss.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Correspondence, chambers, and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Correspondence, chambers, and courtesy copies: Correspondence is disfavored except to report status (e.g., mediation); to get action, file a motion. No letter briefs. Law clerks may be contacted about scheduling and administrative matters only. No courtesy copies unless requested, except evidentiary materials over 25 pages, which should be marked, tabbed, and furnished to chambers. The judge prefers in-person attendance at conferences but allows phone attendance on request for good reason.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions and discovery
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Extensions and discovery: Extension motions must explain why deadlines could not be met (and, for discovery, what remains and how long it will take), and the proposed order must list every affected date. The judge may rule without a response and is stricter as the case advances. Discovery is typically set at 90 to 120 days; if longer is allowed, do not expect an extension. Discovery disputes not requiring review of written responses or a written order are resolved by phone; otherwise file a motion and appear in person. Expert discovery and any Daubert hearing are generally scheduled after fact discovery.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and settlement
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and settlement: At least four civil conferences: an initial Rule 16 conference, a close-of-fact-discovery conference (seek any extension before it), a pretrial conference, and a conference on the jury selection date. The judge discusses settlement in jury cases; in nonjury cases only if complex and all parties consent, otherwise referring to an ADR panel lawyer or private mediator. No settlement discussions while a dispositive motion is pending, and none on jury selection day.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Injunctions
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Injunctions: Expedited hearings are scheduled as needed; TROs rarely issue without both parties present, and if the judge is unavailable, the miscellaneous judge hears TRO motions. Proposed findings and conclusions are required in matters decided by the court, except emergency injunctive relief ruled on from the bench.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Court sits Monday through Thursday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; counsel must be available at 9:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Sidebars are highly disfavored: raise issues at the daily 4:30 p.m. conference, or the objection will generally be resolved in front of the jury. Motions in limine are due by the court-set date or, if none, at least 1 week before trial. Openings and closings are limited to 1 hour per side and may not be split among co-counsel; the jury is charged before closings. Plaintiffs mark exhibits with numbers, defendants with letters; give the court a copy of all exhibits 2 weeks before trial, noting agreed authenticity and admissibility, plus a second set for the record. One attorney per witness; no greeting witnesses, no first names, no pacing. File one combined set of jury instructions marking agreed ones and identifying the profferin

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Motions must be in writing, and oral argument is generally scheduled. Submit proposed voir dire and jury instructions (joint instructions not required) before the pretrial conference; witness lists and exhibits are exchanged on the first day of trial. Tentative guideline findings generally issue the day before sentencing; PSR objections are resolved at sentencing.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Response and reply deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Response and reply deadlines (trap): Responses: 21 days from service for motions to dismiss, 28 days for summary judgment, and 7 days for all other motions unless a specific order says otherwise. No separate briefing order is needed, and a late response may be deemed a concession. Replies without leave: 7 days after service of the response for motions to dismiss and 14 days for summary judgment. Replies on any other motion, and all sur-replies, need leave obtained in advance. The court may decide unopposed motions or those not affecting substantial rights (e.g., withdrawal, setting a conference, most extensions) without waiting for a response.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Page limits and format
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Page limits and format: Briefs on motions to dismiss and summary judgment: 25 pages, excluding tables and exhibits; replies 15 pages. All other motions: 10-page briefs and 10-page replies. 12-point font including footnotes, one-inch margins, double-spaced text (footnotes may be single-spaced). Skip extended recitations of settled standards and keep fact sections non-argumentative with record citations.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Motions generally: Each motion must state whether the movant discussed it with all other parties and their positions. Joint, consented, or uncontested motions must be so titled, and a multi-party motion lacking everyone’s consent must say so on page one. Substantive motions need a separate brief; discovery, extension, and continuance motions generally do not. File a proposed order stating the specific relief as a separate attachment, with both the motion and any response. Cite deposition passages by page and line; the court strongly urges filing non-confidential deposition transcripts in full. Motions to amend must attach a redline of the proposed amended document. Letters to the court are not motions or responses. Flag urgency in the motion; the court may hold a phone conference instead of written responses.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Rule 12 conferral (trap)
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Rule 12 conferral (trap): Before any Rule 12(b) motion, meet and confer about whether amendment can cure the defect. Every such motion must include a certificate of good-faith conferral.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): Meet and confer before filing to see whether claims or issues can be stipulated away. The movant files its concise statement and sends the opponent a Word copy. The opponent responds paragraph by paragraph within the movant’s document, adds any additional facts at the end, and returns a Word copy; replies to additional facts go in the same document, so one combined statement is filed. The court uses the last-filed version. Don’t duplicate the movant’s exhibits; cite exhibits by ECF number and page where possible.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery and case-management disputes
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Discovery and case-management disputes: After conferring, file a brief joint motion covering the nature and scope of the dispute, each side’s position, counsel’s availability over the next 7 days, and any time sensitivity. The court will then rule, set briefing, or set a hearing.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Extensions: Extension motions need a certificate of conferral stating whether the other side consents and, if it opposes, whether it will respond; any response is due within 7 days of filing. The April 2021 chart instead says to tell the court by telephone immediately; the October 2024 order is newer. Proposed orders must include the new date certain (or a blank for it) and reset every affected deadline.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies and argument
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies and argument: If a brief with its appendices or exhibits reaches 50 pages, furnish a paper courtesy copy after e-filing so the ECF header appears. No other courtesy copies unless requested. Motions may be decided without oral argument; a party may request it if it will materially help.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. The opposing party must file a separate response to every motion unless it is joint or unopposed; letters are not motions or responses, and a late response may be treated as a concession. Responses: 7 days for discovery and case management motions, 30 days for summary judgment, 14 days for everything else. Replies may be filed without leave within 7 days (14 for summary judgment) and should address only new matters; surreplies need advance leave. The court does not otherwise issue briefing orders. Motions to amend must attach the proposed pleading in redline, state other parties’ positions, and e

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Page limits and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Page limits and format (trap): Briefs: 10 pages for discovery, case management, and in limine motions; 25 pages (excluding tables) for motions to dismiss and summary judgment; 15 pages for all others. Replies: 15 pages on dismissal or summary judgment, 10 otherwise. 12-point text (footnotes at least 10-point), 1-inch margins, double-spaced text. Material that evades the limits will be treated as outside the record without notice. The judge discourages long background and recitations of settled standards. Arguments must cite current Supreme Court or Third Circuit authority where available.

docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies (trap): If a brief with its appendices or exhibits reaches 50 pages or more, deliver a paper courtesy copy when filing: 3-hole punched in black binders no thicker than 3 inches, cover and spine labeled with case name, number, subject, ECF document, and filing party. No other courtesy copies unless requested.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery and case management disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Discovery and case management disputes (trap): Lead counsel must confer in person or by phone, agree on the scope of the dispute, and contact the law clerk or courtroom deputy for a telephone conference, usually held immediately or within 24 hours. A conference is required before any motion to compel, for sanctions, or for a non-consensual protective order; skipping it can lead to deferral or denial. If the court sets a phone conference before a response is due, the non-movant need not file a written response. “Sauce for the goose” arguments rarely persuade. Fact discovery is ordinarily 150 days. Discovery extension motions, filed before the deadline, must list discovery done and planned, show good cause, list prior extensions, and attach a proposed order with the new date; a first request is routinely granted.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Communications, extensions, and oral argument
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Communications, extensions, and oral argument: Communicate by motion with a proposed order, not letters; the court dockets any case-related correspondence it receives. Call chambers for emergencies or agreed short extensions; unopposed extensions of 5 days or less may be requested by phone. Staff contacts must state that all parties know and concur. Extension motions should state opposing positions, list prior extensions, come at least 5 business days before the deadline, and give the date certain; if several deadlines move, restate them all. Opponents of short extensions must show actual prejudice. Oral argument is often set on motions that would dispose of a claim or defense, sanctions and disqualification motions, and successive scheduling requests, and the court often rules from the bench.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and settlement
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and settlement: Counsel must confer in person or by phone (not email) before any conference so no one is surprised. The attending lawyer, ordinarily lead trial counsel, must know the case well enough to stipulate, argue pending motions, and discuss settlement. Phone conferences are the norm, but settlement conferences, final pretrial conferences, and oral arguments are not ordinarily by phone. For phone conferences, give chambers direct numbers by 4 p.m. the day before (the initial case management order says 48 hours ahead at 412-208-7433). Initial case management conference within 30 days of a responsive pleading or Rule 12 motion; lead counsel needs full settlement authority, and clients and insurers must be reachable by phone. The Rule 26(f) conference must be in person or by phone with all trial counsel; the order includes a Rule 502(d) non

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Sealing and TROs
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Sealing and TROs: Motions to seal must state the specific factual and legal basis, and the proposed order must include the court’s language allowing it to be vacated for cause. TRO and injunction movants must show serious efforts to contact the other side by Rule 65 affidavit or there will be no hearing or TRO. Arrange any bond at filing; motions and responses need affidavits and proposed findings and conclusions, and counsel must be ready to proceed immediately.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Final pretrial conference: all trial lawyers, parties, and insurer representatives with full authority attend in person; motions in limine, instructions, and other issues are argued and generally decided there. In limine briefs are limited to 10 pages. Witness lists with a one-page offer of proof per witness; a Joint Exhibit List Chart filed and a binder of exhibits delivered to chambers; plaintiffs use numbers and defendants letters. One combined set of jury instructions (disputed ones with each side’s authority) with a Word copy; separate sets are not accepted. Bench trials and hearings: plaintiff’s proposed findings and conclusions within 14 days after the close, defendant’s counter-findings 14 days later, each with a brief of up to 20 pages and a Word copy.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Trial: Trial Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; counsel meet the court at 8:30 a.m., sidebars are disfavored, and issues not raised then are generally decided in open court. The jury is often selected the Wednesday before trial; be in the courtroom by 8:45 a.m. on selection day. Individual voir dire is in chambers with one client representative present. Openings and closings usually 30 minutes per side; in civil trials plaintiff closes last. Co-counsel may not split a witness without advance leave (relaxed for newer lawyers). Next day’s witnesses to opponents by 5 p.m. Exhibits go through the court’s electronic system, which counsel must know how to use. Contact the courtroom deputy (Brian Babik) at least 1 week ahead about trial technology, and give chambers a list of outside devices and who will bring them; Mac users bring their own adapter. Confirm

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Newer lawyers and attorney authority
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Newer lawyers and attorney authority: The judge encourages newer lawyers to handle routine and complex matters alike (discovery motions, summary judgment, evidentiary hearings, trial examinations) and will relax the one-lawyer rule so a more experienced lawyer can back up a newer lawyer’s witness examination, if that does not unduly prolong the proceeding, prejudice the opponent, or result in undue “double dipping.” Newer lawyers examining witnesses should be accompanied and supervised by a more experienced attorney. docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases and sentencing (trap): Extension motions at least 2 days before the motions deadline expires, with Speedy Trial Act exclusion language. In the sample criminal pretrial order, in limine briefs are limited to 5 pages, and unobjected exhibits are marked J-1, J-2, etc. in a joint binder supplied by the government. Sentencing memoranda (usually 7–14 days before sentencing) must address each relevant § 3553(a) factor, with a joint status report on whether an evidentiary hearing is needed. The government must obtain writs for in-custody defendants, give 24 hours’ notice of any bond revocation request, and state its post-sentencing custody position at least 24 hours ahead. Travel mot

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Rule 12 motions: meet and confer (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Rule 12 motions: meet and confer (trap): Before filing any Rule 12 motion, including a Rule 12(c) motion, defense counsel must confer with plaintiff’s counsel on whether the pleading defects can be cured. The motion must include a certificate of good-faith efforts to confer, or it will be denied.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Briefing and summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Briefing and summary judgment (trap): Unless ordered otherwise, a principal brief is limited to 20 pages; the court issues briefing schedules for all motions, setting later due dates and page limits. Routine motions (amendment, extensions, continuances) need no brief but must state whether consent was obtained. The court sets a briefing schedule for Rule 56 motions and typically won’t consider motions filed before discovery closes. For most motions it excuses Local Rule 56’s separate concise and responsive statements of fact; cross-motions are briefed like cross-appeals under FRAP 28.1, and complex cases may use issue-specific briefs. Oral argument may be requested on any motion; the judge encourages junior attorneys to argue.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Brief-writing preferences
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Brief-writing preferences: The posted preferences favor short, plain, active-voice briefs with strong topic sentences, a 1–2 page roadmap introduction, and few block quotes, footnotes, or adjectives. Avoid Latin and legalese (including “arguendo,” “infra,” and “supra”), defined terms, and acronyms; use proper names instead of “Plaintiffs” and “Defendants,” and describe opponents respectfully. Cite cases with parentheticals, preferably direct quotations, rather than extended case analysis.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Discovery (trap): No written discovery or other formal discovery before the initial case management conference and the case management order. Propose a realistic discovery deadline: the court dislikes extension motions and is unlikely to grant them, even on consent. For disputes, after conferring, contact chambers; the court typically asks for brief email summaries and then guides, decides, or orders briefing. No discovery motions until after the email exchange, and Rule 37 expenses will be awarded to the prevailing party when permitted.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Initial conference and ADR (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Initial conference and ADR (trap): The Rule 26(f) report uses the judge’s shortened form (fact and expert discovery subjects, deadlines, Rule 502 order, ESI, protective order). The ADR stipulation must set the session within 60 days of the initial case management conference, list attendees by name and title, and include a representative with full settlement authority, or it will be stricken. The conference is usually in person; out-of-town lead counsel may move to appear by phone or video. Be ready for substantive discussion.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Contact, continuances, and court reporters
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Contact, continuances, and court reporters: Contact Courtroom Deputy Peter Kosloski (peter_kosloski@pawd.uscourts.gov, 412-208-7495) for scheduling and to raise discovery disputes; staff give no legal advice. Continuance motions should propose alternative dates near the original date when all counsel are available; good cause includes illness, family emergency, pre-paid vacation, or a prior court proceeding. In civil cases a court reporter is generally present only for arguments on substantive motions, evidentiary hearings, the final pretrial conference, and trial; counsel should request one if they want something on the record.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Trial and presumptive trial dates
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Trial and presumptive trial dates: In certain cases (usually personal-injury, UM/UIM, and non-complex employment and civil rights cases), the court sets a presumptive trial date about 10–18 months after the initial conference; continuances only in extraordinary circumstances. A separate pretrial order sets trial procedures. Counsel stand when speaking for the record and need permission to approach a witness.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Injunctions and class actions
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Injunctions and class actions: For a TRO or preliminary injunction, the court typically schedules a prompt phone conference; serve the defendant, as ex parte motions are rarely granted. Named plaintiffs in class and collective actions must attend all conferences, hearings, settlement conferences, and mediations (in person or remotely); incentive awards require showing active involvement. Expect close scrutiny at preliminary approval. Individual, non-collective FLSA settlements need no court approval; just file a stipulation of dismissal.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Initial case conference about 40 days after arraignment; don’t seek to extend the pretrial-motion deadline again until after it. The government should be ready to summarize its evidence and discovery. For a change of plea, the government must email any plea agreement and its summary of trial evidence to defense counsel and the court 7 days before the hearing. The judge does not prefer Rule 11(c)(1)(C) agreements; serial extensions of the motions deadline are disfavored absent complexity.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Briefs, page limits, and deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Briefs, page limits, and deadlines (trap): Briefs are filed with every motion except discovery, extension, and continuance motions, and are capped at 20 pages; incorporating earlier briefs is prohibited. Double-spaced, at least 12-point font, paginated. Responses: 21 days for dispositive motions and 14 days for non-dispositive motions unless ordered otherwise. The procedures say replies and sur-replies need leave and are capped at 5 pages, but the attached Order on Motions Practice (Exhibit A) allows dispositive replies within 14 days of the response, up to 10 pages, and caps non-dispositive responses at 5 pages; check the order in your case. Reconsideration motions are due within 7 days, with responses 7 days later.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Conferral certificates (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Conferral certificates (trap): Discovery motions, motions in limine, and Rule 12 motions require a certificate of conferral; email exchanges are not enough. Under the standard Rule 12(b) order, parties (including pro se) must confer about whether amendment can cure the defect; motions lacking the certificate are summarily denied, and a nonmovant who fails to engage may face fees, costs, or denial of later leave to amend. Parties should try not to oppose timely early motions to amend.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Motions generally: Communicate with the court only by motion with a proposed order stating the specific relief; no correspondence unless requested. Oral argument only on selected complex matters, by order; the court may open with its tentative ruling and may rule from the bench. No courtesy copies of documents on CM/ECF, but send a courtesy copy of any exhibits or appendices over 20 pages. The form case management and pretrial orders call for courtesy copies of certain filings concurrently with filing.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Position letters and settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Position letters and settlement (trap): At least 3 business days before every case management, settlement, or pretrial conference, each party faxes a confidential position letter (facts, strengths and weaknesses, settlement posture) to chambers at (412) 208-7487. Do not file or share it. Chief trial counsel, the client, and any insurer or underwriter with full settlement authority (to policy limits) must attend settlement conferences in person. The settlement conference form order also requires each party to submit a confidential proposed settlement agreement within 2 business days of the conference. Be ready to discuss and agree to an ADR option at the case management and settlement conferences.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Case management and discovery
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Case management and discovery: Initial case management conference within 30 days of a responsive pleading; chief trial counsel and parties with full settlement authority attend. A Rule 502(d) order is available on request; no trial date is set at this stage. Discovery generally runs 150 days, with extensions for cause if counsel advanced the case. The form case management order limits written discovery to 25 interrogatories, requests for production, and requests for admission, including subparts, and requires periodic joint discovery status reports. Under the form case management order, discovery motion responses are due within 5 days (excluding weekends and holidays), memoranda are capped at 5 pages, and no replies are allowed. Deposition disputes: written motions are discouraged; contact the court jointly through the law clerk at (412) 208-7480.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Strict compliance with Local Rule 56; the argument must cite current Third Circuit authority establishing the elements of each claim. Noncompliance may result in the motion being decided against the party. The court issues a motions order with deadlines. The form case management order sets 20-page memoranda, responses within 30 days, and 10-page replies within 10 days.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions and TROs
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Extensions and TROs: The court is not inclined to grant extensions; requests must be by motion with a proposed order, good cause, and opposing counsel’s position. Postponing court appearances is granted infrequently. For a TRO, show serious efforts to contact the opposing party, supported by a Rule 65(b) affidavit, or no hearing or TRO. Moving and responding papers must include affidavits.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Trial counsel meet with a law clerk about one week before the final pretrial conference, which is held about one week before trial; pending matters are argued and generally ruled on there. Under the form jury pretrial order: witness lists with 1-page offers of proof due 1 month (plaintiff) and 3 weeks (defendant) before trial; designations 2 weeks before, counter-designations 1 week; motions in limine 2 weeks before with responses 10 days before, 5-page briefs; joint stipulations and supplemental voir dire 10 days before. File one unified set of jury instructions marking agreed and disputed instructions; separate sets are not accepted. Trial briefs are capped at 15 pages and most useful at least 14 days before trial. Exhibit binders for the court at least 3 days before trial per the procedures (2 days in the form orders), plus a Joint Exhibit

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Trial runs Monday through Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; counsel meet with the court at 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Sidebars are highly disfavored; issues not raised at those conferences are generally ruled on in front of the jury. Co-counsel may not split a witness examination or closing. Redirect and recross require leave. About 30 minutes is suggested for opening and closing; witness time limits may be set. Exchange the next day’s witness list by 5:00 p.m. Rule 50 and 52 motions must be written with a brief. In bench trials, file numbered proposed findings and conclusions with a brief of up to 10 pages.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Pretrial conference about a week before trial. Voir dire questions at least 1 week before trial and motions in limine and jury instructions at least 2 weeks before, unless the pretrial order says otherwise; sidebars are not permitted. Jencks material expected by the final pretrial conference; Brady violations may bring sanctions, suppression, dismissal, or contempt. Travel outside Western Pennsylvania requires a formal motion. The pre-sentence order sets objections, position statements, tentative findings, and a telephonic conference before sentencing.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Other case types
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Other case types: Bankruptcy appeals: appellant’s brief within 14 days after docketing and appellee’s 14 days later; replies upon notice to the court. RICO plaintiffs must file a RICO Case Statement within 14 days of the complaint. Time limits for class certification and Social Security actions are strictly enforced. Patent cases follow an initial patent scheduling order under the Local Patent Rules.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Motions (trap): Each motion must state the specific relief, its factual and legal grounds, and whether it was discussed with all other parties and their positions. Every substantive motion needs a separate supporting brief, and a proposed order stating the specific relief (not just “granted”) must be filed as a separate attachment. The opposing party must file a separate response to every motion (with a brief for substantive motions) unless the motion is joint or unopposed. Letters are not motions or responses, and a late response may be deemed a concession. Motions to amend must attach the proposed amended pleading, state other parties’ positions, and explain what new law or newly discovered facts support it. Oral argument is at the court’s discretion; a party may request it.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Response deadlines and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Response deadlines and page limits (trap): Responses: 10 days for discovery and other case management motions; 21 days for motions to dismiss and for judgment on the pleadings; 30 days for summary judgment; 14 days for everything else. Replies within 7 days (14 for summary judgment); surreplies only with advance leave. Briefs: 10 pages for discovery, case management, and in limine motions; 20 pages (excluding tables) for motions to dismiss, judgment on the pleadings, and summary judgment; 15 pages for all others. Replies: 15 pages on dismissal or summary judgment, 10 otherwise. 12-point text (footnotes at least 10-point), 1-inch margins, double-spaced text. Arguments must cite current Supreme Court or Third Circuit authority where available; use Westlaw rather than Lexis cites for unpublished opinions.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Conferral certificates (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Conferral certificates (trap): Rule 12(b) motions are discouraged where amendment can cure the defect; the movant must confer first and file a certificate of conferral on whether the deficiencies can be cured. Motions to modify a scheduling order require conferral and a certificate under LR 16.1.B.5. Discovery motions require an in-person or phone meet-and-confer (email alone is not enough) and a certificate of conferral.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes (trap): Before filing any discovery motion, lead counsel must confer, agree on the scope of the dispute, and contact the law clerk or courtroom deputy to request a telephone conference, usually set within 3 days. The court may then direct a motion. The court will not take calls during depositions: put the objection on the record and proceed. Discovery generally runs 150 days and is extended for good cause only if counsel advanced the case. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery; phased discovery may be considered.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Communications and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Communications and courtesy copies: Communicate by motion with a proposed order, not letters; call chambers only in emergencies, and don’t copy the court on correspondence between counsel. Staff may be contacted on administrative matters and status, but counsel must confirm the contact is with all parties’ knowledge and concurrence. No courtesy copies unless requested. Requested copies of voluminous filings must be ECF-stamped printouts, 3-hole punched in black binders no thicker than 3 inches, labeled on cover and spine. Participants’ pronoun or title preferences may be sent by email to tyler_klein@pawd.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and settlement
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and settlement: Joint pre-conference statement (3 pages maximum: facts, claims and defenses, discovery status, trial cost and time estimate, relief sought) due at least 5 business days before the initial case management and post-discovery conferences, and before settlement conferences. Each party may add an optional voluntary position statement of up to 8 pages. The initial conference is usually within 30 days of all answers and is presumptively by phone; lead trial counsel must participate. Settlement conferences, final pretrial conferences, and oral arguments are not ordinarily by phone. Settlement conferences (mainly for jury cases): lead trial counsel and client representatives with full authority attend in person; insurer representatives with full authority up to policy limits attend in person or by phone. No one leaves until excused.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions, sealing, and TROs
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Extensions, sealing, and TROs: Extension requests: a short motion with supporting facts, opposing counsel’s position, and a proposed scheduling order adjusting affected dates, filed at least 5 business days before the deadline. Opponents of short extensions must show actual prejudice. Motions to seal must state the specific factual and legal basis, and the proposed order must include the court’s required language that sealing may be vacated for cause on motion or by the court. TRO and injunction movants must show substantial efforts to contact the other side, by Rule 65 affidavit, or there will be no hearing or TRO. Arrange any bond at filing, support papers with affidavits, and be ready to argue and present witnesses immediately.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial and trial: Final pretrial conference: all trial counsel, the client representative, and the insurer representative, with full authority, attend in person; pending trial issues are argued and generally ruled on, and time limits may be set. Motions in limine and Daubert deadlines come in the pretrial or post-discovery order. One combined set of jury instructions (agreed instructions labeled; disputed ones with each side’s authority), with a Word copy emailed to the law clerks; separate sets are not accepted. Joint Exhibit List Chart filed and two tabbed exhibit binders (black, 3 inches maximum) delivered to chambers; plaintiffs use numbers, defendants letters. Trial Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; counsel available at 8:30 a.m. and after the jury leaves. Co-counsel may not split a witness without advance leave, Rule 50 motions must be w

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Newer lawyers
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Newer lawyers: The judge encourages newer lawyers to argue and examine witnesses and will let a more experienced lawyer assist with an examination if it doesn’t prolong the proceeding or prejudice the other side. Every attorney appearing must have authority suited to the proceeding, for example full authority on scheduling at a scheduling conference.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Extension motions are due at least 2 days before the motions deadline expires, with Speedy Trial Act exclusion language in the proposed order. Sentencing memoranda are expected, and Guidelines, departure, and criminal history issues go in the Position with Respect to Sentencing Factors. Travel motions must state the AUSA’s and probation officer’s positions. The government must obtain writs for in-custody defendants and give 24 hours’ notice of any bond revocation request; arrange civilian attire with the Marshal’s Office.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Motions and briefing (trap): A motion must state the specific relief and its factual and legal grounds, and affirmatively state whether it was discussed with all other parties and their positions. Every motion needs a separate proposed order detailing the relief, not just “granted.” Briefs are filed with the motion and limited to 25 pages, excluding tables. Briefs are not required for discovery motions, extensions, or continuances; the scheduling order forms list similar no-brief motions (including amendments, supplemental pleadings, substitution, and, in the initial order, motions to compel). Responses are generally due in 21 days for dispositive motions and 14 days for non-dispositive motions. The standing order says replies to dispositive motions are due within 7 days but also that replies (other than to Local Rule 56.D submissions) and sur-replies

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Rule 12 motions: meet and confer (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Rule 12 motions: meet and confer (trap): Before any Rule 12 motion, the movant must confer with opposing counsel on whether the defects can be cured, and a motion to dismiss must include a certificate of good-faith efforts to confer.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Routine motions and continuances
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Routine motions and continuances: For routine motions (amendment, extensions, continuances), seek consent and state whether it was obtained. A motion to continue a proceeding must propose at least 2 dates and times near the original date when all counsel are available.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Communications and phone appearances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Communications and phone appearances (trap): Communicate by motion, not letters; no correspondence to the judge unless requested. Law clerks may be contacted on administrative matters, including status, but not the merits. To appear by phone, fax a request to (814) 691-6001 at least 2 days before the conference; no response means it is approved. Status, initial scheduling, and post-discovery conferences may be by phone; settlement and final pretrial conferences may not unless ordered. Counsel call chambers at (814) 691-6297 only once all parties are on the line.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Discovery: If a dispute survives a good-faith conference (which the party seeking intervention must initiate promptly), contact chambers for a telephonic conference; no discovery motions until after it. Refusing to confer may draw Rule 37(a)(5) sanctions. The initial scheduling order includes a clawback procedure: the producing party must move within 30 days of notice if the privilege claim is disputed, and inadvertent disclosure is not a waiver under Fed. R. Evid. 502(d).

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Scheduling and settlement
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Scheduling and settlement: Seven days before the Post-Discovery Status Conference, the parties must jointly submit a proposed Final Scheduling Order with dates for dispositive motions, pretrial statements, motions in limine, Daubert motions and argument, the final pretrial conference, and trial. Counsel must obtain settlement authority before status conferences and are encouraged to bring principals. An insurer representative with full, unilateral settlement authority must attend any ADR session in person if insurance could cover any part of a settlement or verdict.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Per the Final Scheduling Order form, no briefing beyond the motion and response without leave. File a separate “Concise Statement of Undisputed Material Facts” strictly under Local Rule 56.B; the opponent files a paragraph-by-paragraph response under Local Rule 56.C, with additional facts in a “New Matter” section, which the movant may answer. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial (trap): Exhibits not identified in the pretrial narrative statement (other than impeachment exhibits) will not be admitted, and pretrial statements cannot be amended without leave. The absence of a witness is not cause to delay trial. A motion in limine requires a certificate of conference stating the exact time and place of the conference. At the pretrial conference, be ready to state exhibit objections, designate and counter-designate deposition pages and lines, estimate trial length, and have clients present or available by phone.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Oral argument: Requests are considered case by case; the court will likely allow argument if an associate or more junior attorney argues.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Deadlines without briefing orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Deadlines without briefing orders (trap): No separate briefing order generally issues, and awaiting one is no excuse. Responses to non-dispositive motions are due in 10 calendar days; responses to Rule 12 motions in 20 calendar days, with replies 5 calendar days later. Summary judgment oppositions are due in 30 calendar days and replies (including responses to new facts in the responsive concise statement) in 14 calendar days. Reconsideration motions are due within 10 calendar days, with responses 10 calendar days later.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Motions to dismiss (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Motions to dismiss (trap): Meet and confer before a Rule 12(b) motion about whether amendment can cure the defect (including with pro se parties, but not incarcerated pro se litigants). A motion without a certificate of conferral is summarily denied, and one filed without a brief is summarily dismissed. Briefs are capped at 25 pages; replies allowed without leave for Rule 12(b) and 12(c), capped at 5 pages and limited to new matters. Partial motions to dismiss do not excuse filing an answer. Parties should try not to oppose timely early motions to amend.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Motions generally: Every motion needs a separate proposed order stating the specific relief. Briefs are filed with the motion, except for discovery, extension, and continuance motions. Incorporating earlier briefs is prohibited. Double-spaced, at least 12-point font, paginated. Hyperlinks to CM/ECF filings, exhibits, and Westlaw are strongly encouraged (except for pro se parties); links to sealed documents, other websites, or audio/video are prohibited, and cited websites must be attached as dated PDFs. No paper courtesy copies. Oral argument only on selected complex matters, by order; there is no set motion day. Don’t send correspondence to the judge unless requested. Conferences may be rescheduled by phone to the deputy clerk only with all counsel on the line.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Strict compliance with Local Rule 56. Briefs are capped at 25 pages (excluding exhibits and concise statements) and replies at 5 pages; surreplies only with leave. The argument must cite current Supreme Court and Third Circuit authority establishing the elements of each claim. Responses to the concise statement must reprint each original fact followed by the response, seriatim. Concise statements and responses have no page limit; supporting documents go in an appendix.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes: After conferring, file an extremely brief motion, with no supporting brief and the discovery at issue attached, and call chambers so the deputy can schedule a conference. Noncompliance means denial without prejudice. Discovery motions and motions in limine require a certificate of conferral; email exchanges are not enough. Disputes during depositions may be raised by a joint call. Discovery runs 150 days if the parties choose mediation or early neutral evaluation and 120 days for arbitration. Dispositive motions and ADR do not stay discovery.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Remote appearances, extensions, and ADR
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Remote appearances, extensions, and ADR: Requests to participate in a conference by phone must be made by motion more than 2 business days before it, for good cause. Extension and continuance motions must state supporting facts and opposing counsel’s position, suggest alternative dates when all parties are available, and be filed more than 2 business days before the deadline. File an ADR stipulation naming a proposed neutral before the initial case management conference; if the parties can’t agree, the court chooses.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Settlement authority (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Settlement authority (trap): In jury cases, counsel and persons with ultimate settlement authority (including knowledgeable insurer representatives) must attend settlement conferences, including the final pretrial conference, in person. Sanctions may follow if the person present lacks full authority; phone participation only rarely, with prior leave for good cause.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Post-discovery status conference after fact discovery; a final status conference after dispositive rulings, preceded by a settlement meet-and-confer. The final pretrial conference is held immediately before trial. Submit a single agreed set of jury instructions and verdict form using Third Circuit model instructions; for disputed ones, each side submits its version with authority. In bench trials, file numbered proposed findings and conclusions and a supporting brief of up to 20 pages within 20 days after trial, plus editable word-processing copies. Submit a joint glossary of technical terms, if needed, 3 business days before trial. Exhibits are marked P and D and listed in the pretrial narrative statements; get approval in advance for demonstratives in opening.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Trial (Erie)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Trial (Erie): Trial generally runs Monday through Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The court conducts preliminary voir dire; jurors may take notes. Only one attorney per party may examine a given witness. Tell the court in advance about video testimony (not filed with the clerk) and test it on the court’s equipment at least a week before trial. Counsel must be reachable in person or by phone during deliberations. Notify the court before interviewing jurors.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — R&R objections and TROs
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. R&R objections and TROs: Objection briefs of 10 pages or less are encouraged. New authority or evidence not given to the magistrate judge will not be considered without a reason for the omission. No TRO if the other side has been served, if the motion lacks a certification that prompt service can’t be made, or if it lacks a Rule 65(b)(1)(A) affidavit or verified complaint. Support and responses must include affidavits.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Certificate of conferral (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Certificate of conferral (trap): Every motion must attach, as a separate exhibit, a Certificate of Conferral detailing the efforts to resolve the matter and stating whether each other party consents or opposes and whether it will file a response. A missing certificate can get the motion stricken or summarily denied, with possible sanctions. Conferral must include a verbal discussion (phone, video, or in person) on the merits; exchanging emails or letters, or leaving a voicemail the evening before or the day of filing, does not count. Counsel must also confer verbally before any conference with the court so that no one is surprised by another party’s position.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Motions and page limits (trap): Motions must state the specific relief and its factual and legal grounds, with a proposed order filed as a separate attachment stating the specific relief (not “the motion is granted”). Communicate with the court by motion, not email or letter, unless asked. No brief is needed for discovery motions or extension or continuance motions. Dispositive and class certification briefs: 25 pages (replies 15). All other motion briefs: 10 pages (replies 5). Any other written submission: 5 pages. Overlong filings may be stricken. No courtesy copies of anything on CM/ECF unless requested. Oral argument at the court’s discretion; a request should briefly explain why argument would help.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Response deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Response deadlines (trap): Responses: 21 days for motions to dismiss and to compel arbitration; 30 days for summary judgment and class certification; 5 days for discovery and case management motions (such as extensions or rescheduling); 7 days for all other motions. The 2026 version shortens the general deadline from 21 days in the 2021 version. Replies without leave within 7 days of the response (14 days for summary judgment and class certification). Sur-replies are disfavored and need leave. Motions for reconsideration are due within 7 days of the order. For urgent motions, say so in the motion and phone chambers and all counsel. Stipulations to change response times are not a substitute for a motion and court approval.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion may be filed until Judge Hardy holds an informal phone conference and grants leave. After conferring in good faith, the parties jointly contact Courtroom Deputy Kallie Sheets (412-208-7570, Kallie_sheets@pawd.uscourts.gov) with a jointly proposed agenda that fairly identifies the disputed issues. If leave is granted, the response is due within 5 days, replies are typically not permitted, and rulings often come within 7 days. During depositions, the attorneys together may call to see if the court will resolve a dispute then. Discovery ordinarily runs 150 days; any variance must be raised in the Rule 26(f) report and at the initial conference. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Extensions (trap): Extension motions must state all opposing counsel’s positions (and whether they will oppose in writing), list prior extensions, attach a proposed order and Certificate of Conferral, and be titled (with matching docket text) like “[First] Motion for [Un/Contested] Extension of Discovery” or “[First] Motion to Modify Case Management Order.” File at least 5 business days before the deadline when practicable. A first reasonable discovery extension is routinely granted if the motion describes discovery done to date and the specific discovery planned, with a tentative schedule. Don’t assume joint requests will be granted, especially late ones, and don’t informally agree to work “out of time” without a court order.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and ADR

Briefs, exhibits, and proposed orders: Title briefs “Brief in Support of [motion],” “[Respondent]’s Response in Opposition to [motion],” and “Reply in Support of [motion].” Surreplies are not filed in the normal course. Label uploaded exhibits by content (e.g., “Ex. A: Smith Deposition”), not just by letter. File proposed orders with consent, unopposed, or joint motions and email a Word version to chambers. Do not submit proposed orders on contested motions unless the court asks.

docs.t: Judge Richard W. Story (N.D. Ga.) — Extensions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Richard W. Story, N.D. Ga.. Extensions and page limits (trap): Extensions are not granted as a matter of course, even if joint or unopposed. Explain with specificity the unforeseen circumstances, give a full timetable for completing the briefing, state the other side’s position, and file a proposed order. A motion filed before the deadline expires stays that deadline pending a ruling. Requests to exceed Local Rule page limits are likewise not granted as a matter of course and must explain the need with specificity, state consent, and include a proposed order.

docs.t: Judge Richard W. Story (N.D. Ga.) — Courtesy copies, TROs, and oral argument
docs.x: Judge Richard W. Story, N.D. Ga.. Courtesy copies, TROs, and oral argument: Courtesy copies are required only for LR 7.2(B) emergency motions and TRO or preliminary injunction motions, hand-delivered to chambers, Room 140, Gainesville. Courtesy copies of summary judgment motions with voluminous exhibits are optional (hand delivery or mail to the deputy). A TRO or preliminary injunction request must be a separate motion (a request only in the complaint will not be considered); after filing, contact Ms. Kemp for expedited consideration. Motions are usually decided without argument, but the court will grant oral argument on a contested, substantive motion if the request states that a lawyer less than seven years out of law school will argue at least one substantial issue.

docs.t: Judge Richard W. Story (N.D. Ga.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Richard W. Story, N.D. Ga.. Summary judgment (trap): Record citations belong in the brief itself, not just the statement of facts. File the original transcript of each deposition cited, cite page and line right after each reference, and attach only the cited pages, not the whole transcript. Beyond LR 56.1(B), a response to a statement of material facts must copy each numbered statement and respond immediately after it; a reply must copy the original statement and the response, then reply. File in text-searchable PDF.

docs.t: Judge Richard W. Story (N.D. Ga.) — Settlement and dismissal
docs.x: Judge Richard W. Story, N.D. Ga.. Settlement and dismissal: On a tentative settlement or settlement in principle, file a Notice of Settlement stating how much time is needed to finish and dismiss; the notice does not end the case. The court will not sign Rule 41(a)(1) stipulations, which take effect on filing; for a dismissal by court order, file a Rule 41(a)(2) motion with a proposed order.

docs.t: Judge Richard W. Story (N.D. Ga.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Richard W. Story, N.D. Ga.. Pretrial (trap): The proposed consolidated pretrial order is ordinarily due within 30 days after the close of discovery or the ruling on summary judgment, whichever is later. Witnesses and exhibits must be listed; no reserving the right to supplement or adopting another party’s list, and unlisted witnesses and exhibits are excluded absent manifest injustice. Proposed voir dire must not duplicate the judge’s posted background questions, civil qualifying questions, or juror questionnaire (additional questionnaire items may be requested). Email Ms. Kemp the case-in-chief witness list 7 days before the pretrial conference. Motions in limine and Daubert motions are due at least 14 days before the conference, responses 7 days before. Exhibit objections are generally ruled on at trial. Anyone without a blue attorney ID card who wants to bring a laptop or camera

docs.t: Judge Richard W. Story (N.D. Ga.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Richard W. Story, N.D. Ga.. Jury instructions: Requests to charge and verdict forms are due on CM/ECF by noon on the Friday before the trial calendar, with a Word copy of the instructions emailed to Ms. Kemp. File a single unified set: agreed instructions first, then disputed ones showing (by redline or different fonts) the contested language, the proponent, and the legal basis for each side. The court usually charges after closing and gives the jury a written copy.

docs.t: Judge Steve C. Jones (N.D. Ga.) — AI disclosure (trap)
docs.x: Judge Steve C. Jones, N.D. Ga.. AI disclosure (trap): Any use of artificial intelligence, in any capacity, to prepare a filing or submission requires a signed and filed Disclosure of Use of Artificial Intelligence naming the tool and certifying under penalty of perjury that the filer independently reviewed it for accuracy under Rule 11. Do not input or upload any information subject to a protective order into any AI tool. Briefs relying on AI-generated, nonexistent caselaw are unacceptable; violations can draw sanctions up to dismissal or default.

docs.t: Judge Steve C. Jones (N.D. Ga.) — Contact and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Steve C. Jones, N.D. Ga.. Contact and courtesy copies: Courtroom Deputy Pamela Wright (pamela_wright@gand.uscourts.gov, 404-215-1284) is the principal contact; do not discuss the merits with the deputy or the law clerks. No paper courtesy copies except for emergency motions under LR 7.2(B), though the court may request copies of motions with voluminous exhibits. Those go to chambers, Room 1967, by hand or regular mail, bearing the CM/ECF header.

docs.t: Judge Steve C. Jones (N.D. Ga.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Steve C. Jones, N.D. Ga.. Discovery disputes (trap): Before filing a motion to compel, to quash, or for a protective order, confer in good faith, then contact Ms. Wright; the court will hold a recorded conference call or videoconference to try to resolve the dispute without a formal motion. No “Preamble” or “General Objections” in discovery responses; each request needs its own specific objections, and general objections will be disregarded.

docs.t: Judge Steve C. Jones (N.D. Ga.) — Extensions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Steve C. Jones, N.D. Ga.. Extensions and page limits (trap): Extensions cannot be obtained by stipulation; file a joint motion, and even joint, unopposed, or consent motions are not granted as a matter of course. Explain the unforeseen circumstances with specificity, give a timetable, state opposing counsel’s position, and attach a proposed order. Motions to exceed page limits must be filed at least 5 days before the filing deadline; a request filed with the brief will be denied absent a compelling, unanticipated reason. Objections to a magistrate judge’s R&R and responses are limited to 25 pages absent prior permission.

docs.t: Judge Steve C. Jones (N.D. Ga.) — Motions and filing format
docs.x: Judge Steve C. Jones, N.D. Ga.. A: Smith Deposition”), not one combined file; hard-to-navigate filings may have to be refiled. Deposition excerpts go in one text-searchable PDF per witness, with the full transcript (unless under 30 pages) filed separately.
