For sealed or restricted exhibits, put a redacted version or placeholder in the combined PDF and file each sealed exhibit as a separate, descriptively labeled attachment.

docs.t: Judge William C. Griesbach (E.D. Wis.) — Scheduling conference
docs.x: Judge William C. Griesbach, E.D. Wis.. Scheduling conference: After all parties appear, the court notices a Rule 16(b) conference, with the due date for the Rule 26(f) discovery plan. Counsel who know the case should attend, ready to discuss claim value, discovery, defenses, threshold issues, and a schedule.

docs.t: Judge William C. Griesbach (E.D. Wis.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge William C. Griesbach, E.D. Wis.. Trial generally starts at 9 a.m. with counsel there at 8:30 a.m. (at least on day one) and adjourns about 5 p.m. Matters outside the jury’s presence should be raised at breaks, before trial starts, or after the jury leaves. The court conducts voir dire, incorporating counsel’s questions, and usually seats eight jurors in civil cases. Jurors may take notes; instructions are generally read before closings.

docs.t: Judge William C. Griesbach (E.D. Wis.) — Exhibits and courtroom conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge William C. Griesbach, E.D. Wis.. State objection grounds briefly; sidebars are short, and a full record can be made after the jury leaves. An easel and projector screen are available; bring your own laptop or other technology and arrange setup time with staff. Video testimony is available in some cases, including prisoner cases. Hearings are digitally recorded.

Within one business day after full briefing, the parties file all papers in order (motion, response, reply) and the movant files a Notice of compliance stating the motion is fully briefed. An early-filed motion is terminated without prejudice; a compliant certificate filed within one business day relates back. Exceptions: remand motions, cases with a pro se party, Rule 55(b)(2) default judgment, Rule 50(b)/52(b)/59/60 motions, ex parte motions, motions to seal and for leave (filed immediately before the document), emergency motions under L.R. Every page counts toward page limits except pages bearing only a caption, tables, signature block, or certificates; incorporating a prior filing by reference counts its pages. Embed the table of contents and add PDF bookmarks where hard copy would have tabs. Bluebook citations, with italics instead of underscoring, and for unreported cases a Westlaw cite plus full docket number and date. Violations lead to striking or termination without prejudice. docs.x: Judge J. Campbell Barker, E.D. Tex.. Proposed orders and courtesy copies: Each proposed order required by L.R. Injunction orders must meet Rule 65(d) detail. Judge Barker has not opted out of L.R. CV-5(a)(9) courtesy copies; double-sided printing and spiral binding for larger documents are encouraged.

docs.t: Judge J. Campbell Barker (E.D. Tex.) — Sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Campbell Barker, E.D. Tex.. Sealing (trap): A motion to seal must cite authority on sealing judicial records, not just L.R. CV-5(a)(7) or a protective order (June Medical v. docs.x: Judge Colm F. Connolly, D. Del.. Briefing format (trap): In all counseled cases, page limits become word limits at 250 words per page (20 pages = 5,000 words), with a word-count certification. Briefs, letters, motions, and concise statements must be 14-point Times New Roman or similar, with a certification of type, font, and word compliance (November 10, 2022 standing order). Pinpoint citations are required in all briefs, letters, and concise statements; the court will ignore controverted facts or law without one. Every motion must come with a draft order stating the specific relief sought. Do not combine motions that rely on different facts. Non-dispositive motions need the Local Rule 7.1.1 statement.

docs.x: Judge Colm F. Connolly, D. Del.. Discovery and protective-order disputes (trap): No motions without leave: call the Case Manager to set an in-person conference. A motion filed outside this procedure is denied without prejudice. The movant files a letter 72 hours before the conference with an averment that the meet-and-confer included oral communication involving Delaware counsel, a draft order, and a one-paragraph motion stating the relief; oppositions are due 48 hours before. The May 2026 non-patent order caps each letter at 750 words; the page and the 2022 patent orders say three pages. Proposed protective orders are due within 10 days of the scheduling order and must include the court’s “Other Proceedings” paragraph on notice of motions to disclose in another case.

A party with non-recourse third-party litigation funding must file a separate statement within the later of 45 days of the April 18, 2022 order or 30 days of the initial pleading, transfer, or removal, identifying the funder, whether its approval is needed for litigation or settlement decisions, and the nature of its financial interest. Pro hac vice applicants must file the certification in Exhibit A-1 or A-2 of the April 7, 2026 standing order, addressing fee-sharing and nonlawyer ownership or control of their firm.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey L. Schmehl (E.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey L. Schmehl, E.D. Pa.. Trial: Trial is set for a date certain, not a pool. Counsel conduct all civil voir dire, generally 30 minutes per side. Openings up to 30 minutes, closings up to 45. On day one give the court one copy of each exhibit and an exhibit schedule. Without agreement on admissibility, a witness may not testify about an exhibit’s content until it is admitted. Rule 50 and involuntary dismissal motions must be in writing. Unavailable witnesses testify by deposition; no delays for them. During deliberations counsel may leave but must be able to return within 10 to 15 minutes. Examine from the lectern or counsel table; rise to address the court and ask before approaching witnesses or the bench.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey L. Schmehl (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey L. Schmehl, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Oral argument on substantive motions generally allowed on request. Scheduling goes through the criminal deputy (Kenneth Duvak, 610-320-5030). The judge does initial voir dire; counsel may ask preapproved questions, submitted in writing 7 days before trial. Sentencing memoranda are due 5 days before sentencing.

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Communications and filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Communications and filings (trap): All requests go through ECF, almost always by motion; email chambers only when directed or for a scheduling emergency. Questions go to deputy Kerri Christy, 267-299-7510. Case conferences are typically by Microsoft Teams video. All filings, including exhibits, must be text-searchable, with descriptive ECF descriptions and filenames (e.g., “Ex. A - Contract”). Cite docketed documents by docket number (e.g., DI 12), don’t re-attach them, and attach copies of any web pages relied on. File proposed orders on ECF with the request; also email complex ones (e.g., patent scheduling orders) in Word.

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Extensions and disclosure statements
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Extensions and disclosure statements: Extensions only by ECF motion or stipulation showing good cause, even if joint or unopposed; lack of diligence generally defeats good cause. File at least 7 days before the nearest deadline or justify the late request. Trial dates certain move only for a criminal-docket emergency or truly extraordinary reasons. Complete Rule 7.1(a)(2) disclosure is mandatory immediately; LLC, partnership, and similar entities’ citizenship turns on all members or partners. Pro hac vice motions must use the district’s form, and at least one E.D. Pa. bar member must attend hearings and trials absent leave.

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Motions to dismiss and amended pleadings (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Motions to dismiss and amended pleadings (trap): Every Rule 12 motion must be accompanied by a certification (preferably filed separately) that the parties met and conferred on the substance, with each side’s position on whether discovery should proceed while the motion is pending, considering the listed factors. Amended pleadings must always include a redline.

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Motions and courtesy copies (trap): Double-spaced, at least 12-point font (footnotes the same size), 1-inch margins; briefs over 10 pages need a table of contents and table of authorities. Limits: opening and opposition 25 pages or 6,250 words; reply 10 pages or 2,500 words. Exceed page limits without leave only with a word-count certification. Replies need no leave and are due within 7 days of the opposition; the judge may rule any time after the opposition. For dispositive motions or briefs with exhibits, email chambers a single as-filed PDF (ECF headers, all exhibits, bookmarks, text-searchable, filename with case number, docket number, and description). No paper copies unless requested. Argument is ordered when helpful; requests are almost certainly granted if a junior lawyer will speak. Illustrative aids are welcome; slides of case quotations are n

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): One Rule 56 motion per party absent leave. For motions filed after October 31, 2025, file a single, jointly prepared consolidated statement of facts and a joint set of exhibits, or the motion may be struck. The movant serves (not files) numbered facts with cites at least 28 days before the motion deadline; the respondent serves responses directly under each paragraph, plus additional facts, at least 14 days before; the movant may reply under each paragraph and then files the consolidated statement and exhibits with the motion. Cross-movants may file separate statements but share one exhibit set. An argument that expert testimony is inadmissible must be raised in a contemporaneous Daubert motion.

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and discovery
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery: Hold the Rule 26(f) conference at least 21 days, exchange initial disclosures at least 14 days, and file the joint report at least 7 days before the Rule 16 conference, covering the topics in the judge’s sample report (key facts, critical documents, stipulated facts, insurance, specific discovery plan, ESI, and more; generic statements are unacceptable; explain any request for more than 120 days of discovery). Counsel sign an acknowledgment that noncompliant submissions may be struck. Lead counsel must take part in the 26(f) conference and attend Rule 16 conferences absent leave. Discovery should begin before the Rule 16 conference. Discovery motions require a specific, substantive L.R. 26.1 certification and a detailed proposed order stating the precise relief; the judge typically orders expedited opposition and a conf

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): No confidentiality protective order absent statutory requirement or demonstrated good cause (Avandia), though private confidentiality agreements are enforced as contracts. Any proposed order must state that the court may allow disclosure or modify it at any time in the interest of justice. No sealed filing without leave except in emergencies. Move on the public docket well ahead of the deadline, emailing unredacted documents to chambers; if granted, file under seal with the non-public parts highlighted, then file narrowly redacted public versions within 30 days. Send sealed filings to chambers like courtesy copies.

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Trial date and deadlines are typically set at a conference after discovery closes, possibly after summary judgment. Plaintiff files a single integrated pretrial memorandum no later than 14 days before trial covering items A through M (including damages itemization, witness summaries, designations or a designation-exchange agreement, exhibit lists, and voir dire); it becomes the Rule 16(e) order. No trial briefs unless requested. Jury instructions and verdict sheet are filed as a single set no later than 7 days before the final pretrial conference: plaintiff serves Word drafts with citations at least 14 days before that deadline, defendant returns a redline with comments within 7 days, then the parties confer. Follow Third Circuit models, number each instruction on a new page, include preliminary and final instructions, and email Word versions.

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Trial: Courtroom 3B (electronic); arrange anything larger than laptops at least two weeks ahead. Trial days run 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Struck-jury method aiming for 8 jurors, 3 peremptory strikes per side (no extra strikes for overlaps). Exhibits must be offered through a witness and not published until admitted; illustrative aids are admitted, or used in opening, only by agreement. Summations typically follow the charge. In bench trials, submit video depositions electronically with transcripts; evidentiary objections are usually taken under advisement. Junior lawyers are encouraged to take speaking roles, and the judge will accommodate them.

docs.t: Judge John Frank Murphy (E.D. Pa.) — Voluntary dismissal
docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Voluntary dismissal: Do not call or write chambers to mark a case settled. Use a Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i) notice, a stipulation signed by all parties who have appeared, a Rule 41(a)(2) motion, or a docketed request for a Local Rule 41.1(b) order.

docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Chambers contact and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Chambers contact and courtesy copies (trap): Routine scheduling and administrative matters may go by letter, email, or phone to the deputy clerk (Christine Stein, 610-391-7012) or chambers, copying all parties. Don’t contact law clerks unless they contact you. No courtesy copies, paper or digital, unless the court asks. docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Filing and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Filing and format (trap): All submissions in 12-point Times New Roman (footnotes too), double-spaced, one-inch margins; briefs over 10 pages need a table of contents. Post searchable briefs and cite docket documents by ECF number. File each exhibit as a separate, descriptively named ECF attachment (for example, “Exhibit A: Contract”); a single “Exhibits” file will be struck. Submit full-size transcript pages with a cover page and only relevant pages, and don’t submit unpublished decisions available on Westlaw or Lexis.

docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Motions and page limits (trap): All grounds in one comprehensive motion. Opening and opposition briefs are limited to 20 pages including table of contents and attachments; exceeding it needs a motion showing good cause. Replies and sur-replies need leave: attach the brief to the motion for leave, limit it to new issues, and file within 7 days of the prior filing. Replies are capped at 10 pages, sur-replies at 7. Before a Rule 12(b)(6) motion, confer by phone or in person at least 7 days before filing to allow a cure, and certify it; letters or emails don’t count, and noncompliant motions are denied. Request oral argument by letter.

docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): Movant files a separate numbered statement of undisputed facts; respondent files a numbered statement of disputed facts with record citations plus any “statement of additional facts.” Facts not specifically controverted with evidence are deemed admitted; cite title, page, and line. Movant files an appendix of all evidence (respondent a supplemental one); cross-movants file a joint appendix in its own ECF entry the day the first motion is docketed. Appendices must be Bates-stamped and cited by Bates number; evidence outside a timely appendix is not considered. Noncompliance means denial of the motion, or for a respondent, treatment of the motion as uncontested.

docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and scheduling
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and scheduling: Lead trial counsel must attend the Rule 16 conference in person, with settlement authority, and remains lead counsel for all proceedings. File the judge’s Joint Rule 26(f) Report form at least 7 calendar days before; counsel certify having read the Policies and acknowledge that noncompliant submissions will be struck. The form requires a signed stipulation of undisputed facts, insurance disclosure, critical documents, ESI discussion, deposition dates set aside, and initial disclosures exchanged at least 1 business day before the conference; assume no bifurcation of fact and expert discovery, and explain any request over 120 days. Discovery begins without waiting for the conference; a stay pending motions is granted only in extraordinary circumstances. Discovery usually runs 120 days from the conference, with trial abou

docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Continuances and extensions
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Continuances and extensions: No extensions for developments foreseeable at the Rule 16 conference, and untimely discovery is not good cause. Extensions not affecting dispositive-motion or trial dates may be by signed stipulation with a blank signature line for the court. Extensions affecting those dates need a written request (by motion; unopposed may be by letter) stating the basis, other parties’ positions, and proposed dates, made well ahead.

docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes (trap): Simple disputes: file a brief letter on ECF requesting a phone conference. Complex disputes: a Local Rule 26.1(b) motion of no more than 5 pages, with no exhibits or brief; response within 5 days, same limits. The certificate must detail informal efforts, including phone or in-person talks; letters or emails alone, or “reasonable efforts,” lead to denial. Call the court rather than walk out of a deposition, or risk paying rescheduling costs. Privilege logs must describe each withheld email in a chain, not just the top one, though like emails may be grouped.

docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): No sealed filing without leave except in emergencies. File the motion publicly (redacted if needed), give the court and parties unredacted copies, and identify clearly defined, serious injuries (Avandia). Proposed orders must require public redacted versions, or the motion must explain why redaction is impossible. Protective orders need a formal motion, not a stipulated order, with good cause stated in both motion and proposed order. No order may let parties seal without specific court approval, and each must reserve the court’s power to modify and permit disclosure in the interest of justice.

Joint jury instructions and verdict forms in Word to the deputy, marking agreed and contested items with brief positions; flag changes to model instructions. Submit voir dire questions at least 2 days before jury selection; usually 8 civil jurors. No speaking objections; non-jury proposed findings are due at least 7 days before trial. docs.t: Judge John M. Gallagher (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge John M. Gallagher, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Continuance motions must state time sought, opposition, reason, and include an executed Speedy Trial Waiver form. Suppression, Starks, and Daubert hearings are usually at least 14 days before trial. Voir dire questions and the government’s trial memorandum are due 7 days before trial; guilty plea memoranda at least 7 days before the plea hearing. Sentencing motions are due 14 days before sentencing (responses 7 days); sentencing memoranda 7 days before (responses 3 days). Serve copies on Probation.

docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Hearings and conferences
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Hearings and conferences: No set days for argument or hearings; they are scheduled ad hoc, and argument is heard only if the judge thinks it will help. Scheduling, case management, and similar conferences are often by video or phone, with connection details emailed in advance.

A proposed order must be filed with every motion and every response, titled “Order,” with no attorney name or address (add “File Under Seal” to the caption if it is to be sealed). Replies and sur-replies, limited to issues raised in the opposition or reply, may be filed within 7 days of service and are limited to 10 pages. Courtesy copies only when chambers asks (for voluminous filings), marked, tabbed, and bound to lie flat, by mail or hand delivery. Searchable (OCR) briefs are encouraged.

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): The movant files a separate Statement of Undisputed Material Facts in numbered paragraphs. The opponent files a separate statement responding paragraph by paragraph (admitted or disputed) and may add numbered Additional Disputed Material Facts; the movant must respond to those within 7 business days. Facts not addressed are deemed admitted, facts without pinpoint record citations are not considered, and noncompliant summary judgment papers will be stricken.

docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap): Start discovery as soon as the order scheduling the Rule 16 conference arrives. Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting at least 10 days before the conference and, without exception, file the joint 26(f) report at least 5 business days before. Be ready to discuss settlement and consent to a magistrate judge. The 26(f) form says discovery should normally end no more than 120 days after the Rule 16 conference and expects simultaneous expert reports; the policies say the judge generally permits 3 to 6 months. Cases go to a trial pool or a date certain only after discovery is complete and dispositive motions are filed. Discovery disputes: motion under L.R. 26.1(b) with the 26.1(f) certification, a proposed order, and a brief of no more than 10 pages; response limited to 10 pages. The court may rule, confer, refer to a magistrat

docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Continuances and settlement: The judge is extremely reluctant to continue trial dates, especially absent diligence; discovery extensions need good cause. Settlement conferences usually go to a magistrate judge; the judge may instead refer a case to a settlement master at the parties’ cost.

docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Injunctions and non-jury trials: The judge rarely grants ex parte TROs and requires all counsel at the TRO conference unless urgency prevents notice. Expedited discovery is usually allowed for preliminary relief, PI and permanent injunction hearings may be combined, and proposed findings and conclusions are required. Non-jury trials: file a stipulation of uncontested facts, and each party submits proposed findings and conclusions.

docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Trial and courtroom conduct (trap): Court convenes at 9:30 a.m. and may sit to 5 p.m. or later. Counsel conduct civil voir dire with minimal oversight; the judge conducts criminal voir dire. No speaking objections and no continuing objections; state every objection in a word or phrase. Only one attorney per party may examine a witness. Stand to address the court and jury, approach witnesses only with permission, and never approach the jury to hand out exhibits. Exhibits are generally admitted at the close of evidence. Be ready to close immediately after the evidence; time limits for openings and closings are discussed in advance. Object to jury charges on the record at the charging conference. Stay within 15 minutes of the courthouse during deliberations.

If unresolved, email a joint letter of up to 5 single-spaced pages stating each issue and each side’s position by the response deadline (extended 7 days in removed cases). docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. The judge will not retain jurisdiction to enforce confidential settlements; put the agreement on the docket or its material terms in the stipulation of dismissal. docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference (trap): Usually by telephone. Lead trial counsel must participate and have entered an appearance (unless a substitution is pre-approved); if lead counsel is pro hac vice, local counsel must also participate, and pro hac vice applications must be approved beforehand. Email the Joint Rule 16 Conference Information Report to chambers no later than one day before the conference. Parties who skip a meaningful Rule 26(f) meeting have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. File threshold motions before the conference and be ready to argue them, and be ready to discuss settlement with the judge or magistrate judge right after. Expect a final pretrial conference about a month after dispositive motions and a trial pool about a week later.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Motions and page limits (trap): A motion and supporting memorandum together may not exceed 15 pages; oppositions 15 pages. Times New Roman 12-point (footnotes too), one-inch margins, double-spaced; cite exhibit, page, and line. Replies may be filed without leave only for summary judgment or other dispositive motions (with leave for others), up to 7 pages, within 7 days of the opposition. Sur-replies need leave for good cause and are limited to 5 pages. Before a Rule 12 motion on a curable defect, certify that opposing counsel had a chance to cure. The judge warns of Rule 11 sanctions for filings without factual basis and encourages bringing clients to argument on dispositive motions.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: File a separate, concise numbered statement of material facts, each with exhibit, page, and line citations; unsupported facts are not considered. The opponent responds paragraph by paragraph, citing the record for any dispute, and adds additional facts in numbered paragraphs; uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. Submit entire deposition transcripts as exhibits.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Discovery: Exhaust all efforts first. Then email chambers a letter briefly outlining the dispute, certifying good-faith efforts, and requesting a phone conference; do not file a discovery motion until the conference is held. Expert depositions must be completed before the dispositive-motion deadline.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement, injunctions, and sealing
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Settlement, injunctions, and sealing: Early referral to a magistrate judge is encouraged, or a mediator from the court’s list. Notify chambers immediately on settlement and seek dismissal under Local Rule 41.1; papers must be done before trial or the case will be called. TRO requests get an immediate conference with all counsel unless urgency prevents notice; expedited discovery is generally allowed for injunctions. Sealed filings need a motion for leave under Local Rule 5.1.2; highly sensitive documents follow the court’s January 22, 2021 standing order.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Final pretrial and trial submissions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Final pretrial and trial submissions (trap): Cases are usually assigned a two-week trial pool, with 72 hours’ notice where possible (never less than 24). A pending summary judgment motion must be argued at the final pretrial conference. Exchange deposition designations at least one week before the final pretrial conference and counter-designations 3 days before; submit written objections by letter, with transcripts, one day before. Submit pretrial memoranda, a neutral statement of facts, joint voir dire (no more than 15 questions, disputes highlighted), and joint points for charge and verdict slip (one instruction per page, disputes highlighted), filed on the docket and emailed to chambers in Word. Third Circuit models preferred.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Trial practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Trial practice (trap): Testimony starts at 9 a.m.; raise issues 8 to 9 a.m., at breaks, or after the jury leaves, since sidebars are discouraged. Examine from the lectern, give a next-day witness list at the end of each day, and don’t run out of witnesses. One joint, sequentially numbered exhibit set (defendant’s numbers continue from plaintiff’s), with a table of contents including “Admitted” and “Not Admitted” columns; 2 copies for the court and one for witnesses. Admitted exhibits go to the jury on a court laptop via a USB drive with a hyperlinked joint exhibit chart and PDF, video, and audio folders. Openings or closings over 30 minutes need permission; closing is limited to 30 minutes including rebuttal, and plaintiff must reserve rebuttal time or waive it. Objections are one or two words; recross is generally allowed only on new matter from redir

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases (trap): Continuance and extension requests go by motion with proposed order; trial continuance motions are due at least 14 days before trial with a Speedy Trial Act ends-of-justice finding. Upon filing a motion, say whether testimony will be offered and how long. Plea papers go to chambers 2 days before the plea hearing if possible, and plea memoranda must also be filed. The government must give Rule 404(b) notice, with a proposed limiting instruction, before the final pretrial conference. Sentencing continuances are for good cause only and never more than 90 days at a time. Sentencing motions are due 14 days before (responses 7 days); simultaneous sentencing memoranda one week before (responses 3 days). PSR objections may not be raised first in a memorandum.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — AI disclosure (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. AI disclosure (trap): Any attorney or pro se party who used AI in any way to prepare a filing must disclose that in a clear factual statement and certify that every citation to law or the record was verified (August 2026 policies). The March 3, 2025 standing order, narrower in scope, also requires naming the specific generative AI program used when it helped with citations of legal authority.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Contact and filing format
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Contact and filing format: Email chambers for general inquiries. Judicial Assistant Tayai Lester (267-299-7590) handles civil scheduling; Courtroom Deputy Sue Flaherty (267-299-7598) handles criminal matters and trial logistics. Faxes and mail are strongly discouraged. Case communications go by ECF filing; email only for unanticipated schedule changes less than 7 business days before a deadline, private personal or medical scheduling issues, or settlement notice. File searchable PDFs. Everything is 12-point, generally double-spaced, with 1-to-1.5-inch justified margins (26(f) reports, one-page motions, and proposed orders may be single-spaced). Briefs over 25 pages need a table of contents. Courtesy copies only for sealed filings or filings with large attachments (over 50 pages of exhibits or 5 or more exhibits), as a tabbed binder with an exhibit index.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Continuances: no stipulations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Continuances: no stipulations (trap): Changes to operative deadlines may not be filed as stipulations; file a joint unopposed motion with a proposed order. Oppositions to opposed continuance motions are due in 3 business days. Joint discovery continuances are generally granted if made at least 7 business days ahead and they don’t alter key motion deadlines or trial. Changes to argued motion deadlines or trial dates are seldom granted and need good cause at least 14 business days ahead.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Motions (trap): Dispositive motions and memoranda are limited to 25 pages; seek leave for more at least 3 business days before the deadline (unless the overage is only from embedded pictures or charts, which you must certify). Co-parties must file joint motions unless their positions conflict. One reply, up to 10 pages, within 14 business days of the opposition; anything further needs leave, rarely granted. Threshold motions (dismiss, transfer, add or substitute parties) are due 7 days before the Rule 16 conference (7 business days per the 26(f) section), and may be argued there. Oral argument only if it would help; junior attorneys are encouraged to argue. Bring 2 copies of any physical exhibits. Amended pleadings must show changes by comments or track changes; one amendment as of right, then leave.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment and Daubert (trap): File the statement of facts as a separate document with the motion: either joint stipulated facts or the movant’s proposed undisputed facts, in numbered paragraphs with pinpoint cites to exhibit page and line. The nonmovant responds to each fact (undisputed, disputed with cites, or immaterial with cites) and may add facts, which the movant answers in a separate document. Statements must be brief and nonargumentative. A joint appendix is encouraged; otherwise the responder cites the movant’s appendix where possible. Any summary judgment argument that expert testimony is inadmissible must come with a contemporaneous Daubert motion. Daubert motions are due no later than 7 days before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 26(f) and Rule 16 (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Rule 26(f) and Rule 16 (trap): Meet in person or by video (email is insufficient) at least 14 business days before the Rule 16 conference, and submit the judge’s 26(f) form, with key documents attached, at least 7 business days before. Flawed reports are returned; parties not participating in good faith have no voice at the conference. Rule 16 conferences are in person in chambers. Lead counsel must attend; if counsel lack full settlement authority, someone with it must be available by phone throughout. Bring irreversible conflicts in the 3 to 9 months after the conference. Begin discovery on notice of the Rule 16 conference; pending motions are no excuse. Explain any proposed discovery period over 90 days. Expert reports are normally simultaneous.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery and sealing
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Discovery and sealing: Discovery disputes: a motion with the L.R. 26.1(f) certification stating whether a phone conference is requested, a proposed order, and a brief of up to 5 pages on efforts to resolve and authority. The judge often rules without waiting for a response; you may also call chambers. No sealed filings without leave except in emergencies; sealing requires good cause or a pre-litigation confidentiality agreement, and parties can’t stipulate around good cause. Sealing orders must reserve the court’s power to modify and permit disclosure. File a redacted copy within 14 days of a sealing order.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Injunctions
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Injunctions: The judge tries to hold a prompt conference after service. A party seeking pretrial injunctive relief should be ready for a hearing within a month, or seek expedited discovery first.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial (trap): Final pretrial conference generally 7 days before trial. Pretrial memoranda are due 7 business days before it, with witnesses and testimony summaries, expert reports and CVs, a list of in limine motions, deposition notices, unresolved objections with page and line cites, stipulations, and joint voir dire, instructions, and verdict forms. Joint voir dire (on the judge’s template only, or it is not accepted), instructions, and verdict forms go in one Word document by email to the deputy 7 business days before the conference. Attach the model instruction and mark changes in bold with footnotes; put alternative versions in the same document. Complex in limine motions are due 7 business days before the conference. Before voir dire, submit two tabbed binder sets of exhibits numbered consecutively across parties, plus one unmarked set for witnesses an

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Trial: Counsel may not question the whole panel; after the judge questions each venireperson, counsel may ask pre-approved and follow-up questions. Objections by rule number or a brief phrase, without argument. Sidebars only for unanticipated, time-sensitive issues. Meet each morning on witness order; email a witness list to the deputy 2 business days before trial. One attorney per witness. Courtroom 13B is not electronic (a monitor and two AirMedia pucks are available); request other equipment in writing a week before trial. Exhibits are admitted when used; publishing during testimony needs permission before the witness takes the stand. File a list of admitted exhibits on ECF after trial. Stay within 15 minutes during deliberations.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases (trap): Scheduling conference about 50 days after arraignment; the defendant generally attends to address a speedy trial waiver. Continuance motions are due 14 days before the hearing date, capped at 120 days, with the judge’s signed waiver form and an ends-of-justice proposed order. Plea memorandum, agreement, acknowledgment of rights, and sealed supplemental are due 3 business days before the plea hearing (memo in Word to the deputy). Notify chambers and probation 7 business days ahead of any agreed expedited sentencing. Sentencing about 100 days after plea or verdict. Sentencing motions and memoranda are due 7 business days before, responses 3 business days before, no replies without leave; character letters and witness names go to the deputy 7 business days before. Never raise PSR objections first in a memorandum.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Motions (trap): All grounds go in a single motion of no more than 5 double-spaced 12-point pages (like a summary of argument), with a proposed order citing the motion, docket number, and basis, and an attached memorandum of up to 20 pages. Opponents must also attach a proposed order. Except under Rule 56, the motion must recite all parties’ positions after meaningful conferral, which means sharing the arguments and case citations in summary form; failure may mean summary denial. Threshold motions (dismiss, strike, remand, transfer, etc.) require this conferral, and the movant should be ready to argue them at the Rule 16 conference. Replies are optional, without a proposed order, within 7 days of the opposition, 10 pages, new issues only; the judge may rule before a reply. Sur-replies and longer briefs only with leave. Post-trial motions: order and pay a d

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): Separately filed statement of undisputed material facts in numbered paragraphs with pinpoint record cites; the opponent files a separate paragraph-by-paragraph response plus any additional facts. Memoranda limited to 25 pages, with a table of contents if more than two arguments. The movant files a separate appendix of all exhibits, consecutively Bates-stamped (1a, 2a, …) with a table of contents and cited by those numbers; cross-movants prepare a single joint appendix; respondents may add a continuing-numbered appendix. Material outside the appendix won’t be considered; movant noncompliance may mean denial without prejudice, and respondent noncompliance may mean the motion is treated as uncontested. One paper courtesy copy of all Rule 56 submissions (with ECF headers, appendices searchable) by overnight mail or hand delivery to th

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Discovery motions (trap): Scheduling disputes and limited discovery issues: a 3-page motion with a proposed order, no memorandum. The judge may rule before any response unless the opponent emails or faxes chambers within 24 hours of its intent to respond (3 pages) within 48 hours. Other discovery motions: up to 7 pages with a proposed order; response within 3 days, 7 pages. No replies without leave; weekend or holiday responses are due by noon the next business day. The L.R. 26.1(f) certification must be specific and describe the opponent’s position; generalities such as “reasonable efforts” or “couldn’t reach counsel” may lead to summary denial. Motions against non-parties must be served simultaneously on the non-party, with a cover letter pointing to the Policies; non-parties may respond within 3 days. No speaking objections or coaching at depositions;

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and discovery schedule
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery schedule: Discovery begins with the order setting the initial pretrial conference: initial disclosures are due within 7 days of that order, and core party written discovery must start immediately (no third-party discovery or depositions before the conference without an order). Expect discovery to close 90 days after it begins, absent good cause in a complex case. File a comprehensive joint Report of Rule 26(f) Meeting on the judge’s form at least 1 day before the conference, including stipulated undisputed facts, insurance, ESI, expert plans (simultaneous reports, expert discovery within the fact period), ADR, and lead counsel’s conflicts over the next 4 to 8 months. Pending motions don’t excuse the meeting, and noncompliant parties get no input at the conference. Patent non-ANDA cases need a staged Markman disclosure plan

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Correspondence and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Correspondence and contact (trap): No letter requests for extensions; use a motion or stipulation showing good cause. Letters (up to 2 pages, copied to all) only when requested, for an uncontested sentencing extension, for an unanticipated personal scheduling matter, or to report settlement. Don’t copy chambers on correspondence between counsel. No communication with law clerks or interns. Questions go to deputy Ulrike Bower, 267-299-7688, copying the chambers email. Pro se parties may not call or fax chambers without prior approval. Remote conferences may be allowed except with non-custody pro se parties, whose conferences and hearings are held in the courtroom. No recording or AI summaries of off-the-record proceedings.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies, sealing, and AI
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies, sealing, and AI: Courtesy copies only for filings over 35 pages, Rule 56 papers, or on request: the ECF-stamped version delivered to the Clerk’s Office for Judge Kearney at about the time of filing. No confidentiality protective orders in discovery unless required by statute, though private agreements are enforced for good cause; agreements can’t require sealing of everything designated confidential. Move to seal before the substantive filing, as narrowly as possible, emailing the sealed records to ECF_Documents@paed.uscourts.gov under a “Notice of Sealed Documents” and to chambers, with line-by-line justification under Avandia; in camera show-cause hearings may be set. Attach a screenshot of any cited website. False citations, including AI hallucinations, can draw sanctions; double-check all authority.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Pro hac vice and local counsel (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Pro hac vice and local counsel (trap): The moving attorney must have entered an appearance, explain why the client needs this lawyer, state all counsel’s positions, and attach the applicant’s affidavit (bar admissions, discipline history, agreement to be bound, and duty to keep local counsel informed). Oppositions are due within 1 business day. Local counsel must sign all filings and must attend presentations in patent/ANDA, class, collective, qui tam, derivative, multi-party, complex criminal, Special Management, and MDL-transferred cases. Trial dates won’t move for pro hac counsel’s conflicts.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Extensions, amendments, injunctions, and arbitration
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Extensions, amendments, injunctions, and arbitration: Schedule changes need demonstrated good cause in writing; trial continuances only in extraordinary circumstances. Timely stipulated extensions may be approved for good cause if the trial date is unaffected; opposed requests go by short motion. Motions to amend must state all parties’ positions and attach a blacklined or highlighted proposed pleading; amendments as of course also need a blackline exhibit. TRO and preliminary injunction movants should be ready for a hearing within a month or seek expedited discovery. Arbitration cases: finish discovery and dispositive motions before the hearing; after a de novo demand, trial within 60 days of the appeal with no further discovery or dispositive motions absent compelling cause.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Simultaneous pretrial memoranda under L.R. 16.1(c), plus stipulations, highlighted designations with page and line, the specific substance of each witness’s testimony, and an exhibit schedule. Up to 5 motions in limine, grouped by evidentiary category, filed after the memoranda exchange with replies before the pretrial conference; provide two copies of challenged exhibits (hand-delivered if over 10 pages, else emailed). The final pretrial conference aims to resolve all evidentiary issues. Proposed jury instructions follow the Third Circuit models tailored to the facts, separately numbered with a table of contents and pinpoint cites, emailed in Word; all objections in one written motion. Trial briefs only on request.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Trial: Courtroom 6-B is not an electronic courtroom: bring your own equipment, identify it by letter at least 1 week before trial, and test it before jury selection. The judge conducts voir dire with approved follow-ups; 3 alternating peremptory strikes per side (plaintiff first); typically 8 jurors. Openings limited to 30 minutes and closings to 1 hour per side. Objections by rule number or one word only; one attorney per witness; no conferring with a witness during testimony. Joint chronological exhibit book with two copies for the judge at voir dire (unless all electronic); motions to admit exhibits at the close of each case-in-chief. Plaintiff must email all admitted exhibits to chambers before the verdict. Counsel must stay in the courthouse during deliberations and return within 10 minutes of a call.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Kearney (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Criminal: Pretrial motions by the scheduling-order deadline, stating all parties’ positions and whether testimony is expected. Trial continuance motions at least 14 days before trial, stating reasons, the other side’s position, time sought, and conflicts, with a Speedy Trial Act proposed order and the defendant’s signed consent form. Government guilty plea memorandum at least 2 days before the plea hearing, emailed in Word. Plea agreements should propose ranges rather than fixed terms, and the judge may defer accepting a Rule 11(c)(1) recommendation until after the PSR. Sentencing about 110 days after plea or verdict. PSR objections go to probation first, never first in a memorandum. Sentencing motions and memoranda 7 days before, responses 3 days before, no replies without leave; character letters emailed at least 3 days before.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Chambers contact
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Chambers contact: Correspondence is allowed only for scheduling, routine matters, or reporting settlement; everything else must be filed. Contact Courtroom Deputy Michael Coyle (267-299-7720) or chambers; direct contact with law clerks is prohibited. Raise matters with the court only after discussing them with opposing counsel. Settlement conferences may be referred to Magistrate Judge José R. Arteaga on request.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Motions and page limits (trap): All grounds in one comprehensive motion with a proposed order and memorandum; opponents must also attach a proposed order. Replies and sur-replies may be filed without leave within 7 days of the filing they answer. Briefs are limited to 25 pages (double-spaced, 12-point), excluding tables and exhibits; replies 10 pages and sur-replies 5, limited to new issues. Noncompliant briefs may be stricken. Exhibits must be separately numbered, descriptively titled attachments; submit entire deposition transcripts.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Pre-motion conference for Rule 12 motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Pre-motion conference for Rule 12 motions (trap): Except in pro se, bankruptcy, or social security matters, confer with opposing counsel at least 7 days before filing a Rule 12(b)(6), (e), or (f) motion to allow a cure. The motion must state the conference date and certify that the issue could not be resolved, or it will be denied.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): No separate statement of undisputed facts is allowed, except a formal stipulation of facts agreed by all parties. Put all facts in the memorandum with pinpoint record citations (document page, deposition page and line); failure may mean denial or striking. Summary judgment is rarely granted in non-jury cases.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and scheduling
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and scheduling: Scheduled shortly after all defendants answer. A joint Rule 26(f) report with a proposed discovery plan is due to chambers at least 3 business days before; counsel must have settlement authority and know the case. Standard track discovery is usually 120 days from the conference. Dates change only for compelling reasons, by letter detailing the basis, other counsel’s positions, and delay sought; extending trial or dispositive-motion dates is considered only in extraordinary circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes: Meet and confer by phone, video, or in person first; the court may sanction the losing side. Straightforward disputes: docket a letter or motion of no more than 5 pages (double-spaced, 12-point) and request a phone or video conference; response within 5 days, also 5 pages. Complicated disputes require a motion of no more than 10 pages, with a 10-page response within 5 days. Phone conferences are available for disputes during depositions.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Protective orders and sealing
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Protective orders and sealing: Protective orders are approved only where absolutely necessary for good cause and must reserve the court’s inherent power to modify and permit disclosure in the interest of justice. A confidentiality designation does not mean filings will be sealed; the party must show secrecy outweighs public access (Avandia).

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Injunctions and arbitration
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Injunctions and arbitration: TRO and preliminary injunction requests are listed promptly; serve the respondent and give notice of the hearing unless the emergency prevents it. Proposed findings may be required before the hearing. Arbitration track cases get no Rule 16 conference unless there is a de novo appeal; discovery and dispositive motions ordinarily end with the arbitration hearing.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial and trial: Trial date and pretrial deadlines are set at a trial readiness conference after discovery or after dispositive motions. Motion in limine briefs are limited to 5 pages, with no replies. One day before trial, give chambers witness and exhibit lists and 2 tabbed hard-copy binders of exhibits (plus electronic copies if presenting electronically). Prepare a joint list of admitted exhibits at the close of evidence. The judge conducts voir dire; speaking objections are discouraged and sidebars are rare. Stand to address the court; argue from the lectern or counsel table. Unavailable witnesses testify by deposition, and lay opinion support is due with expert reports.

docs.t: Judge Mary Kay Costello (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Mary Kay Costello, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Oral argument on substantive motions is generally allowed on request. The guilty plea memorandum is due at least 3 days before the plea hearing; sentencing memoranda and motions 7 days before sentencing, served on Probation.

docs.t: Judge Mia Roberts Perez (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mia Roberts Perez, E.D. Pa.. Motions and page limits (trap): A motion and its supporting memorandum together, and any opposition, may not exceed 20 pages; seek leave by motion for more. Replies on dispositive motions need no leave but must respond to the opposition and are limited to 7 pages. Sur-replies need leave for good cause and are limited to 5 pages. Both are due within 7 days of the filing they answer, and the judge may rule in the meantime. Oral argument is scheduled as needed by the courtroom deputy.

docs.t: Judge Mia Roberts Perez (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 12 meet-and-confer (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mia Roberts Perez, E.D. Pa.. Rule 12 meet-and-confer (trap): Except in pro se, bankruptcy, and social security cases, a party planning any Rule 12 motion must confer with opposing counsel at least 7 days before filing to allow a cure, and must attach a certification that the parties met and conferred. Noncompliant motions will be denied; the court issues an order to this effect when the complaint is filed.

docs.t: Judge Mia Roberts Perez (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment: joint statement of facts (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mia Roberts Perez, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: joint statement of facts (trap): Every summary judgment motion needs a jointly prepared statement of facts, filed separately, with a joint exhibit list and exhibit index. At least 28 days before the motion deadline the movant serves numbered facts with record cites; at least 14 days before, the respondent serves responses directly under each paragraph with cites; the movant may then reply under each paragraph. This exchange is served, not filed, and yields a single statement. Cross-movants may each file one, but with a single consolidated set of exhibits.

docs.t: Judge Mia Roberts Perez (E.D. Pa.) — Chambers contact and filing format
docs.x: Judge Mia Roberts Perez, E.D. Pa.. Chambers contact and filing format: Phone or email chambers (Perez_Chambers@paed.uscourts.gov) only on scheduling and non-substantive matters, starting with Courtroom Deputy Mia Harvey (267-299-7589), then Judicial Assistant Patrick Mountney (267-299-7580). Law clerks may discuss scheduling but cannot advise. Everything submitted is in 12-point Times New Roman with 1-inch margins. ECF filings, including exhibits, must be text-searchable, with descriptive exhibit file names. Cite docketed documents by docket number and don’t re-file them as exhibits. Parties and intervenors must also disclose any third party funding any part of the litigation, beyond Rule 7.1. At least one E.D. Pa. bar member must attend hearings and trials absent leave.

docs.t: Judge Mia Roberts Perez (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Mia Roberts Perez, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference: Held in person in chambers once an answer is filed (sometimes while a motion to dismiss is pending). Lead trial counsel must attend, with an appearance entered, unless a substitution is approved in advance. Submit the joint Rule 26(f) report on the judge’s template by email to chambers by the deadline in the scheduling notice; flawed or incomplete reports are returned. Explain any proposed discovery period over 90 days. File threshold motions (dismiss, transfer, add parties) before the conference and be ready to argue them there. Parties may ask that Magistrate Judge Pamela A. Carlos conduct settlement discussions.

docs.t: Judge Mia Roberts Perez (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Mia Roberts Perez, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial: A final pretrial conference is held in all civil and criminal cases. File the L.R. 16.1 pretrial memorandum before it, with agreed jury instructions, special interrogatories, and verdict forms on substantive issues only; give alternatives with authority if you disagree. Before the final pretrial conference, submit a joint neutral statement of facts and joint voir dire of no more than 15 questions, highlighting only disputed questions.

docs.t: Judge Mia Roberts Perez (E.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mia Roberts Perez, E.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Cases in the trial pool must be ready on 48 hours’ notice. Requests to extend a trial date must be made in writing to chambers 30 days before trial. Openings are limited to 30 minutes and closings to 45. Objections should be only “objection” and the rule number; sidebars sparingly. Counsel meet each morning on witness and evidence order and tell the court. Counsel decide which exhibits go to the jury; if they disagree, ask for a ruling as soon as the jury retires.

docs.t: Judge Mia Roberts Perez (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Mia Roberts Perez, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: The deputy contacts counsel within 72 hours of arraignment to schedule a status conference on motions and deadlines. The plea memorandum (elements with citations, maximum penalties, plea terms, factual basis), plea agreement, and acknowledgment of rights go to the court 2 days before the change-of-plea hearing. Departure motions (other than 5K1.1) are due 2 weeks before sentencing; 5K1.1 motions 1 week before. Both sides’ sentencing memoranda are due 1 week before; the government must document restitution by victim.

docs.t: Judge Paul S. Diamond (E.D. Pa.) — Preliminary pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul S. Diamond, E.D. Pa.. Preliminary pretrial conference (trap): Held in chambers as soon as practicable after a responsive pleading is filed. Lead counsel must attend, know every aspect of the case, and have full settlement authority, and must bring the client (or, for a corporation, a representative with full settlement authority). Requests to appear by phone or Zoom will not be granted. Before the conference the parties must sign a written clawback agreement (FRE 502(e)) and file it with their Rule 26(f) memorandum no later than 7 days before the conference. The trial date is set immediately after the conference.

docs.t: Judge Paul S. Diamond (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul S. Diamond, E.D. Pa.. Discovery (trap): Discovery should start as soon as possible and ordinarily be well underway by the preliminary pretrial conference. Generally 30 to 75 days is enough unless the case is complex; the judge is not inclined to extend discovery or other deadlines. Discovery is not stayed while any motion is pending, including a motion to dismiss or for a protective order, unless otherwise ordered. After certifying a reasonable effort to resolve it (L.R. 26.1(f)), email chambers a brief letter describing the dispute with the disputed request attached. The judge usually holds a telephone conference promptly, often before any response is due. For disputes during a deposition, phone chambers from the deposition. Rule 34 objections must be specific and say whether anything is withheld; general objections will rarely be appropriate and may draw sanctions. Producing

docs.t: Judge Paul S. Diamond (E.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul S. Diamond, E.D. Pa.. Motions (trap): Double-spaced, 14-point Times New Roman, margins of at least 1 inch. Memoranda capped at 25 pages (excluding tables) and replies at 12; declarations and affirmations at 20 pages each. Leave to exceed only for good cause. Replies are due within 14 days of the response and sur-replies within 7 days of the reply; neither may include declarations or exhibits. The judge normally will not wait for a reply before ruling. Oral argument generally is not required.

docs.t: Judge Paul S. Diamond (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Paul S. Diamond, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: The movant must file a separate, short, concise statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs with specific record cites; omitting it may be grounds for denial. The non-movant responds paragraph by paragraph with record cites, and uncontroverted facts may be deemed admitted.

docs.t: Judge Paul S. Diamond (E.D. Pa.) — Chambers copies
docs.x: Judge Paul S. Diamond, E.D. Pa.. Chambers copies: For summary judgment motions, the movant must deliver a copy of the filings to chambers by 12 noon the next business day, printed single-sided on high-quality opaque white paper. Evidence over 50 pages for any motion goes to chambers in hard copy, in a three-ring binder with an index and right-side tab dividers. No copies of cases available on Lexis or Westlaw. The judge expects a courtesy copy of any appellate brief in an appeal from the judge’s decisions.

docs.t: Judge Paul S. Diamond (E.D. Pa.) — Continuances and late filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul S. Diamond, E.D. Pa.. Continuances and late filings (trap): Continuances and extensions generally will not be granted. A motion needs a detailed good-cause declaration, must disclose prior requests and how they were ruled on, must include a proposed order, and must be filed on ECF no later than 5 business days before the date; later requests are denied absent compelling circumstances (for example, serious injury or illness). A late filing may be docketed only with leave: file a motion for leave to file out of time with a good-cause declaration, attaching the late filing as an exhibit.

docs.t: Judge Paul S. Diamond (E.D. Pa.) — Filing, service, and contact
docs.x: Judge Paul S. Diamond, E.D. Pa.. Filing, service, and contact: All documents, including stipulations and proposed orders, are filed on ECF, not delivered to the Clerk. Defendants not timely served under Rule 4(m) will be dismissed without prejudice. Law clerks may be contacted on scheduling and procedural matters only. Courtroom deputy: Joseph Walton, (267) 299-7730.

docs.t: Judge Paul S. Diamond (E.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Paul S. Diamond, E.D. Pa.. Trial: The judge is extremely reluctant to continue trial dates. Notify the civil deputy or law clerks immediately of conflicts that may affect the trial schedule. Stipulate to as many matters as possible before trial. Each day, tell the court and opposing counsel which witnesses you expect to call the next trial day.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Savage (E.D. Pa.) — Chambers contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Savage, E.D. Pa.. Chambers contact (trap): Written communication about a case must be by filing. Letters are allowed only for an unanticipated personal matter (such as medical problems) or to report settlement, and don’t copy the court on correspondence between counsel. If a filing can’t address a problem in time, call chambers (Deputy Clerk Alex Eggert, 267-299-7480).

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Savage (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Savage, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference: The Rule 26(f) meeting must be a substantive discussion of the discovery plan, facts, law, and settlement; pending motions don’t excuse it, and parties who don’t comply have no voice at the scheduling conference. Lead trial counsel, not an associate, must attend, with settlement authority and ready to argue pending motions. Pro hac vice motions must state the attorney’s admissions, why the party wants that attorney, and why the attorney is especially qualified; the Clerk’s form alone is inadequate and will be denied. The judge’s 26(f) form expects discovery to end 120 to 150 days after the conference and simultaneous expert reports, absent compelling reasons.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Savage (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Savage, E.D. Pa.. Discovery (trap): Rule 26(a) disclosures are due within 14 days of the order scheduling the Rule 16 conference, and discovery starts on notice of the conference regardless of pending motions. Discovery motions are often decided before any response. A motion to compel based on failure to respond timely will be granted; other disputes are ruled on in a phone conference the same or next day. The Local Rule 26.1(f) certification must detail resolution efforts.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Savage (E.D. Pa.) — Default e-discovery order
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Savage, E.D. Pa.. Default e-discovery order: If parties can’t agree on e-discovery before the Rule 16 conference, a default order applies: before the 26(f) conference exchange custodians, systems, limited-access data, retention coordinator and policy, and an e-discovery liaison. Limited-access sources are searched only after the initial search and on narrow requests; productions default to image files with metadata preserved, and native format needs particularized need. A preservation agreement is due within 30 days of discovery, with compliance statements filed within 7 days of identifying custodians.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Savage (E.D. Pa.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Savage, E.D. Pa.. Motions: Oral argument is not routine; request it in the motion or response. Replies may be filed within 7 days of the opposition, limited to 10 pages and to issues in the opposition. No further briefs.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Savage (E.D. Pa.) — Final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Savage, E.D. Pa.. Final pretrial conference (trap): Pretrial memoranda must detail each witness’s testimony; labeling it “liability” or “damages” is insufficient. Give notice of deposition use in the memorandum. Provide one copy of each objected-to exhibit and two copies of an exhibit schedule, in a tabbed three-ring binder. All motions and witness and exhibit objections are ruled on at the conference. Deposition objections must be in writing before the conference, by page and line with the basis, with a highlighted transcript. The trial procedures say outstanding videotape objections must be presented at least 10 days before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Savage (E.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Savage, E.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Trial-pool cases must be ready to start on 48 hours’ notice. Resolve voir dire differences the day before jury selection. Exhibits are admitted at the close of each party’s case-in-chief, not during testimony; publish them at the end of the examination or before a break unless permission is sought before the witness takes the stand. Bring an extra copy of each exhibit at trial. No speaking objections; sidebars are rare. Only one attorney per party per witness or legal point. Edit videotapes beforehand and test courtroom equipment with the deputy. Joint jury instructions cover substantive elements only (no basic instructions); failure to cooperate draws sanctions. Mark modifications to model instructions (additions underlined, deletions bracketed). Counsel must be available on 15 minutes’ notice during deliberations; non-jury cases need a s

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Savage (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Savage, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Suppression, Starks, and Daubert hearings are at least two weeks before trial, and the government must file proposed findings before the hearing begins. Pretrial conferences are held only in complex or multi-attorney cases. Points for charge are due 7 days before trial; the government’s trial memorandum one week before trial; guilty plea memoranda 2 days before the plea hearing. Departure motions (other than §5K1.1) are due two weeks before sentencing, §5K1.1 motions one week before; sentencing memoranda from both sides one week before, with copies to chambers (Room 9614) and Probation. Restitution details go in the government’s memorandum.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Motions and briefing (trap): Briefs supporting or opposing a motion are limited to 30 double-spaced 12-point pages, excluding tables and attachments; briefs of 20 pages or more need a table of contents and table of authorities. Every factual assertion needs a pinpoint record cite, and legal citations need pinpoints too. Responses to Rule 12(b) and Rule 56 motions are due 21 days after service. Replies are allowed within 7 days of the opposition, up to 10 pages, limited to new issues. Sur-replies only with prior permission for good cause, up to 5 pages. The court may rule without waiting for either. Oral argument when requested or helpful, with no set days; clients are encouraged to attend argument on dispositive motions.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies and stipulations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies and stipulations (trap): Send one courtesy copy of any motion, brief, or memorandum over 10 pages to chambers when filed, printed double-sided in a three-ring binder with dividers between exhibits. Do not file stipulations on ECF; submit stipulations and consent decrees needing approval with original signatures (faxed signatures accepted). They are not effective until approved. Spell the judge’s name BEETLESTONE, not BETTLESTONE.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment: joint appendix (trap)
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: joint appendix (trap): The movant must start a meet-and-confer to build a single joint appendix of all exhibits either side will cite, filed by the movant with the motion, consecutively Bates-stamped with a table of contents and cited by Bates number. The opponent may add an addendum continuing the numbering. Material outside the appendix will not be considered. The movant files a numbered Statement of Undisputed Material Facts citing the appendix; the opponent files a Statement of Disputed Material Facts responding after each paragraph and adding its own facts; the movant then files (even without a reply brief) a single Reply Statement responding to the added facts, and emails it to chambers in Word.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Correspondence and contact
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Correspondence and contact: Letters are allowed only for transmittals, when the court asks, uncontested Rule 16 deadline extensions not affecting trial or pool placement, help with a discovery dispute, personal matters affecting participation, and settlement notice; everything else by filing. Law clerk contact is strongly discouraged; phone inquiries go to Deputy Clerk Mike Beck (267-299-7450). For court-set phone conferences, the moving party (the U.S. Attorney’s Office in criminal cases) gathers everyone and then calls the deputy.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Continuances and extensions
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Continuances and extensions: Extensions need compelling circumstances. Requests affecting trial, discovery, or dispositive motion deadlines must be made well ahead, and dispositive motion and trial dates move only in very limited circumstances. Unopposed requests may be made by letter or joint stipulation; opposed requests must be filed as a motion. Trial continuances are strongly discouraged and need good cause: email the request to chambers, copying opposing counsel, with their position (no formal motion needed). If opposed, the requester sets up a conference call with the court.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap): File the joint Rule 26(f) status report on ECF at least 3 business days before the Rule 16 conference; complete initial disclosures at least 7 days before. Lead trial counsel must attend with settlement authority; a party’s unexcused absence can bring monetary sanctions. Begin discovery on receipt of the notice scheduling the conference. Standard-track cases usually get up to 90 days of discovery from the conference; extensions only for a time certain and a specific purpose. Discovery disputes: after L.R. 26.1(f) efforts, file brief letters on the docket; the judge generally holds a phone conference. If a motion to compel is still needed, motion and memorandum together are limited to 10 double-spaced pages, with a response in 5 days under the same limit and a substantive 26.1(f) certification. The court may sanct

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Injunctions, settlement, and arbitration
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Injunctions, settlement, and arbitration: Absent an emergency preventing it, a TRO petitioner must notify the respondent, serve the petition and proposed order if practical, and give notice of the hearing. Proposed findings and conclusions are preferred before the hearing and may be required within 24 hours after. The judge favors consolidating the PI hearing with trial on the merits under Rule 65(a)(2). Settlement conferences may be referred to a magistrate judge; the judge does not take part in settlement talks in non-jury cases. Arbitration cases normally get no pretrial conference or scheduling order; after a trial de novo demand, discovery and dispositive motions are ordinarily not allowed. The judge will consider appointing the Federal Defender for financially eligible petitioners in § 2241 immigration-enforcement cases.

docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Pretrial memoranda (per L.R. 16.1(c)) must add all stipulations, objections to authenticity, admissibility (other than relevance), expert qualifications, and Rule 701 opinions with grounds and authority, and deposition designations with counter-designations. Lead trial counsel must attend the final pretrial conference, where in limine motions (preferably written and filed well in advance) are heard and video deposition objections must be resolved, with tabbed transcripts. The court may impose time limits. Joint substantive jury instructions and verdict forms are due on the scheduling-order date, plus each party’s own on disputed issues, with Word copies to chambers. A joint statement of the case (generally no more than 3 pages) is due to chambers at least 3 days before trial. Non-jury cases: proposed findings and conclusions at least 7 days be

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Exhibits
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Exhibits: Prepare a single set of exhibits numbered sequentially regardless of which side offers them, with no duplicates, in binders with a table of contents (Exhibit/Bates number, description, Stipulations, Introduced, Admitted); two copies for the court. A witness may not testify to an exhibit’s content until it is admitted unless the parties agree. At the close of evidence, give the court a thumb drive of admitted exhibits only, for the jury.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Trial and courtroom conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Trial and courtroom conduct (trap): Trials usually have a date certain; court may sit from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. or later. The judge conducts voir dire with party input and rarely allows juror notes. The jury is usually charged before closings. Stay within 10 minutes of the courthouse during deliberations. Phones must be off, not silent; violators risk confiscation. No food, drink, or gum. Rise to address the court; approach witnesses only with leave; don’t confer with a testifying witness until excused; sidebars are discouraged. Seating or extra-table requests go to the deputy at least 1 week before trial. Give opposing counsel and the court the next day’s witness list in order, and don’t run out of witnesses. Only one attorney per witness or point.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Trial continuance motions are due at least 14 days before trial, stating the defendant’s position, with a Speedy Trial Act proposed order containing ends-of-justice findings. Each party submits two copies of points for charge (numbered, one per page, with authority) and a verdict form at least 3 working days before trial, plus Word copies. The judge conducts voir dire. Plea memoranda are due 5 days before the plea. PSR objections and sentencing memoranda follow the Notice of Sentencing, with memoranda due no later than 5 days before sentencing.

docs.t: Judge Ana C. Reyes (D.D.C.) — Pre-motion conference for dispositive motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Ana C. Reyes, D.D.C.. Pre-motion conference for dispositive motions (trap): Before filing any dispositive motion, file on ECF a notice (not a letter) of no more than 4 double-spaced pages stating the basis, legal standards, and claims at issue; other parties respond within one week in a filing of similar length. Then contact the courtroom deputy to set an in-person conference (video only with permission) 1–2 weeks after the response. For Rule 12(b) motions, the notice’s filing date counts for Rule 12 timing. The requirement does not apply to incarcerated pro se litigants or immigration mandamus cases.
