docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Exhibits: plaintiff (or government) numbers, defendant letters; make all exhibits available for inspection 1 week before the final pretrial conference, with exhibit lists to chambers by the deadline set there. Authentication of inspected exhibits is deemed established unless contested by notice at or before that conference. Disclose computer-generated evidence and data 1 week before trial. Stipulated jury instructions, one per page with authority, double spaced, plus each party’s disputed instructions, go directly to chambers in Word (on USB per the page). The court gives its own introductory and concluding instructions and charges the jury before closing. The court conducts general voir dire but counsel may question jurors; contentious questions are due in writing 3 days before voir dire. Raise mid-trial evidentiary issues before or after the t

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases (trap): Counsel must meet within 10 days of arraignment, or the government files the 03-AO-027 Discovery Notice. Pretrial motions are due 20 days after arraignment; date changes need a motion with a stipulation and Speedy Trial Act waiver if the trial date moves. The defendant must attend all hearings unless excused, and writs must be submitted 4 weeks before the court date. Witness lists, proposed voir dire, a joint case summary, joint jury instructions, verdict form, and trial briefs go through CM/ECF Utilities by the scheduling order deadline. Foundation, chain-of-custody, and scientific-analysis challenges are due at or before the final pretrial conference with an item-by-item good-faith basis (the order gives 7 days before trial for scientific analysis). Use yellow and blue exhibit stickers; witnesses, including law enforcement, tes

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Contact with chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Contact with chambers (trap): Staff will not advise anyone on motion practice (whether, what, how, or when to file); callers are referred to the rules and these guidelines. In the rare case you must call or email the court, include opposing counsel. Do not ask about the status of pending motions, and do not call to confirm a scheduling conference: unless canceled on the docket, it goes forward.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Motions (trap): Seek concurrence on every motion by speaking with opposing counsel in person or by phone, preferably before drafting, and more than pro forma. Failure to seek concurrence or follow L.R. 7.1(a) may get the motion struck. Briefs must be in searchable text, and exhibits filed with the CM/ECF exhibit feature, or the motion may be struck. If a brief and its exhibits exceed 12 pages in total, include a table of contents, a table of authorities, and an index of exhibits. References to briefs, filings, or another party’s argument must cite the docket number and the “PgID” number.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Hearings and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Hearings and courtesy copies: Motions are typically decided on the briefs without a hearing. Hearing continuances are granted only on motion for good cause. No courtesy copies; the judge prefers that none be submitted.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Appearances and conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Appearances and conduct (trap): Pro hac vice admission is not permitted (L.R. 83.20(c)), and waivers are highly disfavored. Telephonic appearances are very rarely allowed and never at scheduling conferences. Business attire in court and on video. Stand when addressing the court, jury, or witnesses and when the jury enters or leaves; ask before approaching the bench, witnesses, or jury, and don’t touch the bench, stand, or jury box. The courtroom has no public WiFi; counsel table offers HDMI, VGA, and 3.5mm audio inputs, and no devices, cords, or adapters are provided. You may arrange a visit to test the equipment.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling and discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling and discovery (trap): The court orders a joint discovery plan on its template and sets a scheduling conference, likely by Zoom. Early discovery by agreement is encouraged. The discovery period is strictly enforced; in rare cases one extension is allowed on a detailed showing of good cause, requested no later than 1 week before discovery closes. Consider contacting the court for informal resolution before filing a discovery motion. Discovery motions generally go to a discovery master or magistrate judge, and parties acting in bad faith bear the master’s costs.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Stipulated orders
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Stipulated orders: Stipulations are encouraged for routine matters such as filing extensions. Submit them in Word or WordPerfect through CM/ECF Utilities > Proposed Orders > Submit Proposed Order; noncompliant stipulations may be summarily struck. Allow 1–2 days for entry.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Jurisdiction, TROs, and ADR
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Jurisdiction, TROs, and ADR: Subject-matter jurisdiction is reviewed in every case; unclear jurisdictional grounds bring an order to show cause why the case should not be dismissed or remanded. Ex parte TRO requests are rarely considered; confer before any preliminary injunction hearing. The court may refer cases to a private mediator from its list (or one the parties jointly pick) or to a magistrate judge. If you mediate privately without a referral, tell the court the mediator’s name, contact information, and date in advance.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Civil pretrial and trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Civil pretrial and trial (trap): The trial date is set in the initial scheduling order. Motions in limine are due at least 10 days before trial. Trial briefs are optional, due 5 days before trial, and may not contain new motions. Exchange exhibits and give the court a joint bench book of all exhibits, after conferring on admissibility. Joint proposed jury instructions are due before the final pretrial conference; any disagreements go in a single filing with agreed, plaintiff’s, and defendants’ instructions and responses. In bench trials, proposed findings and conclusions may be submitted before or during trial. Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., with a break around 11:00; counsel must be seated and ready by 8:30. One lawyer per side handles each advocacy function (an entire opening, each witness). Redirect is allowed only on good cause. Struck-jur

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases (trap): The government must immediately tell the court and defense counsel if any part of the case or investigation was opened in the U.S. Attorney’s Office before August 18, 2008; the judge may recuse. Comply with Local Criminal Rule 12.1 and L.R. 7.1(a) before any pretrial motion. No Rule 11(c)(1)(C) agreements; Rule 11(c)(1)(B) agreements and well-supported 5K1.1 departures are accepted. Negotiated pleas with sentencing restrictions, significant count reductions, or similar concessions are not ordinarily accepted after the final pretrial conference and plea cutoff. At the plea hearing, the AUSA should summarize the agreement in 120 seconds or less. Notices contesting foundation, chain of custody, or scientific analysis are due at least 7 days before trial; motions in limine at least 10 days before trial; proposed jury instruction

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Pro se litigants
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Pro se litigants: Pro se litigants must follow the same rules and guidelines as attorneys. Letters to the court are not pleadings or motions and will be stricken.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): A courtesy copy of all dispositive motion papers (including responses, replies, and all exhibits) must go directly to chambers. For non-dispositive motions, a copy is required when the papers’ exhibits total more than 50 pages. Copies must show the .pdf header across the top, have exhibit tabs extending past the right edge, and be bound book-style along the left margin (comb, zip-band, or wire). Noncompliant copies are returned for reformatting before they are considered. Send the copy the same day you e-file; if it relates to a proceeding within the next 5 days or needs immediate attention, hand-deliver it to chambers by the morning of the next business day.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Motions and deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Motions and deadlines (trap): The clerk sends the hearing notice; dispositive motions are argued about 10 weeks after filing. No briefing schedule is issued, and L.R. 7.1(e) and Rule 6 response and reply deadlines are enforced even when the hearing is far off. Page extensions are not routinely granted. Extensions of time are not granted as a matter of course: explain specifically the unforeseen circumstances and propose a timetable for completing the task. Motions and responses need a separate brief; keep argument and factual summaries out of the motion itself. Never embed a motion in a response, reply, or another motion’s text or footnotes.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Briefing content
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Briefing content: Support the statement of material facts with record citations. Submit cited deposition pages plus the adjacent pages; if more than 5 pages are cited or the deposition is especially relevant, include the entire transcript. Underline or highlight specific references where applicable. Use well-chosen authority rather than boilerplate, and submit copies of cited unpublished or specialty-reporter opinions with the brief.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Discovery: Discovery may begin once the answer is received. It averages 3 to 4 months (6 to 12 months for complex or foreign discovery), and the court will honor a reasonable Rule 26(f) schedule. Serve discovery early enough to be answered and completed by the cutoff. Parties may stipulate to a short discovery extension only if no other case management date must move; submit the stipulation and order through CM/ECF Utilities (Proposed Order). Stipulated protective orders must comply with Rule 26(c) and may not pre-authorize sealed filings (sealing is governed by L.R. 5.3). Discovery motions are routinely referred to the magistrate judge; after referral, communicate only with that chambers.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling and status conferences
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling and status conferences: After the answer, the court requires the parties to submit, not file, a short statement of the case summarizing facts, legal basis, and proposed discovery; a Rule 26(f) discovery plan may be submitted instead. The scheduling order issues from these, with a conference only for unusual case management issues. Status conferences may be requested for good cause by letter and are often held by conference call.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — ADR and settlement
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. ADR and settlement: Facilitative mediation with an experienced facilitator is strongly encouraged, ideally after most discovery and before dispositive motions; it can be arranged without contacting chambers. Case evaluation under L.R. 16.3 requires a filed stipulation agreeing to be bound by all of Mich. Ct. R. 2.403, including sanctions, and must be completed before the final pretrial conference. A settlement conference is typically set before the close of discovery. Parties, trial attorneys, insurance representatives, and others needed to resolve the case must attend unless excused in advance for explained reasons.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial conference (trap): Generally 2 weeks before trial; pending motions in limine are heard the same day. Jury cases: proposed voir dire and joint jury instructions are due to chambers by close of business 1 week before the final pretrial conference, with instructions submitted through CM/ECF Utilities (Proposed Order). Bench trials: proposed findings, conclusions, and trial briefs through the same function on the same deadline.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Jury trials start on Tuesdays and run Monday through Friday, normally 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.; counsel must be in court by 8:15 a.m. The weekly schedule is set at the start of each trial week. In bench trials, provide two copies of exhibits to the court.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — TROs
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. TROs: Rule 65 governs. TROs without notice are rarely granted. Call the courtroom deputy when you file a TRO motion.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal sentencing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Criminal sentencing (trap): On the day of a plea or verdict, defense counsel must arrange a probation interview within 7 days of conviction. The PSR is due within 56 days of conviction, and defense counsel must review it (and any addendum) with the defendant in person. PSR objections go to probation and opposing counsel, not the clerk, within 14 days of receipt, in a distinct document clearly marked as objections; improperly identified objections may be returned. Sentencing motions and memoranda are optional but must be filed at least 1 week before sentencing, with a copy to the probation officer. Habeas, Social Security, and prisoner civil rights cases generally go to the magistrate judge for a report and recommendation.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Informal matters and conferences
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Informal matters and conferences: No set time for informal matters (minor issues such as deadline changes or minor disputes). Notify opposing counsel, find out their availability, and call the judicial assistant to set an in-court or telephone conference. Most minor, agreed deadline changes can be handled by filing a motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents; the judge rules on these as soon as possible. For an emergency motion needing a formal hearing on the record, call chambers. After the Case Management Order is entered, counsel may call chambers to set a scheduling or status conference or a conference call about problems keeping the case from moving forward.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference (trap): Usually set after all defendants have answered or responded to the complaint; a party wanting it sooner must file a motion. Conferences are in person, usually in chambers (in the courtroom, on the record, when a party is pro se). Out-of-town counsel may participate by conference call but must give chambers contact information at least one business day before. Do not send an unprepared substitute or a lawyer who cannot commit on trial counsel’s calendar; be ready to discuss the facts, the Rule 16 Order’s topics, and settlement.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Before any discovery motion, the moving party must actually speak to opposing counsel, in person or by telephone, and certify the attempt in the motion; motions without the certification are denied without prejudice. If opposing counsel won’t return calls, detail those efforts in the certification. The judge either sets a hearing or rules on the papers. To request a hearing, say so in the motion or memorandum and call chambers once briefing is complete. For emergencies, call chambers for a preliminary telephone conference.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Expert disclosures (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Expert disclosures (trap): Non-retained experts (such as treating physicians and employees whose duties don’t regularly involve expert testimony) must be identified and given a Rule 26(a)(2)(C) summary of opinions and supporting facts, on the same date as the party’s other expert disclosures unless the CMO says otherwise. Undisclosed opinions may be excluded, and objections to sufficiency must be made promptly. Be ready at the Rule 16 conference to discuss expected expert types and the timing of reports and depositions; absent a stipulation, Rule 26 applies.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Most civil cases are referred to mediation; be ready to discuss timing at the Rule 16 conference and consider what discovery is needed for a meaningful mediation. Once referred, ADR deadlines are binding and may be extended only by court order.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Trial setting and final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Trial setting and final pretrial conference: Most cases are set on a firm three-week trial docket; assume your case is #1 unless told otherwise. St. Louis juries are picked at 9:00 a.m. or 1:15 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays. If the case is still on the docket two weeks before trial, chambers will call to set a final pretrial conference, normally two or three business days before trial; be ready to argue motions in limine there. For Cape Girardeau or Hannibal trials, the final pretrial conference is held in St. Louis unless you are told otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire and jury selection (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire and jury selection (trap): Before the case is called, supply an agreed, neutral brief statement of the case to read to the panel. Juror lists are not available in advance and must be returned to the clerk after selection. Attorneys usually conduct part of voir dire after the judge’s introductory questions; questions go to the panel as a whole first, with follow-ups to those who respond. No rapport-building questions, promises, speeches, argument, or talk about yourself. If the judge conducts all voir dire, proposed questions are due no later than two business days before trial. Challenges for cause are made outside the panel’s presence. Peremptories are exercised from the number to be seated plus total strikes, plaintiff first; in civil cases all remaining jurors deliberate and no alternates are designated.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Trial practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Trial practice (trap): Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; preliminary matters may not be raised at the start of the day but are heard 30 minutes before start, at lunch, or at day’s end. Examine from the lectern; no permission is needed to hand a witness an exhibit, but don’t hover over the witness or jury. No recross as of right: approach the bench and state the areas sought, which must be new matter from redirect. Exhibits in opening need opposing counsel’s consent and advance notice to the judge. Pre-mark exhibits (plaintiffs numbers, defendants letters; defendants with more than 78 exhibits should use a scheme like AA, AB … rather than AAAAA). Bring a list of exhibits received without objection, show each exhibit to opposing counsel before a witness, and show demonstratives in advance of trial. Before trial, tell opposing counsel which deposition po

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Jury instructions: Eighth Circuit Model Instructions for boilerplate and covered matters; Missouri Approved Instructions (or another state’s) for state-law issues. Meet and confer and, whenever possible, submit one joint package. Submit two complete sets: a clean set headed only “Instruction No. ___” and a set showing source, offering party, and numbers. Give the court a clean copy on disk at the final pretrial conference. Without agreement, expect the instruction conference in the evening after the trial day.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom technology and decorum
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom technology and decorum: The judge strongly encourages using the evidence camera (ELMO). Schedule training (usually 30 minutes or less) with the Case Management Team before trial; none on the day of trial. Confer with the Clerk’s office before using your own computer, and bring your own audio tape player. Stand when speaking and when the jury enters; address witnesses and counsel by last name with titles (never first names, even clients); no food, gum, drinks other than water, or cell phone use; no expressions to the jury from counsel table; young children only with an adult seated with them in the gallery.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Scheduling, informal matters, and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Scheduling, informal matters, and contact (trap): No regular informal matters docket. Most minor agreed deadline changes are handled by a written motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents. Telephone conferences on scheduling disputes are sometimes available; notify opposing counsel before seeking one. For an emergency needing a formal hearing on the record, call chambers to schedule it. In civil cases, do not email the judge or chambers staff unless specifically told to. In criminal cases, counsel may email the Judicial Assistant, Brian Crow (brian_crow@moed.uscourts.gov), about scheduling and logistics only, not substance.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Courtesy copies and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Courtesy copies and proposed orders: Courtesy copies of bulky summary judgment motions are helpful; no courtesy copies of other filings are needed. Any courtesy copy must show the ECF header (document number, page number, and filing date) on every page. File proposed orders in ECF as an exhibit to the motion, and also email them in Word format to Brian Crow.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Before any discovery motion, meet and confer and certify that you did. Exchanging “nasty letters or emails” does not count, and the judge does not want them attached to motions; counsel must actually talk. If the opponent won’t return calls, say so in the certification. The judge either sets discovery motions for hearing or rules on the papers. For an emergency discovery dispute, schedule a telephone conference on the record.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference and ADR
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference and ADR: Civil Rule 16 conferences are usually set after all defendants answer; a party wanting one sooner must file a motion. Follow the Order Setting Rule 16 Conference and the Case Management Order. Come prepared to discuss the facts, everything in the Rule 16 order (including settlement), and likely types of expert witnesses. Do not send an unprepared substitute attorney. Most civil cases are referred to mediation; be ready to discuss timing of the referral at the Rule 16 conference.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Experts (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Experts (trap): Absent stipulation or CMO provisions, Rule 26(a)(2) governs disclosure. Experts are limited to opinions and bases disclosed in discovery (report or deposition) and, absent unusual circumstances, may not supplement or change opinions after expert discovery closes; CMO deadlines override different deadlines in rules or statutes. Expert reports are hearsay and usually not admitted (impeachment use is allowed). Do not “tender the witness as an expert” or ask the judge to tell the jury a witness is an expert, and do not ask witnesses whether they consider themselves experts. Experts may not opine on the law or sum up the evidence.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Trial settings and final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Trial settings and final pretrial conference (trap): Most cases are set on a firm two-week trial docket mixing jury and non-jury, civil and criminal cases. Juries are picked at 9 a.m. and 1:15 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays in St. Louis. Unless told otherwise, assume you are #1 on the docket. Appear 30 minutes before scheduled jury selection for a final pretrial conference on evidentiary issues, motions in limine, and scheduling; an earlier, longer conference may be set or requested. In civil cases, exhibits not objected to in the pretrial submissions are received at the start of trial; bring a list of them. Order daily copy through the Case Management Team well in advance.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire: The jury panel list (names, municipality, employers, occupation, and spouse’s employer and occupation) is handed out as jurors enter; it is not provided in advance. Return all copies after selection. After the judge’s introductory questions, counsel may conduct part of voir dire. Ask general questions of the whole panel, then follow up with those who respond. No speeches, arguing the case, seeking promises, or questions just to hear jurors speak; submit in writing any questions you want the judge to ask. Cause challenges are made outside the panel’s presence; plaintiff then defense make peremptories. In civil cases the first seven or eight remaining jurors are seated (all “real” jurors); in criminal cases the first twelve, with alternates depending on trial length.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Trial conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Trial conduct (trap): Openings, examinations, and closings from the lectern; no permission needed to approach the witness, but never hover over the witness or jury. State objections by legal basis only, standing. No recross as of right: approach the bench and state the areas sought; allowed only if redirect raised something new. Pre-mark exhibits per the CMO (plaintiff/government numbers, defendants letters). Closing arguments presumptively 20 minutes; plaintiff or government must use more than 50% of its time in the opening part. Jurors may take notes. Evidence presentation equipment is expected to be used at all trials; schedule training (about 30 minutes) with the Case Management Team, and confer with the clerk’s office first if using your own computer.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Depositions and jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Depositions and jury instructions: If you will read less than you designated, tell opposing counsel in advance so objections and counter-designations can be resolved; the judge expects disputes worked out first. Give advance notice of video depositions so objections can be ruled on in time for editing. The court reporter does not transcribe deposition testimony: you must provide a page-and-line list of what was actually read or shown. The judge uses 8th Circuit Model instructions for boilerplate and sends written instructions to the jury. Email Word versions of proposed instructions to Brian Crow.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom decorum
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom decorum: Stand when the jury enters and leaves and whenever speaking. Attorney phones silenced; client, witness, and spectator phones off. No photos or recording; laptops for audience members need advance approval. No food, drink other than water, or gum. Address witnesses and opposing counsel by last name and title, never first names, even your own client.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Comply with Local Rule 3.04 before any discovery motion or memorandum (including non-parties served with subpoenas); noncompliant filings will be denied. Letters, emails, or texts do not satisfy meet-and-confer. If unresolved, the parties must jointly file a single memorandum of no more than 3 pages requesting a conference, stating their attempts at resolution and concisely describing (e.g., in bullet points) the issues. Lead counsel or counsel with authority to resolve the dispute must appear in person at the discovery conference. With incarcerated pro se litigants, confer only in writing, and discovery motions may be filed without requesting a conference.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): Local Rule 13.05 governs sealing in civil and criminal cases; the court strongly prefers redaction to sealing and requires a sufficient legal and factual basis (citing IDT Corp. v. eBay and Flynt v. Lombardi). Noncompliant protective orders and motions will be denied. A proposed protective order addressing sealed filings must require leave of court to file under seal and provide for lifting the seal at the end of the case. One addressing discovery disputes must expressly require the Requirement No. 7 discovery procedure.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Motions and record citations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Motions and record citations (trap): Comply with Local Rule 4.01. Record citations must be consistent and, whenever possible, include the CM/ECF docket entry number; the court will not search the record. With numerous exhibits, file an “Exhibit Key” listing the docket entry for each exhibit (e.g., “Exhibit AA appears at Doc. [22-27].”). Duplicative filings are prohibited: parties with the same counsel moving on the same or similar grounds must file a single motion, memorandum, and statement of uncontroverted material facts; parties with different counsel are encouraged to coordinate.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Extensions, unopposed motions, and CMO changes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Extensions, unopposed motions, and CMO changes (trap): Extension motions must state all parties’ positions, show in the title any prior requests (e.g., “Third Request for an Extension”), and cite and apply the legal standard (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(b); Fed. R. Crim. P. 45(b)); consent alone is not enough. Label joint, unopposed, or consent motions as such in both the body and the CM/ECF title. To change a CMO term not amendable by stipulation under Rule 29, file a motion before the deadline, soliciting all parties’ consent.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference: Usually set after all defendants have filed a responsive pleading; contact chambers to request an earlier one. Absent truly exceptional circumstances, lead counsel must appear in person, prepared on the facts and the joint scheduling plan.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Most civil cases are referred to ADR, usually for about 60 days. Plaintiff’s counsel is lead counsel for coordinating ADR and must work with opposing counsel to select a neutral. Notify the court immediately upon settlement.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — AI and sanctions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. AI and sanctions (trap): Filers are responsible for any AI-generated content under Rule 11. Any filing that hallucinates citations or misstates the law, or was not properly reviewed or reasonably investigated, “will result in” sanctions. Failure to comply with any part of the Requirements may draw sanctions ranging from fees and penalties to striking pleadings, dismissal, or default judgment (Local Rule 5.04).

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Withdrawal and e-filing
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Withdrawal and e-filing: A motion to withdraw that leaves an individual unrepresented should include an affidavit showing the client’s consent; without consent, request an ex parte hearing. Create PDFs by printing or publishing to PDF, not by scanning paper copies, so they are text-searchable.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom rules
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom rules: On arrival, lead counsel reports to the courtroom deputy and introduces others; no one may speak without an entered appearance. Stand and speak into the lectern microphone; stand when the judge or jury enters or exits. No photos, recording, or broadcasting; laptops and tablets only at counsel tables; no food, gum, drinks other than water, or audible devices; phones off unless authorized in advance. Dress appropriately and tell clients and witnesses the rules.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Informals (trap)
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Informals (trap): All informal matters must be submitted in writing and filed in CM/ECF; they reach the judge within 24 hours of filing, and rulings go to counsel through CM/ECF. If an informal needs more immediate attention, or to request a conference, call the judicial assistant (Beverly Goff) or the Case Management Team (314-244-7533).

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Trial docket (trap)
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Trial docket (trap): One-week trial docket: all cases are set on Monday and ride the docket for the week, so be ready for trial at any time during the setting week. Criminal cases take priority over civil. Cases are tried in the order best suited to the docket (considering age and anticipated length). If a case settles, the next case is expected to be ready. Bumped cases receive a new setting. Notify the Judicial Assistant or Team Leader well in advance if a case needs special attention.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference: Usually in person; by telephone on the parties’ request if an attorney is more than 100 miles away (the court initiates the call). Conferences with a pro se party are held in the courtroom on the record. A proposed Joint Scheduling Plan is due no later than 10 days before the conference; plaintiff initiates the meeting and files it unless ordered otherwise. Lack of cooperation does not excuse filing; a separate plan must attach a memorandum explaining why a joint plan could not be filed.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Case management order changes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Case management order changes (trap): Requests to change the CMO must be in writing and filed. Changes to trial dates and dispositive-motion deadlines are not routinely granted and need a statement of good cause.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): Proposed protective orders must follow Local Rule 13.05 and include a date certain for lifting the seal or returning documents; a proposed order without one will be denied without prejudice.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Civil cases (except habeas) are referred to ADR on the parties’ request. Plaintiff’s counsel (or agreed counsel) is lead counsel and must notify the clerk of the agreed neutral within twenty days of the referral’s start; ADR deadlines are binding and extendable only by court order. Notify the court immediately whether or not a settlement is reached; after settlement, file a Stipulation for Dismissal within thirty days.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Pretrial conference and voir dire
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Pretrial conference and voir dire: Pretrial conferences are discretionary; if required, held no later than seven (7) days before trial. After the court’s initial questions, counsel may conduct voir dire subject to time limits set at the pretrial conference. The court may conduct voir dire itself; then counsel are encouraged to submit questions no later than five (5) days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Jury Evidence System
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Jury Evidence System: The judge uses the Jury Evidence System for jury trials. Provide the clerk digital copies of all admitted exhibits: documents in Word or PDF, photos as JPEG, and videos as WMV or MP4.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Other
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Other: Patent cases: counsel should be familiar with the court’s Local Patent Rules. Schedule attorney admissions through the judicial assistant or Case Management Team, who also handle docket questions.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Scheduling, conferences, and contact
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Scheduling, conferences, and contact: Most minor agreed deadline changes can be made by a motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents. The judge is generally available for telephone conferences on minor issues; notify opposing counsel before seeking one, and call chambers to set a scheduling or status conference or an emergency hearing. Criminal matters go to the judicial assistant; civil matters to the law clerks. Staff can discuss scheduling, logistics, procedure, and chambers preferences, but not substance.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 and case management
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 and case management: After all defendants answer, the court orders a joint proposed scheduling plan and enters a CMO based on it unless a party requests, or the court orders, a Rule 16 conference. Rule 16 conferences are in person in chambers unless ordered otherwise (in the courtroom, on the record, if a party is pro se). Out-of-town counsel may appear by Zoom or phone with prior approval. Don’t send an unprepared substitute or a lawyer who can’t commit on trial counsel’s calendar.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes: Meet and confer and certify it in the motion (Local Rule 3.04); if your opponent won’t return calls, say so in the certification. The judge typically rules on the papers unless a hearing is needed; for emergencies, call chambers for a telephone conference.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Briefing and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Briefing and courtesy copies (trap): Include a Westlaw citation for unreported decisions. Label e-filed exhibits as referenced in the brief (e.g., Smith deposition, Acme policy), per Section II.F. of the CM/ECF Procedures Manual. Courtesy copies of all pretrial materials are required, and copies of motions with voluminous exhibits may be requested; print them after e-filing so ECF headers show. Mail or hand-deliver to chambers at 111 South Tenth Street, Suite 3N, St. Louis, MO 63102.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Generative AI (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Generative AI (trap): Signers are fully responsible for GenAI-assisted content and must independently verify all quotations, citations, and analysis before filing. Do not put confidential litigation material (e.g., protected discovery or sealed documents) into GenAI tools that may retain, train on, or disclose it. Violations may draw sanctions.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Most civil cases are referred to mediation; when proposing a mediation date, consider the discovery needed and time to exchange it. Once referred, ADR deadlines are binding and may be extended only with the court’s approval.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Trial setting and final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Trial setting and final pretrial conference: Most cases are set on a firm two-week trial docket; assume your case is first unless told otherwise. St. Louis juries are picked at 9:00 a.m. or 1:15 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays. Final pretrial conferences are normally the Thursday before the Monday of trial; be ready to argue motions in limine there. Schedule courtroom-technology training with the Case Management Team before trial (none on trial day), and confer with the Clerk’s office before using your own computer.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire and jury selection
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire and jury selection: Supply an agreed, neutral brief statement of the case before the case is called. Juror lists are given shortly before the panel enters and must be returned after selection. Attorneys usually conduct part of voir dire after the judge’s introductory questions; no unnecessary questions (such as preferred news sources), promises, speeches, argument, or talk about yourself. Cause challenges are made outside the panel’s presence; peremptories are taken from the number to be seated plus total strikes, plaintiff first, and in civil cases no alternates are designated.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Jury instructions (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Jury instructions (trap): Use Eighth Circuit Model Instructions whenever possible, and always for introductory and boilerplate instructions; instructions from other sources need supporting case authority. Meet and confer and file a joint packet of agreed instructions plus separate packets of disputed ones, annotated on the record. Email clean Word copies headed “Instruction No. ___” (top center) to chambers, plus a clean merged full packet showing disputes in redline.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Trial practice and decorum
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Trial practice and decorum: Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; preliminary matters are heard 30 minutes before start, at lunch, or at day’s end, not when the jury is ready. Examine from the lectern; no permission needed to hand a witness an exhibit. State objections’ legal basis without argument. Pre-mark exhibits (plaintiffs numbers, defendants letters), bring a list of exhibits admissible without objection, and show demonstratives to opposing counsel before trial. Before trial, tell opposing counsel which deposition portions you will actually offer and give advance notice of video depositions. Exhibits in opening need consent and notice to the judge. Stand when speaking; address witnesses and counsel by last name (never first names, even clients); no food, gum, drinks other than water, or cell phones; no expressions to the jury from counsel table.

docs.t: Judge Maria Lanahan (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Maria Lanahan, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Follow Local Rule 3.04 before any discovery memorandum or motion; this applies to anyone served with a subpoena too. Meet and confer means actually speaking to each other (unless a party is self-represented and incarcerated). Noncompliant motions are denied without prejudice. If still unresolved, the parties must jointly file a motion requesting a telephone conference, summarizing positions and resolution efforts in no more than three (3) pages. Email related documents (requests, objections) to Abby Ojolola at abby_ojolola@moed.uscourts.gov. Protective orders must require compliance with Local Rule 13.05 for sealing and expressly require this discovery-dispute procedure.

docs.t: Judge Maria Lanahan (E.D. Mo.) — Motions and record citations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Maria Lanahan, E.D. Mo.. Motions and record citations (trap): Comply with Local Rule 4.01. Record citations must include a CM/ECF docket entry number whenever possible; the court will not search the record for poorly cited evidence. With numerous exhibits, file an “Exhibit Key” listing where each exhibit appears (e.g., “Exhibit AA appears at Doc. [22-27].”). No duplicative filings: co-parties with the same counsel moving on the same or similar grounds must file a single motion, memorandum, and statement of uncontroverted material facts. Label joint, unopposed, or consent motions as such in both the body and the CM/ECF title. Convert documents to PDF by printing or publishing, not scanning.

docs.t: Judge Maria Lanahan (E.D. Mo.) — Extensions and CMO amendments (trap)
docs.x: Judge Maria Lanahan, E.D. Mo.. R. Civ. P. 6(b); Fed. R. Crim. P. 45(b)); consent of all parties is not sufficient. To change a CMO provision that can’t be changed by stipulation under Rule 29, file a motion to amend before the deadline, seeking consent and labeling it “unopposed” or “consent” as appropriate.

docs.t: Judge Maria Lanahan (E.D. Mo.) — Sealing
docs.x: Judge Maria Lanahan, E.D. Mo.. Sealing: Local Rule 13.05 governs; noncompliant motions are denied. Provide a sufficient legal and factual basis for any sealing request (citing IDT Corp. v. eBay, Flynt v. Lombardi, and Kaiser v. St. Luke’s).

docs.t: Judge Maria Lanahan (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Maria Lanahan, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference: Usually set after all defendants file a responsive pleading; contact chambers to request an expedited conference. Absent truly exceptional circumstances, lead counsel must appear in person, prepared to discuss the facts and the joint scheduling plan.

docs.t: Judge Maria Lanahan (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge Maria Lanahan, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Most civil cases are referred to ADR, usually for 60 days. Plaintiff’s counsel is lead counsel and works with opposing counsel to select a neutral. Notify the court immediately upon settlement.

docs.t: Judge Maria Lanahan (E.D. Mo.) — AI use (trap)
docs.x: Judge Maria Lanahan, E.D. Mo.. AI use (trap): Attorneys and pro se litigants must ensure any generative-AI-drafted language is fully checked by a human using print reporters or traditional legal databases. Sanctions for non-existent caselaw or misrepresented cases can include fines, striking a document, and dismissal.

docs.t: Judge Maria Lanahan (E.D. Mo.) — Withdrawal of counsel
docs.x: Judge Maria Lanahan, E.D. Mo.. Withdrawal of counsel: A motion to withdraw that leaves an individual unrepresented should include an affidavit documenting the individual’s consent; without consent, request an ex parte hearing.

No food, drink other than water, gum, or audible devices; phones off unless authorized in advance. Self-represented litigants must follow the Federal Rules, Local Rules, and these Requirements.

docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Case management orders (trap): Civil and criminal CMO deadlines are strictly enforced. Modifications require a motion to amend and are granted only on a showing of exceptional circumstances.

Notify the court immediately of settlement and file a Stipulation for Dismissal within thirty (30) days.

docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Final pretrial conference and jury instructions: Appear 30 minutes before jury selection for an on-the-record final pretrial conference in the designated courtroom (8:30 for a 9:00 a.m. selection; 12:45 for 1:15 p.m.) on evidentiary issues, motions in limine, and scheduling. Use 8th Circuit Model Instructions when possible (boilerplate must be based on them); instructions from other sources need case authority. Meet and confer and, when possible, submit one joint package with a “clean” copy (only “Instruction No. ___”) and a “dirty” copy of each, and email Word versions to Brian Crow. docs.t: Judge Rodney W. Sippel (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire
docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire: The judge introduces and asks introductory questions; submit specific questions in writing. Each party must give the judge a list of potential witnesses the morning of trial. Counsel get twenty minutes of voir dire. Cause challenges are made outside the panel’s presence; plaintiff then defense make strikes. Return all jury lists after selection.

docs.t: Judge Rodney W. Sippel (E.D. Mo.) — Trial conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Trial conduct (trap): Do not raise preliminary matters at the start of the trial day; the court is available 15 minutes before the start, at lunch, or at day’s end. No speaking objections: stand and state the legal basis in a word or phrase. Bench conferences and sidebars are disfavored; make record arguments at breaks. No recross as of right (only if redirect raised something new). Closings presumptively twenty minutes. Disclose witness identity and order at least 24 hours before the trial day they are called. Show each exhibit to opposing counsel before a witness, and show demonstratives and summaries before trial. Only one lawyer per party may question a witness. Disputes over tape-recording transcripts must be raised at least five (5) days before trial if counsel cannot resolve them.

docs.t: Judge Rodney W. Sippel (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom decorum
docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom decorum: Notify the Deputy Clerk on arrival and introduce others. No comments, expressions, or signals toward the jury or witnesses; violators may be ejected, and signaling a testifying witness is treated as contempt. Children may watch only with an adult seated with them who is not a party, attorney, or case agent.

docs.x: Judge Stephen R. Clark, E.D. Mo.. docs.x: Judge Stephen R. Clark, E.D. Mo.. Pleadings and amendments (trap): After filing a complaint, counterclaim, or crossclaim, give opposing counsel a .doc or .docx copy. docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Motions: conferral statement (trap): Every motion must state on the first page whether it is opposed or unopposed. docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Motions in limine and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Motions in limine and Daubert (trap): Each party gets one omnibus motion in limine, not to exceed 40 pages, filed by the scheduling-order deadline and addressed at the pretrial conference as needed. An untimely motion will not be considered absent manifest injustice; do not wait until trial to seek exclusion of evidence you knew was coming. Motions in limine must concern specific evidence; motions asking that the parties be ordered to follow the Federal Rules of Evidence are discouraged. Raise objections to scientific and expert evidence by timely motion in limine, and Daubert issues by a Daubert motion under the scheduling-order deadline.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Civil extensions and settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Civil extensions and settlement conferences (trap): Extension requests (including of the scheduling order) must be in writing and, absent an emergency, filed at least 48 hours before the deadline. They must meet the FRCP standards as applied by the Tenth Circuit and LCvR 7-1(i). The gap between the discovery deadline and trial is not an invitation to extend deadlines while keeping the trial date; any extension will likely affect the trial setting. Parties are expected to attend a settlement conference midway through discovery. A request to continue it because discovery is incomplete will not be granted absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Civil pretrial conference and trial
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Civil pretrial conference and trial: Counsel must meet before the pretrial conference to review all proposed exhibits; claims at trial of having “never seen” a listed exhibit are viewed with disfavor. One week before the conference, give the court two notebooks of exhibits that still have objections. At the conference, be ready to argue exhibit objections, pending dispositive motions, and pending motions in limine, and to address anything likely to cause sidebars or lengthy argument at trial. The court intends to end the conference with the case ready for trial and prefers record-making at recesses or before or after the trial day. Civil trials are set on a trailing docket behind criminal cases; counsel learn their position at pretrial. No continuance merely because of the number of criminal cases, which routinely resolve on the eve of trial, so

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Evidentiary hearings
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Evidentiary hearings: For any hearing expected to be evidentiary, email the courtroom deputy proposed witness and exhibit lists 3 business days before, and give the deputy 4 paper copies of a typewritten witness list and exhibit list before the hearing.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Criminal hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Criminal hearings (trap): All counsel, including out-of-state counsel, must attend all criminal hearings in person, and are encouraged to arrive 15 minutes early. Pretrial conferences are set on a pretrial docket and heard in ascending case-number order; one expected to run more than 10 minutes, or with pending motions the court wishes to hear, may be moved to a separate time or the end of the docket. Sentencings and revocations go on a sentencing docket; if one will run more than 30 minutes, notify the courtroom deputy as soon as possible.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Criminal continuances and speedy trial waivers (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Criminal continuances and speedy trial waivers (trap): Title every motion as unopposed, agreed, or opposed, and state each party’s position, including co-defendants’ (LCrR 12.1 and General Chambers Rule 5(a)). No proposed order is required. Unless the case is declared complex, a motion to continue trial requires a speedy trial waiver on the court’s required form, signed by defendant and counsel, specifically stating the excludable dates (from the current trial docket date to the requested one). Each defendant in a multi-defendant case must file one. The court will not rule without a correct, executed waiver on file. File the waiver with the motion if possible; if it is not on file before the pretrial conference, the motion is taken up there, but the court discourages using pretrial conferences just to obtain waivers. docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Criminal motions and discovery status reports (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Criminal motions and discovery status reports (trap): Responses are due within 7 days of the motion’s filing (LCrR 12.1(E)). Replies only with leave, limited to 5 pages. One motion to suppress per defendant absent leave. Motions on probation or supervised release must also state the U.S. Probation Office’s position. File the joint status report on discovery in CM/ECF as a “Status Report,” with a substantive update: materials yet to be produced, materials requested but not produced, the reasons, the expected timing, and any anticipated discovery motion. Failing to file it without notice is unacceptable. A JSR is unnecessary if a change of plea hearing is already set. If the case is ready for a plea, notify the courtroom deputy on or before the JSR due date; skipping the JSR merely because a plea is anticipated is unacceptable. Meet and confer in

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Changes of plea
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Changes of plea: When a defendant is ready to plead, email the courtroom deputy (Katherine_Hayes@oked.uscourts.gov) with dates that work and dates to avoid. Most plea hearings are referred to the criminal duty magistrate judge. Plea documents (petition to enter plea of guilty, and plea agreement and supplement if applicable) generally must be received at least 3 business days before the hearing. Absent good cause, any superseding information must be filed at least 3 days before.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Courtroom conduct
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Courtroom conduct: Electronic devices must be off (use at trial may be approved for good cause). No food, gum, or mints, and no beverages other than bottled water. Do not put feet or objects that could mar surfaces on courtroom furniture. LGnR 3 governs courtroom behavior. Only the attorney questioning a witness may object to that testimony or argue at a sidebar. Do not greet or introduce yourself to adverse witnesses; start cross-examination without preliminaries, and do not face or address jurors while questioning. Handle physical evidence with disposable gloves; give the courtroom deputy advance notice of biological or biohazard exhibits, preferably at the pretrial conference and no later than the day exhibit lists are due. The court strongly encourages new or inexperienced attorneys to participate and will allow multiple attorneys to speak i

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (E.D. Okla.) — Electronic discovery
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Electronic discovery: The page links the court’s 2008 ESI guidelines (adapted from the District of Kansas), which ask counsel to learn their clients’ systems before the Rule 26(f) conference and to confer there on preservation, email, deleted and backup data, metadata, form of production, costs, and clawback or quick-peek agreements; the FRCP control over any conflict.

docs.t: Judge Ronald A. White (E.D. Okla.) — Changes of plea (trap)
docs.x: Judge Ronald A. White, E.D. Okla.. Changes of plea (trap): All plea forms must be completed and signed by all parties at least 3 business days before the change of plea hearing, and emailed in PDF to the courtroom deputy of the assigned U.S. magistrate judge (Toni Moore for Judge West, Joe Church for Judge Robertson, or Paige Bruce for Judge Jackson), not to Judge White’s chambers. Required forms: Consent to Proceed Via Video Teleconference, Consent to Magistrate for Change of Plea, the Waiver of Jury Form for Judge White, and a Waiver of Indictment if applicable. docs.t: Judge Ronald A. White (E.D. Okla.) — Contact
docs.x: Judge Ronald A. White, E.D. Okla.. Contact: Judge White is a senior judge in Muskogee (PO Box 1009, Muskogee, OK 74402; 918-684-7920). The courtroom deputy is Teka Stephens.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment: “alternative method” (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: “alternative method” (trap): Unless the Scheduling Order says otherwise, Rule 56 motions use the alternative method: the motion is an outline of the issues, no more than 5 double-spaced pages (excluding the stipulated facts), with no supporting memorandum under L.R. 7.1(c). It must affirm under Rule 11 that the non-movant has no legally sufficient evidentiary basis and request judgment. No later than 14 days before the dispositive motion deadline, the parties must meet and confer on material facts; the motion must include a concise joint Statement of Stipulated Material Facts in numbered paragraphs. Response due 21 days after service (25 pages, with evidence cited by exhibit, page, and line); the movant must file a Reply within 14 days (25 pages); optional Sur-reply within 7 days (10 pages). No leave needed for the Reply or Sur-reply. Fo

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Other motions and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Other motions and courtesy copies: Other civil motions follow L.R. 7.1, but memoranda and responses are capped at 15 double-spaced pages; replies and sur-replies may be filed without leave and are capped at 10 pages. Attach proposed orders to the motion or memorandum. Do not send filings to chambers instead of using ECF. No paper courtesy copies unless requested; email courtesy copies are allowed but not necessary. Motions are usually decided on the papers, with argument only when the judge finds it helpful.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Chambers communications
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Chambers communications: Telephone, email, or fax to chambers is allowed only for scheduling and other non-substantive matters; never ex parte on substance. Law clerks cannot give advice or grant relief. Civil: Kristen Pepin, (267) 299-7490, Chambers_of_Judge_Cynthia_M_Rufe@paed.uscourts.gov. Criminal and transcripts: Erica Pratt, (267) 299-7499, Erica_Pratt@paed.uscourts.gov. Do not email the judge directly. Stipulations needing approval or the judge’s signature must be emailed or faxed to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference: Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting at least 14 days before the Rule 16 conference, even if motions are pending; it must be substantive. Noncompliant parties will have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. The Rule 16 conference is by telephone. File the Rule 26(f) report at least 7 days before, stating whether and when the parties will be ready to discuss settlement. Lead trial counsel must participate and must have entered an appearance (unless a substitution is approved); pro hac vice applications must be approved before the conference.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes and extensions
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes and extensions: Straightforward discovery disputes may be raised in a telephone conference requested by a letter emailed or faxed to chambers, but only after exhaustively addressing the dispute with opposing counsel. Complicated matters need a formal motion. Extensions only for compelling circumstances and only if no other deadline is affected. Unopposed requests must say so and may be made by motion, letter, or joint stipulation; opposed requests must be filed as a motion.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): No confidentiality protective order unless required by statute or for demonstrated good cause (In re Avandia, 924 F.3d 662), though private confidentiality agreements are enforced as contracts. Any proposed protective order must include the judge’s required language that protected material may be filed under seal only by court order authorizing sealing of the specific material. No sealed filing in a civil case without leave, except in an emergency (then email or fax the documents and explain). Move publicly on ECF well ahead of the deadline, narrowly, stating opposing counsel’s consent, and email unredacted documents to chambers at the same time. If granted, file unredacted versions under seal on ECF with non-public portions highlighted, then file narrowly redacted public versions within 30 days.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement and ADR
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Settlement and ADR: Notify chambers promptly on settlement and request dismissal under L.R. 41.1 or another terminating procedure. The Scheduling Order requires a joint report, emailed or faxed to chambers and not filed, on whether the parties want a magistrate judge settlement conference, L.R. 53.3 mediation, or other ADR. The judge strongly encourages settlement conferences with Magistrate Judge Carol Sandra Moore Wells. To continue a settlement conference before Judge Wells, contact Judge Wells’s chambers directly; if the continuance exceeds 14 days, get Judge Rufe’s approval first.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Scheduling order and trial
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Scheduling order and trial: The sample Scheduling Order may allow adding or dropping claims or parties within 60 days without leave, sets defendant’s responsive expert reports 30 days after plaintiff’s, and dispositive motions 30 days after that. Trial is usually set after dispositive motions are resolved: the court orders a settlement status report, then asks for jointly proposed trial dates. The pretrial conference is shortly before trial; be ready to discuss motions in limine, voir dire, and trial procedures.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal motions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Criminal motions and continuances (trap): Pretrial motions are due at least 30 days before trial; supporting memoranda (25 pages) as soon as possible and no later than the hearing. Co-defendants may not join each other’s motions without leave. Post-trial memoranda and responses are capped at 25 pages; replies and sur-replies need leave and are capped at 10 pages. Trial continuance motions are due at least 14 days before trial, with a proposed order containing a detailed Speedy Trial Act ends-of-justice finding (18 U.S.C. § 3161(h)(7)). No letter requests. The pretrial conference is at least 3 days before trial. The judge conducts extensive voir dire; counsel may ask follow-up questions.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Sentencing
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Sentencing: Sentencing continuances are for good cause only, and requests over 90 days are generally not considered. Any further continuance needs a joint written request showing good cause and, if granted, a joint written status update every 30 days. Sentencing motions are due 14 days before sentencing (responses 7 days before); sentencing memoranda 7 days before (responses 3 days before).

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Meet and confer before motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Meet and confer before motions (trap): Before any discovery motion, Rule 12(b) motion, or other dispositive motion, the movant must confer with opposing counsel by substantive verbal communication (letters or emails don’t count) at least 5 days before filing, discuss the substance, and offer a chance to cure. A report that opposing counsel was unavailable or that reasonable efforts were made is insufficient. If unresolved, file a certification with the motion giving the date(s) and length of the discussion and a one-sentence description of each issue; each counsel should sign and date it. The court will deny a 12(b)(6), (e), or (f) motion or discovery motion that doesn’t comply, and a party that fails to respond to conferral attempts may be sanctioned. An amended complaint filed to cure deficiencies raised in the conference, with a certification attach

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Motions and briefs (trap): Briefs supporting or opposing a motion are limited to 25 pages (motions in limine excepted); leave to exceed requires a motion filed before the deadline showing good cause. Use 12-point Times New Roman, double spacing, one-inch margins, and numbered pages; all PDFs must be text-searchable. No reply briefs without leave. Move for leave within 5 days of the response, email a courtesy copy to chambers, highlight the specific issues needing reply, and do not attach a proposed reply. The court rules without a response and the order sets the reply’s scope and due date. File each exhibit as a separately numbered attachment with an objective, descriptive title (e.g., “6/14/19 Deposition of John Doe”). Oral argument is scheduled only when it helps the court; motions are frequently decided on the papers even if argument is requested.

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies: When exhibits or attachments to any filing exceed 20 pages, deliver one hard copy of the exhibits to chambers within 48 hours of docketing. More than two exhibits go in a binder, tabbed, with a table of contents matching the filing. For a Joint Statement of Undisputed Facts the moving party provides the copy; for cross-motions the parties agree who does (plaintiff if they can’t agree).

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): At least 28 days before moving, all parties must meet and confer on a neutral Joint Statement of Undisputed Facts, with exhibits, covering every undisputed fact any party will rely on; relevance or materiality is no reason to exclude a fact. No party may file a unilateral statement of undisputed facts; other facts go in the memorandum with record citations, and cite the Joint Statement where possible. If no agreement is reached, the movant must certify that. If briefing shows the parties actually agreed on enough material facts, the court may hold a hearing on sanctions or reject the filings and require a revised Joint Statement. Absent a scheduling-order deadline, oppositions are due in 30 days.

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Communication, extensions, and sealing
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Substantive communications must be docketed. Extensions, even joint or unopposed, require a motion on the docket showing good cause, made as early as possible; requests on the deadline day are typically denied. Exceptions: a filed joint stipulation (with a judge’s signature line) extending time to answer or move against an initial complaint by no more than 30 days, and unfiled agreements extending discovery deadlines that don’t alter the dispositive motion deadline. docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap): The Rule 16 conference is held as soon as possible after all defendants answer (contact chambers if not scheduled in a reasonable time). Lead trial counsel must attend (or substitute counsel with deep knowledge of the case if lead counsel is on trial), ready to address substance, settlement, and scheduling. A joint Rule 26(f) report in the judge’s format (a separate patent format exists) is due 5 days before. Discovery starts when the order scheduling the Rule 16 conference issues, not at the conference, and the discovery period runs from that order; it should normally end 90–120 days from that notice. The report form asks for initial disclosures already produced, signed authorizations (e.g., HIPAA), insurance details with the policy attached, and the latest demand and offer in jury cases only. docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Removed cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Removed cases (trap): If the notice of removal didn’t attach the state court complaint as a separately named exhibit, file an Amended Notice of Removal doing so; this doesn’t change deadlines. Within 21 days of removal, docket any state court answer without revision, and either reformat pending preliminary objections or dispositive motions to federal and local standards or file an answer (which withdraws them without waiving any legal issue).

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Settlement: Request a settlement conference by letter or email when all parties sincerely want one. Bench trials go to Magistrate Judge Lynne Sitarski or the court’s mediation program. In jury cases, Judge Weilheimer may conduct the conference only if all parties agree, in writing or on the record, that the judge may keep presiding if it fails. Conferences with Judge Weilheimer are in the courthouse with everyone with settlement authority present. Email a confidential settlement memorandum (not docketed or shared) with case strengths and weaknesses, critical documents, the latest offer and demand, settlement authority, and other helpful information. The Guidelines say 7 days before; the separate requirements sheet says at least 5 days.

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial conference and motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial conference and motions in limine (trap): Held after dispositive motions are decided (or if none are filed); lead trial counsel (or deeply knowledgeable substitute) must attend, and the court conducts settlement negotiations as part of it (parties not attending in person must be available by phone). A date-certain trial is usually set 60–90 days out. At least 7 days before, each counsel dockets a Pretrial Conference Memorandum: narrative of up to 3 double-spaced pages, witness list with up to two sentences per witness, exhibit list, stipulations, trial length, unavailable dates, damages claimed, the latest settlement negotiations (jury cases only), and whether the parties want an in-person settlement conference. Unlisted witnesses and exhibits may be precluded. Only verified conflicts count as unavailability (trial attachment, scheduled medical

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Trial dates are continued only for verified, truly emergency circumstances. The judge has no assigned courtroom; chambers gives the assignment at least 1 week before trial. Ask chambers whether you must bring your own technology. Bring 3 copies of all exhibits in pre-marked, tabbed three-ring binders with a 12-point table of contents in table format (number, description, identified, admitted); a joint binder is preferred.
