docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Pro hac vice and newer attorneys
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Pro hac vice and newer attorneys: While a pro hac vice motion is pending, local counsel must attend every appearance, including phone and video. If pro hac vice counsel shows unfamiliarity with the Local Rules or the judge’s protocols, the court may require local counsel at all appearances or revoke admission. The judge encourages letting newer associates argue; notify the court at sidebar or by email in advance with the associate’s and supervising counsel’s names, and supervising counsel may supplement.

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Patent cases
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Patent cases: The patent Rule 26(f) form adds a default schedule (initial contentions 1–2 weeks before the Rule 16 conference), an interim outside-counsel-only protective order, and disclosure of licenses and settlement agreements by the Rule 16 conference. Motions to compel require a conference with the court first. Claim construction: briefs are served, not filed, then combined into one Joint Claim Construction Brief term by term; a party proposing “plain and ordinary meaning” must explain it, and failing to propose a function and structure for an arguable means-plus-function term waives it. No Markman testimony without prior approval; absent other agreement, plaintiff picks the first term and sides alternate. Expert-report timeliness or scope objections must be raised within one week of the report or are waived; Daubert motions are due by the dispos

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Generative AI disclosure (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Generative AI disclosure (trap): Anyone who uses generative AI to prepare a filing must disclose that use, identify precisely which portions contain generated content, identify the tool and how it was used, and certify that every citation to the law or record was verified under Rule 11. Noncompliance may bring referral to the court’s Disciplinary Committee or a state bar, striking of the filing, monetary sanctions, or other sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Briefs and motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Briefs and motions (trap): Briefs are capped at 25 double-spaced pages in 12-point font, excluding tables and exhibits; any brief over 10 pages needs a table of contents and table of authorities. Footnotes are discouraged and should not contain citations. Noncompliant briefs may be stricken. To exceed 25 pages, move before the deadline; a pending motion does not extend the deadline. Put all grounds in one comprehensive motion (for example, not separate motions to dismiss per count). Replies are due within 7 days of the opposition, capped at 10 pages, and limited to new issues; no replies on motions in limine. Sur-replies need leave on motion.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Exhibits and summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Exhibits and summary judgment: File each exhibit as a separately numbered attachment titled with an objective description (for example, “6/14/19 Deposition of John Doe”). Text-searchable exhibits are encouraged. Rule 56 motions need a numbered statement of material facts with specific record citations; the opposition must respond paragraph by paragraph and may add numbered additional facts. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted, and failure to cite the record may defeat relief. Motions and responses need an exhibit index. The judge will rarely, if ever, grant summary judgment in a non-jury case.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Hearings, argument, and contact
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Hearings, argument, and contact: No set days for argument or evidentiary hearings; the judge schedules them when warranted. Request oral argument by letter or in the motion or response. In criminal cases argument on a substantive motion is generally allowed on request. Correspondence is allowed only on scheduling, discovery disputes, routine matters, or settlement; all else must be filed. Calls go to Courtroom Deputy Katie Rolon, 267-299-7530; never contact law clerks. Raise matters only after discussing them with opposing counsel, and be ready to state their position. For telephone conferences, the moving party (in criminal cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office) initiates the call and contacts the deputy once all are on. No cell phones.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 and continuances (trap): The Rule 16 conference is set shortly after all defendants answer. Submit a joint Rule 26(f) report with discovery plan to chambers at least 3 business days before. Parties who skip a substantive 26(f) meeting have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. Lead trial counsel must attend, with authority to discuss everything including settlement, and be ready on all claims, defenses, and L.R. 16.1(b) and Rule 16 and 26(a) topics. The trial date is set at the Rule 16 conference. Dates change only for a compelling reason, sought by letter detailing the basis, all counsel’s positions, and the delay sought. Settlement talks, “summer months,” other cases, and lack of diligent discovery are not compelling. Moving trial or the dispositive motion deadline is considered only in extraordinary circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Discovery: Standard-track discovery is usually 90 to 120 days from the Rule 16 conference; raise any need for more time at a conference. Routine disputes go to a telephone conference after a reasonable effort to resolve them; the judge may first require a joint letter. A motion to compel that follows is capped at 5 double-spaced pages in 12-point font (motion and memorandum together), with a 5-page response within 5 days. Sanctions may go to the prevailing party. Telephone rulings are available during depositions that would otherwise have to be adjourned. Lay opinion evidence under FRE 701 on liability or damages must be disclosed with supporting documents by the expert-report deadline.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): Protective orders and confidentiality agreements are approved only where absolutely necessary and for good cause, and must include the language: “the court reserves its inherent power to modify the terms of this agreement and permit the disclosure of information where the interest of justice so requires.” A confidentiality designation does not mean filings will be sealed; the party must show the interest in secrecy outweighs public access (Gratz Coll. v. Synergis). Pro hac vice motions without the fee are denied; admitted counsel must register for CM/ECF within 7 days.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Injunctions, settlement, and arbitration
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Injunctions, settlement, and arbitration: TRO and preliminary injunction requests are listed promptly; the judge may hold a pre-hearing conference and require proposed findings and conclusions before the hearing. The Scheduling Order refers cases to a magistrate judge for settlement; the judge does not take part in settlement talks in non-jury cases. Arbitration-track cases get no Rule 16 conference or Scheduling Order unless there is a de novo appeal; finish discovery before the arbitration hearing, after which discovery and dispositive motions are ordinarily not allowed.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial memoranda (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial memoranda (trap): Beyond L.R. 16.1(c), include all stipulations; particularized objections to authenticity, admissibility (other than relevance), expert qualifications, and FRE 701 lay opinion; and case-in-chief deposition designations by page and line with counter-designations. Exhibits should not include pleadings, written discovery responses, or transcripts without a specific reason. Submit one unified, tailored set of jury instructions and one verdict form; on disagreements give competing versions with an explanation. Use Third Circuit models where possible. File on the docket and email Word versions to Chambers_of_Judge_Pappert@paed.uscourts.gov. Raise videotaped-deposition objections with the pretrial memoranda, then edit the tapes per the ruling.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Trial: Submit one agreed set of voir dire questions 7 days before trial; the judge conducts voir dire and allows suggested follow-ups. Jurors may take notes. docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Communicating with chambers (trap): Written communication must be by filing. Don’t copy the court on correspondence between counsel; no faxes. Law clerks can’t give advice or grant continuances; don’t call them unless they call you. Phone the courtroom deputy only when writing can’t timely address scheduling, witness, exhibit, video-replay, or discovery-call arrangements.

File motions to dismiss, amend, transfer, add parties, and other threshold motions before the Rule 16 conference, and be ready to argue them there. docs.t: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Discovery: Rule 26(a) disclosures are due within 14 days of the order scheduling the Rule 16 conference, and discovery must start immediately on notice of that conference; pending motions don’t excuse it. Expect to report progress at the conference. For disputes, comply with Local Rule 26.1(f) with a certification detailing efforts to resolve; telephone conferences are encouraged, and a discovery motion may be decided before any response is filed. If the parties can’t agree on e-discovery, the default Order Governing Electronic Discovery applies (liaisons, sequenced searches, image-file production, a retention agreement within 30 days, and a statement of compliance within 7 days of identifying custodians).

docs.t: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: The motion must include a separate Statement of Undisputed Facts in numbered paragraphs limited to facts bearing on dispositive material issues. The opposition responds paragraph by paragraph and adds any further facts in separate numbered paragraphs; facts not controverted are admitted. Every fact must cite the specific record source, with page and line for documents and depositions.

docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Settlement, ADR, and confidentiality orders: Counsel must attend a settlement conference with the magistrate judge named in the scheduling order (the document names Magistrate Judge Carol Sandra Moore Wells), with parties or persons with full settlement authority unless excused in advance. Early ADR is strongly encouraged; explore court-annexed mediation (Local Rule 53.2.1) with clients and explain any decision not to participate in the Rule 26(f) report. Stipulated confidentiality or sealing orders need a detailed good-cause statement (Pansy) and must include, or substantially track: “The Court retains the right to allow disclosure of any subject covered by this stipulation or to modify this stipulation at any time in the interest of justice.”

docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Bring one copy of each exhibit and three copies of an exhibit schedule; at trial provide two copies of each exhibit, numbered consecutively in a single tabbed three-ring binder. The conference lasts 2–4 hours and is meant to resolve all evidentiary issues: confer first and come ready to argue remaining objections. Written deposition objections (page and line, basis, highlighted transcript) are due before the conference; video-deposition disputes at least 10 days before it. Cases in the trial pool must be ready to start on 48 hours’ notice.

Disputed instructions need authority, and modified model instructions show additions underlined and deletions bracketed. docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Replies need leave; motions ripe on response (trap): A motion is “ripe” once the response is filed. No set days for argument; the judge orders argument or grants a request made in writing in the motion, response, or reply.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Except in pro se prisoner cases, the parties must meet and confer about material facts at least 14 days before any Rule 56 motion is filed. The motion must include a Concise Statement of Stipulated Material Facts in numbered paragraphs, with record citations when possible. Any party relying on other facts must file a numbered Concise Statement of Additional Facts citing the precise pages of the record. A pending Rule 56 motion does not stay Scheduling Order deadlines; seek any extension by letter or motion.

docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Contact and correspondence: Phone inquiries go to Deputy Malissa Wolenski, (215) 597-1178; communication with law clerks is strongly discouraged. docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Preliminary pretrial conference: Usually set within 30 days after all defendants answer. Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting at least 14 days before; parties who don’t comply have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. At least 3 business days before, submit to chambers (not docketed) the completed Scheduling Information Report and the Rule 26(f) discovery plan. The report covers Rule 26(a) disclosures, readiness for trial, settlement timing, expected dispositive motions, trial time, and reasons for any discovery period over 4 months. Counsel must have client authority on all subjects including settlement, and be ready to argue any pending motions.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery and confidentiality
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Discovery and confidentiality: Discovery usually runs 60 to 90 days from the initial conference. R. 26.1(g). Confidentiality orders are entered only on a specific good-cause finding under Pansy v. Borough of Stroudsburg; private confidentiality agreements are allowed. Expert testimony is limited at trial to what was disclosed (CV and Rule 26(a)(2)(B) information) by the scheduling order dates, except for good cause.

docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Settlement, arbitration, and injunctions: The judge takes an active role in settlement, typically starting at the initial conference, and may hold an early settlement conference with parties or corporate principals present. Non-jury cases are usually referred to a magistrate judge for settlement. Damages are presumed not to exceed the $150,000 arbitration limit unless timely certified otherwise (L. Civ. R. 53.2.3(C)). After a trial de novo demand, expect a standard scheduling order, ordinarily no new discovery, and trial within 30 days. For TROs and injunctions, the judge usually holds a conference before scheduling a hearing and handles expedited discovery by phone.

docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Jury instructions and trial: File joint substantive instructions and verdict forms, plus each side’s instructions on disputed issues, each on a separate double-spaced page with accurate quotes and pinpoint citations; procedural instructions are not needed. Late submission can waive a claim or defense (L. Civ. R. 16.1); supplemental instructions are accepted until closings. The final pretrial conference is usually the week before trial. Give the court 3 copies of the exhibit schedule at the start of trial and 2 copies of each exhibit at first use. Offer exhibits after the first witness testifies about them; objected exhibits may not be testified to until received. Openings are usually 20 to 30 minutes and closings 30 to 45. docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Trial continuance motions need a proposed order with Speedy Trial Act findings and conclusions. Both sides should submit sentencing memoranda, framed by the Sentencing Guidelines, at least one week before sentencing.

Expect a pre-hearing conference; proposed findings and conclusions are preferred before the hearing and may be required within 24 hours after. Arbitration-track cases generally get no pretrial conference; finish discovery before the arbitration date. A trial de novo is expected within 60 days of the request. docs.x: Judge Karen S. Marston, E.D. Pa.. Pro hac vice and pro se: The judge does not accept the Clerk’s standard pro hac vice form. Pro se litigants who receive substantive help from a lawyer must identify the lawyer and the lawyer’s contribution in the filing.

docs.t: Judge Karen S. Marston (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Karen S. Marston, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial and trial: The final pretrial conference is about 2 weeks before trial. Pretrial memoranda are due at least 7 days before it and must describe each witness’s testimony in detail, plus stipulations, particularized objections (authenticity, non-relevance admissibility, expert qualifications, FRE 701), and deposition designations with counter-designations. One unified set of tailored jury instructions (Third Circuit models) and one verdict form; competing versions with explanations where disputed. File and email Word versions to Chambers_Judge_Marston@paed.uscourts.gov. Voir dire questions may be submitted 10 days before trial; the judge conducts individual voir dire at sidebar or in the jury room. Trial briefs 7 days before trial. Motions in limine: 5-page briefs, no more than 5 per party without leave. Joint exhibit book in hard copy and on a thu

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Meet and confer before any motion (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Meet and confer before any motion (trap): Before filing any motion, including under Rule 12 or 56, 28 U.S.C. § 1441, or § 1404, confer with opposing counsel at least 7 days before filing to discuss its substance and offer a chance to cure pleading deficiencies. It must be substantive verbal communication; letters, emails, or a report that counsel was unavailable or that reasonable efforts failed are insufficient. If unresolved, file a certification with the motion giving the date(s) of discussion and stating that the parties couldn’t resolve it. Nonconforming motions will be denied. This doesn’t apply where either side is pro se or to bankruptcy or Social Security appeals.

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Communicating with chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Communicating with chambers (trap): Scheduling and non-substantive matters may be raised by phone or by a letter sent by email; an email request without a letter attached will not be considered. Everything else must be filed. Contact the deputy, Leesa Ciamaichelo (267-299-7550 or 267-299-7559), or Judge_Hodge_Chambers@paed.uscourts.gov; never the judge’s personal email. Stipulations needing approval must be emailed to chambers and state the basis for the relief, or they will be rejected. All other filings go through ECF only (attach proposed orders to the motion); the court won’t act on anything not docketed. Counsel and parties may email chambers the names, pronouns, and honorifics they want the court to use. Anyone using generative AI for filings or discovery papers must comply with Rules 11(b) and 26(g) and ethical rules.

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies and formatting (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies and formatting (trap): Mail or ship one courtesy copy of any submission of 25 pages or more, including exhibits; exhibits printed double-sided, marked, tabbed, and in a 3-ring binder. Courtesy copies are not accepted by email. Use 12-point Times New Roman with one-inch margins; PDFs must be text-searchable.

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Extensions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Extensions and continuances (trap): Request extensions by emailed letter stating the basis and opposing counsel’s position, with a proposed order; opponents respond by letter. Unopposed requests must be a stipulation signed by all counsel, emailed with a signature line for the judge, and are not automatically granted. Deadlines can’t be extended without approval. A request filed less than 2 business days before the deadline may not be decided in time. Trial and hearing continuances are granted reluctantly, only for compelling circumstances and good cause, especially if counsel haven’t been diligent.

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefs
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Motions and briefs: Put all grounds in one comprehensive motion (e.g., a motion to dismiss shouldn’t be split by count). Opening and opposition briefs are limited to 25 pages; a motion to exceed must be filed before the deadline showing good cause. Replies may be filed within 7 days of service of the opposition, up to 10 pages, addressing only opposition issues. Surreplies require leave and are limited to 5 pages. Request oral argument by letter or in the motion or response; the judge decides case by case and is most likely to hold it on dispositive motions.

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): The motion (25 pages, excluding the statement) must outline the issues targeted, affirm under Rule 11 that the non-movant lacks a legally sufficient evidentiary basis, include a separate concise Statement of Undisputed Material Facts in numbered paragraphs with exhibit, page, and line cites, and request judgment. The movant must give opposing counsel a Word version of the statement. The response is due 28 days after service (the 2023 Rule 26(f) form’s Schedule A says 30 days after the dispositive motion deadline), up to 25 pages, with a separate statement answering each numbered paragraph using the movant’s Word file plus numbered additional facts. Reply within 14 days, up to 10 pages; the non-movant may file an optional surreply within 7 days of the reply, up to 10 pages. A joint appendix of exhibits is encouraged; any appendix n

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and discovery
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery: The Rule 16 conference is set once an answer is filed (sometimes while a preliminary motion is pending), by video or in person. Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting no later than 14 days before it; pending motions don’t excuse it, and noncompliant parties have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. File on ECF and email chambers the Rule 26(f) report on the judge’s template at least 7 days before the conference, with specific dates for all pretrial deadlines and when the parties will be ready to discuss settlement. Lead trial counsel must participate and enter an appearance first unless a substitution is approved; pro hac vice applications must be approved beforehand. Counsel need settlement authority or a client with authority present or available by phone. Schedule A’s standard plan: fact discovery 120 days from the c

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement, confidentiality orders, and injunctions
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Settlement, confidentiality orders, and injunctions: Settlement is addressed at all stages; early referral to a magistrate judge is encouraged. On settling, notify chambers immediately and request dismissal under Local Rule 41.1. Stipulated confidentiality or sealing orders require Rule 26(c)(1)(G) good cause (Pansy) and must include, or substantially track: “The Court retains the right to allow disclosure of any subject covered by this stipulation or to modify this stipulation at any time in the interest of justice.” For TROs and preliminary injunctions, the judge will hold a conference if needed and decide as soon as possible, generally permits expedited discovery, and may require proposed findings and conclusions. A trial scheduling order setting all pretrial deadlines issues after dispositive motions are decided (or if none are filed); the final pretr

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases (trap): Pretrial motions and responses follow the scheduling order and are heard before trial. In multi-defendant cases motions are heard jointly; joining a codefendant’s motion requires leave, with supporting memoranda (20 pages) no later than 7 days before the hearing. Post-trial responses are limited to 20 pages; replies and surreplies need leave and are limited to 10. Continuance motions must be filed at least 14 days before trial (no letters) with a proposed order containing Speedy Trial Act ends-of-justice findings; without the defendant’s signed waiver, a hearing will be set. Guilty plea memorandum, plea agreement, and acknowledgment of rights go to chambers by email 7 days before the change-of-plea hearing. The judge conducts voir dire (counsel email proposed questions in Word and may ask follow-ups on request); a pretrial conferenc

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — AI disclosure (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. AI disclosure (trap): Any attorney or pro se party who used AI in any way to prepare a filing in a case assigned to Judge Baylson must disclose that use in a clear, plain factual statement and certify that every citation to law or the record has been verified as accurate (Standing Order of June 6, 2023, repeated in the Notice).

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies and email (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies and email (trap): When pleadings or motions come with lengthy (over 20 pages) or multiple exhibits, mail or deliver to chambers a bound, tabbed paper copy with exhibits. Courtesy copies may not be emailed. Email to chambers is not allowed except in direct reply to a chambers email, when the court directs an email submission, or with express permission in very limited circumstances. The Conference Information Report is the exception: it is emailed (or faxed to 267-299-5078) to chambers. Scheduling letters are accepted, but not substantive correspondence; changes to ordered or rule deadlines need a stipulation or motion. Calls to law clerks are discouraged; scheduling goes to Deputy Clerk Lori DiSanti for civil and criminal matters.

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and replies
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Motions and replies: Replies are allowed without leave within 7 days of service of the opposition, capped at 15 pages and limited to refuting the opposition. Surreplies need leave and should be sought only if the reply raised new arguments or citations (in summary judgment cross-motions, surreplies follow the reply rules). Expert-testimony motions must be made promptly and before dispositive motions (or, if none, before the final pretrial conference). Threshold motions (dismiss, amend, transfer, add parties) should be filed before the preliminary pretrial conference when possible. Oral argument is usually set for dispositive or complex motions without controlling appellate authority. Questions may be sent in advance; answer them at argument without submitting anything in writing beforehand. Junior attorneys who worked on the briefs are encouraged to argue

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: The movant files a “Statement of Undisputed Facts” in numbered paragraphs with record references, preferably as a separate document. The respondent answers each paragraph in a “Statement of Disputed or Undisputed Facts” with record references and may add numbered additional facts. The movant’s reply is due within 7 days (15 pages) and must answer the respondent’s additional facts paragraph by paragraph. Record cites must be specific (document, deponent and page, or declaration paragraph). Index and tab exhibits. The parties may stipulate to a briefing schedule.

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — Preliminary pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Preliminary pretrial conference: Held, usually by telephone and for about 10 minutes, roughly 60 to 90 days after filing or answer, or soon after reassignment. If trial or associate counsel truly cannot attend, call chambers to reschedule. Before it, counsel must confer under Rule 26(f) on jurisdictional defects, settlement, schedules, discovery, and a trial pool date, and email the Conference Information Report (discovery completion date, any protracted-discovery segments, preferred settlement forum, and trial time estimates). Make Rule 26(a) initial disclosures before the conference and start discovery before or right after it; no discovery report need be filed unless ordered. Bates-stamp produced documents.

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery and scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Discovery and scheduling (trap): One deadline covers both fact and expert discovery, generally 120 days after the conference; all reasonably foreseeable discovery must be served, noticed, and completed by then. Later discovery is allowed only by agreement and without delaying trial. File a Motion to Compel promptly under L.R. 26.1(f) when responses are not forthcoming; it will be granted without waiting for an opposition. Other discovery motions are usually resolved by telephone conference, often before a response. To change the Scheduling Order, agree on dates and submit a letter or stipulation in the original order’s format; otherwise request a telephone conference. Stipulations go on CM/ECF with a signature block for the judge. Unexcused violations are sanctionable under Rule 16(f).

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement and confidentiality
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Settlement and confidentiality: A settlement conference is required in every case, before a court-appointed or independent mediator, a magistrate judge, or Judge Baylson; counsel largely control the timing. The court will not pressure parties to settle. Confidentiality agreements need no court approval. If submitted for approval, they must define the protected materials specifically and may not restrict use of confidential materials by the court or at any hearing or trial.

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — Final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Final pretrial conference: Held near the trial pool date, in court or by phone; all trial counsel must attend. Raise logistics (out-of-order witnesses, video depositions), significant legal and evidentiary issues, and objections to the other side’s exhibits; the court sets dates for motions in limine and designations. Objections to authenticity, expert qualifications or admissibility, and FRE 701 lay opinion must be stated with particularity in the pretrial memorandum (L.R. 16.1(c)) or by motion. Requests for an offer of proof go to opposing counsel before trial, with a motion if unsatisfied. The court may impose time limits on a party’s case or on specific witnesses. Motions in limine may be filed after dispositive motions are decided or near the trial pool date; responses within 7 days.

docs.t: Judge Michael Baylson (E.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Cases should be tried within one year of filing and no later than two years. The trial pool date is when you must be ready to start; actual start may depend on another trial. Before a jury trial, each party files proposed voir dire, jury instructions with pinpoint citations, jury interrogatories, and a trial memorandum; the Notice says “at least seven (3) days” before trial, so confirm the date. For non-jury trials, deliver 2 copies of proposed findings and conclusions and a trial memorandum to chambers (Room 3810) at least 3 days before and file the originals. Counsel may conduct voir dire without the judge present: general yes/no questions to the panel, then individual sidebar questioning on “yes” answers, with alternating strikes. Trial days run 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; give advance notice of legal issues. Sidebars are not allowed unless the

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling and deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling and deadlines (trap): Trials are set on Tuesdays at 9:00 a.m. ET. Typical deadlines counted back from trial: joinder/amendment and plaintiff’s experts 37 weeks; defendant’s experts 33 weeks; final witness list 31 weeks; close of discovery 27 weeks; dispositive and Daubert motions 23 weeks; pretrial disclosures 7 weeks; motions in limine 6 weeks; jury instructions or proposed findings 3 weeks; final pretrial conference 15 days. The scheduling order is modified only for good cause, and the dispositive motion deadline will not be extended absent extraordinary circumstances; untimely dispositive motions may be summarily denied. If the trial date moves, all other dates stay in place unless changed on motion. All civil trials and pretrial hearings are held in Chattanooga. A motion to try the case in another division must be filed after t

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): Judge Atchley prefers not to receive statements of undisputed material facts and will disregard one unless it is jointly filed, contains no argument, and states facts rather than positions. If a “response” to the statement is filed, the court treats it as not jointly filed and disregards it.

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and hearings
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Communications and hearings: Write to the court only on routine matters (scheduling, settlement), by email to Atchley_Chambers@tned.uscourts.gov, copying opposing counsel. Law clerks may be contacted, but not about the merits; requests for action must be made by motion. Calls to chambers should include a representative of each side when possible. Nondispositive motions are set for argument at the court’s discretion. Request argument by motion explaining why it would help, and give advance notice if you will present evidence so a court reporter can attend. For an expedited TRO, preliminary injunction, or other emergency hearing, email chambers, copying a representative of each side if possible.

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Page limits and sealing
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Page limits and sealing: Requests to exceed Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits are generally denied absent good cause; the court may disregard the excess or summarily deny the motion. A confidentiality designation does not justify sealing. Move for leave under Rule 26(c), Local Rule 26.2, and Procter & Gamble Co. v. Bankers Trust Co., 78 F.3d 219 (6th Cir. 1996); sealing motions are closely scrutinized.

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): All discovery, including depositions, requests for admission, and discovery motion practice, must be completed by the deadline; serve written requests early enough that responses are due before it. The parties may continue discovery by agreement afterward, but the court will not resolve disputes arising after the deadline (the page adds: absent exceptional circumstances). Meet and confer, then bring unresolved disputes to the court promptly. Rebuttal expert disclosures are due 30 days after the other side’s disclosure; the final witness list may be supplemented within 5 days after service, then only with leave for good cause. All deposition testimony to be offered at trial must be disclosed by the pretrial disclosure date.

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Daubert and motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Daubert and motions in limine (trap): Motions to exclude expert testimony under Rule 702 must be filed by the Daubert deadline; the court will not entertain one styled as a motion in limine. Argument on motions in limine is generally heard at the final pretrial conference, but rulings may be deferred to trial.

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Final pretrial conference and order
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Final pretrial conference and order: The final pretrial conference is held at 3:00 p.m. ET in Courtroom 1A, Chattanooga; every lawyer who will participate in trial must attend in person. Email the agreed final pretrial order, following the posted sample, to atchley_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov at least 5 business days before the conference. The sample warns that omitting a jury demand from the order has been argued to waive it, so state the demand. After conferring on authenticity and admissibility, file an exhibit list with pre-marked exhibits at least 5 business days before the conference. Trial briefs are due at least 3 business days before; they are optional in jury cases, and proposed findings and conclusions are required in bench trials. Disclose courtroom technology to the other side and the court by the date set in the order. Give the c

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Jury instructions: Under Local Rule 51.1, file a single joint proposal; where disagreements can’t be resolved, include competing instructions. Support every instruction with authority (Local Rule 7.4) and email a Word copy to chambers. The form order says the court models its final instructions on the Sixth Circuit Criminal Pattern Jury Instructions and proposed instructions should follow that form. The judge also posts a model civil charge to be tailored to the case.

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Trial: Stand to address the court or object, and question witnesses from the podium. Several lawyers may try a case, but only one may address a given witness. Examination beyond redirect and recross is usually not allowed. No formal motion to admit exhibits is needed; offer them individually, not collectively. Exhibit objections are handled at or before the final pretrial conference where possible. No written Rule 50 motion is required. Counsel may conduct voir dire, subject to limits. Jurors may take notes, get written instructions, and take all exhibits to the jury room unless directed otherwise. During deliberations, be able to return within 10 minutes; the judge conducts any polling. Civil trials go forward on the set date unless a criminal trial takes priority; a case not reached is held in line through the trial week. Do not deliver exp

docs.t: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr. (E.D. Tenn.) — Mediation
docs.x: Judge Charles Edward Atchley Jr., E.D. Tenn.. Mediation: The parties must discuss using the Federal Court Mediation Program; information is on the court’s website or from the Division Manager in Chattanooga.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): Magistrate Judge Steger does not permit Statements of Undisputed Material Facts and will summarily disregard them. Instead, the motion and responsive briefs must support each factual assertion with citations to “particular parts of materials in the record” (such as specific page numbers); unsupported assertions are disregarded. Under the form scheduling order, all Daubert motions, Rule 12 motions, and Rule 56 motions are due no later than 11 weeks before trial; untimely motions may be summarily denied. Flag a possible Daubert hearing before the dispositive-motion deadline.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and proposed orders: The preferred way to communicate is a formal written motion filed on ECF. Information from calls or emails with clerk’s office or chambers staff is not part of the record and does not bind the court. The judge strongly discourages ex parte contact with law clerks, and any contact must not address the merits. Email all proposed orders, and other documents on specific request, in Word format to steger_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Motion hearings and page limits
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Motion hearings and page limits: Non-dispositive motions are usually set for oral argument, with notice from the court. If you plan to present evidence, notify the court in advance so a court reporter can be arranged. Telephonic motion hearings may be allowed when counsel’s offices are a significant distance from the court, unless the number of lawyers or the subject matter makes it impractical; request one through the judicial assistant. Follow Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits (cover sheet, tables, and certificate of service excluded). Requests to exceed are not routinely granted absent compelling reasons, and a noncompliant brief may be disregarded or the motion summarily denied.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): Serve written discovery early enough that responses are due before the deadline. Parties may agree to discovery after the deadline, but the court generally will not resolve disputes arising after it expires. Confer civilly and promptly; if that fails, bring the dispute promptly, preferably by motion specifying the relief sought. The discovery deadline is usually about 13 weeks before trial. Extensions for good cause are viewed favorably; otherwise deadlines are enforced.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Sealing and protective orders
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Sealing and protective orders: Confidentiality designations do not justify filing under seal; move for leave under the court’s Order Governing Sealing Confidential Information (filed at the start of each case), Local Rule 26.2, and ECF Rule 12.2. Proposed confidentiality orders inconsistent with those will likely not be entered.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling order deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling order deadlines (trap): The form order counts back from trial: plaintiff’s expert disclosures 21 weeks, defendant’s 17 weeks; joinder and amendments 17 weeks; final witness lists 15 weeks; discovery (including evidence depositions) closes 13 weeks; Rule 26(a)(3)(A)(ii)–(iii) pretrial disclosures 9 weeks, with objections due 10 days after service; motions in limine, jury instructions, and verdict form 3 weeks; final pretrial conference 2 weeks. Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting within 10 days and file the discovery plan within 10 days after it. Report by 13 weeks before trial whether the Federal Court Mediation Program could help. If the trial date moves, all other dates stay as set unless the court orders otherwise. Repeated resettings are not granted absent compelling necessity.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial submissions
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial submissions: Jury instructions must cover each claim and affirmative defense (elements, burden, and standard), each type of relief, and a verdict form, with citations under Local Rule 7.4; follow the form of the Sixth Circuit pattern instructions. Counsel must confer and certify they tried to resolve differences, and email the instructions in Word to chambers. Bench trials: proposed findings and conclusions are due 3 weeks before trial (with a jurisdictional statement and chronological facts; conclusions stating elements, burden, standard, and remedies) and emailed to chambers in WordPerfect-compatible format. Post-trial briefs are typically required. At least 5 days before the final pretrial conference, disclose to the other side and the court the courtroom technology you plan to use. File the final pretrial order by the final pretrial c

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial conduct
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Trial conduct: Counsel arrive at 9 a.m.; trial starts at 9:30 a.m. Examine from the lectern, never approach a witness in a jury trial without permission, and never stand near the jury box. One attorney per witness for examination and objections. Counsel may participate in voir dire; challenges are submitted on a form, and back-striking is not allowed. Jurors may take notes but may not question witnesses. Examination beyond re-direct and re-cross is typically not allowed. Pre-mark exhibits per the exhibit list and stipulate to admissibility where possible; stipulated exhibits need not be moved in individually. Sidebars are discouraged. Post-verdict contact with jurors (Local Rule 48.1) is allowed only in extraordinary circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — TROs and settlement
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. TROs and settlement: For expedited hearings on TROs or preliminary injunctions, file a motion; proposed findings and conclusions are encouraged but not required. Expedited discovery may be ordered on application. Parties are urged to settle, using mediation or other ADR if helpful.

docs.t: Judge Clifton Leland Corker (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Clifton Leland Corker, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): A summary judgment motion must come with a separate, concise statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs, each supported by no more than two record citations. The opponent files a separate response to each fact stating that it is (1) undisputed, (2) undisputed only for purposes of the motion, or (3) disputed, with a specific record citation. The response may add a concise statement of additional material disputed facts, in numbered paragraphs with specific citations. Fact statements may not contain argument. If either side fails to file its required statement, the court may strike that party’s motion or opposition.

docs.t: Judge Clifton Leland Corker (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Clifton Leland Corker, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery disputes (trap): Meet and confer first. Judge Corker prefers that civil discovery disputes go to a telephone conference with the assigned magistrate judge, with all attorneys on the call, before any motion is filed; contact the magistrate judge’s chambers to set it. Serve written discovery early enough that responses are due before the deadline. The parties may agree to discovery after the deadline, but the court generally will not resolve disputes arising afterward. Reasonable, good-cause extension requests get favorable consideration; otherwise deadlines are enforced.

docs.t: Judge Clifton Leland Corker (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and conferences
docs.x: Judge Clifton Leland Corker, E.D. Tenn.. Nondispositive motions are usually set for oral argument, with notice of date and time from the court. Give advance notice if you will present evidence so a court reporter can attend.

docs.x: Judge Clifton Leland Corker, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling: Discovery length and trial dates are set at the initial scheduling conference with heavy weight on counsel’s input, depending on complexity, and are expected to be followed. The court will try to accommodate out-of-town parties and lawyers if told of specific problems.

docs.x: Judge Clifton Leland Corker, E.D. Tenn.. Give the courtroom deputy advance notice of videotaped testimony. Do not deliver expert reports to the court without advance permission and notice to all counsel.

docs.x: Judge Cynthia R. Wyrick, E.D. Tenn..
