Motions in limine (non-expert) and other nondispositive motions about 60 days before trial; responses to motions in limine about 30 days before, and to other nondispositive motions 14 days after filing. Criminal motions in limine are due at least 15 days before trial unless otherwise set. 30 days before the final pretrial conference: final witness lists, exhibit lists, deposition designations, exhibit inspection, and damages lists; evidence depositions must be done. Written authenticity or admissibility objections are due 21 days before the conference or are waived. If the trial date moves, other dates not expressly tied to it stay. Civil trials

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial order and filings
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial order and filings: Plaintiff serves a draft pretrial order 45 days before the final pretrial conference (held about 2 weeks before trial); defendant responds within 5 business days. If no agreement, plaintiff notifies chambers at least 21 days before the conference; failure may mean dismissal. File the proposed order 5 days before the conference, including novel questions of law or evidence and trial length in 8-hour days. At least 7 days before trial: final witness list, damages list, deposition designations, expert resumes, briefs on contested legal issues, proposed findings and conclusions (bench issues), and jointly submitted pre-marked exhibits (plaintiff numbered 1, 2, 3; defendant lettered A, B, C; multiple parties identified on each). Electronic exhibits for JERS are strongly encouraged to the courtroom deputy by then, preferabl

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: The judge conducts preliminary voir dire and usually allows counsel to follow up; peremptory challenges go on a form. Opening time limits are set at the final pretrial conference; closing limits during trial. Stand and examine from the lectern; one attorney per witness, including objections. Keep sidebars to a minimum and raise issues at breaks. Give the courtroom deputy advance notice of video testimony, and at least 2 days’ notice to use the evidence presentation system. Move each exhibit in individually before publishing it, unless admitted by stipulation; raise known exhibit objections by the final pretrial conference. No examination beyond redirect and recross absent exceptional circumstances. To have the jury polled, ask at the pretrial conference and again promptly after the verdict.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Criminal sentencing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Criminal sentencing (trap): To get an evidentiary hearing on a PSR objection, expressly request it when filing the objection or the response (L.R. 83.9(c)). A party presenting witnesses at sentencing must file a Notice (Other) at least 14 days before the hearing, giving each witness’s legal name and estimated testimony time; late notice may mean exclusion.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Settlement and dismissal
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Settlement and dismissal: On a full settlement, promptly file a Notice of Settlement, then a Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(ii) stipulation signed by all parties who have appeared, including former parties (L.R. 68.1). When seeking dismissal, identify which provision of Rule 41 applies. In employment discrimination cases, a joint report on suitability for the Federal Mediation Program is due about 5.5 months before trial. Default and default judgment requests should use the court’s posted procedures and forms.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Dispositive motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Dispositive motions (trap): Except on subject matter jurisdiction, each party generally gets one dispositive motion per stage (one motion to dismiss, one summary judgment motion), one supporting memorandum per motion, and one response to each opposing motion. The limits apply per party, not per counsel; consolidated or joint responses are encouraged. Statements of undisputed material facts are not required and will not be considered unless jointly submitted. Factual assertions without proper record citation will not be considered. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery; motions to stay are granted only in unusual circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Page limits and replies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Page limits and replies (trap): Local Rule 7.1(b) limits exclude the cover sheet, tables of contents and authorities, and certificate of service. Noncompliant briefs may be disregarded or the motion summarily denied. Move to exceed sufficiently before the brief is due; such motions are rarely granted absent compelling reasons. Replies are not required (L.R. 7.1(c)); if one becomes necessary, it may not exceed 10 pages.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and hearings
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and hearings: The preferred communication is a formal motion filed on ECF. Anything conveyed by phone or email from chambers or clerk’s staff is not part of the record and does not bind the court. Copy all parties on any correspondence. Ex parte contact with staff is strongly discouraged; any contact must go to dumitru_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov, avoid the merits, and include all counsel of record. In-person conferences and hearings are strongly preferred; request telephonic participation well in advance by email. To request oral argument, file a separate motion with a memorandum of no more than 5 pages; the court gives weight to requests that give a young lawyer a chance to argue. Courtesy copies are not required unless requested; any paper copies must be bound, collated, and double-sided. Email proposed orders in Word to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling conference and ESI
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling conference and ESI: Be ready to discuss reasonable deadlines under Rule 16; counsel’s input gets significant weight. Before the conference, agree as far as possible on an ESI protocol covering sources and search limits, form of production, preservation, inadvertently produced privileged ESI, and cost allocation, and be ready to argue any disagreement. Extensions are entertained only if they do not affect the trial date or the court’s ability to decide dispositive motions, and must be sought by motion before the deadline, with the movant showing necessity. If the trial date changes, other dates stay in place.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): Discovery and all related motion practice must be completed by the deadline; serve requests early enough that responses and objections are resolved before it. The parties may continue by agreement afterward, but the court will not address disputes arising after the deadline. Bring disputes promptly, preferably by motion specifying the relief sought. If all parties agree a phone conference would avoid motion practice, request one by email to chambers. Per the form order, any Daubert motion must be filed before the discovery deadline, and the court should be told early if a Daubert hearing may be needed.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Form scheduling order deadlines
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Form scheduling order deadlines: Counted back from trial: plaintiff’s experts 21 weeks, defendant’s 17 weeks, rebuttal within 30 days after defendant’s; joinder and amendment 17 weeks; final witness list and notice on mediation 15 weeks; discovery 13 weeks; dispositive motions 11 weeks; pretrial disclosures (filed and served) 9 weeks; motions in limine 4 weeks; jury instructions 3 weeks; final pretrial conference no later than 2 weeks. Objections to designations and exhibits, and counter-designations, are due within 10 days after service. Also within 10 days of the pretrial disclosures, jointly submit (not file) electronic full deposition transcripts with each side’s designations highlighted in different colors, and electronic copies of all exhibits numbered continuously across parties with a master list. Disclose courtroom technology to the other side

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Motions in limine: Each party files a single motion listing all in limine issues with one brief of no more than 25 pages; the response is limited to 25 pages and any reply to 10. The court may reserve ruling until the issue arises at trial.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury instructions and findings
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Jury instructions and findings: File one set of joint proposed jury instructions, verdict forms, and interrogatories 3 weeks before trial, covering each claim, defense, element, burden, standard of proof, and type of relief, with authority; email Word copies to chambers. Phased trials need separate sets for each phase. For disputed items, each side submits its version with a brief, supported explanation; an item submitted in only one version is assumed agreed. Follow the form of the Sixth Circuit Pattern Jury Instructions, and certify that you conferred to resolve differences. Bench trials: proposed findings and conclusions with authority (L.R. 52.1) are due 4 weeks before trial, with facts in chronological order and conclusions stating elements, burden, standard, and remedy without argument; email them in WordPerfect or a compatible format.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Trial conduct (trap): Counsel appear at 9:00 a.m. for preliminary matters; trial starts at 9:30 a.m. Stand at the lectern to examine, never approach a witness without permission, and never stand near or lean on the jury box. Jurors may not question witnesses. Counsel may lead voir dire within limits, then submit challenges on the deputy’s form; no back-striking of previously seated jurors. Share any visuals, video, or audio for openings with opposing counsel before trial. Only one lawyer per side may examine and object during a given witness. Sidebars are discouraged; raise matters during breaks. Resolve the method for recorded testimony with the other side before trial. Know Local Rule 43.3 and give the deputy 3 copies of the exhibit list before trial. Stipulated exhibits need not be moved in individually. Exhibits that can be electronic must be, and j

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury deliberations and settlement
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Jury deliberations and settlement: Jurors may take notes during the proof but not openings or closings. During deliberations, give the deputy a mobile number and be able to return within 10 minutes. The deputy polls on request, and post-verdict juror contact will not be permitted absent extraordinary circumstances. Mediation or other ADR is urged in every case. Tell the court immediately upon settlement, and file a stipulation or agreed order of dismissal within 30 days or by the trial date, whichever is sooner.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling (trap): Scheduling orders are entered directly, without an in-person conference. Questions about the trial date go to the judicial assistant within 7 days of receiving the order; after that, a motion for continuance is required. Any schedule change requires a motion with a proposed agreed order; continuances need cause, and successive resettings need compelling necessity. If the trial date moves, all other dates stay unless the court orders otherwise. The form order counts back from trial: amendments, joinder, and all Rule 12 and Rule 56 motions due 150 days before (untimely dispositive motions may be summarily denied); employment discrimination cases file a joint mediation-suitability report at 150 days.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and courtesy copies: Written correspondence is discouraged; copy all counsel if you send it. Law clerks may be contacted (chambers 865-545-4762, ext. 2, or varlan_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov) but not about the merits; include all sides on calls and copy all counsel on emails. No courtesy hard copies unless the court asks; any requested copy must be printed after e-filing so it bears the ECF header. If you file on the day of a hearing or trial, notify chambers or the courtroom deputy by email or phone.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Hearings and page limits
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Hearings and page limits: Oral argument is decided case by case, and the court may set argument on its own. Out-of-town counsel wanting to appear by phone at a conference (other than the final pretrial conference, generally in person) must contact the judicial assistant at least 1 week ahead. Follow Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits; reasonable requests to exceed them may be granted in complex cases.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery and depositions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery and depositions (trap): Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting within 15 days of the scheduling order and file the discovery plan within 10 days after; the order lists specific e-discovery topics to resolve. Discovery, including evidence depositions, closes 90 days before trial, and motions to compel must be filed at least 30 days before that deadline. Discovery disputes follow three steps: meet and confer; a conference with the assigned magistrate judge (who may rule); and only then a written motion certifying compliance with both steps and Rule 37(a)(1). Deposition rules: no instructions not to answer except for privilege or a court-ordered limit; no suggestive objections; no private conferences with the witness while a question or short line of questioning is pending except to decide on privilege; deposing counsel must give the witness’s counsel copi

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Experts and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Experts and Daubert (trap): Expert disclosures are due 150 days before trial for plaintiff and 120 days for defendant; rebuttal within 30 days after the other side’s disclosure. A motion for a Daubert hearing must be filed no later than 90 days before trial or challenges are waived. If a Daubert hearing is requested, file the challenged experts’ reports at least 5 days before the hearing.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Status report and pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Status report and pretrial order (trap): A joint status report is due on the discovery deadline, covering completion of discovery, whether argument would help on pending dispositive motions, planned pretrial motions, jury or nonjury and trial length, settlement and mediation, and other matters. Plaintiff serves a draft pretrial order 45 days before trial (47 if by mail); defendant responds within 5 working days. If no agreement after a face-to-face conference, plaintiff notifies chambers at least 31 days before trial. The agreed pretrial order is due 30 days before trial; failure may be treated as failure to prosecute.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial filings: Final witness lists 45 days before trial (supplement within 5 days after service). Rule 26(a)(3) disclosures, motions in limine, and jury instructions (or proposed findings and conclusions for bench trials) are due 30 days before trial. Motions in limine are generally heard at the final pretrial conference. Objections to deposition designations or exhibits meant to be treated as motions in limine need a supporting brief; undisclosed objections other than under Rules 402 and 403 are waived. Confer on exhibit authenticity and admissibility before the final pretrial conference. Trial briefs: the form order requires briefs on novel or unusual legal questions at least 15 days before trial, while the Judicial Preferences say at least 7 days; follow your case’s order. Give the courtroom deputy at least 5 working days’ notice before the pretr

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: Counsel arrive at 8:30 a.m. for preliminary matters; trial begins at 9 a.m. A case not reached is held in line for that week. Bring the original and one copy of labeled, numbered exhibits. The judge conducts preliminary voir dire and allows counsel to follow up; challenges go on a form, and back-striking is not permitted. One attorney per witness; examination beyond redirect and recross is generally not allowed. Keep sidebars to a minimum and give advance notice of videotaped testimony. Juror lists may be used only for jury selection and must be returned or destroyed afterward. Jurors may take notes except during openings and closings; exhibits go to the jury room except firearms and illegal narcotics.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Closing arguments (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Closing arguments (trap): Agree on time limits before closings and follow them strictly. Stay within arm’s length of the DEPS podium and no closer to the jury than its jury-side edge; remove flip-chart pages after use. Objections during closing must state only the legal ground. Refer to witnesses by proper names, not first names alone (unless commonly so called at trial), refer to opposing counsel only as “Plaintiff’s counsel” or “Defendants’ counsel,” and show no reaction to opposing argument.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Injunctions and settlement
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Injunctions and settlement: TROs and injunctions follow Rule 65; briefing as in other cases, and expedited discovery on motion. Do not send appellate filings. The judge encourages mediation and other ADR; magistrate judges may be involved case by case. To consent to trial by a magistrate judge, notify the judicial assistant.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Chambers copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Chambers copies (trap): For any dispositive motion, and any other motion or responsive pleading over 25 pages including attachments, mail or hand deliver a courtesy hard copy to chambers. Other courtesy copies are appreciated and go to the Clerk’s Office.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): File a separate, concise statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs, each supported by no more than two record citations. The opponent files, with its brief, a separate response to each fact stating that it is (1) undisputed, (2) undisputed only for the motion, or (3) disputed, with a specific record citation, and may add numbered additional disputed facts with citations. No argument in these statements; failure to file one may lead the court to strike the motion or opposition.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and conferences
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and conferences: Written correspondence is discouraged; if sent, copy all counsel. Law clerks may be contacted, but not on the merits. Telephone conferences are encouraged and are scheduled through Senior Law Clerk Penny Arning; save motions needing a court appearance for complicated matters the parties can’t agree on. Oral argument is decided case by case and may be requested. Requests to exceed Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits in complex cases are usually granted. Sealing requires strict compliance with Local Rule 26.2 and Procter & Gamble Co. v. Bankers Trust Co., 78 F.3d 219 (6th Cir. 1996).

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery and extensions (trap): Try to resolve disputes yourselves, then by telephone conference with the assigned magistrate judge; only then file a motion (which may be referred to the magistrate judge) with the Rule 37 certification. A standard case should finish discovery in 8 or 9 months and be ready for trial within 1 year. Except for the dispositive motion and Daubert deadlines and the trial date, deadlines may be modified by agreement of all counsel. Continuances are discouraged; lack of timely trial preparation is not good cause. In the sample orders, discovery closes 60 days before trial and motions to compel are due at least 30 days before that.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Experts and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Experts and Daubert (trap): Sample orders: plaintiff’s experts 150 days before trial, defendant’s 120 days, rebuttal within 30 days after. A motion for a Daubert hearing must be filed at least 90 days before trial or the challenge is waived, and the challenged expert’s report must be filed before the hearing. A party offering a computer-generated animation must say so with its expert disclosures and give the animation to all parties 45 days before pretrial disclosures (or the close of expert discovery, if earlier).

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Sample scheduling order deadlines
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Sample scheduling order deadlines: Counted back from trial: amendment and joinder 180 days; dispositive motions 120 days; pretrial disclosures 60 days; final witness and exhibit lists 45 days (amend within 5 working days after service); motions in limine and jury instruction requests 15 working days; trial briefs on novel legal issues 7 working days. Email jury instruction requests to Phillips_Chambers@tned.uscourts.gov in WordPerfect format as well as filing them. A Rule 26(a)(3) objection meant to be treated as a motion in limine needs a supporting brief; objections not disclosed, other than under Federal Rules of Evidence 402 and 403, are waived absent good cause. For the court’s evidence presentation system, notify courtroom deputy Jason Huffaker at least 5 working days ahead. If a party will use display equipment, the parties confer and file a j

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial order (trap): File an agreed pretrial order 30 days before trial and email it to chambers in WordPerfect format. Plaintiff serves a draft 45 days before trial (47 if served by mail); defendant responds within 5 working days. If the parties cannot agree after a face-to-face conference, plaintiff must notify chambers at least 31 days before trial; failure to file or notify may be treated as failure to prosecute (Rule 41(b)). A final pretrial conference is held shortly before trial, where motions in limine are addressed and usually resolved; in the non-jury sample, one is set only by separate notice.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: Be present at 8:30 a.m. for preliminary matters; trial starts at 9:00 a.m., and a case not reached is held in line through the trial week. At the start of trial, give the court 2 copies of your exhibit list and 2 sets of exhibits, hole-punched in three-ring binders. The court conducts preliminary voir dire and counsel may add questions; back-striking is not permitted. Stand to examine, at or near the podium; never approach a witness in a jury trial without permission or have close contact with the jury box. Only one lawyer per side may examine a witness, and examination beyond redirect and recross requires compelling circumstances. Stipulate to as many exhibits as possible; stipulated exhibits need not be moved individually. Time limits for openings and closings are agreed at trial and enforced. Give the courtroom deputy advance notice of vide

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Jury: A charge conference is held after the close of proof, where additional instruction requests are considered. Counsel may propose verdict forms, but the court prepares the form submitted. Jurors may take notes and take properly admitted exhibits into deliberations. During deliberations, be able to return within 10 minutes. The court polls every jury, and counsel may not interview jurors after verdict absent extraordinary circumstances (L.R. 48.1).

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Bench trials
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Bench trials: Proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law, which serve as final argument, are filed after trial (the sample sets 30 days), supported by authority, and emailed to chambers in WordPerfect format. Facts go in chronological order as proved at trial; conclusions must be concise and not argumentative.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Injunctions, ADR, and criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Injunctions, ADR, and criminal cases: Rule 65 is strictly applied, and extraordinary relief is granted only in extraordinary circumstances. Expedited discovery requires compelling circumstances and may not be used in cases that clearly do not qualify for Rule 65 relief. Mediation, arbitration, and other ADR are encouraged, and reasonable extensions to pursue them are usually granted. In criminal cases, the assigned magistrate judge controls pretrial preparation; trial practice is the same as in civil cases.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): Statements of undisputed facts are not required and will not be considered unless jointly submitted; follow Rule 56’s record-citation standards instead. Before any summary judgment motion, the parties must confer and build a single joint appendix of exhibits, consecutively paginated with a table of contents, filed by the movant with the first motion and cited by page number. Include only cited deposition pages. The non-movant may add a consecutively numbered addendum with its opposition. Material outside the appendix and addendum will not be considered. Each party gets only one motion to dismiss and one summary judgment motion (jurisdictional issues excepted), one supporting memorandum per motion, and one response per opposing motion; consolidated or joint responses are encouraged.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Briefing limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Briefing limits (trap): Replies are not required (L.R. 7.1(c)); any reply is capped at 10 pages, and only the first 10 pages of a longer reply will be considered. Requests for 5 extra pages in opening and answering briefs are typically granted in sufficiently complex cases but rarely for replies; move at least 10 days before the brief is due, if the schedule allows. Extension motions must be filed well before the deadline and specifically define the reasons for and length of the extension. Contacting a law clerk does not extend any deadline; only a timely motion can.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Hearings and communications
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Hearings and communications: Oral argument is set when the court finds it useful. To request it, file a separate motion with a memorandum of no more than 5 pages; the court weighs whether argument offers a speaking opportunity for a young lawyer. At scheduled hearings, be ready to present evidence; failing to arrange it is no ground for a continuance. Emergency (Rule 65) hearings are often set the same day the petition is filed; pre-hearing briefing is welcome. Correspondence may not substitute for motions and must be copied to all parties. To speak with a law clerk, email mcdonough_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov explaining why, with a callback number. No printed courtesy copies unless requested.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Case management conference: The court usually holds an in-person case-management conference at the start of each case. Every lawyer who will actively handle discovery, motions, or trial must attend in person, ready to discuss legal theories, disputed facts, anticipated evidence, and the Rule 16(a) and 16(c)(2) topics. Out-of-district lawyers are encouraged to use local counsel. Typical deadlines before trial: expert disclosures, joinder, and amendments 29 weeks; rebuttal experts 25 weeks; final witness list 23 weeks; discovery close 19 weeks; dispositive and Daubert motions 15 weeks; pretrial disclosures 6 weeks; motions in limine 5 weeks; jury instructions or proposed findings 3 weeks; final pretrial conference the Monday two weeks before trial. Discovery typically takes about 8 months. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery, and stays a

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery: Confer before raising disputes; leave from a magistrate judge is not needed to file a discovery motion. Do not contact the opposing side’s experts. Rebuttal experts may only challenge the opinions or methods of a previously disclosed expert, no broader in scope. Discovery, including evidence depositions, expert depositions, and requests for admission, must be completed by the cut-off. Confidentiality agreements bind the parties, but sealing requires Local Rule 26.2 and the sealing order entered at the start of the case.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions in limine and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Motions in limine and Daubert (trap): Each party may file only one motion in limine identifying all evidence to be excluded, with one brief of no more than 25 pages; separately filed motions in limine will be summarily denied. Attach the challenged evidence where practicable. Motions to exclude expert testimony under Rule 702 must be filed by the Daubert deadline; they will not be entertained as motions in limine.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Final pretrial conference (trap): The final pretrial conference (3 p.m., Courtroom 3, Chattanooga) must be attended in person. Submit an agreed final pretrial order following the posted sample by the conference; it supplants the pleadings, so include your jury demand to avoid a waiver argument. File trial briefs on anticipated evidentiary and legal issues at least 3 business days before the conference. Before the conference, file an exhibit list and provide pre-marked exhibits, and be ready to argue admissibility; unprepared counsel risk adverse rulings. Jury instructions are submitted as one joint proposal, with competing versions of unresolved instructions, all with citations (L.R. 7.4), and emailed to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Trial (trap): Counsel lead voir dire under the court’s direction: for-cause challenges first, then peremptories; jurors called later are seated at the end of the box, and no back-striking. Openings and closings rarely exceed 30 minutes per party. Share any visual, video, or audio aids with opposing counsel before use. Examine from the lectern, standing if able; one attorney per witness for questioning and objections. Offer each exhibit when it is authenticated and its admissibility established, not at the end of testimony or of your case. Give the courtroom deputy three copies of the exhibit list before trial. No vouching, testifying, or ad hominem attacks in closing. All exhibits that can be electronic must be; jurors view them electronically, and firearms and controlled substances stay out of the jury room. During deliberations, be able to re

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Criminal cases: Plea and motion deadlines set by the magistrate judge are enforced unless modified by motion to the court. Be ready to justify appeal or § 2255 waivers in Rule 11(c)(1)(A) or (B) agreements. Brady material is deemed requested at the defendant’s first appearance with counsel, and the government should disclose exculpatory and mitigating information as soon as practicable; early Jencks production is encouraged. Rule 17(c)(1) pretrial subpoenas require a motion, filed well before the plea deadline and trial.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Settlement and referrals
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Settlement and referrals: Tell the court immediately upon settlement and promptly file a stipulation or agreed order of dismissal, in any event before the trial date (L.R. 68.1). Social Security and ERISA dispositive motions are typically referred to a magistrate judge for a recommendation.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Contacting chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Contacting chambers (trap): Before calling chambers with a case question, review the docket and the Local Rules, and have the docket available during the call. Raise unresolved disputes promptly by requesting a telephonic discovery conference or by motion; either way the parties must file a joint discovery dispute statement describing the specific requests and each side’s position with facts and authority. Protective orders and sealing (trap): A proposed stipulated protective order (Appendix L form) will be rejected unless it requires a party using “confidential” material on a motion to file that material under seal, and binds the parties before and after entry. Materials used in open court at trial lose the confidential designation. On a motion to dismiss or for summary judgment, only the supporting confidential documents, not the motion itself, may be filed under seal.

docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Trials are set on a two-week stand-by basis; counsel must keep in touch with the courtroom deputy (330-884-7435) for the exact date. By 4:00 p.m. 10 days before trial: an agreed preliminary statement for the jury, joint voir dire, jury instructions, interrogatories, and verdict forms (one joint filing: agreed, plaintiff’s opposed, and defendant’s opposed, all with citations), and trial briefs. Witness and exhibit lists 3 business days before trial; unlisted witnesses and exhibits are excluded absent good cause. Stipulated facts: plaintiff circulates a draft 14 days before the pretrial conference, responses at 10 days, meet at 7 days, and file the signed final stipulation 3 days

docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Paper exhibits must bear numbered stickers with the case number, and every page of a multi-page exhibit is separately numbered (e.g., Plaintiff 1-1). Binders are no longer required. Exchange demonstratives 2 days before trial. Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday; arrive 30 minutes early. Stand to address the court and examine from the lectern, state only the legal basis for objections, use surnames, and only one lawyer per side per witness (the lawyer objecting on direct takes cross). docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances and settlement
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Continuances and settlement: No trial or hearing is continued without a written motion stating the reason (in civil cases, endorsed by all moving parties and lead counsel). A motion based on a conflicting trial assignment must attach it (criminal: describe it) and be filed within 15 days after learning of the conflict and at least 30 days before trial. Report a settlement immediately by calling 330-884-7435; failure can draw sanctions, and jury costs are assessed under LR 54.1 if settlement comes after a jury is called.

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Motions to travel filed within 48 hours of the travel will be denied and must state whether the AUSA objects. Discovery requests are docketed as “Notices” unless court intervention is needed; report any discovery failures in writing on the cutoff date. By 4:00 p.m. 10 days before trial, the same jury materials and trial briefs as civil (briefs may be ex parte). docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Motion to dismiss does not stop the case (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Motion to dismiss does not stop the case (trap): A timely Rule 12(b) motion to dismiss does not excuse an answer, discovery, or compliance with other orders. The answer is due the same day as plaintiff’s opposition to the motion. Exceptions: a motion challenging personal jurisdiction, or a stay sought and granted while the motion is pending. Then the motion is decided first, and if it is denied in whole or part the answer is due 20 days after the order.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Pre-CMC substantive motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Pre-CMC substantive motions (trap): Substantive motions filed before the Case Management Conference (e.g., to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, to confirm or vacate an arbitration award, to remand): opening memorandum and response 20 pages each, response due within 30 days of the motion; reply 10 pages, due within 14 days of the response. After a motion for a more definite statement is granted, the responsive pleading is due within 14 days of notice of the order, or the pleading may be stricken. No sur-replies without advance leave.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Briefing format and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Briefing format and page limits (trap): One-inch margins; double-spaced 12-point Times New Roman; footnotes at least 10-point Times New Roman; citations in the text, not footnotes. All filings, and exhibits if possible, must be text searchable. Noncompliant filings may be stricken or deemed untimely. Excessive or lengthy footnotes may be treated as evading page limits, with the brief or footnotes stricken. Relief from page limits needs a separate motion filed well before the deadline, showing good cause, the extra pages sought, and all parties’ positions. A request filed with the overlength brief will be denied, and the brief may be stricken or treated as ending at the last permitted page.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances and extensions
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Continuances and extensions: Motions to continue or extend must be in writing, well in advance, and (unless joint) state whether they are opposed. Requests made after a submission, discovery, or dispositive-motion deadline has passed are denied absent excusable neglect. For an unopposed motion to continue a conference or hearing, propose three alternative dates and times when all counsel are available.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes (trap): Meet and confer in person, by video, or by phone first; email never suffices. If unresolved, jointly notify chambers by phone (216-357-7200) or email (Brennan_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov); the court will set a call and may require a certificate of compliance stating how the parties conferred. A discovery motion filed without these steps will be denied. Serve requests early enough that responses are due before the cut-off, and raise disputes early enough to finish by the deadline. Discovery the parties agree to continue past the cut-off gets no court supervision absent extreme prejudice and will not move dispositive-motion or trial dates.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment: Typically one summary judgment motion per party. No summary judgment motion before the close of discovery without express leave.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Sealing and redactions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Sealing and redactions (trap): Seek leave before filing anything redacted, usually at least 7 days before the deadline: explain each redaction, certify conferral with the producing party and state its position, and simultaneously give the court an unredacted copy with proposed redactions marked. Sealing an entire document is permitted only rarely. Justify every request document by document under Shane Group, Inc. v. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan, 825 F.3d 299 (6th Cir. 2016); a confidentiality designation under a protective order is not enough. A protective order deviating from Appendix L to the Local Rules requires emailing chambers a redlined Word version of the changes; joint proposals are viewed more favorably.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Hearings, conferences, and attendance (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Hearings, conferences, and attendance (trap): Conferences and hearings are in person unless the court says otherwise. A request for phone or video must be filed at least 7 business days ahead; joint requests are liberally granted. Lead counsel, client representatives with full settlement authority, and insurance representatives must attend hearings and conferences in person, except the CMC, telephonic status conferences in the scheduling order, and discovery-dispute status conferences. A request to excuse attendance must be in writing at least 7 calendar days ahead. File a joint status report 3 business days before any status conference covering discovery, settlement, whether a mediator would help, and anticipated discovery issues. Only lead counsel need attend a telephonic status conference.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Removal and jurisdictional declarations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Removal and jurisdictional declarations (trap): In a diversity removal, if the pleadings or notice of removal do not identify the citizenship of every member or partner of each LLC, LLP, partnership, or similar party, counsel must file a declaration within 14 days of the notice of removal (corporations: State of incorporation and principal place of business). Missing the deadline risks sanctions or remand. An entity intervenor in a diversity case must file the same citizenship declaration with its motion to intervene, plus the corporate disclosure statement.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Rule 26(f) report and ESI
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Rule 26(f) report and ESI: Use the judge’s Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting form, which calls for initial disclosures no later than 5 business days before the CMC, a track recommendation, ADR position, and a proposed telephonic status conference at least one month before the close of fact discovery. If the parties have not agreed on an ESI method by the time the report is filed, the default standard in Appendix K to the Local Rules applies.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Artificial intelligence ban (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Artificial intelligence ban (trap): No attorney or pro se party may use artificial intelligence in preparing any filing. Violations can bring sanctions including striking the filing, economic sanctions or contempt, and dismissal of the lawsuit. The ban does not cover information gathered from legal search engines (such as Westlaw or LexisNexis) or internet search engines (such as Google). Parties and counsel must immediately tell the court if they discover AI use in any document filed in their case.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Deadlines expire at 5 p.m. (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Deadlines expire at 5 p.m. (trap): Unless otherwise ordered, every court-set filing deadline expires at the close of business, meaning 5:00 PM on the deadline date. Anything later is late and may be stricken, not considered, or sanctioned.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Continuances and extensions (trap): No hearing is continued and no deadline extended without a written motion stating the reason, filed before the date or deadline passes; a motion based on a conflict must be filed as soon as counsel learns of the conflict. Every such motion (except one joined by all parties) must state whether the other parties oppose. An opposed motion must be filed at least 7 days before the date or deadline, and the opposition is due within 3 days after the motion is filed. Noncompliance may mean denial.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Motions and page limits (trap): Motions and briefs must follow Loc. R. 7.1 unless ordered otherwise. No supplemental motion, document, sur-reply, or exhibit for or against a dispositive motion is accepted without prior leave unless the case management order addresses it. Length limits under Loc. R. 7.1(f) are strictly enforced. A motion to exceed them must show good cause and be filed at least 7 days before the filing deadline; one filed together with the overlong memorandum will be denied.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Formatting
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Formatting: All filings must meet Loc. R. 10.1, and e-filed documents (including exhibits, if possible) must be text-searchable. Nonconforming documents may be stricken.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Sealing (trap): Nothing is filed under seal without statutory authority or a court order. Seek leave first, explaining the basis and stating whether other parties oppose; if the document is tied to a deadline, the motion for leave is due at least 7 days before it. Sealing a whole document or exhibit is permitted only rarely. Justify every redaction or sealing request under Shane Grp., Inc. v. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mich., 825 F.3d 299 (6th Cir. 2016), analyzing each document in detail with reasons and legal citations.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Disclosure statements
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Disclosure statements: Nongovernmental corporate parties and would-be intervenors must disclose any parent corporation and any publicly held corporation owning 10% or more of their stock, or state that none exists. In diversity cases (including removed cases), every party and intervenor must name and establish the citizenship of everyone whose citizenship is attributed to it; an LLC must identify the name and citizenship of each member and every sub-member. Allegations of residence rather than domicile or citizenship are insufficient (Prime Rate Premium Fin. Corp. v. Larson).

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Contacting chambers: Direct case questions to Courtroom Deputy Clerk Stephanie Siner at (216) 357-7180. Do not contact the law clerks about the case. No ex parte calls on substantive matters, including case management deadlines, requests to file briefing, or the status of pending motions; raise those by motion on the docket. Routine calls (such as dial-in information) are acceptable. For a deposition dispute needing immediate help, the parties may call chambers jointly.

If any claim allows fee-shifting, each party must bring a preliminary estimate or budget of anticipated fees and expenses to the CMC. Plaintiff must serve a written demand with a monetary breakdown of damages at least 1 week before the status conference; defendant responds with an offer by the conference. docs.t: Judge Christopher A. Boyko (N.D. Ohio) — Dispositive motions and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Dispositive motions and extensions (trap): Unscheduled summary judgment motions may not be filed without leave. No supplemental motion, document, sur-reply, or exhibit on a dispositive motion is accepted without prior leave unless the case management order addresses it. Extension requests are entertained only if filed before the deadline in question and only if they state whether opposing counsel consents or objects.

docs.t: Judge Christopher A. Boyko (N.D. Ohio) — Status reports
docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Status reports: If the case management order requires them, file status reports every 45 days covering discovery, settlement discussions, pending motions, and any developments that might prompt a request to deviate from the schedule. Missing them can bring sanctions from denial of extensions to dismissal under Rule 41(b).

docs.t: Judge Christopher A. Boyko (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes and protective orders (trap): Follow Local Rule 37.1. The court will take no calls and no motions to compel until compliance is shown, and certification requires affidavits of counsel attesting to good-faith efforts to resolve the dispute (filed, mailed, or faxed). Stipulated protective orders must strictly track Appendix L to the Local Civil Rules or Appendix A to the Local Patent Rules, and the parties must certify that the proposed language conforms.

docs.t: Judge Christopher A. Boyko (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Settlement conferences (trap): Plaintiff serves a written itemized damages demand with a brief explanation at least 10 days before the conference; defendant serves a written offer with explanation at least 5 days before. If no settlement, plaintiff’s counsel delivers or faxes (216-357-7156) both letters to chambers by noon 2 business days before the conference; do not file them. Parties with ultimate settlement authority must attend in person; insurers and uninsured corporations must send representatives with authority up to the opposing side’s existing demand (or offer). A client available by phone is not acceptable. Motions to excuse attendance, for undue hardship only, are due 7 days before the conference, and excused parties must be reachable by phone. docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial: briefs and pretrial filings (trap): Trial briefs are required in every case, due 7 days before the final pretrial (14 days before trial if none), and must be exchanged. They include facts, controlling law (emphasizing possible Rule 50 issues), witnesses with subject matter, an exhibit index, evidentiary issues, and a trial-length estimate. Unlisted witnesses (lay or expert) may not testify except in extraordinary circumstances; unlisted exhibits need good cause. Motions in limine are filed with the trial brief; responses are due 3 days before the final pretrial (7 days before trial if none). Bench trials: number proposed findings and conclusions in the trial brief, citing witnesses or exhibits and legal authority. docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Request equipment training at least 3 business days before trial. Notify opponents of deposition testimony at least 7 days before the final pretrial; objections are due 3 days before it (14 and 7 days before trial if no final pretrial), and the proponent briefs within 2 days after objections. docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases (trap): Continuance motions must state with particularity why a trial date beyond the Speedy Trial Act period is justified and include the defendant’s written consent. No plea agreement is accepted later than 1 day before trial. Notify the court in writing immediately of any discovery failure, or it will not continue trial on that ground. Pretrial motions, including suppression, are due 14 days before the final pretrial and oppositions 7 days before; any suppression hearing is held at the final pretrial. The government must respond in writing to suppression motions. A motion for a criminal history report is due 35 days before the final pretrial. docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Motions and briefing (trap): Motions are decided on the briefs; oral argument is rare. Unopposed motions are not automatically granted. Dispositive-motion memoranda are limited to 10 pages (expedited), 20 (standard and administrative), 30 (complex), and 40 (mass tort); all other motions 15 pages. Leave to exceed must be sought well before the deadline, is rarely granted, and a request filed with the overlength brief will be denied; the request does not extend the filing deadline. No sur-replies without advance leave. Emergency motions are rarely granted ex parte; the movant generally must notify the other side and give it a copy. A defendant filing a partial motion to dismiss must answer the remaining counts on time; the motion does not extend that deadline (standing order of Aug. 29, 2018).

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Courtesy copies and late filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Courtesy copies and late filings (trap): Chambers will not accept courtesy copies unless the court requests them. Anything filed within 2 business days of a conference, hearing, final pretrial, plea, or trial must also be sent to chambers and opposing counsel the same day it is filed. The posted orders variously say by fax (216-357-7195), email, or CM/ECF plus same-day service. In criminal cases, a plea agreement must reach the court at least one day before a scheduled plea.

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Parties must attend in person (for entities, a person with knowledge and full settlement authority), plus an insurance representative with full authority if coverage arguably exists. Move well in advance to be excused. Plaintiff’s counsel arranges the planning meeting and files the jointly signed report (and faxes it to chambers) by the deadline in the order. Before the CMC, plaintiff must make a written demand with a monetary breakdown of damages and defendant must counteroffer; note both in the report. Initial disclosures are due 7 days before the CMC and must be filed with the court at least 2 days before it. Formal discov

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Removed cases
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Removed cases: A standing order in removed cases requires each party to file a signed statement on when defendants received or were served with the summons and complaint, any served defendant who did not join removal and why, whether served defendants are Ohio citizens, and the reason for any untimely removal. Plaintiff must give a detailed monetary breakdown of damages.

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes: Steps in order: good-faith efforts by counsel; a short letter to the court to trigger a telephone conference; position letters (no more than 2 pages) if solicited; then a Rule 37 motion. The judge does not usually refer discovery matters to a magistrate judge. No discovery materials are filed without leave except to support dispositive motions. The court prefers entire depositions to excerpts, filed with the memorandum they support.

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement and status conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Settlement and status conferences (trap): Every pretrial conference is treated as a settlement conference; parties and counsel must attend prepared to discuss settlement, with a person with full settlement authority for entities. The judge often mediates with the parties’ consent. Counsel must confer within 72 hours before the status hearing or settlement conference. Each counsel then faxes the court (but does not file or exchange) a confidential status/settlement report of no more than 5 pages covering the facts, discovery status, the demand and offer, and issues for the court, by the date set (the practices page says at least 5 days, or 5 business days, before). Requests for a conference on non-discovery issues require a letter certifying good-faith efforts and outlining the issues. Non-motion correspondence is not docketed but is kept in the public case f

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Contact with chambers
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Contact with chambers: No ex parte communications. Counsel may contact the courtroom deputy, judicial assistant, or law clerks on procedural matters only. Continuances are rarely granted; in civil cases a continuance motion must be signed by the parties themselves.

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial preparation
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial preparation: Lead counsel and parties attend the final pretrial with full authority; counsel must confer with clients and each other on final settlement posture at least 2 business days before. Each side gets a set number of hours for its whole case. Exchange proposed jury instructions 10 calendar days before the final pretrial, then file one joint submission (agreed, plaintiff’s opposed, defendant’s opposed) with citations; objections must give reasons and authority, not just “objection.” Submit only case-specific law; the court gives boilerplate instructions. Bring a CD with the instructions, the joint preliminary statement (1 page), proposed voir dire, and witness list to the final pretrial. docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Trial: Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. with a 1-hour lunch and two 15-minute breaks (the practices page says 5:00 p.m.); counsel must be in the courtroom from 8:30 a.m. Parties must be present whenever the jury is seated. The court conducts voir dire, then one counsel per party briefly questions the panel (about 10 minutes per party). Peremptories use an “informed strike” method by rounds; a pass forfeits that challenge, and consecutive passes by both sides end challenges. Examinations need not be from the lectern; ask permission to approach a witness. Show any opening-statement exhibits to opposing counsel in advance. Jurors may take notes and submit written questions. Raise Daubert challenges well before trial, and arrange daily transcripts.

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases (trap): A plea under a written plea agreement must be taken by the pretrial conference date; the practices page also describes a change-of-plea deadline about 2 weeks before trial after which no plea agreements are accepted. The defendant must attend the pretrial and final pretrial. Written pleas are strongly preferred; binding agreements are acceptable. Motions other than motions in limine are due within 30 days after arraignment. By 3 business days before the final pretrial: stipulations signed by counsel and the defendant, a joint preliminary statement (up to 2 pages), trial briefs, exhibit lists, motions in limine, proposed voir dire, and the joint jury instructions; witness lists are emailed to chambers only (not filed or exchanged). Exhibit objections by noon 1 business day before the final pretrial. Jencks and reciprocal Jencks material

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: The CMC is held by telephone: counsel for all parties get on one line and call the court at 216-357-7160. Lead counsel must participate; a motion to excuse lead counsel for undue hardship is due at least 7 days before the CMC. The Rule 26(f) meeting is arranged by plaintiff’s counsel (defense counsel in removed cases), with initial disclosures at or within 10 days after it. File the Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting on the court’s form at least 3 working days before the CMC, including an e-discovery plan or agreement to the Appendix K default standard. Plaintiff’s counsel must confirm that the defendant’s counsel (or an unrepresented defendant) received the CMC order. If the case resolves before the CMC, submit a jointly signed stipulation of settlement or dismissal or notify the court that one is coming.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Early settlement demand (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Early settlement demand (trap): Plaintiffs must give defendants a written demand with a description and monetary breakdown of damages at least 1 week before the CMC, and defendants must respond with an offer no later than the CMC date.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment and courtesy copies (trap): No summary judgment motion before discovery closes without express leave, and all summary judgment arguments go in a single motion; multiple summary judgment motions need express leave. Submit courtesy copies to chambers of all dispositive motions, oppositions, and replies, with all supporting material.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Contacting chambers: No ex parte calls to chambers on substantive issues, including case management deadlines, requests to file briefing, or the status of pending motions; file a motion on the public docket instead. Routine calls (such as dial-in information) are acceptable, and a deposition dispute needing immediate help may be raised by a joint call.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Continuances (trap): A trial or hearing continuance in a civil case requires a written motion stating the reason, endorsed in writing by all parties and lead counsel of record. A motion based on a conflicting trial assignment must attach a copy of that assignment and be filed within 15 days after counsel learns of the conflict and at least 30 days before trial (the criminal order has the same timing but no endorsement requirement).

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial filings (trap): Trials are set at 8:30 a.m. in Courtroom 15A. Trial briefs (facts, law, witness list with subjects, exhibit index, evidentiary issues, and, for jury trials, proposed voir dire and jury instructions) are due 5 days before a jury trial or 10 days before a bench trial, and exchanged 5 days before trial. Unlisted witnesses (lay or expert) testify only in extraordinary circumstances; unlisted exhibits need good cause. Stipulations of uncontested facts are due 10 days before trial, prepared after an in-person conference; no examination is allowed on facts that could have been stipulated. A joint statement of disputed facts is due 5 days before a jury trial or 10 days before a benc

docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. For cross-motions the court prefers a four-brief schedule (opening; combined cross-motion and response; combined response and reply; reply). No surreplies without leave, rarely given. Replies should not raise new evidence or arguments. Notices of supplemental authority may not exceed 350 words and must cite a PageID or point argued orally. Motions for reconsideration, however styled, are limited to 2 pages (or 500 words) or will be struck; no response unless the court asks. TRO, PI, and emergency motions must certify that the motion is necessary after conferring

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Record citations and exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Pleadings, jurisdiction, and dismissals (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Pleadings, jurisdiction, and dismissals (trap): An answer is required even if a Rule 12 motion is filed or planned; the motion does not extend the answer deadline, and a Rule 12(b)(6) motion may be treated as one under Rule 12(c). Amendments (by motion or as of right) must attach a redline or comparison, and a motion must say whether the defendant consents under Rule 15(a)(2). Dismiss fewer than all parties or claims by Rule 21 motion (stating whether anyone objects), not Rule 41; Rule 41 filings for that purpose will be struck.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Rule 26(f) report and case management conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Rule 26(f) report and case management conference (trap): Exchange initial disclosures preferably at least 7 days before the Rule 26(f) conference (otherwise within 14 days after it, and be ready to explain why). Schedule the conference no later than receipt of the CMC notice, and include any pro se party. Use the judge’s Rule 26(f) Report form. The form also requires a litigation-funding disclosure of anyone with a financial interest, funding role, interest in proceeds, or control over strategy or settlement, which may be emailed ex parte to chambers and must be updated. The CMC is in person unless all parties move to go virtual at least 7 calendar days ahead, after filing the report. Motions to reschedule or to excuse or require

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion of any kind (compel, quash, protective order, subpoena, sanctions) may be filed until counsel confer in person or by phone (not just email or text), then contact chambers at (216) 357-7265 or Calabrese_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov for a phone or Zoom conference. The court may then call for letters of up to 2 pages before setting any briefing. Boilerplate and general objections are generally treated as waiving all objections, including privilege. Burden objections must explain or quantify the burden. A party unsure about responsiveness may submit documents for in camera review. Serve requests early enough that responses are due before the cut-off (e.g., 31 days ahead for a 30-day response). Disclose lay trial witnesses at least 30 days before the discovery cut-off or they will be precluded. Rebuttal expert

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Depositions (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Depositions (trap): Local Rule 30.1 is strictly enforced. Objections are limited to “Objection, Form” or “Objection, Foundation” unless the questioner asks for the reason or privilege is asserted. Interjections such as “if you know” or “if you remember” are treated as coaching. Don’t interrupt answers, repeat or paraphrase prior testimony (defending counsel’s repetition counts as a speaking objection), or mislead the witness. Evasive answers are treated as a failure to testify and may bring an additional deposition; yes-or-no questions get yes, no, or a statement that they can’t be answered that way. Agreements to change the 7-hour limit are enforced only if in writing; 7 hours means on the record, excluding breaks.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Sealing and redaction
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Sealing and redaction: Redactions (generally a few words) require a motion for leave, typically at least 7 days before the deadline, explaining each redaction, certifying conferral with the producing party and its position, and emailing chambers an unredacted copy with proposed redactions marked. Sealing an entire document is allowed only rarely. A confidentiality designation under a protective order is not enough; the movant must justify sealing document by document under Shane Group. Once approved, file the redacted version, serve the unredacted version, and file it under seal.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment, conferences, and settlement
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment, conferences, and settlement: One summary judgment motion per party without leave; no responsive summary judgment motion unless ordered (all dispositive motions are due on the CMO deadline), and motions in limine may not substitute for summary judgment. Tell the court when the deadline is set if cross-motions are expected. For a status conference, give the court and other parties a summary of each issue at least 3 days ahead. Scheduling conflicts with court-set conferences: confer and file a notice with the reason and 3 alternative dates (not for trial dates or CMO deadlines). Contact chambers by phone or email only for discovery issues and scheduling. Final pretrial: lead trial counsel, parties (for entities, the person most familiar with the facts, not in-house counsel), and a representative with full and final authority up to the

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Newer lawyers
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Newer lawyers: If a notice is filed before the ruling saying a lawyer with 5 or fewer years in practice will argue all or a material part of a motion (including objections to an R&R), the court will hear oral argument. Requests to split witness examinations or arguments at trial should be raised at the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases (trap): Lead counsel must attend all proceedings, and the defendant must attend the final pretrial and trial. Responses to any motion are due in 7 days unless set otherwise; travel motions filed within 48 hours of travel are denied absent emergency. The government must answer discovery requests within 1 week; motions to compel are due within 1 week of a denial or non-response, and requests are docketed as notices. The order includes a sua sponte Brady directive, with in camera review of favorable but arguably immaterial information. Plea agreements go to chambers by e

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Motions to dismiss and early conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Motions to dismiss and early conference (trap): Chambers schedules an Initial Telephone Conference once the defendant appears; be ready to brief the judge on the facts, settlement talks, and key issues. The CMC is set during that call. No motion to dismiss may be filed before the Initial Telephone Conference. The judge requires counsel to discuss the basis for any such motion and routinely lets plaintiff amend to cure; an answer date falling before the conference is automatically tolled.

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment pre-motion letters (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment pre-motion letters (trap): No summary judgment motion may be filed until counsel meet and confer and exchange letters. The movant briefly outlines the merits with key record and legal citations; the opponent responds in writing identifying the genuine disputes of material fact. Keep letters short (bullet points encouraged); sample letters are posted on the judge’s page. File the letters as a joint attachment to a Motion for a Telephone Conference. The judge then discusses the motion and, if appropriate, sets a briefing schedule. More generally, no dispositive motion may be filed until counsel confer on its merits and enough discovery is done for the movant to represent there are no disputed material facts; timing must not disrupt the case schedule or trial date.

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Motions and briefing (trap): No reply briefs without prior authorization. LR 7.1 deadlines and page limits otherwise apply. Noncompliant briefing will be struck by the Clerk. Every motion, procedural or substantive, must state in the caption whether it is “opposed” or “unopposed,” so counsel must confer before filing any motion. Oral argument is held when helpful, often with questions sent in advance; the judge encourages newer lawyers to argue.

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Courtesy copies (trap): Promptly deliver a bound, tabbed courtesy hard copy of all motion briefing and supporting materials (double-sided encouraged). docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: Initial disclosures must be exchanged at least 2 weeks before the CMC, and they mean actual documents, not just a list.
